children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 1
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s>, 1

children.text: parameśaṃ namaskṛtya bharadvājam ṛṣiṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) and then to the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s>,

children.text: harād indrakramāyātaṃ jñānaṃ śṛṇuta suvratāḥ || MrgT_1,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Hear, O virtuous ones, the knowledge that came from <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) in the lineage of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: * he suvratāḥ parameśvarabhaktiprakarṣaparipoṣitaśobhātiśayatvāt suṣṭhu śobhanaṃ vrataṃ śāstrīyaniyamānuṣṭhānaṃ yeṣāṃ ta eva śrotāraḥ saṃbodhitāḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:1
children.translated_text: 'O virtuous ones'—because their splendor is exceedingly nourished by the intensity of devotion to <s>Parameśvara</s>, those whose vow (<s>vrata</s>) is excellent—meaning the observance of scriptural regulations—those very listeners are addressed.

children.text: * yad vakṣyaty upasaṃhāre bhavatsu śivaśītāṃśujyotsnāpāṇḍuṣv idaṃ mayā // MrgTV_1,1.1:2
children.translated_text: As [the sage] will say in the conclusion: 'This [teaching] was given by me to you who are pale as the moonlight of <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: * tadicchayā mayaivoktam iti // MrgTV_1,1.1:3
children.translated_text: 'By His will alone was this spoken by me.'

children.text: * harād indrakramāyātaṃ jñānaṃ śṛṇuta ākarṇayateti sambandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:4
children.translated_text: 'The knowledge that came from <s>Hara</s> in the lineage of <s>Indra</s>—hear'—that is, 'listen'—this is the syntactic connection.

children.text: * harati paśubhyaḥ pāśān puṃso 'py ūrdhvaṃ padaṃ tatas tu haraḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:5
children.translated_text: 'He who takes away (<s>harati</s>) the bonds from bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) and also elevates a person to the higher state—therefore He is <s>Hara</s>.'

children.text: * iti yady api yaugikīyaṃ saṃjñā ananteśādiṣv api sāmānyā tathāpi indraśabdasaṃnidher ihomāpatāv eva haraśabdo jñeyaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:6
children.translated_text: Though this etymological designation is general and applies also to <s>Ananteśa</s> and others, nevertheless, due to the proximity of the word <s>Indra</s>, the word <s>Hara</s> here should be understood as referring to <s>Umāpati</s> (the Lord of Umā) alone.

children.text: * yathāhuḥ arthaḥ prakaraṇaṃ liṅgaṃ śabdasyānyasya saṃnidhiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:7
children.translated_text: As they say: 'Meaning, context, indication, and the proximity of another word—'

children.text: * proktāḥ sāmānyaśabdānāṃ viśeṣasthitihetavaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:8
children.translated_text: 'These are declared to be the causes for determining the specific referent of general words.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.1:9
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * kuta etad iti ced yasmād aindre asmin kāmikabhede bhagavata umāpater vaktṛtvena indrasya ca śrotṛtvenaiva sambandhaḥ pratītaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:10
children.translated_text: If one asks 'how is this known?'—because in this <s>Aindra</s> (Indra-related) division of the <s>Kāmika</s> [tantra], the relationship is understood with the Blessed <s>Umāpati</s> as the speaker and <s>Indra</s> as the listener alone.

children.text: * tathā hi purastād ihaiva munīnām indro vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: For indeed, later in this very [text], <s>Indra</s> will say to the sages:

children.text: * śivodgīrṇam idaṃ jñānaṃ mantramantreśvareśvaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This knowledge was emitted by <s>Śiva</s>, through the lords of <s>mantras</s> and the lords of <s>mantreśvaras</s>,

children.text: * kāmadatvāt kāmiketi pragītaṃ bahuvistaram // MrgTV_1,1.1:11
children.translated_text: Because it grants desires, it is celebrated extensively as <s>Kāmika</s>.'

children.text: * tebhyo 'vagatya dṛgjyotirjvālālīḍhasmaradrumaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having learned from them, He whose fire-of-the-eye's flames consumed the tree of <s>Kāma</s> (desire),

children.text: * dadāv umāpatir mahyam iti // MrgTV_1,1.1:12
children.translated_text: <s>Umāpati</s> gave [it] to me'—thus [Indra will say].

children.text: * tasmāddharāt śrīkaṇṭhanāthāt indrādikrameṇāyātam iti avatīrṇam // MrgTV_1,1.1:13
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'descended from <s>Hara</s>, the Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, in the lineage beginning with <s>Indra</s>'—meaning it has come down [in this succession].

children.text: * kiṃ tat // MrgTV_1,1.1:14
children.translated_text: What is it?

children.text: * jñāyante anena vidyācaryākriyāyogā iti jñānaṃ śāstram // MrgTV_1,1.1:15
children.translated_text: 'That by which <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>caryā</s> (conduct), <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), and <s>yoga</s> are known'—this is the <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), meaning the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture).

children.text: * kiṃ kṛtvā śṛṇuta // MrgTV_1,1.1:16
children.translated_text: Having done what? Listen.

children.text: * parameśvaraṃ namaskṛtya sṛṣṭisthitisaṃkṣobhaṇādibhiś cidacillakṣaṇaṃ viśvam īṣṭe itīśaḥ īdṛktvaṃ cānanteśādīnām apy astīti paramapadena viśeṣaṇam // MrgTV_1,1.1:17
children.translated_text: 'Having bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s>'—He who rules the universe characterized by consciousness and insentience through creation, maintenance, agitation, and so forth—that is <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord). Since such lordship also exists in <s>Ananteśa</s> and others, the qualifier '<s>parama</s>' (supreme) distinguishes Him.

children.text: * paramaś cāsāv anyeṣāṃ tadanugrahataḥ śivatvābhivyakteḥ īśaś ca svātantryeṇa sthityādikaraṇāt parameśaḥ taṃ namaskṛtya kāyavāṅmanobhis tasmin prahvībhūya // MrgTV_1,1.1:18
children.translated_text: He is 'supreme' because the <s>Śiva</s>-nature of others is manifested by His grace alone, and He is 'Lord' because He independently performs maintenance and so forth. '<s>Parameśa</s>'—having bowed to Him, that is, having become humble before Him through body, speech, and mind.

children.text: * tat ity anantaraṃ tantrāvatārakaṃ bharadvājam ṛṣim iti ṛ gatāv iti dhātvarthataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca gatyarthānāṃ jñānārthatvād avagataparamārthatayā ṛṣiḥ taṃ namaskṛtya śṛṇuteti śrotḥṇāṃ namaskāropadeśaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:19
children.translated_text: 'Then'—meaning 'thereafter'—'to the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> who brought down the <s>tantra</s>'—from the root ṛ meaning 'to go,' and since all roots meaning movement also convey knowledge, an <s>ṛṣi</s> is one who has realized the supreme truth. 'Having bowed to him—listen!' is an instruction to the listeners to pay homage.

children.text: * anamaskṛtaparameśvarāṇām apraṇatagurūṇāṃ ca nirvighnasaṃhitādhigamanāsaṃbhavāt // MrgTV_1,1.1:20
children.translated_text: Because for those who have not bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s> and who have not prostrated before the <s>guru</s>, it is impossible to study the scripture without obstacles.

children.text: * yaś ca śrotṛjanam evaṃ śikṣayati so 'rthāt kṛtatathāvidhavidhiḥ pravṛtta iti gamyate // MrgTV_1,1.1:21
children.translated_text: And one who thus instructs the listeners is understood to have himself performed such rites and then commenced [teaching].

children.text: * tena yathā parameśvaraṃ guruṃ ca nutvāham upadeṣṭuṃ pravṛttas tathā yūyam api pravartadhvam iti vyavasthitam // MrgTV_1,1.1:22
children.translated_text: By this it is established: 'Just as I, having bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s> and the <s>guru</s>, have commenced to teach, so too should you proceed.'

children.text: * yathā caitad indrasyomāpatinā upadiṣṭaṃ tadgranthaparisamāptau yady api granthe evāsti tathāpi vyākhyānopakrame sambandhāder avaśyābhidheyatvāt kiṃcid ucyate // MrgTV_1,1.1:23
children.translated_text: Although [the account of] how this was taught by <s>Umāpati</s> to <s>Indra</s> is in the text itself at the conclusion of the work, nevertheless, since the connection and other matters must be stated at the beginning of the commentary, something is said here.

children.text: * kadācid atiruciraratnaprakaravinicitakanakamayakamanīyamahītalamanoharasaptamajaladhitaṭaviharaṇahevākinaṃ nīlopalatviṣaṃ caturbhujaṃ dvikaṃdharādharaṃ mukhadvayena vedādhyayanasurāpānasaṃkarakāriṇam asuranivahaparivṛtaṃ durmadaṃ mahāsuraṃ tridaśapatir apaśyat // MrgTV_1,1.1:24
children.translated_text: Once, the lord of the gods saw a great <s>asura</s>—who sported on the charming ground of the seventh ocean's shore adorned with clusters of most beautiful gems set in gold; who had the luster of a blue lotus; who was four-armed, bearing two necks; who by his two mouths simultaneously practiced Vedic recitation and liquor-drinking, creating confusion; who was surrounded by hordes of <s>asuras</s>; who was insolently proud.

children.text: * atha tathāvidhadurācāradarśanajanitakopākulitamunigaṇasahitaḥ śatakratur akṣamamāṇo labdhavaratvāt prasabham astrair avadhyatām asya buddhvā phenenāntarnihitavastreṇa asurasya śirodvayaṃ cicheda // MrgTV_1,1.1:25
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra), accompanied by groups of sages agitated with anger born from witnessing such wicked behavior, unable to tolerate it, knowing that the <s>asura</s> was invulnerable to weapons due to having received a boon, severed the two heads of the <s>asura</s> with a cloth concealed within foam.

children.text: * tadvyāpādanataś ca brahmahatyājanitam agham āśaṅkamānas tatpraśāntaye bhagavantam acyutaṃ nāmnāṃ sahasreṇa ṛgyajuḥsāmabhiś cāstauṣīt // MrgTV_1,1.1:26
children.translated_text: Apprehending the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (brahmin-killing) arising from that slaying, he praised the Blessed <s>Acyuta</s> (Viṣṇu) with the thousand names and with <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> hymns, for the pacification of that sin.

children.text: * prasannena ca hariṇā navoditabhāsvadbhāsvaraṃ sarvabhūtābhibhāvukaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ kavacaṃ prayacchatā proktam // MrgTV_1,1.1:27
children.translated_text: And the pleased <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), while bestowing the <s>Nārasiṃha</s> (Man-Lion) armor, radiant as a newly risen sun and overpowering all beings, said:

children.text: * yathaitat saṃnaddhadehas tvam uttarakuruṣu bhagavantaṃ pinākinam ārādhaya varṣasahasrānte ca taṃ dṛṣṭvābhimatam āsādayiṣyasi ity uktvā antarhite surārau sarvaṃ tad indreṇa kṛtam // MrgTV_1,1.1:28
children.translated_text: 'Having thus armored your body, worship the Blessed <s>Pinākin</s> (Śiva) in <s>Uttarakuru</s>, and after a thousand years, having seen Him, you will obtain your desire.' Having spoken thus, when the enemy of the gods had vanished, <s>Indra</s> accomplished all of that.

children.text: * atha pratyakṣībhūte bhagavati pinākini nikhiladuḥkhāntaś cāsya saṃjātaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:29
children.translated_text: Then, when the Blessed <s>Pinākin</s> (Śiva) became directly visible to him, the end of all suffering was born for him.

children.text: * śrīmatkāmikākhyaṃ cāsmai parameśvara upadideśa // MrgTV_1,1.1:30
children.translated_text: And <s>Parameśvara</s> taught him the glorious [tantra] called <s>Kāmika</s>.

children.text: * yataś cendrasya nṛsiṃharūpiṇaḥ samupadiṣṭam idam umāpatinā tato mṛgendrasya śrotṛtvān mṛgendrasaṃjñayā prathitam // MrgTV_1,1.1:31
children.translated_text: And since this was taught by <s>Umāpati</s> to <s>Indra</s> in the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> (the Man-Lion), it became known by the name <s>Mṛgendra</s> ('Lord of Beasts') because he was the listener.

children.text: * sambandhas tv atra ṣaṭprakāraḥ parādiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:32
children.translated_text: The connection here is of six kinds, beginning with the supreme.

children.text: * tathāhi sargādau parameśvaraḥ ūrdhvaprāgdakṣiṇottarapaścimasrotaḥpañcakabhedabhinnaṃ jñānaṃ svecchānugṛhītavidyeśvarāṣṭakaprabodhanānantaraṃ tad abhivyaktaṃ mantreśvarādibhyo vakṣyamāṇavad ādideśa // MrgTV_1,1.1:33
children.translated_text: For at the beginning of creation, <s>Parameśvara</s> divided the knowledge into five streams—upper, eastern, southern, northern, and western—and after awakening the eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge) graced by His own will, taught that manifested [knowledge] to <s>Mantreśvaras</s> and others, as will be described.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe /
children.translated_text: As is also stated in the glorious <s>Kiraṇa</s> [tantra]:

children.text: * sṛṣṭyanantaram eveśaḥ śivān sṛṣṭvā dṛśātmajān /
children.translated_text: 'Immediately after creation, the Lord, having created the <s>Śivas</s> born from His gaze,

children.text: * jñānam ekaṃ vibhajyāśu teṣāṃ tatsaṃkhyayāvadata // MrgTV_1,1.1:34
children.translated_text: Quickly dividing the one knowledge, taught them according to their number.'

children.text: * kāmikaṃ praṇavākhyasya śivākhyasya tu yogajam /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Kāmika</s> [stream] for the one named <s>Praṇava</s>, and the <s>Yogaja</s> for the one named <s>Śiva</s>,'

children.text: * ityādi // MrgTV_1,1.1:35
children.translated_text: And so forth.

children.text: * atra cātmajān iti ātmanaiva niradhikaraṇenānugraheṇānugṛhītān ity āśayaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:36
children.translated_text: Here, 'born from Himself' means 'graced by His own grace without any external instrumentality'—this is the purport.

children.text: * tebhya umāpatiḥ prāpa tasmāc ca śakraḥ tato 'pi bharadvājaḥ tatsakāśāt tu hārītaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:37
children.translated_text: From them, <s>Umāpati</s> (Śiva) received it; from Him, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra); from him, <s>Bharadvāja</s>; and from him, <s>Hārīta</s>.

children.text: * sa punaḥ svaśiṣyebhyaḥ prāheti purastāt sarvaṃ spaṣṭīkariṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:38
children.translated_text: He in turn told his own disciples—we shall clarify all of this later.

children.text: * abhidheyāś ceha jñānakriyāyogacaryāḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:39
children.translated_text: And the subjects treated here are <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), <s>yoga</s>, and <s>caryā</s> (conduct).

children.text: * prayojanaṃ tv atra tattvajñaptiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:40
children.translated_text: The purpose here, however, is the knowledge of reality (<s>tattva</s>).

children.text: * tatprayojanam api bhuktimuktī /
children.translated_text: And the ultimate purpose of that is <s>bhukti</s> (worldly enjoyment) and <s>mukti</s> (liberation).

children.text: * parameśvarasadbhāvaprasādhakapramāṇopanyāsas tadbādhakanirākaraṇaṃ ca yady api tatpraṇītāgamaprāmāṇy asādhanāya prathamam evopayujyate tathāpi śāstrakāreṇaiva agre tad vivecitam atas tatraiva vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:41
children.translated_text: Although the presentation of proofs establishing the existence of <s>Parameśvara</s> and the refutation of objections to it are useful first of all for establishing the authority of the <s>āgama</s> composed by Him, nevertheless, since the author of the <s>śāstra</s> himself has discussed this later in the text, we shall address it there.

children.text: * kevalam etāvad eveha pratijānīmahe // MrgTV_1,1.1:42
children.translated_text: Here we merely make this assertion:

children.text: * yad uktam /
children.translated_text: As has been stated:

children.text: * āyurvedāc ca gaṇitān mantravādāc ca sasvarāt /
children.translated_text: 'From <s>Āyurveda</s>, from mathematics, from <s>mantravāda</s> (science of mantras) along with phonetics,

children.text: * rasopaniṣadāṭopād āptaḥ sa parigṛhyate // MrgTV_1,1.1:43
children.translated_text: And from the grandeur of the <s>Rasopaniṣad</s> (science of alchemy)—that teacher is accepted as authoritative.'

children.text: * iti tac cāptatvaṃ sāñjanatvād asarvārthadṛśāṃ darśanāntarapraṇetḥṇāṃ svasvaviṣayam eva nityanirmalaniratiśayasarvārthajñānakriyāśaktes tu sarvadā sarvānugrahapravṛttasya parameśvaratvād eva sarvādhiṣṭhātuḥ sarvaviṣayam // MrgTV_1,1.1:44
children.translated_text: And that authoritativeness is limited to their own respective domains for the founders of other philosophical systems, since they are impure and do not see all things; but for <s>Parameśvara</s>, because He is the supreme ruler of all, ever engaged in gracing all, possessing eternal, pure, unsurpassed power of knowledge and action regarding all things—His authoritativeness covers all domains.

children.text: * evaṃ vividhaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭasya vaktur vipralambhakatvāsaṃbhavān nāprāmāṇyam // MrgTV_1,1.1:45
children.translated_text: Since a speaker endowed with such manifold qualities cannot possibly be a deceiver, there is no invalidity of His teaching.

children.text: * etac ca yathāvasaraṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:46
children.translated_text: And we shall discuss this at the appropriate occasion.

children.text: * tad evam īdṛgrūpo bhagavān āgamasya kartā // MrgTV_1,1.1:47
children.translated_text: Thus, the Blessed Lord of such nature is the author of the <s>āgama</s>.

children.text: * āgamas tu taṃ jñāpayati // MrgTV_1,1.1:48
children.translated_text: And the <s>āgama</s> in turn makes Him known.

children.text: * ataś ca dvayor api visadṛśakriyatvān nātretaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ syāt // MrgTV_1,1.1:49
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the two have dissimilar functions, there is no fault of mutual dependence.

children.text: * yathā kaścid evaṃ vakti devadatto 'ham āyāta iti // MrgTV_1,1.1:50
children.translated_text: Just as someone says, 'I am <s>Devadatta</s>, I have come.'

children.text: * tadvākyaśravaṇāc ca tadanye manyante hanta devadatto 'yam āyāta iti // MrgTV_1,1.1:51
children.translated_text: And upon hearing that statement, others think, 'Ah, this <s>Devadatta</s> has come.'

children.text: * na cātra devadattasya tadvākyasya cetaretarāśrayatvaṃ yuktam // MrgTV_1,1.1:52
children.translated_text: Yet it is not appropriate to charge <s>Devadatta</s> and his statement with mutual dependence.

children.text: * tadukteṣu ca dṛṣṭārtheṣu viṣabhūtarasavādādiṣu tadāgamasya phalavattvam upalabhyādṛṣṭārthasyāpi tacchāsanasyāvitathatvam anumīyate ity alam anena prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.1:53
children.translated_text: And since the fruitfulness of that <s>āgama</s> is observed in its teachings concerning visible matters such as poisons and alchemy, the non-falsity of His teaching regarding invisible matters is also inferred. But enough of this—let us follow the main topic.

children.text: * tad evaṃ hārītamuniḥ svaśiṣyāṇāṃ jñānopadeśaṃ pratijñāya indrakramāyātatvaṃ darśayitum āha // MrgTV_1,1.1:54
children.translated_text: Thus, the sage <s>Hārīta</s>, having promised his disciples the teaching of knowledge, in order to show its descent in the lineage of <s>Indra</s>, said:

children.text: nārāyaṇāśrame puṇye bharadvājādayo dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the holy hermitage of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the twice-born <s>Bharadvāja</s> and others

children.text: tepuḥ śivaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tadekāhitamānasāḥ || MrgT_1,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: Performed austerities, having installed <s>Śiva</s>, with their minds fixed solely on Him.

children.text: * badaryāśramanāmni viṣṇor āśrame tadāśramatvād eva pāvane bharadvājaprabhṛtayo munayas tepur iti sambandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.2:1
children.translated_text: In the hermitage of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>Badarī</s>—which is purifying by being His hermitage—the sages beginning with <s>Bharadvāja</s> performed austerities—this is the syntactic connection.

children.text: * bharadvājādīnām ṛṣīṇām advijatvaprasiddhyasaṃbhavāt dvijā iti viśeṣaṇaṃ vāgīśvarīgarbhasaṃyojanasaṃjananādinā kṛtadīkṣātvenotkarṣavattvaṃ na punar upanītatvamātraṃ smārtavad dvijaśabdeneṣṭam adīkṣitānāṃ tantrādiśravaṇānadhikārāt pratyuta pratyavāyaśruteḥ // MrgTV_1,1.2:2
children.translated_text: Since it is impossible that the sages <s>Bharadvāja</s> and others were not twice-born, the qualifier 'twice-born' indicates their superiority through having been initiated via union with the womb of <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> and other rites, not merely Vedic <s>upanayana</s> investiture; for the uninitiated have no right to hear <s>tantras</s>, and indeed there are scriptural warnings of adverse consequences for them.

children.text: * śivaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyeti lohabāṇaliṅgādāv ādhāre sāmānyamantrādinā parameśvarapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ parikalpyety āśayaḥ anyathā yathāvad viditatattadvidhānānāṃ purastāt pratiṣṭhādiviṣayasya praśnasyānupapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,1.2:3
children.translated_text: 'Having installed <s>Śiva</s>' means having performed the installation of <s>Parameśvara</s> in a support such as a metal or crystal <s>liṅga</s> through general <s>mantras</s>—this is the intent. Otherwise, the later question about installation procedures would be pointless for those who already knew those rites properly.

children.text: * tasminn evaikasminn āhitam ekāgrīkṛtaṃ mānasaṃ yais te tathāvidhāḥ santaḥ tepuḥ śivārādhanalakṣaṇaṃ tapaś cakrur ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.2:4
children.translated_text: Those whose minds were placed and concentrated on that One alone—being such, they performed austerities characterized by the worship of <s>Śiva</s>—this is the meaning.

children.text: atha tān bhāvitān matvā kadācit tridaśādhipaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, considering them to be spiritually mature, the lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), at some point,

children.text: tad āśramapadaṃ bheje svayaṃ tāpasaveṣabhṛt || MrgT_1,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Personally assumed the guise of an ascetic and went to that hermitage.

children.text: * anantaraṃ ca tān bhāvitān tatraśraddhālūn jñātvā kasmiṃścit kāle munirūpadhārī śakraḥ tadīyam āśramaṃ siṣeve // MrgTV_1,1.3:1
children.translated_text: And thereafter, knowing them to be devoted and faithful, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), assuming the form of a sage, at some point in time visited their hermitage.

children.text: * tataś ca // MrgTV_1,1.3:2
children.translated_text: And then:

children.text: sa taiḥ sampūjitaḥ pṛṣṭvā tāṃś ca sarvān anāmayam /
children.translated_text: Having been duly honored by them, and having inquired about the well-being of them all,

children.text: provāca codanādharmaḥ kim arthaṃ nānuvartyate || MrgT_1,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'Why is the dharma enjoined in scripture not being followed?'

children.text: * sa indras tair bharadvājādibhir āśramasamucitenātithisatkāreṇābhyarcitas tān bharadvājādīn pratyekaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭvābravīt // MrgTV_1,1.4:1
children.translated_text: That <s>Indra</s>, having been honored by <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others with guest-hospitality befitting a hermitage, having asked each of the sages beginning with <s>Bharadvāja</s> about their welfare, said:

children.text: * kiṃ tad ity ata āha codanādharmaḥ kim arthaṃ nānuvartyata iti // MrgTV_1,1.4:2
children.translated_text: 'What is that?' To this he said: 'Why is the dharma of injunction not being followed?'

children.text: * codaneti kriyāyāḥ pravartakaṃ vacanam āhuḥ tadāmnāto dharmaḥ kim iti nānuṣṭhīyate codanaiva hi dharme pramāṇaṃ pramāṇam eva codanā ity evam anyayogāyogavyavacchedanena tataḥ pravartamānānām aihikasyāmutrikasya ca phalasyāvisaṃvādāt // MrgTV_1,1.4:3
children.translated_text: '<s>Codanā</s>' they call the utterance that prompts action; the dharma taught therein—why is it not being practiced? For <s>codanā</s> (injunction) alone is the means of knowing dharma, and the means of knowing is indeed <s>codanā</s>—by thus distinguishing what is appropriate and inappropriate, since for those who act accordingly there is no discordance regarding this-worldly and other-worldly results.

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: As is also stated:

children.text: * śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmam anutiṣṭhan hi mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, a man who follows the dharma declared in <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>smṛti</s> (remembered tradition)'

children.text: * iha kīrtim avāpnoti pretya cānuttamāṃ gatim iti // MrgTV_1,1.4:4
children.translated_text: *Here he obtains fame, and after death the supreme destination.

children.text: * tadviparītaṃ tu trayībāhyaṃ liṅgārādhanādi ca yat tat trayībāhyatvād eva phalguprāyam // MrgTV_1,1.4:5
children.translated_text: *But what is contrary to that — worship of the <s>liṅga</s> and the like, which is outside the three [Vedas] — that, by the very fact of being outside the three [Vedas], is mostly worthless.

children.text: * yad āha bhaṭṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: *As <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [Kumārila] has said:

children.text: * tathātikrāntavedoktamaryādāvyavahāriṇām /
children.translated_text: *'For those who transgress the boundary prescribed by the Veda and conduct [themselves accordingly],

children.text: * saṃvādiṣv api vākyeṣu neṣyate mānahetutā // MrgTV_1,1.4:6
children.translated_text: *even in statements that are concordant, authority as a source of valid knowledge is not accepted.'

children.text: * manur api /
children.translated_text: *<s>Manu</s> also [says]:

children.text: * yā vedabāhyāḥ smṛtayo yāś ca kāścit kudṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: *'Those <s>smṛtis</s> (remembered traditions) that are outside the Vedas and whatever evil views [there are] —

children.text: * sarvās tā niṣphalāḥ pretya tamobhūtā hi tāḥ smṛtāḥ // MrgTV_1,1.4:7
children.translated_text: *all of these are fruitless after death, for they are declared to be made of darkness.'

children.text: * ity evaṃ jaiminimatānusāriṇaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.4:8
children.translated_text: *Thus [spoke those] who follow the doctrine of <s>Jaimini</s>.

children.text: * tasya vacaḥ śrutvā // MrgTV_1,1.4:9
children.translated_text: *Having heard his words,

children.text: ta ūcur nanv ayaṃ dharmaś codanāvihito mune /
children.translated_text: They said: 'But this <s>dharma</s> is prescribed by [Vedic] injunction (<s>codanā</s>), O sage!

children.text: devatārādhanopāyas tapasābhīṣṭasiddhaye || MrgT_1,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: [It is] the means of propitiating the deity, for the attainment of one's desires through austerity.'

children.text: * te bharadvājādayaḥ indraṃ tāpasarūpatvān muniśabdenāmantrya nanv iti prativacanam avocan // MrgTV_1,1.5:1
children.translated_text: *Those [sages], <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others, addressing <s>Indra</s> with the word 'sage' because of his ascetic guise, spoke this reply beginning with 'But':

children.text: * yo 'yam asmābhir abhihito rudrākhyadevatāprasādanopāyalakṣaṇo dharmaḥ tapasā samīhitasiddhyartham āsevyate sa codanayaivābhihito vyavasthāpitaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.5:2
children.translated_text: *'This <s>dharma</s> described by us, characterized as the means of propitiating the deity called <s>Rudra</s>, which is practiced through austerity for the attainment of one's desires — it is prescribed and established by <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) alone.'

children.text: * tathā hi codanā nāma liḍloṭtavyadādiśabdavyavasthāpitavidhiniṣedharūpayajanādikriyāpravartakavacanam abhidhīyate // MrgTV_1,1.5:3
children.translated_text: *For <s>codanā</s> is defined as the verbal expression — established through verb-forms like the optative (<s>liṅ</s>), imperative (<s>loṭ</s>), and the <s>tavya</s>-suffix — that impels [one toward] activities such as sacrifice, in the form of injunctions and prohibitions.

children.text: * yathā jyotiṣṭomena yajeta svargakāmaḥ na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayet ityādi // MrgTV_1,1.5:4
children.translated_text: *For example: 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>' [injunction]; 'One should not eat the <s>Kalañja</s> [mushroom]' [prohibition]; and so forth.

children.text: * tac ca mukhyatayā śrautaṃ dharmarūpaṃ tanmūlatvāc ca smārtam api // MrgTV_1,1.5:5
children.translated_text: *And that [injunction], in its primary form, is <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic revelation) in the form of <s>dharma</s>; and because it has that [Veda] as its root, the <s>smārta</s> (traditional) [form] is also [authoritative].

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ tasmāc chrutismṛtī eva pramāṇaṃ dharmagocare // MrgTV_1,1.5:6
children.translated_text: *And thus it has been said: 'Therefore, in the domain of <s>dharma</s>, <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> alone are the means of valid knowledge.'

children.text: * iti tathā // MrgTV_1,1.5:7
children.translated_text: *And also:

children.text: * vedo 'khilo dharmamūlaṃ smṛtiśīle ca tadvidām /
children.translated_text: *'The entire Veda is the root of <s>dharma</s>, and [so are] the <s>smṛti</s> (traditions) and conduct of those who know it.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.5:8
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * tadāsatāṃ tāvad evaṃvidhāḥ śrutyādisadāgamārthāvirodhinyaḥ paurāṇikyaḥ saṃhitāḥ anyāś ca kāścana śrutayo yāsām idaṃ tātparyam // MrgTV_1,1.5:9
children.translated_text: *Setting those [Mīmāṃsā arguments] aside — there exist Purāṇic <s>saṃhitās</s> (collections) of this kind, which do not contradict the meaning of the good <s>āgamas</s> (scriptures) beginning with <s>śruti</s>, and also certain other <s>śrutis</s> (revelations), whose purport is this:

children.text: * yathā mahābhāratādau /
children.translated_text: *As in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and other [texts]:

children.text: * ye bhaktā varadaṃ devaṃ śivaṃ rudram umāpatim /
children.translated_text: *'Those who are devoted to the boon-granting god <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s> —

children.text: * ihaloke sukhaṃ prāpya te yānti paramāṃ gatim // MrgTV_1,1.5:10
children.translated_text: *having attained happiness in this world, they go to the supreme destination.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.5:11
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * sarvarūpaṃ bhavaṃ jñātvā liṅge yo 'rcayati prabhum /
children.translated_text: *'One who, knowing <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva) to be of all forms, worships the Lord in the <s>liṅga</s> —

children.text: * tasminn abhyadhikāṃ prītiṃ karoti vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.5:12
children.translated_text: *the Bull-bannered One (<s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>) shows supreme delight in him.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.5:13
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: *Likewise:

children.text: * ādityā vasavo rudrā munayaś ca mahaujasaḥ /
children.translated_text: *'The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and sages of great splendor,

children.text: * vidhival liṅgam ārādhya padam iṣṭatamaṃ gatāḥ // MrgTV_1,1.5:14
children.translated_text: *having worshipped the <s>liṅga</s> according to prescribed rites, attained the most desired state.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.5:15
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: *Likewise:

children.text: * mṛdbhasmagośakṛtpiṣṭaguḍakhaṇḍādiliṅgakam /
children.translated_text: *'A <s>liṅga</s> [made] of clay, ashes, cow-dung, flour, molasses, sugar-candy, and the like —

children.text: * sampūjayan pratiṣṭhāpya śraddhāvān adhigacchati // MrgTV_1,1.5:16
children.translated_text: *one who worships it after installing [it], if endowed with faith, attains [the desired goal].'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.5:17
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * tatrāprāmāṇyam abhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ yad abhiprāyeṇedam abhidhīyate bhavadbhiḥ sa tāvat śrutyartha eva smaryatāṃ tatra hi // MrgTV_1,1.5:18
children.translated_text: *Even conceding their non-authoritativeness [for the sake of argument], we say: the intention with which this is stated by you — let that be recognized as the very meaning of <s>śruti</s>. For:

children.text: vede 'sti saṃhitā raudrī vācyā rudraś ca devatā /
children.translated_text: 'There exists in the Veda a <s>Raudrī</s> (pertaining to <s>Rudra</s>) collection, and <s>Rudra</s> is the deity to be invoked.

children.text: sāṃnidhyakaraṇe 'py asmin vihitaḥ kālpiko vidhiḥ || MrgT_1,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: And for bringing about [his] presence, a rite prescribed in the <s>Kalpa</s> (ritual manual) is enjoined.'

children.text: * rudro devatāsyā iti raudrī saṃhitā ṛgyajuḥsāmalakṣaṇe cātharvaṇe ca vede 'sti /
children.translated_text: *A <s>Raudrī saṃhitā</s> — called so because <s>Rudra</s> is its deity — exists in the Veda characterized by <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, as well as in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

children.text: * yajurvede hi rudraikādaśinī saṃhitā śrūyate yasyāṃ bhagavanto rudrāḥ sarvābhipretasādhakāḥ paṭhyante /
children.translated_text: *For in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Rudraikādaśinī Saṃhitā</s> (Collection of the Eleven <s>Rudras</s>) is heard, in which the blessed <s>Rudras</s>, accomplishers of all desired ends, are recited.

children.text: * ṛgvede 'pi /
children.translated_text: *In the <s>Ṛgveda</s> also:

children.text: * tryambakaṃ yajāmahe // MrgTV_1,1.6:1
children.translated_text: *'We worship <s>Tryambaka</s> (the Three-eyed One)' [ṚV 7.59.12].

children.text: * imā rudrāya tavase kapardine // MrgTV_1,1.6:2
children.translated_text: *'These [hymns] to <s>Rudra</s>, the mighty one, the one with matted locks' [ṚV 1.114.1].

children.text: * imā rudrāya sthiradhanvane giraḥ // MrgTV_1,1.6:3
children.translated_text: *'These songs to <s>Rudra</s>, the one of firm bow' [ṚV 2.33.1].

children.text: * ityādikā ṛgvidhānāmnātās tattadviśiṣṭavidhānaphalā vidyanta eva /
children.translated_text: *Such [hymns] and others, enumerated in the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, with their respective specific prescribed results, certainly exist.

children.text: * sāmavede 'py asti /
children.translated_text: *In the <s>Sāmaveda</s> also there is [such material].

children.text: * śrūyate hi sāmnāṃ vidhāne /
children.translated_text: *For it is heard in the <s>Sāmavidhāna</s> (rules for the <s>Sāman</s> chants):

children.text: * ā vo rājā tad vo varga ājyadohāni devavratāni caiṣā raudrī nāma saṃhitaitāṃ prayuñjāno rudraṃ prīṇāti // MrgTV_1,1.6:4
children.translated_text: *'<s>Ā vo rājā</s> [is the first chant], <s>tad vo</s> [begins] the section, together with the <s>ājyadoha</s>-chants and the <s>devavrata</s>-chants — this is called the <s>Raudrī Saṃhitā</s>; one who employs it pleases <s>Rudra</s>.'

children.text: * iti /
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * evam ātharvaṇe 'pi rudrārādhanavidhayaḥ tanmantrasaṃhitāś ca sambhavanti // MrgTV_1,1.6:5
children.translated_text: *Likewise in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> also, rites for the propitiation of <s>Rudra</s> and collections of his <s>mantras</s> are found.

children.text: * na ca kevalaṃ saṃhitāmātram evāsti // MrgTV_1,1.6:6
children.translated_text: *And not merely the <s>saṃhitā</s> (collection) alone exists.

children.text: * tatra tatra rudra eva devatā vācyarūpatayā śrūyate yam uddiśya /
children.translated_text: *Here and there, <s>Rudra</s> himself is heard as the deity in the form of the one addressed, with reference to whom [it is said]:

children.text: * eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ saha svasrāmbikayā taṃ juṣasva svāhā /
children.translated_text: *'This is your share, O <s>Rudra</s>, together with your sister <s>Ambikā</s>; enjoy it! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

children.text: * iti śrutiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.6:7
children.translated_text: *Thus [says] the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: * na caitāvat yāvatkālpika iti kalpo vedāṅgaṃ tadukto vidhiḥ bhagavataḥ sāṃnidhyakalpanāya śrūyate // MrgTV_1,1.6:8
children.translated_text: *And this is not all — inasmuch as [the verse says] '<s>kālpika</s>' (pertaining to <s>Kalpa</s>), a rite prescribed in the <s>Kalpa</s> — which is a <s>Vedāṅga</s> (limb of the Veda) — is heard for bringing about the presence of the Lord.

children.text: * tathā hi kāṭhake sūtrapariśiṣṭīye rudrakalpe /
children.translated_text: *For thus in the <s>Kāṭhaka Rudrakalpa</s>, a supplement to the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: * triṣavaṇam udakopasparśanam ity uktvoktaṃ darbheṣv āsīno darbhamuṣṭiṃ dhārayamāṇo rakṣobhyopyavijñeyo bhavati śākayāvakapayobhaikṣabhakṣaḥ ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ pratyakṣībhavantaṃ bhagavantaṃ paśyati /
children.translated_text: *Having said 'ablution three times daily,' it states: 'Seated on <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass), holding a handful of <s>darbha</s>, he becomes unrecognizable to [hostile] beings; subsisting on vegetables, barley-gruel, milk, and alms-food, within six months he sees the Lord becoming directly visible.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.6:9
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * evaṃ ca śraddadhānamanasāṃ jaiminīyacchāyāśrayiṇām api codanāpradarśito 'yam astīva prasiddhaḥ panthāḥ kiṃ punaḥ parameśvaraprakāśanavihatamahāmohatimiratayā vispaṣṭadṛṣṭīnām anyeṣām // MrgTV_1,1.6:10
children.translated_text: *Thus, even for those of faithful minds who take shelter under the shadow of the <s>Jaiminīya</s> school, this path indicated by <s>codanā</s> (Vedic injunction) exists as an acknowledged [way]; how much more so for others whose vision is clear, the great darkness of delusion having been dispelled by the illumination of the Supreme Lord!

children.text: ity ukte 'pi paraṃ bhāvaṃ jijñāsuḥ prahasan prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when [they] had spoken thus, the Lord, wishing to know their supreme devotion, smiling,

children.text: tān āha mithyā jñānaṃ vaḥ śabdamātraṃ hi devatā || MrgT_1,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: said to them: 'Your knowledge is false, for deity is merely a word.'

children.text: * evam api kathite tadīyaṃ bhaktiprakarṣaṃ jñātum icchur indratvena paramaiśvaryayogāt prabhuḥ prabhavanaśīlaḥ sa tān munīn sasmitam āha // MrgTV_1,1.7:1
children.translated_text: *Even when [the sages] had spoken thus, he — being the Lord through his identity as <s>Indra</s> and through the possession of supreme sovereignty, the Lord whose nature is to prevail — wishing to know the intensity of their devotion, spoke to those sages with a smile.

children.text: * kiṃ tat // MrgTV_1,1.7:2
children.translated_text: *What [did he say]?

children.text: * mithyā jñānaṃ vaḥ yuṣmākaṃ sambandhi yad etalliṅgārcanādiśivārādhanapratipādakaṃ jñānaṃ śāstraṃ tan mithyā na satyaṃ tat praṇetṛtathāvidhadevatānupapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,1.7:3
children.translated_text: *'Your knowledge is false' — the knowledge belonging to you, that is, the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) that teaches the worship of <s>Śiva</s> through the adoration of the <s>liṅga</s> and the like — that is false, not true, because of the impossibility of the existence of such a deity as the author [of the scripture].

children.text: * yataḥ karmānuṣṭhānād eva phalaṃ na devatātaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.7:4
children.translated_text: *Because the fruit [of sacrifice] comes from the performance of the ritual action alone, not from the deity.

children.text: * śabdamātraṃ hi devatā // MrgTV_1,1.7:5
children.translated_text: *'For deity is merely a word.'

children.text: * na khalu vayaṃ pratyakṣetarapramāṇāpahnavapravṛttadurācāracārvākavadasaṃbhavam eva devatāyāḥ pratipadyāmahe // MrgTV_1,1.7:6
children.translated_text: *'Certainly, we do not hold that the deity is entirely non-existent, as do the wicked <s>Cārvākas</s> who proceed by denying all means of valid knowledge other than perception.'

children.text: * kiṃ tarhi // MrgTV_1,1.7:7
children.translated_text: *'What then?'

children.text: * vidyata eva devatā sā tu śabdān nātiricyate api tu ayogolakavahnivad anupalabhyamānavācyārthapṛthagbhāvaḥ śabda eva teṣu teṣu kriyāviśeṣeṣu aṅgabhāvaṃ gacchan yāgasampradānadevatā viśeṣākhyāṃ labhate // MrgTV_1,1.7:8
children.translated_text: *'The deity indeed exists, but it does not exceed the word. Rather, like fire in an iron ball — whose separate existence from the designated object is imperceptible — it is the word itself that, entering into the status of a subsidiary element in each respective ritual act, obtains the specific designation of "deity to whom the sacrifice is offered."'

children.text: * tad uktam /
children.translated_text: *As it has been said:

children.text: * avinirbhinnaśabdārthaṃ dhyāyed oṃkāram īśvaram /
children.translated_text: *'One should meditate on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the Lord, whose word and meaning are undifferentiated.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.7:9
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * na cātra kaścid eka eva viśveśitāstīti niyamaḥ pratijñātuṃ śakyaḥ anekākārasuprasiddhabahutaradevatāviśeṣaśravaṇāt // MrgTV_1,1.7:10
children.translated_text: *'And here no restriction can be affirmed that there exists one single ruler of all, because of the hearing [in the Vedas] of very many well-known deities of various forms.'

children.text: * tac cedam anupamamahimnaḥ śabdarūpasyaivaṃ vijṛmbhitaṃ yad ekam api sat tat tad devatāviśeṣapratītihetutām ātmapratītihetutāṃ cābhyeti // MrgTV_1,1.7:11
children.translated_text: *'And this is the unparalleled glory of the word-form that has thus manifested — that though it is one, it becomes the cause of the cognition of this or that specific deity, and also the cause of the cognition of the Self.'

children.text: * tathaiva śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: *In this very way, the <s>śruti</s> [says]:

children.text: * indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇam agnim āhur atho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān /
children.translated_text: *'They call him <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and he is the divine, beautiful-winged <s>Garutmān</s>.

children.text: * ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadanty agniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānam āhuḥ // MrgTV_1,1.7:12
children.translated_text: *The wise call the One Being by many names — they call him <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Mātariśvan</s>' [ṚV 1.164.46].

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.7:13
children.translated_text: *Thus.

children.text: * tat saṃsthitam etac chabdātmikā devateti // MrgTV_1,1.7:14
children.translated_text: *'Therefore it is established that the deity is of the nature of the word.'

children.text: * evam anvayenābhidhāya vyatirekeṇāmum evārthaṃ draḍhayitum āha // MrgTV_1,1.7:15
children.translated_text: *Having stated this by positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), he spoke to strengthen this very meaning by negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>):

children.text: śabdetaratve yugapadbhinnadeśeṣu yaṣṭṛṣu /
children.translated_text: 'If [the deity] were other than the word, [then] when sacrificers in different places [sacrifice] simultaneously,

children.text: na sā prayāti sāṃnidhyaṃ mūrtatvād asmadādivat || MrgT_1,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: it could not attain presence [at each of their sacrifices], because of being corporeal, like us.'

children.text: * śabdavyatiriktā hi yadi devatā vidyate kiṃ vigrahavatī avigrahā ubhayarūpānubhayarūpā vā // MrgTV_1,1.8:1
children.translated_text: *'For if a deity exists that is different from the word — is it corporeal, incorporeal, of both natures, or of neither nature?'

children.text: * anubhayarūpatve viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ svasiddhāntaviruddhānekāntavādābhyupagamaḥ vyastapakṣadvayodbhāvitadoṣaprasaṅgaś ca // MrgTV_1,1.8:2
children.translated_text: *'If of neither nature, there would be the superimposition of contradictory attributes, the acceptance of a non-exclusive position contradicting one's own established doctrine, and the consequence of faults arising from both alternatives taken separately.'

children.text: * avigrahatve śabdenaiva kim aparāddham // MrgTV_1,1.8:3
children.translated_text: *'If incorporeal, what wrong has the word itself done [that it should be rejected]?'

children.text: * vigrahavattve tu bhinnadeśāvasthiteṣu yugapat prārabdhayāgeṣu yajvasu mūrtatvāt tasyāḥ sāṃnidhyānupapattiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.8:4
children.translated_text: *'But if corporeal, then when sacrificers situated in different places simultaneously commence their sacrifices, the presence [of the deity at each place] is impossible because of its corporeality.'

children.text: * nanu mūrtatve saty api sāṃnidhyaṃ parasparavidūradeśasthopasthātṛjanopahṛtasaparyayor arkendubimbayor dṛṣṭam ity anaikāntikaṃ mūrtatvam // MrgTV_1,1.8:5
children.translated_text: *'[Objection:] But even in the case of corporeality, presence [at multiple places] is observed in the case of the orbs of the sun and moon, whose worship is offered by people situated in mutually distant places — therefore corporeality [as a reason for impossibility of presence] is inconclusive.'

children.text: * nānaikāntikam arkendubimbayoḥ svaprabhābhāsvarayor uccataratvena sakaladeśopalakṣyasthānamātrasthayor bahujanopalambhayogyadeśāvasthānam eva sāṃnidhyaṃ bhavatāṃ pratibhāti na vāstavam // MrgTV_1,1.8:6
children.translated_text: *'It is not inconclusive. In the case of the orbs of the sun and moon, which are luminous with their own radiance, being situated at an extremely high elevation — being merely located in a position observable from every place — the "presence" that appears to you is [merely their] being situated in a position accessible to the perception of many people; it is not real [presence at those places].'

children.text: * tathā cātyuttuṅgaraṅgotsaṅgavartinī nartakī vidūradeśavartibhir bhūyobhiḥ prekṣakaiḥ prekṣyamāṇā naikaikaṃ prati prākāmyaśaktyā sāṃnidhyaṃ bhajate // MrgTV_1,1.8:7
children.translated_text: *'Likewise, a dancer performing on an extremely elevated stage, though watched by numerous spectators situated in distant places, does not possess presence toward each one individually through the power of omnipresence.'

children.text: * tasmāt samakālam anekagṛhabhojanopanimantritānāṃ yathāsmākam anekagṛhabhojanaṃ na dṛṣṭam evaṃ devatāyās tulyakālaṃ bhinnadeśasthayāgasāṃnidhyaṃ mūrtatvān na saṃbhāvyam iti śabdamātratvam evāsyāḥ sādhīyaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.8:8
children.translated_text: *'Therefore, just as we, when simultaneously invited to dine at many houses, are not observed eating at many houses [at once], so too, the presence of the deity at sacrifices in different places at the same time is not conceivable because of its corporeality — therefore, its being merely a word is the stronger [position].'

children.text: * kiṃca // MrgTV_1,1.8:9
children.translated_text: *'Moreover:'

children.text: na ca tatsādhakaṃ kiṃcit pramāṇaṃ bhāty abādhitam /
children.translated_text: 'Nor does any uncontradicted means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) appear that would establish it [i.e., the deity as a real entity].'

children.text: * na kila tathāvidhavyatyayadaśāvirahitaparamaparokṣavapuṣaḥ prakṛṣṭātiśayaiśvaryopapannajñānānantamahimno devatāviśeṣasya sādhakaṃ kim api pramāṇaṃ pratibhāti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:1
children.translated_text: *'Indeed, no means of valid knowledge whatsoever appears that would establish [the existence of] a specific deity — one whose form is supremely beyond perception, never devoid of the capacity to reverse [ordinary states], endowed with exalted and extraordinary sovereignty, and of infinite glory of knowledge.'

children.text: * tathā hi aparokṣatvena sakalapramāṇajyeṣṭhasya pratyakṣasya tāvan nāsau gocaraḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:2
children.translated_text: *'For firstly, it is not within the range of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), which, by virtue of its directness, is the chief of all means of valid knowledge.'

children.text: * na hy atīndriyaviṣayagrahaṇakṣamatvaṃ pratyakṣasya sambhavati // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:3
children.translated_text: *'For perception cannot have the capacity to apprehend a supersensory object.'

children.text: * atha vyavahitaviprakṛṣṭārthaviṣayaṃ yogipratyakṣaṃ tat sattāniścāyakam iti cet tan na yasmād asmadādyatīndriyārthadarśino yoginaḥ sūkṣmādiviṣayas tatpratyakṣaṃ tena ceśaḥ sākṣātkriyate ity etat sarvam anupapannaṃ pramāṇābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:4
children.translated_text: *'If [you say] that the perception of yogis, whose object is hidden and distant things, ascertains its existence — that is not so, because [the claim that] yogis who see supersensory objects like us [exist], that their perception has subtle objects as its domain, and that the Lord is directly realized by it — all of this is unestablished due to the absence of a [prior] means of valid knowledge [to establish the yogis' capacity].'

children.text: * atīndriyo 'tīndriyārthadarśī ca kaścit sādhayitum iṣṭas tasya tathāvidhapuruṣapratyakṣeṇāsiddhena sādhanaṃ prāmāṇikasyāpi bhavataḥ kim iti na trapāvaham // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:5
children.translated_text: *'What is desired to be proved is something supersensory, and also someone who sees supersensory objects — to prove that by means of the unestablished perception of such a person: is this not embarrassing even for you who claim to be an authority?'

children.text: * nanv asty atrānupahatasāmarthyam anumānaṃ tathā hi jagad idam urvīparvatasaritsamudrādi dharmi kāryam iti sādhyo dharmaḥ sāvayavatvāt yad yat sāvayavaṃ tat tat kāryaṃ yathā valabhiprākārapuṣkariṇyādi // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:6
children.translated_text: *'[Objection:] But here there is inference (<s>anumāna</s>) with unimpaired capacity! For: this world — earth, mountains, rivers, oceans, and the like — is the subject; "it is an effect" is the property to be established; because it has parts; whatever has parts is an effect — like a hall, a wall, a lotus-pond, and so forth.'

children.text: * vipakṣavyāvṛttaś cāyaṃ hetur yatra kilātmādau kāryatvaṃ nāsti tatra sāvayavatvam api nāstīti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:7
children.translated_text: *'And this logical reason is excluded from the counter-instance — for where, as in the case of the Self and the like, there is no being-an-effect, there also is no having-parts.'

children.text: * na cāsya hetor īśvaraśarīreṇānaikāntikatvaṃ yathāhur jaiminīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: *'Nor is there inconclusiveness of this logical reason with regard to the body of the Lord, as the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> maintain —'

children.text: * anekāntaś ca hetus te taccharīrādinā bhavet /
children.translated_text: And your reason [for inferring God] would be inconclusive through that [counter-example of] bodies and the like.

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:8
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tasyāpi tadicchākāryatvena asmābhir iṣyamāṇatvād iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:9
children.translated_text: Because even that [body etc.] is accepted by us as being an effect of His will.

children.text: * siddhe ca jagataḥ kāryatve 'pi yad yat kāryaṃ tat tad viśiṣṭajñānakriyopapannakartṛkāvinābhāvi ghaṭapaṭādivat // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:10
children.translated_text: Even when the world's character as an effect is established, whatever is an effect is invariably concomitant with an agent possessing distinguished knowledge and activity, like a pot, cloth, and the like.

children.text: * kāryaṃ cedaṃ jagat // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:11
children.translated_text: And this world is an effect.

children.text: * tasmād idam api niratiśayajñatvakartṛtvasampannaṃ nirmātāraṃ gamayati // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:12
children.translated_text: Therefore, this world too implies a creator endowed with unsurpassable knowledge and agency.

children.text: * yaś cātra nirmātā sa kaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:13
children.translated_text: And who is the creator here?

children.text: * īśvara iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:14
children.translated_text: It is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).

children.text: * kim etan na pramāṇaṃ bhavet // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:15
children.translated_text: Would this not be a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)?

children.text: * etad yady abādhitaṃ syāt yāvatā paramāṇvindriyāder jagadbhāgasyāsiddhaṃ sāvayavatvam iti bhāgāsiddho 'yaṃ hetuḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:16
children.translated_text: This would be valid if it were uncontradicted; but since the composite nature of that part of the world consisting of <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms), sense-faculties, and the like is unestablished, this reason has an unestablished qualifier.

children.text: * paramāṇūnām ācaitanye sati anekatvād ghaṭādivat kāryatvam avyabhicāri iti kila bhavatām abhyupagamaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:17
children.translated_text: Your position, it seems, is that atoms, being non-conscious and multiple, invariably have the character of being effects, like a pot and the like.

children.text: * yad apy etat dṛṣṭāntīkṛtaṃ valabhiprākārapuṣkariṇyādi tad gatam upādānasahakārikāraṇādyānuguṇyavaiguṇyāt nirvṛttasadasatsaṃniveśaṃ sāvayavatvam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:18
children.translated_text: As for what is used as an example—palace roofs, ramparts, pools, and the like—that is understood: the compositeness with its good and bad arrangements arises from the suitability or unsuitability of material and auxiliary causes.

children.text: * tadanyad eva tattatsaṃniveśasadṛśam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:19
children.translated_text: What is other than that—namely, the natural world—merely resembles those particular arrangements.

children.text: * itarad eva hi mahīmahīdharādigataṃ sāvayavatvaṃ vastusādṛśyāvalambanapūrvavyāptidarśanāhitasaṃskārā ca tadanuguṇasādhyasādhanārthaṃ prāmāṇikam iti pravartata iti yuktaṃ na punaḥ sāvayavatvaśabdamātrasāmānyāśrayeṇa // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:20
children.translated_text: For the compositeness found in earth, mountains, and the like is altogether different; and the inferential warrant, based on latent impressions deposited by prior observation of invariable concomitance relying on the resemblance of things, operates for inferring what is to be proved and what proves it in accordance with that observed resemblance—this is proper. But it is not proper to infer on the basis of the mere generality of the word 'composite.'

children.text: * yad āha dharmakīrtiḥ /
children.translated_text: As <s>Dharmakīrti</s> has said:

children.text: * siddhaṃ yādṛg adhiṣṭhātṛbhāvābhāvānuvṛttimat /
children.translated_text: 'That which is established as conforming to the presence and absence of a governing agent of a specific kind—

children.text: * saṃniveśādi tad yuktaṃ tasmād yad anumīyate // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:21
children.translated_text: Such arrangement and the like—it is proper to infer from that.'

children.text: * vastubhede prasiddhe 'pi śabdasāmyād abhedinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even when a real difference between things is well-known, to treat them as identical because of verbal similarity—

children.text: * na yuktānumitiḥ pāṇḍudravyād iva hutāśane // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:22
children.translated_text: Is not a proper inference—like inferring fire from a pale substance.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:23
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * api ca valabhyādīnāṃ pakṣāntarbhāve dṛṣṭāntābhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:24
children.translated_text: Moreover, if palace roofs and the like are included in the thesis, there is no example left.

children.text: * na cetaratrāntarbhāvaḥ tadā īśvarasya sarvakartṛtvahāniḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:25
children.translated_text: But if they are included elsewhere as examples, then <s>Īśvara's</s> omnipotent creatorship is lost.

children.text: * sthapatyādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyinau bhāvābhāvau valabhyādīnāṃ dṛṣṭau // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:26
children.translated_text: The existence and non-existence of palace roofs and the like are observed to follow the positive and negative concomitance of architects and the like.

children.text: * na ca dṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇam apahāya kāraṇāntaraṃ tadīśvarākhyaṃ kalpayitum upapannam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:27
children.translated_text: And it is not appropriate to set aside an observed cause and postulate another cause called '<s>Īśvara</s>.'

children.text: * evaṃ hi sati sarvatra kāryakāraṇabhāvo viplaveta // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:28
children.translated_text: For if this were so, the causal relation would be undermined everywhere.

children.text:
* tad uktam /
* yasmin sati bhavaty eva yat tato 'nyasya kalpane /
children.translated_text: As it has been stated: 'When something exists and a particular effect invariably occurs, to postulate something else as the cause—'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:30
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * kiṃ ca na tāvad aśarīrajagannirmātṛdevatāviśeṣābhyupagamo yuktaḥ tasya jagallakṣaṇakāryasampādanāsaṃbhavāt // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:31
children.translated_text: Furthermore, it is not reasonable to accept a bodiless deity as the special creator of the world, because for such a bodiless being, the accomplishment of the effect characterized as the world is impossible.

children.text: * yad āha /
children.translated_text: As it has been said:

children.text: * kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptaṃ sadaiva yat /
children.translated_text: 'An effect is always invariably concomitant with an agent possessed of a body;

children.text: * kāryatvāt tena jagataḥ kartā dehī prasajyate // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:32
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the world's character as an effect, the consequence would be that the creator is embodied.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:33
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tataś ca dharmisvarūpaviparītasādhakaḥ kāryahetuḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:34
children.translated_text: And therefore the reason 'being an effect' proves something contrary to the intended nature of the subject [<s>Īśvara</s>, who is supposed to be bodiless].

children.text: * śarīravattve tv asmadādivad utpattipralayayogitvam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:35
children.translated_text: But if <s>Īśvara</s> has a body, then he would be subject to origination and dissolution, just like us.

children.text: * tac cāsya śarīraṃ svanirmitaṃ kartrantaranirmitaṃ vā // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:36
children.translated_text: And that body of his would be either self-created or created by another agent.

children.text: * svanirmitatve kim asau tatsargakāle saśarīraḥ śarīrarahito vā // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:37
children.translated_text: If self-created: was he, at the time of that creation, embodied or bodiless?

children.text: * dehendriyarahitasya na kvacit kiṃcit kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam ity uktam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:38
children.translated_text: It has already been stated that for one devoid of body and sense-faculties, no effect whatsoever is observed anywhere.

children.text: * śarīravāṃś cet śarīraṃ sṛjati tarhi tad apy asya śarīraṃ kiṃ kṛtam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:39
children.translated_text: And if he creates a body while already having a body, then by whom was that prior body of his created?

children.text: * svakṛtatve 'nyakṛtatve vānavasthety evamādibādhakasadbhāvāt sādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ na kiṃcid upapadyate // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:40
children.translated_text: Whether self-created or created by another, there is an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>); thus, due to the presence of such defeating considerations, no validating means of knowledge is established.

children.text: * athocyate vākyam āgamalakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇam asti yad atyantātīndriyārthaniścāyakaṃ tataḥ pravartamānasyābhipretasampatter dṛṣṭatvāt // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:41
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said: 'There exists a verbal testimony characterized as scripture (<s>āgama</s>), which is a means of knowledge ascertaining objects entirely beyond the senses, because one who acts in accordance with it is observed to attain the desired result'—

children.text: * tad āhuḥ akṣaliṅgātigo hy arthaḥ puṃsaḥ śāstreṇa darśyate /
children.translated_text: As they say: 'For the object that transcends sense-perception and inference is revealed to a person by scripture (<s>śāstra</s>).'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:42
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * etad eva nirākartum āha // MrgTV_1,1.9ab1:43
children.translated_text: It is precisely this that the author says in order to refute:

children.text: * vākyam āgamalakṣaṇaṃ purāṇetihāsādigītam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:1
children.translated_text: The verbal testimony characterized as scripture, celebrated in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, and the like—

children.text: * yathāha mahābhāratādau bhagavān vyāsamuniḥ /
children.translated_text: As the Blessed sage <s>Vyāsa</s> has said in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and elsewhere:

children.text: * sa śivas tāta tejasvī prasādād yāti te 'grataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That radiant <s>Śiva</s>, my child, by his grace goes before you;

children.text: * sendrādiṣu ca deveṣu tasyaivaiśvaryam ucyate // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:2
children.translated_text: And among the gods beginning with <s>Indra</s>, it is his sovereignty alone that is proclaimed.'

children.text: * taṃ gaccha śaraṇaṃ devadevādiṃ bhuvaneśvaram /
children.translated_text: 'Go to him for refuge, the God of gods, the first, the Lord of the universe'—

children.text: * ityādi // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:3
children.translated_text: And so forth.

children.text: * śrutāv api /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) also:

children.text: * yo rudro 'gnau yo 'psu ya oṣadhīṣu yo vanaspatiṣu /
children.translated_text: 'That <s>Rudra</s> who is in fire, who is in water, who is in plants, who is in trees—

children.text: * yo rudro viśvā bhuvanā viveśa tasmai rudrāya namo 'stu // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:4
children.translated_text: That <s>Rudra</s> who has entered all the worlds—to that <s>Rudra</s> let there be homage.'

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: * tryambakaṃ yajāmahe /
children.translated_text: 'We worship <s>Tryambaka</s> (the Three-eyed One)'—

children.text: * ityādi // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:5
children.translated_text: And so forth.

children.text: * tad etad anyathāsiddham atra hi paurvāparyaparyālocanānirākṛto yathāśrutaśrutisamutpādito vākyārthaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:6
children.translated_text: All this is otherwise explicable; for here the meaning of the statement, generated from the literal hearing of the <s>Śruti</s> without refutation by consideration of context and sequence—

children.text: * ato naiva pratītimātrāvipralabdhabuddhayas tatheti pratipattiṃ bhāvayanti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:7
children.translated_text: Therefore, those whose minds are not deceived by mere superficial understanding do not cultivate the conviction 'it is so.'

children.text: * tathā kila viṣaṃ bhakṣaya mā cāsya gṛhe bhuṅkthāḥ ity atra viṣabhakṣaṇe 'bhyanujñānaṃ śrūyamāṇam api na vākyārthaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:8
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the statement 'Eat poison, but do not eat in his house'—although permission to eat poison is what is literally heard, that is not the intended meaning of the statement.

children.text: * kiṃ tarhi // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:9
children.translated_text: What then?

children.text: * pratikūlagṛhabhojananiṣedha eva tātparyam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:10
children.translated_text: The purport is solely the prohibition of eating in an unfriendly house.

children.text: * evaṃ bhāratādāv upākhyānadvāreṇa sodyogasya vijigīṣor dviṣadupaśamo nirvighnaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca svadharmānuṣṭhānam abhyudayāyety evam arthaḥ stutivādaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:11
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and elsewhere, through the medium of narratives, the real meaning is a laudatory statement (<s>stutivāda</s>) to the effect that for an energetic warrior seeking conquest, the pacification of enemies is unimpeded, and the performance of the <s>Kṣatriya's</s> own <s>dharma</s> leads to prosperity.

children.text: * śrutau tu mantrārthavādapadānāṃ kāryātiśayāvedanaṃ vinā puruṣāpravṛtteḥ śraddhāvahavividhābhyudayajñānopajananapratītyaṅgatvaṃ na svarūpayāthārthyam ity aṅgatvam iti na taduktimātrād viśiṣṭadevatāsadbhāvāvedakatvam // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:12
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Śruti</s>, the passages of <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages) serve as ancillaries to the generation of faith-inspiring diverse knowledge of prosperity—since without indicating a superior result, people would not engage in action—and their ancillary role is just that, not truthfulness regarding their literal content; therefore, from such statements alone, the real existence of a special deity is not established.

children.text: * tathā cāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus they say:

children.text: * stutivādakṛtaś caiṣa janānāṃ mativibhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This delusion of people's minds is caused by laudatory statements (<s>stutivāda</s>);

children.text: * paurvāparyāparāmṛṣṭaḥ śabdo 'nyāṃ kurute mitim // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:13
children.translated_text: A word not examined in its context produces a different understanding.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:14
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * atha sakalalokasiddhā prasiddhir anapahnavanīyā vidyate yat sarvo hy ayam āvidvadaṅganābālo janaḥ parameśvarasyecchāvidhipreritaḥ pravartate daivam evātra kāraṇam iti bruvāṇo dṛśyate ca upākhyānāni ca dakṣamakhamathanakāladamanakāmadāhāndhakavadhatrailokyākramaṇādyuparacitāni bahuśaḥ paṭhantaḥ kathayantaḥ śṛṇvantaś copalabhyante taduddeśena cārthaviniyoganiyamajapatapaḥprabhṛtikleśakāriṇīm api karmapaddhatim anutiṣṭhanto 'smān avagamayanti yad uta santi devatāviśeṣā ity āha // MrgTV_1,1.9ab2:15
children.translated_text: Now, the opponent says: there exists a universally established convention that cannot be denied—namely, that all these people, from the unlettered to women and children, are observed to act as impelled by the will and ordinance of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), declaring 'Fate alone is the cause here'; and narratives composed about the destruction of <s>Dakṣa's</s> sacrifice, the subjugation of <s>Kāla</s> (Death), the burning of <s>Kāma</s> (Desire), the slaying of <s>Andhaka</s>, the striding over the three worlds, and the like are observed being recited, narrated, and heard by many; and for his sake, people are observed following the path of ritual action—including the arduous practices of property-dedication, observances, <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), and the like—all of which makes us understand that special deities exist. The author says in response:

children.text: vākyaṃ tad anyathāsiddhaṃ lokavādāḥ kva sādhavaḥ || MrgT_1,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: That verbal testimony is otherwise explicable; where are popular sayings (<s>lokavāda</s>) ever authoritative?

children.text: * aparyālocitapaurvāparyagatānugatamūrkhajanapravartitāt pravādamātrād asakṛddṛṣṭavyabhicārād vastusiddhim icchan aho bata vṛthaiva dainyāspadatām upayāto 'si // MrgTV_1,1.9cd:1
children.translated_text: Wishing to establish the existence of a real entity from a mere popular rumor set in motion by foolish people following one another without examination of context—a rumor that has been observed to deviate many times—alas, you have come to a state of pitiable wretchedness in vain!

children.text: * atha pratyayitapuruṣapravartitaḥ pravādaḥ tarhi āgama evāsau // MrgTV_1,1.9cd:2
children.translated_text: Now, if the popular tradition was set in motion by a trustworthy person, then it is simply scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

children.text: * pratyayitatvaṃ ca tasya katamena pramāṇena siddhaṃ tatpravartitād āgamaprāmāṇyāc ca tatsiddhiḥ tatsiddhyā ca āgamaprāmāṇyam itītaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ nityatve tv āgamasya kārya evārthe prāmāṇyaṃ na siddhe iti na yuṣmadabhimatadevatāviśeṣaḥ katham api sidhyatīti // MrgTV_1,1.9cd:3
children.translated_text: And by which means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is that person's trustworthiness established? If from the authority of the scripture set in motion by him—but his trustworthiness is established from the authority of scripture, and the authority of scripture from his establishment—this is the fault of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). If scripture is eternal, its authority applies only to what is to be accomplished, not to what is already established. Therefore, the special deity of your conception is not established in any way.

children.text: * evaṃ śakroktim abhidhāya hārītamuniḥ svoktyā svaśiṣyān āha // MrgTV_1,1.9cd:4
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed <s>Śakra's</s> statement, the sage <s>Hārita</s> said to his own disciples in his own words:

children.text: ity anīśavacovārivelānunno 'bdhineva saḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus pushed by the tide-waters of words denying <s>Īśvara</s>, like an ocean,

children.text: śakreṇa na cacālaiṣāṃ dhīśailaḥ sāragauravāt || MrgT_1,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Śakra</s>—yet the mountain of their intellect did not waver, due to the weight of its substance.

children.text: * ity anenoktena krameṇa īśvaranirākaraṇavacanāny eva nimnamārgānusaraṇād vārīṇi teṣāṃ velā samullāso jalavṛddhir iti yāvat tayā nunnaḥ prerito 'py eṣāṃ bharadvājādīnāṃ sambandhī matiparvataḥ sāravattvāt gurutvāc ca hetoḥ na cacāla na cakampe /
children.translated_text: By this sequence just stated: the words refuting <s>Īśvara</s>, following a downhill course, are the waters; their surge is the tide—that is, the rising of the waters; yet even though pushed, that is, impelled, by that tide, the mountain of intellect belonging to <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others did not waver, did not tremble, due to its being substantial and weighty.

children.text: * kena nunna ity āha abdhineva śakreṇa /
children.translated_text: By whom pushed? He says: 'By <s>Śakra</s>, like an ocean.'

children.text: * yathā kila velācalaḥ samudrajalataraṃgadṛḍhāhataḥ svāvaṣṭambhān na calati evaṃ munimatis tīkṣṇāgratvādisādharmyāt parvatena rūpakīkṛtā ca svasthairyān na vyacalat // MrgTV_1,1.10:1
children.translated_text: Just as a shore-mountain, though firmly struck by the waves of ocean-water, does not move due to its own firmness, so the mind of the sage, metaphorically compared to a mountain because of its similarity in sharpness of peak and the like, did not waver from its own steadiness.

children.text: * tataś cendraṃ prati te punar idam abhyadadhuḥ // MrgTV_1,1.10:2
children.translated_text: And then they again presented this to <s>Indra</s>:

children.text: na jātu devatāmūrtir asmadādiśarīravat /
children.translated_text: 'The form of a deity is never like the body of beings such as ourselves;

children.text: viśiṣṭaiśvaryasampannā sāto naitan nidarśanam || MrgT_1,1.11 ||
children.translated_text: She is endowed with supreme sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>)—therefore this analogy is not an illustration.'

children.text: * vibhūtiyogatāratamyam asmadādilocanagocaracāri sāmānyapuruṣamātrāśrayaṃ dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭavigrahasya devatāviśeṣasya aṇimādyaiśvaryasampattim anumāpayati tat kathaṃ prākāmyaśaktijanitaṃ yugapad anekadeśamātrasaṃnidhimātram asaṃbhāvyaṃ manyase // MrgTV_1,1.11:1
children.translated_text: The gradation of the conjunction of supernatural powers, observed and falling within the range of perception of beings like us, resting in ordinary persons alone, leads to the inference of the wealth of sovereignty such as <s>aṇimā</s> (atomicity) and the rest for the special deity whose form is unseen. How then do you consider it inconceivable that mere simultaneous presence in multiple places, generated by the power of <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), could obtain?

children.text: * na hi kadācid asmadādiśarīravat devatāmūrtiḥ kleśakarmavipākāśayayoginy avyāpikā vā icchāmātreṇāsmadādisṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsakaraṇakṣamaviśiṣṭaiśvaryasampannatvāt // MrgTV_1,1.11:2
children.translated_text: For the divine form is never like the body of beings such as ourselves—subject to afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), <s>karma</s>, fruition (<s>vipāka</s>), and latent dispositions (<s>āśaya</s>), or limited in scope—because it is endowed with supreme sovereignty capable of creating, sustaining, and destroying beings like us by mere will.

children.text: * mūrchitāṇutrāṇāddhi mūrtitvam asmadādimūrtitvavilakṣaṇaṃ cāsyāḥ // MrgTV_1,1.11:3
children.translated_text: For its embodiment arises from the aggregation of atoms for protection, and this embodiment of hers is distinct from the embodiment of beings like us.

children.text: * tataś ca yugapad anekadeśasaṃnidhinirākaraṇāyopāttasya mūrtitvākhyasya hetor aprayojakatvam // MrgTV_1,1.11:4
children.translated_text: Therefore, the reason called 'embodiment,' adduced for the purpose of refuting simultaneous presence in multiple places, is ineffectual.

children.text: * dṛṣṭāntaś cānupapannaḥ sādhyadharmāsiddhatvāt // MrgTV_1,1.11:5
children.translated_text: And the example is untenable, because the property to be proved is not established in it.

children.text: * sādhyo hi dharmas tulyakālam anekadeśāsaṃnidhilakṣaṇo 'tra sarvātmanā nāsti yasmād asmadādimadhyavartināṃ mūrtimatāṃ satām apy aṇimādisiddhiprakarṣayogināṃ yogināṃ yugapad anekadeśasaṃnidhir adyatve 'pi nāsaṃbhāvyaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.11:6
children.translated_text: For the property to be proved—namely, the characteristic of non-presence in multiple places simultaneously—does not exist here in its entirety, since even among embodied beings existing among us, for <s>yogins</s> who excel in the attainments of <s>aṇimā</s> (atomicity) and the rest, simultaneous presence in multiple places is not inconceivable even in the present.

children.text: * na ca niratiśayasakalotkarṣayoginaḥ parameśvarasya svadarśanābhiniveśibhiḥ kumbhakārādinidarśanakaluṣīkriyamāṇajagannirmāṇasya kiṃkāyaḥ kimāśrayaḥ kimupakaraṇa ity ādyasadvikalpaviplavo 'nupraviśati // MrgTV_1,1.11:7
children.translated_text: And for <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), who possesses the unsurpassed conjunction of all supreme qualities, the groundless speculative assault—'Of what body? What support? What instrument?'—advanced by those attached to their own doctrines, who sully the concept of the creation of the world with illustrations like the potter, does not apply.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ siddhacūḍāmaṇinā /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said by the Crest-Jewel of the <s>Siddhas</s>:

children.text: * kim īhaḥ kiṃkāyaḥ sa khalu kim upāyas tribhuvanaṃ kim ādhāro dhātā sṛjati kimupādāna iti ca /
children.translated_text: 'What effort? Of what body? What indeed is his means for the three worlds? What support does the Creator have? What material cause?'—

children.text: * atarkyaiśvarye tvayy anavasaraduḥstho hatadhiyaḥ kutarko 'yaṃ kāṃścin mukharayati mohāya jagatām // MrgTV_1,1.11:8
children.translated_text: Your sovereignty is beyond reasoning; this futile logic (<s>kutarka</s>), ill-placed and destroying the intellect, makes some people garrulous, leading only to the delusion of the world.

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.11:9
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * yathā cāśarīradevatāviśeṣasambhavo 'saṃbhavadbādhas tatheśvarasiddhiprakaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.11:10
children.translated_text: And how the possibility of a particular deity without a body is not contradicted — that we shall explain in the section on the proof of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).

children.text: * sa tu tathā tathā pratipādyamāno 'pi na tannirākaraṇapravaṇānāṃ prayojanahetur bhaviṣyatīti // MrgTV_1,1.11:11
children.translated_text: But even though he is thus repeatedly demonstrated, he will not become a cause of purpose for those inclined to refute him.

children.text: * atra daivopahatatvam evāparādhyati // MrgTV_1,1.11:12
children.translated_text: In this matter, it is only their being afflicted by fate that is at fault.

children.text: * yathāha rājānaka utpaladevaḥ /
children.translated_text: As <s>Rājānaka Utpaladeva</s> has said:

children.text: * samujjvalannyāyasahasrasādhito 'py upaiti siddhiṃ na vimūḍhacetasām // MrgTV_1,1.11:13
children.translated_text: Though established by a thousand brilliant proofs, [the truth] does not attain success for those whose minds are deluded.

children.text: * maheśvaraḥ pāṇitale sthito 'pi san palāyate daivahatasya sanmaṇiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.11:14
children.translated_text: Even when the great jewel stands in the palm of the hand, it flees from one who is struck by fate.
Thus.

children.text: * īdṛśābhyāṃ ca hetudṛṣṭāntābhyāṃ sādhyasiddhyupagame 'nyatrāpy ayam eva nyāyaḥ prasajyata ity āha // MrgTV_1,1.11:16
children.translated_text: And when the establishment of the thesis is accepted through such a reason and example, the same principle would apply elsewhere as well — he says:

children.text: athāstv evaṃ ghaṭe nyāyaḥ śabdatvād indraśabdavat /
children.translated_text: Now then, let this same principle apply to the pot, on account of its being a word, like the word '<s>Indra</s>'.

children.text: * bhavatā kila śabdamātraṃ hi devatā iti pratijñātam ataḥ śabdavyatiriktadevatānabhyupagame saty etad āpatitaṃ yad uta vācakavyatiriktavācyārthāsambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: You have indeed maintained that a deity is merely a word; therefore, when there is no acceptance of a deity apart from the word, this consequence follows — namely, the impossibility of a referent apart from the signifier.

children.text: * indrādiśabdānāṃ nānyo vācyo 'rtho vidyate /
children.translated_text: For words such as '<s>Indra</s>' and the like, there exists no other referent.

children.text: * evaṃ śabdatvāviśeṣāt ghaṭādāv api ayam eva nyāyo 'stu na caitad yuktam anubhavavirodhāt // MrgTV_1,1.12ab:1
children.translated_text: Thus, since there is no difference in being a word, let this same principle apply to the pot and so forth as well. But this is not correct, because it contradicts experience.

children.text: * tathā hi // MrgTV_1,1.12ab:2
children.translated_text: For instance:

children.text: nādatte ghaṭaśabdo 'mbhaś candraśabdo na rājate || MrgT_1,1.12 ||
children.translated_text: The word 'pot' does not carry water, nor does the word 'moon' shine.

children.text: * ghaṭate ceṣṭate arthakriyām iti ghaṭaḥ candati hlādayati dīpyate ceti candra ity evaṃvidhayā śabdavyutpattyā śabdavyatiriktavācyārthāsaṃbhavato ghaṭaśabdasyaivodakāharaṇaṃ candraśabdasyaiva cāhlādanādi prāptaṃ na cānayos tad asti api tu tadvācyayoḥ pṛthubudhnodarādyākārabhāsvarabimbasvarūpayos tattadarthakriyākaraṇakṣamatvaṃ dṛṣṭam // MrgTV_1,1.12cd:1
children.translated_text: Since '<s>ghaṭa</s>' (pot) means 'that which functions, that which performs purposeful activity,' and '<s>candra</s>' (moon) means 'that which delights, that which shines' — through such etymological derivation of words, when the impossibility of a referent apart from the word is maintained, it would follow that the word 'pot' itself should carry water and the word 'moon' itself should delight, and so forth. But neither of these has that capacity; rather, it is observed that the referents denoted by them — having the form of a wide-bottomed vessel and the nature of a luminous orb — are capable of performing their respective purposeful activities.

children.text: * tato na vācyavācakayor aikyam // MrgTV_1,1.12cd:2
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no identity between the signified and the signifier.

children.text: * tataś ca na śabdamātraṃ devatā kiṃ tarhi tadvācyaiveti siddham // MrgTV_1,1.12cd:3
children.translated_text: And therefore, a deity is not merely a word; rather, it is established that a deity is indeed the referent of that word.

children.text: * idānīṃ vākyaṃ tadanyathāsiddham iti paramatam anusaṃdhāya dūṣayati // MrgTV_1,1.12cd:4
children.translated_text: Now, he refutes the opposing view that the [Vedic] sentence is otherwise established, by following the opponent's position:

children.text: athānyaviṣayaṃ vākyam astu śakrādivācakam /
children.translated_text: Now, let the sentence referring to <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and others have a different subject matter;

children.text: karmarūpādiśabdānāṃ sārthakatvaṃ kathaṃ bhavet || MrgT_1,1.13 ||
children.translated_text: how then would there be meaningfulness for words denoting action, form, and the like?

children.text: * indro vajrī hiraṇmayaḥ ityādīni vākyāni śakrādidevatāliṅgāni mantrārthavādaparāṇi tv eṣāṃ svarūpayāthārthyam iti yad bhavadbhir abhihitaṃ tat tathāstu svārthapratipādanaparāṇāṃ tu śrūyamāṇānāṃ karmarūpādiśabdānāṃ katham arthavattvaṃ syāt // MrgTV_1,1.13:1
children.translated_text: Sentences such as '<s>Indra</s> is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the golden one' and so forth are indicators of deities such as <s>Śakra</s>; but these pertain to <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages), and their literal truth consists in their own meaning — so you have said. Let that be so. But for words denoting action, form, and the like, which are heard as conveying their own meaning, how would there be meaningfulness?

children.text: * tatra karmaśabdāḥ kriyābhidhāyinaḥ vrīhīn avahanti ityādayaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.13:2
children.translated_text: Among those, words of action are those denoting activities, such as 'they thresh the rice' and the like.

children.text: * evaṃ rūpaśabdāḥ jātyādiśabdāś ca // MrgTV_1,1.13:3
children.translated_text: Likewise, words of form and words of class and so forth.

children.text: * yathā śvetaṃ chāgam ālabheta ity atra śvetaśabdasya rūpābhidhāyinaḥ chāgaśabdasya ca jātivācinaḥ śakrādiśabdavat śabdatvāviśeṣāt svarūpayāthārthyāsaṃbhave saty ānarthakyaṃ tataś ca codanāvākyānām akiṃcitkaratvam // MrgTV_1,1.13:4
