children.translated_text: Just as in 'one should sacrifice a white goat,' the word 'white,' which denotes form, and the word 'goat,' which denotes class — since, like the words '<s>Śakra</s>' and the rest, there is no difference in being words, when the literal truth of their own meaning is impossible, they become meaningless; and consequently, the injunctive sentences accomplish nothing.

children.text: * yad vā śakrādivācakasya vākyasyānyaviṣayatve kalpyamāne tadviṣayāṇām indro vṛtram avadhīt ityādīnāṃ karmaśabdānāṃ sahasradṛgvajrapāṇyādīnāṃ ca rūpādyabhidhāyināṃ śabdānāṃ katham arthavattvaṃ syāt // MrgTV_1,1.13:5
children.translated_text: Or, if it be supposed that the sentence referring to <s>Śakra</s> and the like has a different subject matter, then for words of action in sentences whose subject is that — such as '<s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>' and the like — and for words denoting form and the like, such as 'the thousand-eyed one,' 'the thunderbolt-handed one,' how would there be meaningfulness?

children.text: * na cārghajaratīyanyāya upapādayituṃ śakyo yena vidhiśabdānām eva svarūpayāthārthyaṃ nendrādiśabdānām iti syāt // MrgTV_1,1.13:6
children.translated_text: Nor can the principle of <s>arghajaratī</s> be maintained, by which only injunctive words would have literal truth but not words such as '<s>Indra</s>' and the like.

children.text: * yad apy uktaṃ lokavādāḥ kva sādhavaḥ iti tad ayuktam // MrgTV_1,1.13:7
children.translated_text: As for what has been said — 'where are the reliable ones among popular sayings?' — that too is incorrect.

children.text: * yataḥ // MrgTV_1,1.13:8
children.translated_text: Because:

children.text: pravādo 'py akhilo mithyā samūlatvān na yuktimat /
children.translated_text: Even popular tradition, if entirely false, is not reasonable since it has a basis;

children.text: sa ced amūlo bhūtānāṃ hatāḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ || MrgT_1,1.14 ||
children.translated_text: if it were without a basis, all activities of beings would be destroyed.

children.text: * nadyās tīre guḍaśakaṭaṃ paryastam ityāder nirmūlasyāpi pravādasya ekāntena na mithyātvaṃ kadācit saṃvāditatvāt // MrgTV_1,1.14:1
children.translated_text: Even for a baseless rumor such as 'a cart of jaggery has overturned on the riverbank,' absolute falsity does not hold, since it is sometimes corroborated.

children.text: * tataś ca sarvapravādo na satya ity etan na yuktimat na pramāṇopapannam iti yāvat samūlatve sati mithyātvāsiddheḥ // MrgTV_1,1.14:2
children.translated_text: And therefore, [the proposition] that all popular tradition is untrue is not reasonable — that is, it is not supported by valid means of knowledge — since falsity is not established when a basis exists.

children.text: * mūlaṃ cāsyāgamaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.14:3
children.translated_text: And the basis of this is <s>āgama</s> (scripture/tradition).

children.text: * tathā cāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus they say:

children.text: * prasiddhim āgamaḥ prāpto loka ity abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: That which has reached well-known acceptance is called <s>āgama</s> (tradition) in the world.

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.14:4
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * atha nirmūlo yaḥ pravādaḥ sa cen mithyārūpaḥ tad apy ayuktaṃ yasmād evaṃ kalpyamāne bhūtānāṃ sarvāḥ pravṛttayo vyāhanyeran // MrgTV_1,1.14:5
children.translated_text: Now, if a tradition that has no basis is said to be false, that too is incorrect, because if such were supposed, all activities of beings would be obstructed.

children.text: * sarvo hi hitaprepsur ahitajihāsur vā na pramāṇaghaṭanāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ puraskṛtya lokavyavahāre dṛṣṭaphale sevākṛṣyādāv adṛṣṭaphale veṣṭāpūrtādau pravartate kiṃ tu prāyaśo gatānugatikapravādamātrādhivāsitamatiḥ // MrgTV_1,1.14:6
children.translated_text: For indeed, everyone — whether seeking benefit or wishing to avoid harm — does not engage in worldly transactions of visible result such as agriculture and service, or those of invisible result such as <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrificial and charitable acts), by first constructing valid means of knowledge and then proceeding accordingly; rather, for the most part, one acts with an understanding habituated merely by tradition following the course of predecessors.

children.text: * kīdṛśaṃ ca bhavatā pravādasya mūlam anveṣṭavyam // MrgTV_1,1.14:7
children.translated_text: And of what kind is the basis of tradition that you seek?

children.text: * yadi cirakālapravṛttatvena bahujanoddhoṣsthayamāṇatvaṃ tad yuktam eva // MrgTV_1,1.14:8
children.translated_text: If it is the confirmation by many people through long-established practice, then that is perfectly reasonable.

children.text: * anyathā pravāda eva nāsau tathā ca sati nāsya mithyātvam // MrgTV_1,1.14:9
children.translated_text: Otherwise, it would not even be a tradition, and in that case, its falsity would not apply.

children.text: * cirataram anekajanaprathitatve 'pi kuto 'syodbhava ity evaṃ vidhimūlaṃ parīkṣyate tarhy āgamaparīkṣaiveyaṃ na lokavādavicāraḥ // MrgTV_1,1.14:10
children.translated_text: If, even when something has been widely known among many people for a very long time, you investigate the origin-based root of it, asking 'from where did this arise?' — then this is an examination of <s>āgama</s> (scripture) itself, not an inquiry into popular tradition.

children.text: * na caitad evaṃ yato bhavadbhir api śrutirūpād āgamād anya eva sajjanasevito vyavahāraḥ śiṣṭācārākhyo dharmamūlatvenābhyupagata ity alaṃ pradveṣeṇa // MrgTV_1,1.14:11
children.translated_text: And this is not so, because even by you, a custom practiced by good people, distinct from the <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture), called <s>śiṣṭācāra</s> (the conduct of the learned), has been accepted as a root of <s>dharma</s>. So enough with this hostility.

children.text: * tad evaṃ samūlena lokapravādeneśvarākhyaviśiṣṭadevatāsaṃbhavaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.14:12
children.translated_text: Thus, through popular tradition which has a basis, the existence of a distinguished deity called <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is established.

children.text: * tathā hi // MrgTV_1,1.14:13
children.translated_text: For instance:

children.text: upamanyur haraṃ dṛṣṭvā vimanyur abhavan muniḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Upamanyu</s>, having seen <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), became free from anger — that sage.

children.text: * kiṃ na nāmākhilajanapratītam etad yan munir upamanyuḥ parameśvareṇa varapradāne nānugṛhītaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.15ab:1
children.translated_text: Is it not universally known among all people that the sage <s>Upamanyu</s> was favored by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) in the granting of boons?

children.text: * tathā ca mahābhārate ānuśāsanike parvaṇi bhagavadvyāsamuninopamanyuvākyaṃ pradarśitam /
children.translated_text: And thus, in the <s>Anuśāsana Parvan</s> of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the words of <s>Upamanyu</s> are presented by the blessed sage <s>Vyāsa</s>:

children.text: * āha māṃ bhagavān īśaḥ prahasann iva śaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord), <s>Śaṃkara</s> (the Auspicious One), said to me, as if smiling:

children.text: * vatsopamanyo prīto 'smi paśya māṃ munipuṃgava // MrgTV_1,1.15ab:2
children.translated_text: 'O child <s>Upamanyu</s>, I am pleased; behold me, O best of sages.'

children.text: * dṛḍhabhakto 'si viprarṣe mayā jijñāsitas tv asi /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Brahman-seer</s>, you are firm in devotion; you have indeed been tested by me.'

children.text: * anayā vatsa sadbhaktyā te 'tyarthaṃ prītavān aham // MrgTV_1,1.15ab:3
children.translated_text: 'O child, by this excellent devotion of yours, I am exceedingly pleased.'

children.text: * tasmāt sarvān pradāsyāmi varān ye manasi sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, I shall grant you all the boons that are in your heart.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,1.15ab:4
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * athocyate mithyaitad upamanyunātmaprabhāvakathanāyoktam atra hi kiṃ pramāṇaṃ yad evam asau bhagavatānugṛhīta iti /
children.translated_text: Now if it is objected: 'This is false — <s>Upamanyu</s> said this to proclaim his own greatness; what proof is there that he was indeed favored by the Blessed One?' —

children.text: * tad asad yasmāt // MrgTV_1,1.15ab:5
children.translated_text: That is wrong, because:

children.text: kathaṃ tasya vaco mithyā yasya vaśyaḥ payonidhiḥ || MrgT_1,1.15 ||
children.translated_text: How can the words of one be false, for whom the ocean of milk was obedient?

children.text: * yasya kila sakalamunijanapratyakṣaparidṛśyamānaḥ kṣīrābdhiḥ svādhīnaḥ tasya vacasaḥ kiṃ nāma mithyātvam /
children.translated_text: For one whose command the entire ocean of milk obeyed, visibly witnessed by all the assembled sages — how can his words be called false?

children.text: * ayam āśayaḥ parameśvarāt prāptavaro 'ham ity anṛtavāditvaṃ tadānīṃ tasya bhavet yadi dugdhodadhivaśīkāraḥ pracuramunijanapratyakṣo na syāt /
children.translated_text: The purport is this: his claiming 'I obtained boons from <s>Parameśvara</s>' could be considered untruthful only if the subjugation of the milk-ocean, witnessed directly by numerous sages, did not occur.

children.text: * yadi ca saṃvādīny api vacāṃsi mithyā tarhi na kiṃcit satyavacanam /
children.translated_text: And if even corroborated words are false, then nothing would be a true statement.

children.text: * praśāntarāgadveṣāṇāṃ sākṣātkṛtabhūtabhaviṣyadarthānāṃ munīnām api mithyāvāditvābhyupagame manvādayo 'pi dattadakṣiṇās tvayety aho svadarśanakauśalam // MrgTV_1,1.15cd:1
children.translated_text: If the false speech even of sages — who are free from passion and hatred, who have directly perceived past and future events — is accepted, then by you, even <s>Manu</s> and others are 'those who have given their sacrificial fee' [i.e., dismissed as unreliable]. Ah, what skill in one's own doctrine!

children.text: * kiṃ ca // MrgTV_1,1.15cd:2
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: kroḍīkṛto hi pāśena viṣajvālāvalīmucā /
children.translated_text: For the white [bull, <s>Nandin</s>], seized by the serpent-noose that emits streams of poisonous flames,

children.text: huṃkṛtya mocitaḥ patyā dṛṣṭaḥ śveto ghanair janaiḥ || MrgT_1,1.16 ||
children.translated_text: was released by the Lord with a mere <s>huṃkāra</s> (the sound 'huṃ') — this was seen by multitudes of people.

children.text: * viṣānalārciḥparamparākṣepabhīṣaṇenāśīviṣapāśena vivaśīkṛtaḥ śvetaḥ pātīti patis tena patyā trāṇaśīlena parameśvareṇa huṃkāramātraṃ kṛtvā krodhāgninā bhasmīkṛtya mocitaḥ iti ghanair aviralair bhūyobhir janair asmatsajātīyair muniprabhṛtibhiś ca dṛṣṭaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.16:1
children.translated_text: The white one [<s>Śveta</s>], overpowered by the serpent-noose — terrifying with its succession of flames of poisonous fire — was released by the Lord, <s>Pati</s> (the Protector), whose nature is to rescue, by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), who merely uttered the sound '<s>huṃ</s>' and reduced [the serpent] to ashes with the fire of his wrath. This was seen by dense, uninterrupted multitudes of people of our own kind, as well as sages and others.

children.text: * atrāpi trikāladarśibhir devaiś ca pravartite pravāde yady asamāśvāsas tarhi āgamam eva na sahata iti vaktavyaṃ tathā ca sati śrutir api asahanasya bhavataḥ prāmāṇyalābhe dainyena bhītabhītā mukham anvīkṣata iti tadanukampayā saṃrakṣyatām atisāhasam // MrgTV_1,1.16:2
children.translated_text: Even regarding this, if you have no faith in a tradition set forth by gods who see the three times and by others, then it must be said that you simply cannot tolerate <s>āgama</s> (scripture) at all. And in that case, the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation) too, gazing about frightened and pitiable in search of authority before you who cannot tolerate it — out of compassion for her, restrain this excessive rashness.

children.text: * nanu mithyātvahetūnāṃ doṣāṇāṃ kartrāśrayatvād akṛtakatvena nityatvāt śrutes tasyāḥ prāmāṇyāya ko 'yam upahāsaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.16:3
children.translated_text: But [you may object]: since the defects that cause falsity reside in the author, and since the <s>Śruti</s> is eternal due to its being uncreated, what is this mockery regarding its authority?

children.text: * na kaścit kiṃ tu kartrabhāvaniścaye pramāṇaṃ notpaśyāmaḥ pratyuta svayaṃbhuve namaskṛtya ityādivākyavat racanāvattvāt kartṛvyāpārāvivanābhāvitvam utprekṣāmaha ity alam anena // MrgTV_1,1.16:4
children.translated_text: None at all. But we do not perceive any means of valid knowledge for ascertaining the absence of an author. On the contrary, from statements like 'having bowed to the Self-Existent One' and the like, and because it possesses composition, we surmise the inseparability of an author's activity — but enough of this.

children.text: * prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.16:5
children.translated_text: Let us return to the main topic.

children.text: iti vādānuṣaṅgeṇa haraśaṃsāpraharṣitān /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the course of the debate, those who were delighted by the praise of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva),

children.text: sāśrugadgadavācas tān vīkṣya prīto 'bhavad dhīraḥ || MrgT_1,1.17 ||
children.translated_text: seeing them speaking with tears and choked voices, the steadfast one [<s>Indra</s>] became pleased.

children.text: * uktavaddevatāstitvaprastāvāyāyātaparameśvarapraśaṃsāharṣapravṛttānandāśruvaśād avispaṣṭagirastān bharadvājādīn dṛṣṭvā indras tān prati paraṃ tutoṣa ity evaṃ hārītamuniḥ svaśiṣyān āha // MrgTV_1,1.17:1
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, seeing that <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others had, on account of the praise of <s>Parameśvara</s> that arose incidentally from the discussion about the existence of deities as described above, begun to shed tears of joy, their voices becoming indistinct — seeing them thus, he was exceedingly pleased toward them. So sage <s>Hārīta</s> tells his own disciples.

children.text: svaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa vajrī devaḥ śatakratuḥ /
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt-wielding god, <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra), revealed his own form,

children.text: taruṇādityasaṃkāśaṃ stūyamānaṃ marudgaṇaiḥ || MrgT_1,1.18 ||
children.translated_text: resplendent like the rising sun, being praised by the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: * pratyagrārkabhāsvaraṃ devair gaṇaiś ca stūyamānam ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ vajrapāṇir devaḥ śatakratuḥ prakaṭīcakāra /
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt-handed god <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra) made manifest his own form — radiant as the newly risen sun, being praised by the divine hosts and attendants.

children.text: * tejo'tiśayayogasya hetutayā śatakratur vajrīti ca viśeṣaṇadvayam /
children.translated_text: The two epithets '<s>Śatakratu</s>' and 'wielder of the thunderbolt' are given to indicate the cause of his surpassing splendor.

children.text: * kuliśasya svabhāva evāyaṃ yad adbhutaprabhābhāsvaratvaṃ śatakratutvāc ca tajjanitapuṇyaprabhāvād adbhutabhūrimahaḥsamūhatvam iti // MrgTV_1,1.18:1
children.translated_text: It is the very nature of the thunderbolt that it possesses wondrous brilliance and radiance; and being '<s>Śatakratu</s>' (performer of a hundred sacrifices), through the merit born therefrom, he possesses a wondrously abundant mass of splendor.

children.text: te tam ṛgbhir yajurbhiś ca sāmabhiś cāstuvan natāḥ /
children.translated_text: They praised him, bowing, with <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> verses.

children.text: so 'bravīd ucyatāṃ kāmo jagatsu pravaro 'pi yaḥ || MrgT_1,1.19 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'State your desire, even the greatest in all the worlds.'

children.text: te vavrire śivajñānaṃ śrūyatām iti so 'bravīt /
children.translated_text: They chose the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>. He said: 'Let it be heard.'

children.text: kiṃ tv eko 'stu mama praṣṭā nikhilaśrotṛsaṃmataḥ || MrgT_1,1.20 ||
children.translated_text: 'But let one among you be the questioner, approved by all the listeners.'

children.text: * te bharadvājādayas taṃ pratyakṣīkṛtasvasvarūpam indraṃ ṛgyajuḥsāmabhiḥ prahvāḥ santas tuṣṭuvuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s> and the others, bowing, praised <s>Indra</s>, who had revealed his true form, with <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> hymns.

children.text: * sa ca sarvajagatpravaro varo bhavadbhir abhyarthyatām iti tān āha /
children.translated_text: And he, the most excellent in all the worlds, said to them: 'Let a boon be requested by you.'

children.text: * te tadaivam uktāḥ pārameśvaraṃ jñānaṃ śāstraṃ vṛtavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: They, being thus addressed, chose the knowledge pertaining to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture).

children.text: * sa tu tadabhyarthitaṃ jñānopadeśaṃ dātuṃ tān prativacanaṃ śrūyatām ity āha kiṃ tu mamaika eva bhavatāṃ madhyāt sakalaśrotṛjanābhimato yathāvasaram anuktavastunaḥ praṣṭā bhavatu sarvaiś caiva bhavadbhiḥ śrūyatām iti // MrgTV_1,1.20:1
children.translated_text: He, in order to give the instruction in knowledge that was requested by them, spoke to them in reply, saying 'Listen!' — he said: 'Let one from among you, who is accepted by all listeners, be the questioner of matters not yet spoken, as occasion arises, and let all of you listen.'

children.text: * evaṃ bhagavatā śakreṇokte sati // MrgTV_1,1.20:2
children.translated_text: Thus, when the blessed <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) had spoken —

children.text: atha teṣāṃ bharadvājo bhagavān agraṇīr abhūt /
children.translated_text: Then, the blessed <s>Bharadvāja</s> became the leader among them,

children.text: vāgmī pragalbhaḥ papraccha nyāyataḥ surapūjitam || MrgT_1,1.21 ||
children.translated_text: eloquent and bold, he questioned the one worshipped by the gods, in proper form.

children.text: * athānantaraṃ teṣāṃ madhyād aiśvaryādiguṇayogāt bhagavān vividhaśāstrābhyāsādhivāsapraśasyavāgyuktatvāc ca vāgmī praṣṭavyāvasareṣu akauśalāpratipattyādyayogāt pragalbhaś ca bharadvājo munir nyāyata iti nyāyena śiṣyocitayā nītyā yuktyupapannapūrvapakṣakaraṇena vā indram apṛcchad iti // MrgTV_1,1.21:1
children.translated_text: Then, from among them, due to his possession of qualities such as lordliness, the blessed one — eloquent due to his praiseworthy skill in speech cultivated through practice of various <s>śāstras</s> (treatises), and bold due to his freedom from errors such as incompetence in occasions for questioning — the sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> questioned <s>Indra</s> properly, that is, by proper method, in the manner befitting a disciple, or by formulating the prior position supported by reasoning.

children.text: * āha // MrgTV_1,1.21:2
children.translated_text: He said:

children.text: kathaṃ maheśvarād etad āgataṃ jñānam uttamam /
children.translated_text: How did this supreme knowledge come from <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord)?

children.text: kiṃ ca cetasi saṃsthāpya nirmame bhagavān idam || MrgT_1,1.22 ||
children.translated_text: And with what purpose in mind did the Blessed One create this?

children.text: * yad etad bhagavatā asmabhyam upadeṣṭum ārabdham itarebhyo jñānebhyaḥ sātiśayaphalatvāc chreṣṭhatamaṃ jñānaṃ tat kathaṃ maheśvarāt praśāntasvarūpān niṣkalāc chivāt prasṛtam // MrgTV_1,1.22:1
children.translated_text: That which the Blessed One has begun to teach us — this knowledge that is the most excellent among other knowledges due to its surpassingly superior fruits — how did it issue forth from <s>Maheśvara</s>, whose nature is tranquil, who is partless, who is <s>Śiva</s>?

children.text: * jñānaṃ hi dvirūpam avabodharūpaṃ śabdarūpaṃ ca // MrgTV_1,1.22:2
children.translated_text: For knowledge is of two forms: the form of understanding and the form of verbal expression.

children.text: * tad avabodharūpaṃ śabdarūpārūḍhaṃ sarveṣu pravartate // MrgTV_1,1.22:3
children.translated_text: That understanding-form, having ascended to the verbal-expression form, operates in all.

children.text: * tatrāditaḥ parameśvarād avabodharūpam eva tāvat kathaṃ prāptaṃ kathaṃ ca śabdarūpatām etya bahubhedabhinnaṃ sampannam // MrgTV_1,1.22:4
children.translated_text: Of these, first, how was the understanding-form alone obtained from <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), and how, having assumed the form of verbal expression, did it become manifold, divided into many branches?

children.text: * kiṃ cākalayya bhagavān idam akarot // MrgTV_1,1.22:5
children.translated_text: And with what purpose did the Blessed One make this?

children.text: * na hy anabhisaṃhitaprayojanaḥ kaścit kartā kiṃcit kāryaṃ kurvan dṛṣṭaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.22:6
children.translated_text: For no agent who acts without a considered purpose has ever been seen performing any action.

children.text: * tasya ca bhagavata etat karaṇe kiṃ kāraṇam ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.22:7
children.translated_text: And what is the reason for the Blessed One's making of this — such is the meaning.

children.text: * athātra prativacanam // MrgTV_1,1.22:8
children.translated_text: Now, the reply to this:

children.text: sṛṣṭikāle maheśānaḥ puruṣārthaprasiddhaye /
children.translated_text: At the time of creation, <s>Maheśāna</s> (the Great Lord), for the accomplishment of the aims of man (<s>puruṣārtha</s>),

children.text: vidhatte vimalaṃ jñānaṃ pañcasroto 'bhilakṣitam || MrgT_1,1.23 ||
children.translated_text: fashions pure knowledge, characterized by five streams.

children.text: * sargaprārambhe parameśvareṇa puruṣārthasya bhuktimuktyātmanaḥ sampattyarthaṃ vimalam ity avabodhātmano nādarūpatvena prathamaṃ prasṛtatvād agṛhītopādhibhedaṃ paratas tūrdhvaprāgdakṣiṇapaścimottarasrotaḥpañcakenābhitaḥ samantāt prasṛtatvena lakṣitam iti sadāśivarūpeṇa darśanātmatāṃ prāpitaṃ jñānaṃ nirmitam iti kramaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.23:1
children.translated_text: At the commencement of creation, <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) [fashioned] knowledge for the attainment of <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the aim of man), whose nature is enjoyment and liberation — 'pure' meaning having the nature of understanding, because it was first emitted in the form of sound, without the divisions of limiting adjuncts being grasped; but thereafter, being characterized by the five streams going upward, eastward, southward, westward, and northward, being emitted everywhere in all directions — in the form of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, brought to the nature of vision. This is the sequence of the fashioning of knowledge.

children.text: * prayojanaṃ ca pūrvapraśnitam upavarṇitam // MrgTV_1,1.23:2
children.translated_text: And the purpose that was asked about earlier has been described.

children.text: * kiṃ ca // MrgTV_1,1.23:3
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: tadvartivācakavrātavācyān aṣṭau maheśvarān /
children.translated_text: The eight <s>Maheśvaras</s> (Great Lords) who are the referents of the group of signifying <s>mantras</s> abiding therein,

children.text: saptakoṭiprasaṃkhyātān mantrāṃś ca parame 'dhvani || MrgT_1,1.24 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>mantras</s> numbering seventy million, in the supreme course (<s>adhvan</s>) —

children.text: * mantroddhāraprakaraṇābhidhāsyamānajñānamadhyavartino vācakavrātasya mantragaṇasya ye vācyā anantādayo 'ṣṭau vidyeśās tāṃs tathā māyīyasyāśuddhasyādhvanas tatkālam anāvirbhāvāc chuddhavidyābhuvane kṛtasthitīn saptakoṭisaṃkhyātān mantrān parameśvaro vidhatta iti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.24:1
children.translated_text: The referents of the group of signifying <s>mantras</s>, the assemblage of <s>mantras</s>, abiding within the knowledge to be described in the section on mantra-extraction — the eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge) beginning with <s>Ananta</s>; and likewise, due to the non-manifestation of the impure <s>māyīya</s> course at that time, stationed in the realm of pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyābhuvana</s>), seventy million <s>mantras</s> — <s>Parameśvara</s> fashioned them. The connection is with the previous [verse].

children.text: * kālasāmānye 'pi prathamalakārasya spaṣṭatvāt sṛṣṭikāle vyadhād ity arthaḥ pratisargakālaṃ vā tathā karotīti vartamānataiva // MrgTV_1,1.24:2
children.translated_text: Even though the time is general, because the first present tense is clear, the meaning is 'he fashioned at the time of creation'; or, he does likewise at the time of each re-creation — hence the present tense is appropriate.

children.text: * tatra vidyeśvarāṇāṃ vāmādiśaktiyogitvena svasamaprabhāvāvirbhāvanaṃ nāma karaṇaṃ mantrāṇāṃ tv āgamāpagamāt prakaṭīkṛtadṛkkriyatvam // MrgTV_1,1.24:3
children.translated_text: Among these, the 'making' of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> means the manifestation of their inherent power equal to themselves through union with the <s>Vāmā</s> and other <s>śaktis</s> (powers); but for the <s>mantras</s>, it is the making manifest of their vision and action through the approach and withdrawal of the <s>āgama</s> (scripture).

children.text: * ubhayeṣām apy eṣāṃ parameśvarāj jñānakriyāśaktyor uddīpanaṃ jñeyam na punar muktāṇuvan nirmalīkaraṇam adhikāramalenāparatvān mukter asyā iti vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.24:4
children.translated_text: For both of these, the awakening of the powers of knowledge and action by <s>Parameśvara</s> should be understood, but not a purification like that of liberated souls, because their liberation, being subsequent, is [still accompanied] by the impurity of their commission — this we shall explain.

children.text: * tad evaṃ mantramaheśvarān mantrāṃś coktvā mantreśvarān vaktum āha // MrgTV_1,1.24:5
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken of the <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s> (Great Lords of Mantras) and the <s>mantras</s>, in order to speak of the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (Lords of Mantras), he says:

children.text: aṣṭādaśādhikaṃ cānyac chrutaṃ māyādhikāriṇām /
children.translated_text: And another one hundred and eighteen, belonging to those who preside over <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: mantreśvarāṇām ūrdhvādhvasthiteśopamatejasām || MrgT_1,1.25 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (Lords of Mantras), stationed in the higher course, of splendor equal to the Lord —

children.text: * māyāyām adhikāriṇo māyādhikāriṇas teṣām uparitanaśuddhādhvavartividyeśvarasamānadhāmnām aṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ vidhatta iti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.25:1
children.translated_text: Those who have authority over <s>māyā</s> are the <s>māyādhikārins</s>; of those, one hundred and eighteen who possess brilliance equal to the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> stationed in the higher pure course — he fashioned them. The connection is with the previous [verse] itself.

children.text: * tatra maṇḍalino 'ṣṭau vakṣyamāṇāḥ krodhādyāś cāṣṭāv eva rudrāṇāṃ ca brahmāṇḍadhārakāṇāṃ śataṃ śrīkaṇṭhavīrabhadrau cety evam aṣṭādaśottaraṃ śataṃ prāgvan mantreśvaratve śivena niyuktam ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,1.25:2
children.translated_text: Among them: eight <s>Maṇḍalins</s> (those who are to be described), eight beginning with <s>Krodha</s> (Wrath) and the like, one hundred <s>Rudras</s> who uphold the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), and <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Vīrabhadra</s> — thus one hundred and eighteen were appointed by <s>Śiva</s> to the office of <s>Mantreśvara</s>, as before. This is the meaning.

children.text: teṣu vyaktaḥ sa bhagavān idaṃ yogyeṣu siddhaye /
children.translated_text: Among those, the Blessed One is manifest; for those who are qualified, for the sake of attainment,

children.text: prakāśayaty ato 'nyeṣu yo 'rthaḥ samupapadyate || MrgT_1,1.26 ||
children.translated_text: he reveals [this knowledge], and for others, whatever meaning is appropriate [comes forth].

children.text: * teṣv anantādiṣu mantramaheśvareṣu maṇḍalyādiṣu ca mantreśvareṣv abhivyakto deva idam ity anantaropakrāntaṃ jñānaṃ prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: Among those — the <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s> beginning with <s>Ananta</s>, and the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> beginning with the <s>Maṇḍalins</s> — the Lord, being manifest, reveals the knowledge that has been described in what precedes.

children.text: * kasmin viṣaye kim arthaṃ prakāśayatīty āha yogyeṣu siddhaye paripakvāñjanatvān niratiśayaśreyaḥprepsuṣu bhuktyarthaṃ muktyarthaṃ ca vaktīty arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: In what domain and for what purpose does he reveal it? He says: 'For those who are qualified, for the sake of attainment' — meaning: to those whose impurities have fully ripened, who desire the supreme good beyond compare, he speaks for the purpose of enjoyment and for the purpose of liberation.

children.text: * ato 'nyeṣv iti etacchāstrārhebhyo ye 'nye aparipakvāñjanatayā paśuśāstrānuvartinas teṣu viṣayeṣu yaḥ kāpilapāñcarātrādi prāpyo 'rthaḥ samyag iti taduktayogyatānusāreṇopapadyate anuguṇo bhavati taṃ prakāśayati /
children.translated_text: 'For others' means: in the domains of those who, being of unripened impurity, follow the <s>śāstras</s> of the bound souls (<s>paśuśāstras</s>), different from those worthy of this <s>śāstra</s> — whatever attainable meaning, such as <s>Kāpila</s>, <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, and so forth, is appropriate, that is, conforms to the capacity of what can be stated to them, becomes fitting — that he reveals.

children.text: * paśuśāstrapraṇetḥn adhiṣṭhāya tattacchāstraprakāśanam api pāramparyeṇa kuruta iti yāvat // MrgTV_1,1.26:1
children.translated_text: By presiding over the authors of the <s>paśuśāstras</s>, he indirectly accomplishes the revelation of each respective <s>śāstra</s> as well — such is the import.

children.text: * athāsya jñānasyāsmabhyam abhidhīyamānasya kim abhidhānam ity āha // MrgTV_1,1.26:2
children.translated_text: Now, what is the name of this knowledge being taught to us? He says:

children.text: śivodgīrṇam idaṃ jñānaṃ mantramantreśvareśvaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: This knowledge, emitted by <s>Śiva</s>, by the lords of <s>mantras</s>, <s>mantreśvaras</s>, and <s>maheśvaras</s>,

children.text: kāmadatvāt kāmiketi pragītaṃ bahuvistaram || MrgT_1,1.27 ||
children.translated_text: because it grants desires, has been celebrated as <s>Kāmika</s>, in great detail.

children.text: * parameśvarāt proktena krameṇa prasṛtam etaj jñānaṃ śāstraṃ skandasya devyās tad anyeṣāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak śrotḥṇāṃ bahutvād bahubhedatvena vistaram abhimatakāmadatvāt kāmikatvenopadeṣṭṛbhir mantrāṇāṃ mantreśvarāṇāṃ ceśvarair mantramaheśvarair anantādibhir upadiṣṭam // MrgTV_1,1.27:1
children.translated_text: This knowledge, this <s>śāstra</s>, emitted by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) in the order described — being the scripture of <s>Skanda</s>, of the Goddess, and of the various other listeners separately — due to the multiplicity of listeners, it has become extensive with many divisions. Because it grants desired objects, it has been taught as the '<s>Kāmika</s>' by the lords of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mantreśvaras</s>, that is, by the <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s> beginning with <s>Ananta</s>.

children.text: * tebhya āgamayya kasmai kiyatā granthena ko dattavān ity āha // MrgTV_1,1.27:2
children.translated_text: Having received it from them, to whom did he give it, and in how many verses? He says:

children.text: tebhyo 'vagatya dṛgjyotirjvālālīḍhasmaradrumaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having learned from them, he whose tree of desire was consumed by the flame-tongues of the fire of his third eye,

children.text: dadāv umāpatir mahyaṃ sahasrair bhavasaṃmitaiḥ || MrgT_1,1.28 ||
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Umā</s> gave it to me in thousands equal to the existences.

children.text: * tebhyo 'nanteśādibhyas tṛtīyanetrāgniśikhānirdagdhasmaratarur bhagavān umāpatir adhigamya bhavasaṃkhyair ekādaśabhiḥ sahasraiḥ saṃkṣipya mahyam adāt // MrgTV_1,1.28:1
children.translated_text: From those, beginning with <s>Ananta</s> and the other <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s>, the Blessed One, the Lord of <s>Umā</s>, whose tree of desire (<s>Smara</s>, i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>) was burned by the flame of the fire of his third eye — having learned it, he condensed it into eleven thousand [verses], equal to the number of existences (<s>bhava</s>), and gave it to me.

children.text: * so 'ham idānīm // MrgTV_1,1.28:2
children.translated_text: And I now —

children.text: tatrāpi vistaraṃ hitvā sūtraiḥ sārārthavācakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even from that, abandoning the elaborate portions, through <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms) that express the essential meaning,

children.text: vakṣye nirākulaṃ jñānaṃ taduktair eva bhūyasā || MrgT_1,1.29 ||
children.translated_text: I shall teach this knowledge in an unconfused manner, mostly using those very expressions.

children.text: * tatrāpi arthavādānuvādarūpaṃ vistaraṃ tyaktvā sārārthābhidhāyibhir bāhulyena kvacit taduktaiḥ kvacic cātmīyair nirākulaṃ kramaṃ jñānaṃ śāstram abhidhāsye itīndro munīn āheti hārītaḥ svaśiṣyān brūte // MrgTV_1,1.29:1
children.translated_text: Even from that, abandoning the elaborate portions in the form of explanatory narratives and restatements, through aphorisms that express the essential meaning — for the most part using those very expressions of the original, and in some places my own — I shall teach this knowledge, this <s>śāstra</s>, in unconfused sequence. Thus <s>Indra</s> tells the sages — this is what <s>Hārīta</s> tells his own disciples.

children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 2
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> (Knowledge Section), Chapter 2

children.text: athānādimalāpetaḥ sarvakṛt sarvavicchivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the one who is free from beginningless impurity, the all-doer, the all-knower, <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: pūrvavyatyāsitasyāṇoḥ pāśajālam apohati || MrgT_1,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: removes the web of bonds from the soul that has been displaced since beginningless time.

children.text: * sambandhābhidheyaprayojanāni prathamam eva vivecitāni // MrgTV_1,2.1:1
children.translated_text: The connection (<s>sambandha</s>), subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), and purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) have already been elucidated at the very beginning.

children.text: * athety ānuṣaṅgikasambandhādikathanād anantaraṃ vidyākhyaḥ pādaḥ prakramyate // MrgTV_1,2.1:2
children.translated_text: 'Now' (<s>atha</s>) — after the statement of the incidental connection and so forth, the chapter called <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge) is commenced.

children.text: * atra ca śāstre patipaśupāśākhyās trayaḥ padārthāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.1:3
children.translated_text: And in this <s>śāstra</s>, there are three categories of reality (<s>padārtha</s>): <s>pati</s> (the Lord), <s>paśu</s> (the bound soul), and <s>pāśa</s> (the bonds).

children.text: * paśūnām asvātantryāt pāśānām ācaitanyāt tadvilakṣaṇasya patyuḥ pañcavidhakṛtyakāritvam tatkārakāṇi svaśaktirūpāṇi māyādīni ca kriyā ca dīkṣādyā tatphalaṃ ca paśūnām anugrahākhyena karmaṇā parakaivalyāsādanam ityādi abhidhāsyamānam // MrgTV_1,2.1:4
children.translated_text: Because the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) lack independence, and because the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) lack consciousness, the five-fold activity-making of the Lord (<s>pati</s>), who is distinct from both — his own powers in the form of <s>māyā</s> and so forth, which are the instruments of that activity, and the action of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and the like, and its fruit: the attainment of supreme isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) for the bound souls through the act called grace (<s>anugraha</s>) — all this is to be described.

children.text: * tadgarbhīkāreṇedaṃ mūlasūtram // MrgTV_1,2.1:5
children.translated_text: Encompassing all of that, this is the root <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism):

children.text: * anādimalāpeta iti // MrgTV_1,2.1:6
children.translated_text: 'Free from beginningless impurity' —

children.text: * anādiśabdaḥ kriyāviśeṣaṇam // MrgTV_1,2.1:7
children.translated_text: The word 'beginningless' (<s>anādi</s>) qualifies the action.

children.text: * anādi kṛtvā malāpetaḥ svabhāvanirmalaḥ parameśvaraḥ tathā anādiś cāsau malāpetaś ca tatprasādāt pradhvastasamastamalo muktāṇuvargaḥ kiṃ ca anāder malād apetaḥ svābhāvikamalavidāraṇāt parameśvareṇa prakaṭīkṛtadṛkkriyaḥ kiṃcid avaśeṣitatvād ādimatā adhikāramalena yukto mantramantreśvaramantramaheśvaravarga ity evaṃ samāsatrayakaraṇāt muktāṇubhir vidyeśvarādibhiś ca sahitaḥ patipadārthaḥ atra sūcitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.1:8
children.translated_text: By one compound: 'Free from beginningless impurity' — <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), who is pure by his own nature, having removed impurity since beginningless time. Also: by another compound: both beginningless and free from impurity — the class of liberated souls (<s>muktāṇu</s>) whose every impurity has been destroyed by his grace. Furthermore: separated from beginningless impurity — the class of <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Mantreśvara</s>, and <s>Mantramaheśvara</s> beings, whose vision and action have been made manifest by <s>Parameśvara</s> through the cleaving of their natural impurity, yet who are still endowed with the impurity of their commission since some remainder persists. Thus, through the three possible analyses of the compound, the category of <s>pati</s> (the Lord) is indicated here, together with liberated souls and <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and the rest.

children.text: * tasya ca trividhasyāpi sarvajñatā sarvakartṛtvaṃ ca vidyate muktātmanāṃ tu saty api sarvārthadṛkkriyatve pāśajālāpohanasāmarthyam asti na tv apohanakartṛtvam // MrgTV_1,2.1:9
children.translated_text: And of all three types, omniscience and universal agency exist. For liberated souls, however, although the power of seeing and acting upon all objects exists, the capacity to remove the web of bonds exists, but not the agency to remove them.

children.text: * yatas te karaṇīyasyābhāvāt na pravartante ataḥ svātmany eva śreyoyogāc chivatvam eteṣāṃ vidyeśvarāṇāṃ śivapadaprāptihetutvāt bhagavatas tu sarvānugrahapravṛttatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.1:10
children.translated_text: Because they, having no duty remaining, do not engage in activity. Therefore their <s>Śivahood</s> consists in the bliss pertaining to their own self alone. For these <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, it is because they are causes of attaining the state of <s>Śiva</s>. But for the Blessed One, it is because he is engaged in the grace of all.

children.text: * tathā ca muktātmanām apravṛttatvāt vidyeśvarāṇāṃ ca parameśvarapāratantryāt svatantraḥ sa bhagavān // MrgTV_1,2.1:11
children.translated_text: And thus, because liberated souls do not engage in activity, and because the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> are dependent on <s>Parameśvara</s>, that Blessed One alone is independent.

children.text: * kiṃ karotīty āha pūrvavyatyāsitasyāṇoḥ // MrgTV_1,2.1:12
children.translated_text: What does he do? He says: 'Of the soul that has been displaced since beginningless time' —

children.text: * pāśajālaṃ vyapohatīti aṇor iti vijñānākalapralayākalasakalatvena trirūpasya tathā vijñānākalapralayākalātmanor viparyavasitamaleśvaraśaktyadhikāratadanyathābhāvabhedāt pratyekaṃ dvividhayoḥ sakalasyāpi tribandhanabaddhasya kutaścid upāyāt prakṣīṇakarmatayā kevalakalādiyuktasya ca evaṃ dviprakārasyāsyaiva ca pratyekaṃ videhasadehabhedāt pratibhedaṃ ca malādyadhikāravirahiṇas tadyuktasya cety aṣṭaprakārasya ittham anekabhedabhinnasyātmanaḥ parameśvaraḥ pāśajālaṃ yathāsaṃbhavam apohatīti saṃbandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.1:13
children.translated_text: He removes the web of bonds — the connection is: <s>Parameśvara</s> removes, as appropriate, the web of bonds from the soul (<s>āṇu</s>) which is of three types as <s>vijñānākala</s>, <s>pralayākala</s>, and <s>sakala</s>; and furthermore, of the <s>vijñānākala</s> and <s>pralayākala</s> types, each being twofold due to the distinctions of the impurities of <s>mala</s>, lordly power (<s>īśvaraśakti</s>), commission (<s>adhikāra</s>), and their transformation; of the <s>sakala</s> type as well, bound by three bonds, and also as one whose <s>karma</s> has been exhausted through some means and who possesses only the <s>kalā</s> and so forth — thus of two varieties; and of each of these again, divided into bodiless and embodied; and of each division again, as lacking or possessing the commission of <s>mala</s> and the rest — thus of eight varieties; in this way, <s>Parameśvara</s> removes the web of bonds from the soul, which is divided into many such distinctions, as appropriate.

children.text: * yasya ca yathā cāpohati tat sarvaṃ yathāvasaram agre vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.1:14
children.translated_text: And for whom and in what manner he removes them — all of that we shall explain in due course as occasion arises.

children.text: * kīdṛśasyāṇor ity āha pūrvavyatyāsitasyeti pūrvair anādikālīnair malakarmamāyāparameśvaranirodhaśaktyākhyair yathāsaṃbhavaṃ hetutayā sthitair vyatyāsitasya parameśvarād vaisādṛśyaṃ prāpitasya tatpreryasya bandhāntarayoginaś ca // MrgTV_1,2.1:15
children.translated_text: Of what kind of soul? He says: 'That has been displaced since beginningless time' — displaced by those from beginningless time, namely <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), the obstructing power of <s>Parameśvara</s> (<s>nirodhaśakti</s>), which stand as causes as appropriate — displaced from <s>Parameśvara</s>, that is, brought to dissimilarity with him, impelled by him, and subject to the obstruction of bondage.

children.text: * ayam arthaḥ maleneśvaranirodhaśaktyā karmabhiś ca sadbhir aṇor aśivatvaṃ tataś ca bandhāntarayogaḥ tadapohane tu śivatvam // MrgTV_1,2.1:16
children.translated_text: This is the meaning: through the obstructing power of impurity (<s>mala</s>) and the Lord's power of restriction (<s>nirodhaśakti</s>), and through <s>karmas</s>, the soul (<s>aṇu</s>) attains non-<s>Śiva</s>-hood, and from that comes the state of bondage and obstruction; but upon the removal of these, <s>Śiva</s>-hood [is attained].

children.text: * evaṃ ca śivavaisādṛśye ta evānādayo hetavaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.1:17
children.translated_text: And thus, the very same beginningless causes account for the dissimilarity with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: * śivas tv apratibaddhaniratiśayasarvārthadṛkkriyāśaktiḥ teṣāṃ yogyatām apekṣya anugrahe pravṛttaḥ pāśavrātam apohati nirasyati // MrgTV_1,2.1:18
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, however, whose unobstructed and unsurpassed power of seeing and acting upon all objects — having regard for their fitness — being engaged in grace, removes, that is, destroys the web of bonds (<s>pāśa</s>).

children.text: * upasargād asyatyūhyor vā vacanam ity apohatipadam // MrgTV_1,2.1:19
children.translated_text: The word 'apohati' (removes) is formed by the rule that governs [the verbs] 'asyati' and 'ūhati' when preceded by a preverb.

children.text: * tad evam akhilatantrārthasūcanād etan mūlasūtram // MrgTV_1,2.1:20
children.translated_text: Thus, since it indicates the meaning of the entire <s>tantra</s>, this is the root <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism).

children.text: * tathā cehaiva vyākhyānāvasare vakṣyati yatra bīja ivārūḍho mahātantrārthapādapaḥ ābhāti mūlasūtraṃ tad athaśabdādyalaṃkṛtam iti // MrgTV_1,2.1:21
children.translated_text: And thus, at the occasion of commentary here itself, he will say: 'That root <s>sūtra</s>, adorned with the word "atha" and the rest, in which the great tree of the <s>tantra</s>'s meaning appears as if risen from a seed, shines forth.'

children.text: tripadārthaṃ catuṣpādaṃ mahātantraṃ jagatpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: The great <s>tantra</s>, whose meaning is threefold and whose sections are four, the Lord of the universe,

children.text: sūtreṇaikena saṃhṛtya prāha vistaraśaḥ punaḥ || MrgT_1,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: having condensed it into a single <s>sūtra</s>, then expounded it in detail.

children.text: * pāśasadbhāve hy ātmanāṃ janmasthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvānugrahakṛt bhagavān bhavatīti patipaśupāśātmavyatiriktaṃ na kiṃcit padārthāntaraṃ prayojanavad eṣv evānyeṣām antarbhāvād iti tripadārthatvam uktam // MrgTV_1,2.2:1
children.translated_text: For when the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) exist, the Blessed One becomes the agent of creation, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and grace for the souls — thus there is no other category of reality possessing purpose distinct from <s>pati</s> (Lord), <s>paśu</s> (soul), and <s>pāśa</s> (bonds), since all others are subsumed within these; hence the threefold meaning is stated.

children.text: * kiṃ ca pāśajālam apohatīty apohatikriyākṣiptāḥ kriyācaryāyogapādāḥ patipaśupāśoktyākṣiptaś ca vidyāpāda iti pādacatuṣṭayopakṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.2:2
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'removes the web of bonds' — the sections on <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), <s>caryā</s> (conduct), and <s>yoga</s> are implied by the verb 'apohati' (removes) and its implied action; and the <s>vidyāpāda</s> (knowledge section) is implied by the mention of <s>pati</s>, <s>paśu</s>, and <s>pāśa</s> — thus the indication of the four sections has been accomplished.

children.text: * mahātantram iti darśanāntarebhyo 'dhikaphalatvāc chivabhedakatvena paratvād vā mahat tantritatattatprameyatvāc ca tantram // MrgTV_1,2.2:3
children.translated_text: 'Great <s>tantra</s>' — because it yields results superior to other philosophical systems, or because it is supreme through the capacity to differentiate <s>Śiva</s>, and because it is a <s>tantra</s> whose subject matter is thoroughly investigated.

children.text: * ekenaivāmunā sūtreṇa saṃhṛtya saṃgṛhya punar vistareṇaitad eva prameyaṃ jagatpatiḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthaḥ prāha // MrgTV_1,2.2:4
children.translated_text: Having condensed, that is, gathered together by this single <s>sūtra</s> alone, the Lord of the universe, the Blessed <s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s>, then expounded this very subject matter in detail.

children.text: * mūlasūtrāt sarvakṛt sarvavid iti viśeṣaṇadvayaṃ vyācaṣṭe // MrgTV_1,2.2:5
children.translated_text: From the root <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the two qualifications 'all-doer' and 'all-knower'.

children.text: jagajjanmasthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvavimuktayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Creation, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and liberation of the world —

children.text: kṛtyaṃ sakārakaphalaṃ jñeyam asyaitad eva hi || MrgT_1,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: this fivefold activity (<s>kṛtya</s>), together with its instruments and fruits, is to be known as this alone.

children.text: tena svabhāvasiddhena bhavitavyaṃ jagatkṛtā /
children.translated_text: By that [Lord], who is the maker of the world, it must be that he is established by his own nature;

children.text: arvāksiddhe 'navasthā syān mokṣo nirhetuko 'pi vā || MrgT_1,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: if [he were] established by something prior, there would be infinite regress; or liberation would be without cause.

children.text: * jagato janmavaj jantucakrasya bhogopayogiparikarasahitasya paunaḥpunyena tattadvividhayoniṣu udbhāvanaṃ janma sthitis tadicchāniruddhasya sarvalokasya svagocare niyogaḥ sthāpanaṃ dhvaṃsa ādānaṃ jagadyonāv upasaṃhāraḥ tirobhāvo yathānurūpād bhogād apracyāvaḥ saṃrakṣaṇākhyayāny atroktaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.4:1
children.translated_text: Creation of the world means the repeated production of the assemblage of beings, together with the apparatus conducive to enjoyment, in various kinds of wombs; maintenance is the assignment and establishment of all the worlds in their respective domains, governed by his will; destruction is the withdrawal into the source of the world; concealment is the non-deviation from enjoyment appropriate to [each being's condition], designated by the name 'preservation'.

children.text: * yad āha vārttikakāraḥ // MrgTV_1,2.4:2
children.translated_text: As the author of the <s>Vārttika</s> has said:

children.text: * svasaṃskārocitād bhogād apracyāvaḥ śarīriṇām // MrgTV_1,2.4:3
children.translated_text: The non-deviation of embodied beings from enjoyment suited to their own dispositions —

children.text: * proktaṃ saṃrakṣaṇaṃ nāma nyāyena parikalpanam iti // MrgTV_1,2.4:4
children.translated_text: this has been called 'preservation,' an arrangement according to justice.

children.text: * vimuktiśabdenātrānudhyānarūpo 'nugraha ity etat parameśvarasya saṃbandhi pañcavidhaṃ kṛtyaṃ kārakaiḥ śaktyādibhiḥ phalena ca bhuktimuktyātmanā sahitaṃ jñeyam avaboddhavyam // MrgTV_1,2.4:5
children.translated_text: By the word '<s>vimukti</s>' (liberation), here [is meant] grace (<s>anugraha</s>) in the form of contemplation — this fivefold activity pertaining to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), together with its instruments such as <s>śakti</s> (power) and the rest, and together with its fruit in the form of enjoyment and liberation, is to be known, that is, understood.

children.text: * etac ca na māyādibhiḥ karmabhir vā nirvartayituṃ śakyam ācaitanyāt nāpi puruṣeṇāsya malaniruddhaśaktitvāt // MrgTV_1,2.4:6
children.translated_text: And this cannot be accomplished by <s>māyā</s> and the rest, or by <s>karmas</s>, because they lack consciousness; nor by the <s>puruṣa</s> (individual soul), because his powers are obstructed by impurity (<s>mala</s>).

children.text: * na cānīśvaro 'tra kartā yuktaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.4:7
children.translated_text: Nor is it reasonable that a non-lord (<s>anīśvara</s>) be the agent in this matter.

children.text: * yaś caitat sṛṣṭyādi kartuṃ śaknoti so 'vaśyaṃ tadviṣayajñaḥ cikīrṣitakāryaviṣayāṇāṃ jñānaviśeṣāṇām aṃśenāpi vaikalye tattatkāryāniṣpatteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.4:8
children.translated_text: And whoever is capable of performing this creation and so forth, he must necessarily be a knower of that domain; for if there were even a partial deficiency in the specific kinds of knowledge pertaining to the objects of intended action, the corresponding effects would not be accomplished.

children.text: * ataś ca sarvakartrā sarvajñena tena ca svabhāvasiddhena jagataḥ kartrā bhavitavyam // MrgTV_1,2.4:9
children.translated_text: And therefore, by that all-doer, all-knower who is established by his own nature, must the maker of the world exist.

children.text: * arvāg iti ādimattvena siddhe tasminn abhyupagamyamāne yadi kāraṇāt kutaścit tasyāsāv anugrahas tasyāpi kāraṇaṃ tatkāraṇasyāpi kāraṇāntaraṃ mṛgyam ity anavasthā // MrgTV_1,2.4:10
children.translated_text: 'Arvāk' (prior) — if, upon accepting that he is established as having a beginning, his lordship comes from some cause, then one must seek a cause for that [cause] too, and a further cause for that cause — hence infinite regress.

children.text: * athāsya vinaiva kāraṇaṃ svata eva tathāvidham aiśvaryaṃ tad akasmāj jātaṃ tarhy eṣa nirhetuko mokṣo 'nyān apekṣaṇāt sarvasyaiva syāt tasyāpi vā na syāt // MrgTV_1,2.4:11
children.translated_text: But if, without any cause whatsoever, such lordship arises of its own nature spontaneously, then this would be liberation without cause — and since it would depend on nothing else, it would apply to everyone, or alternatively, not even to him.

children.text: * yad āhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As they have said:

children.text: * nityaṃ sattvam asattvaṃ vā hetor anyān apekṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: A thing is either eternally existent or eternally non-existent, because it depends on something other [than itself];

children.text: * apekṣāto hi bhāvānāṃ kādācitkatvasaṃbhavaḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.4:12
children.translated_text: for it is through dependence that the occasional occurrence of things becomes possible.

children.text: * tasmāt svabhāvasiddhanityaniratiśayanirmalasarvārthadṛkkriyaḥ patipadārthaḥ pūrvam uddiṣṭo 'nena lakṣitaḥ parīkṣyate purastāt // MrgTV_1,2.4:13
children.translated_text: Therefore, the category of <s>pati</s> (the Lord), indicated earlier, whose eternal, unsurpassed, immaculate power of seeing and acting upon all objects is established by his own nature — is characterized by this [<s>sūtra</s>] and will be examined further on.

children.text: * idānīṃ paśupadārthaṃ lakṣayitum āha // MrgTV_1,2.4:14
children.translated_text: Now, in order to characterize the category of <s>paśu</s> (the bound soul), he says:

children.text: caitanyaṃ dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tad asty ātmani sarvadā /
children.translated_text: <s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness), in the form of vision and action (<s>dṛk</s> and <s>kriyā</s>), always exists in the <s>ātman</s> (self),

children.text: sarvataś ca yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukham || MrgT_1,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: and [it is] all-pervasive, since in liberation it is heard to be omnidirectional (<s>sarvatomukha</s>).

children.text: sad apy abhāsamānatvāt tan niruddhaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Though existent, because it does not manifest, it is perceived as obstructed;

children.text: vaśyo 'nāvṛtavīryasya so 'ta evāvimokṣaṇāt || MrgT_1,2.6 ||
children.translated_text: it is subject to that [obstruction], and because of its non-liberation from the one whose power is unveiled, [it remains bound].

children.text: * jñānakriyātmakaṃ yac caitanyaṃ tad ātmany asti na tu śarīrasamavetam iti cārvākanirākaraṇe vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.6:1
children.translated_text: <s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness), whose nature is knowledge and action, exists in the <s>ātman</s> and not as inherent in the body — we shall explain this in the refutation of the <s>Cārvāka</s> [materialists].

children.text: * tac ca sarvadaivāsti na tu muktāv eva // MrgTV_1,2.6:2
children.translated_text: And it exists at all times, not only in liberation.

children.text: * muktau tu saṃvittyabhāvo yathā vaiśeṣikair iṣṭaḥ tathāvidhāyā moharūpāyā mukter nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.6:3
children.translated_text: But [the view that] in liberation there is an absence of awareness, as held by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> — since that kind of liberation, having the nature of delusion, will be refuted.

children.text: * tac cātmanaś caitanyaṃ jñānakriyātmakaṃ sarvatomukham asti na tu kṣapaṇakānām iva dehapramāṇakatvaniyamād avyāpi paśupadārthaprakaraṇe vyāpakatvasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.6:4
children.translated_text: And this consciousness of the <s>ātman</s>, whose nature is knowledge and action, is omnidirectional (<s>sarvatomukha</s>) — it is not non-pervasive due to being limited to the measure of the body, as the <s>Jainas</s> (<s>kṣapaṇakas</s>) hold, since the pervasiveness [of the soul] will be stated in the section on the category of <s>paśu</s>.

children.text: * atra hetum āha yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukhaṃ muktātmanāṃ sarvatomukhasya caitanyasya śravaṇād ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.6:5
children.translated_text: Here he states the reason: 'since in liberation it is heard to be omnidirectional' — the meaning is: because of the scriptural testimony (<s>śruti</s>) that the consciousness of liberated souls is omnidirectional.

children.text: * na ca teṣāṃ tadānīm eva tad utpadyate iti vācyaṃ sadutpatteḥ satkāryavādaprakaraṇe 'bhidhāsyamānatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.6:6
children.translated_text: Nor can it be said that [consciousness] is produced in them only at that time, because there is no origination of what already exists — since this will be discussed in the section on <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine of pre-existent effect).

children.text: * atha muktāv eva tathāvidhacaitanyaśruteḥ pūrvaṃ ca tadanupalambhād anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ sarvatomukhatvaṃ caitanyasya kuta ity āśaṅkānirāsāyāha sad apy abhāsamānatvād ityādi // MrgTV_1,2.6:7
children.translated_text: Now, if omnidirectional consciousness is testified only in liberation, and since prior to that it is not apprehended, one might argue by positive and negative concomitance that in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) consciousness is not omnidirectional — to dispel this doubt, he says 'though existent, because it does not manifest' and so forth.

children.text: * satyam anupalambhaḥ saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ tathāvidhasya caitanyasya // MrgTV_1,2.6:8
children.translated_text: It is true that in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, such consciousness is not apprehended.

children.text: * sa tv anyathāsiddhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.6:9
children.translated_text: But that [non-apprehension] is otherwise established [i.e., has another explanation].

children.text: * vyañcakābhāvakṛto hi yo 'nupalambhaḥ sa nābhāvasādhakaḥ api tu asati vyañjake yaś cāyam anupalambhaḥ sa vyañjakābhāvakṛtaḥ ataś ca nāsattvaṃ sādhayati // MrgTV_1,2.6:10
children.translated_text: For non-apprehension caused by the absence of a manifesting agent does not prove non-existence; rather, this non-apprehension is indeed caused by the absence of a manifesting agent, and therefore does not establish non-existence.

children.text: * tac ca sarvatomukhatvaṃ sad api yasmān na prathate tataḥ kenāpi pratibaddham ity avasīyate // MrgTV_1,2.6:11
children.translated_text: And that omnidirectionality, though existent, since it does not manifest — from that it is ascertained that it is obstructed by something.

children.text: * asmāc ca hetor anāvṛtanijasāmarthyasya mukteḥ purā sa ātmā vaśya iti // MrgTV_1,2.6:12
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, the <s>ātman</s>, prior to liberation from one whose inherent power is unveiled, is subject [to bondage].

children.text: prāvṛtīśabale karma māyākāryaṃ caturvidham /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāvṛti</s> (the veiling power), the potency [of the Lord], <s>karma</s>, and the products of <s>māyā</s> — fourfold —

children.text: pāśajālaṃ samāsena dharmā nāmnaiva kīrtitāḥ || MrgT_1,2.7 ||
children.translated_text: the web of bonds (<s>pāśa</s>), in brief; their properties have been indicated by name alone.

children.text: * prāvṛṇoti prakarṣeṇācchādayati ātmanāṃ dṛkkriye iti prāvṛtiḥ svābhāviky aśuddhir mala ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.7:1
children.translated_text: <s>Prāvṛti</s> — that which exceedingly covers, that is, conceals the vision and action of the souls — is the innate impurity (<s>mala</s>); this is the meaning.

children.text: * īṣṭe svātantryeṇetīśaḥ tadīyaṃ balaṃ rodhaśaktir dvitīyaḥ pāśaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.7:2
children.translated_text: '<s>Īśa</s>' — he who rules independently; his potency (<s>bala</s>) is the obstructing power (<s>nirodhaśakti</s>) — this is the second bond.

children.text: * tathā hy agre vakṣyati tāsāṃ māheśvarī śaktiḥ sarvānugrāhikā śivā dharmānuvartanād eva pāśa ity upacaryate iti // MrgTV_1,2.7:3
children.translated_text: For thus it will be said further on: 'That power of the Great Lord (<s>Māheśvarī śakti</s>), which is gracious to all and auspicious — by merely conforming to the [soul's] <s>dharmas</s>, it is figuratively called a "bond" (<s>pāśa</s>).'

children.text: * kriyate tattatphalārthibhir iti karma tasya cānāditvam ādyakoṭer anupalabhyamānatvāt yataḥ // MrgTV_1,2.7:4
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is so called because it is performed by those who desire various fruits; and its beginninglessness is because the first limit cannot be apprehended, since —

children.text: * śarīravataḥ karma karaṇaṃ tac ca śarīraṃ karmārabdhaṃ tānyapi śarīrāntareṇa kṛtāni tac ca karmajam iti so 'yaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pāśaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.7:5
children.translated_text: for one who has a body, action is performed, and that body is produced from <s>karma</s>, and those [actions] too were performed with another body, and that too was born of <s>karma</s> — thus this is the third bond.

children.text: * mātyasyāṃ śaktyātmanā pralaye sarvaṃ jagat sṛṣṭau vyaktiṃ yātīti māyā // MrgTV_1,2.7:6
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> — that in which, in the form of potency, during dissolution the entire world is absorbed, and during creation it comes to manifestation.

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīmatsaurabheye /
children.translated_text: As has been said in the venerable <s>Saurabheyasaṃhitā</s>:

children.text: * śaktirūpeṇa kāryāṇi tallīnāni mahākṣaye vikṛtau vyaktim āyānti iti // MrgTV_1,2.7:7
children.translated_text: 'Effects merged therein in the form of potency at the time of great dissolution come to manifestation at the time of transformation.'

children.text: * svakāryeṇa kalādinā sahiteyam apy anādikālīnā caturthaḥ pāśa iti // MrgTV_1,2.7:8
children.translated_text: This [<s>māyā</s>], together with its own effects beginning with <s>kalā</s> and the rest, which also exist from beginningless time — is the fourth bond.

children.text: * etad ātmanāṃ sahajasāmarthyapratibandhakatvāt pāśānāṃ jālam iva jālaṃ samāsataḥ saṃkṣepād uktam // MrgTV_1,2.7:9
children.translated_text: This web of bonds, like a net, because it obstructs the innate power of the souls, has been stated in brief, that is, in summary.

children.text: * yeṣāṃ ca ye dharmā vyāpārās te nāmnaiva pradarśitāḥ anvarthena svābhidhānena sūcitās tathāpi yathāvasaraṃ vakṣyante // MrgTV_1,2.7:10
children.translated_text: And the properties and functions of these [bonds] have been indicated by name alone — that is, suggested by their self-explanatory designations; nevertheless, they will be explained in detail as occasion arises.

children.text: * atha padārthatrayopasaṃhāraḥ // MrgTV_1,2.7:11
children.translated_text: Now, the conclusion regarding the three categories of reality:

children.text: iti vastutrayasyāsya prākpādakṛtasaṃsthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, of this triad of realities, whose establishment was made in the preceding section (<s>pāda</s>),

children.text: caryāyogakriyāpādair viniyogo 'bhidhāsyate || MrgT_1,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: the application through the sections on <s>caryā</s> (conduct), <s>yoga</s>, and <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action) will be described.

children.text: * ittham asyaiva padārthatrayasya vidyāpāde sthitasya caryādipādatrayeṇa viniyogo vibhajanam abhidhāsyate vakṣyate // MrgTV_1,2.8:1
children.translated_text: In this manner, the application — that is, the distribution — of this very triad of categories, established in the <s>vidyāpāda</s> (knowledge section), through the three sections on <s>caryā</s> and the rest, will be described, that is, will be stated.

children.text: * evaṃvidhena vidhinā patiḥ pāśopaśamanaṃ kṛtvā paśūnāṃ kaivalyado bhavati ātmanām iti pratipadam eṣām eva praviveko 'bhidhāsyata ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.8:2
children.translated_text: By such a procedure, the Lord, having effected the pacification of the bonds, becomes the bestower of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation) for the bound souls — the meaning is that the discrimination of these very [categories] will be described point by point.

children.text: * tatphalakathanāyāha // MrgTV_1,2.8:3
children.translated_text: To state the fruit of that, he says:

children.text: viniyogaphalaṃ muktir bhuktir apy anuṣaṅgataḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruit of this application is liberation (<s>mukti</s>); enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) also [arises] incidentally;

children.text: parāparavibhāgena bhidyete te tv anekadhā || MrgT_1,2.9 ||
children.translated_text: by the distinction of higher and lower, these two are divided in many ways.

children.text: * tasya ca viniyogasya vibhajanasya muktiḥ phalam anuṣaṅgataḥ anuniṣpannatayā muktir api vakṣyamāṇā bhautikadīkṣādibhiḥ samabhilaṣitabhogopabhogāt parataḥ parakaivalyāvirbhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.9:1
children.translated_text: And the fruit of that application, that is, distribution, is liberation; incidentally — that is, as a consequent outcome — enjoyment too: liberation to be described hereafter, [arising] from the material initiation (<s>bhautikī dīkṣā</s>) and the rest, after the experience of desired enjoyments, and thereafter the manifestation of supreme <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation).

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ rurusaṃhitāyām // MrgTV_1,2.9:2
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said in the <s>Rurusaṃhitā</s>:

children.text: * dīkṣāpūtā gaṇapatiguror maṇḍale janmavantaḥ siddhā mantrais taruṇadinakṛnmaṇḍalodbhāsidehāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.9:3
children.translated_text: Those purified by initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), born in the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of the <s>Gaṇapati guru</s>, perfected by <s>mantras</s>, their bodies radiant as the orb of the rising sun —

children.text: * bhuktvā bhogān suciram amarastrīnikāyair upetāḥ srastotkaṇṭhāḥ śivapadaparaiśvaryabhājo bhavantīti // MrgTV_1,2.9:4
children.translated_text: having enjoyed pleasures for a long time, attended by hosts of celestial women, they become weary with longing and attain the supreme lordship of the state of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: * tena bhuktimuktī parāparavibhāgena bahudhā bhidyete // MrgTV_1,2.9:5
children.translated_text: Therefore, enjoyment and liberation are divided in many ways by the distinction of higher and lower.

children.text: * tatra parā muktiḥ pātālādikalāntādhvavartivicitraiśvaryasampannatattadbhuvanādhipatyaṃ tattadbhuvanavāsitvamātraṃ cāparā // MrgTV_1,2.9:6
children.translated_text: Among these, supreme enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) is the possession of the varied lordship of the realms from <s>pātāla</s> to the end of <s>kalā</s>, including dominion over respective worlds; and the lower is merely dwelling in those respective worlds.

children.text: * evaṃ parā muktiḥ parameśvarasāmyam aparā tu mantramantreśvaratvam // MrgTV_1,2.9:7
children.translated_text: Likewise, supreme liberation (<s>mukti</s>) is equality with <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord); the lower is the state of <s>Mantra</s> or <s>Mantreśvara</s>.

children.text: * āsāṃ ca yathā bahubhedatvaṃ tathāgre vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.9:8
children.translated_text: And how these have many subdivisions — that we shall explain further on.

children.text: * athānyebhyo darśanebhyaḥ ko 'sya pārameśvarasya jñānasya viśeṣa iti muniḥ praṣṭum āha // MrgTV_1,2.9:9
children.translated_text: Now, what is the distinction of this knowledge of <s>Parameśvara</s> from other philosophical systems? The sage (<s>muni</s>) asks:

children.text: vedāntasāṃkhyasadasatpādārthikamatādiṣu /
children.translated_text: In the doctrines of <s>Vedānta</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the realists (<s>Sadasatpādārthika</s>), and others,

children.text: sasādhanā muktir asti ko viśeṣaḥ śivāgame || MrgT_1,2.10 ||
children.translated_text: liberation with its means exists [as well] — what then is the distinction in the <s>Śivāgama</s>?

children.text: * vedāntavidāṃ mateṣūpaniṣadādiśāstreṣu ṣaṣṭitantrādiṣu sadasadvādinām arhatāṃ ca mateṣv akalaṅkatritayaprasūtiṣu dravyādipadārthavādikāṇādādiśāstreṣu ādigrahaṇāt saugatādimateṣv api yato muktis tatsādhanāni ca śrūyante tataḥ ko 'sau śivāgame viśeṣaḥ iti viśeṣajijñāsayā tadvyavasitasya muneḥ praśnaḥ na saṃdigdhatvenādāv eva viśeṣasambhāvanāniścayataḥ śrotuṃ pravṛttatvāt nāpi viparyastatvena te vavrire śivajñānam ity abhyarthanāpravṛttatvena darśanāntarānabhiniviṣṭatvapratīteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.10:1
children.translated_text: In the doctrines of the <s>Vedānta</s> scholars — in the <s>Upaniṣads</s> and other scriptures; in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> and other works; in the doctrines of the <s>Arhats</s> (Jains) who hold that existence and non-existence [are both real], in the works born of the spotless triad; in the <s>Kaṇāda</s> and other scriptures that propound categories such as substance and the rest — by the word 'and so forth,' in the <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) and other doctrines as well — since liberation and the means to it are heard [in all these], what then is the distinguishing feature of the <s>Śivāgama</s>? With this desire to know the distinction, the sage who was settled in that [understanding] asks his question — not out of doubt, since from the very beginning he had proceeded with the certainty of expecting a distinction; nor with a contrary view, since from the fact that they entreated saying 'teach us the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>,' it is understood that they were not attached to other philosophical systems.

children.text: * tattadāgamaśrutā muktis tatsādhanāni ca purastāt teṣu teṣv avasareṣu granthakṛtaivānubhāṣya dūṣayiṣyanta iti nāsmābhiḥ pṛthak prayatnena darśyante // MrgTV_1,2.10:2
children.translated_text: The liberation and the means to it that are heard in those various <s>āgamas</s> (scriptures) will be cited and refuted by the author himself at the appropriate places later on; therefore they are not demonstrated separately by us with special effort.

children.text: * atra siddhāntaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.10:3
children.translated_text: Here is the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.text: praṇetrasarvadarśitvān na sphuṭo vastusaṃgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the authors [of other systems] are not all-seeing, the collection of realities [in their works] is not clear;

children.text: upāyāḥ saphalās tadvac chaive sarvam idaṃ param || MrgT_1,2.11 ||
children.translated_text: the means [they prescribe] are [likewise only partially] fruitful; in the <s>Śaiva</s> [doctrine], all this is supreme.

children.text: * praṇetāro hiraṇyagarbhādyāḥ kaṇādapatañjalikapilaprabhṛtayaś ca te cāsarvajñāḥ aparatvenābhimatāḥ svaprameyād ūrdhvavartino yuktyāgamopapannasya prameyajātasya tair anavagamāt // MrgTV_1,2.11:1
children.translated_text: The authors — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Patañjali</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and the rest — they are not omniscient; they are considered to be non-supreme, because they did not comprehend the class of knowable objects that are established by reasoning and scripture and that extend beyond their own domain of inquiry.

children.text: * tad svabhāvapuruṣāvyaktakarmakālātmavādibhiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:2
children.translated_text: Thus, by the proponents of <s>Svabhāva</s> (inherent nature), <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self), <s>Avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), <s>Karma</s> (action), <s>Kāla</s> (time), and <s>Ātman</s> (self) —

children.text: * uktaṃ /
children.translated_text: it has been said:

children.text: * parameśam adṛṣṭvaiva muktir mithyaiva kalpitā iti // MrgTV_1,2.11:3
children.translated_text: Without seeing <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord), liberation is merely a false fabrication.

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: * sugato yadi sarvaśaḥ kapilo neti kā pramā // MrgTV_1,2.11:4
children.translated_text: If the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) [knows] everything, and <s>Kapila</s> denies [some things], what is the standard of valid knowledge?

children.text: * athobhāv api sarvajñau mitibhedas tayoḥ katham iti // MrgTV_1,2.11:5
children.translated_text: If both are omniscient, how is there a difference in their understanding?

children.text: * tair yataḥ praṇītāni śāstrāṇi ata evaiteṣu vastusaṃgraho 'py asphuṭaḥ puṃspratibaddhāpavargajñānam aspaṣṭam ity arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:6
children.translated_text: Since the scriptures were composed by those [non-omniscient authors], therefore the collection of realities in those [works] too is unclear — the knowledge of liberation dependent on individual souls is indistinct. This is the meaning.

children.text: * ye cātropāyāḥ puṃsprakṛtivivekajñānabrahmādvaitābhyāsaṣoḍaśapadārthajñānādayaḥ phalāni ca svargāpavargalakṣaṇāni tat sarvaṃ tadvad aspaṣṭam eva tathātathāvakṣyamāṇanirvāhāsahatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.11:7
children.translated_text: And whatever means are [taught] therein — the knowledge of the distinction between <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) and <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), the practice of non-duality with <s>Brahman</s>, the knowledge of the sixteen categories, and the rest — and the fruits characterized as heaven and liberation: all that is likewise unclear, because it cannot withstand the refutations to be presented as described.

children.text: * tasmāt tebhyo 'syāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ yad iha sarvaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ yataḥ paśupāśātītaniratiśayasarvārthajñānakriyātmanā parameśvareṇedam ādiṣṭam iti praṇetṛgataṃ paratvam upāyānām api dīkṣādīnāṃ paridṛṣṭasaṃvāditatvāt paratvam // MrgTV_1,2.11:8
children.translated_text: Therefore, the distinguishing feature of this [Śaiva system] over those is that here everything is excellent, because this was taught by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) who transcends <s>paśu</s> (bound souls) and <s>pāśa</s> (bonds), and who is of the nature of unsurpassed omniscience and omnipotence — thus the supremacy pertains to the author; and the supremacy of the means such as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and others is also [established] because their results are seen to be verified.

children.text: * tathāhi saddīkṣādinā brahmahatyādimahāpātakayogino 'py apetapātakatvaṃ dṛṣṭam ity ato viṣasya māraṇātmakaśaktyapaharaṇavat pāśānāṃ bandhakatvavyapagamaḥ siddhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:9
children.translated_text: For indeed, through genuine <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the like, even those guilty of the great sins of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin) and the rest are seen to become free of sin; therefore, just as the lethal potency of poison can be removed, so the removal of the binding power of the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) is established.

children.text: * tad śuddhiṃ vrajati uktaṃ /
children.translated_text: That [soul] attains purity. As has been said:

children.text: * tulāyāṃ dīkṣāto brahmahetyato mukhyāt // MrgTV_1,2.11:10
children.translated_text: On a balance, [the merit of] <s>dīkṣā</s> [outweighs] even the primary [sin of] <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin).

children.text: * pratyayato jānīyād bandhanavigamaṃ viṣakṣayavat iti // MrgTV_1,2.11:11
children.translated_text: From direct experience one should know the removal of bondage, just as [one knows] the neutralization of poison.

children.text: * phalaṃ cehānyasarvadarśanadṛṣṭād bhogāpavargalakṣaṇāt phalāt prakṛṣṭam // MrgTV_1,2.11:12
children.translated_text: And the fruit here is superior to the fruit characterized as enjoyment and liberation that is seen in all other philosophical systems.

children.text: * uktaṃ hi śrīmanmataṃgake agnihotrādibhiḥ pūtās tathā cāndrāyaṇādibhiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:13
children.translated_text: For it has been said in the glorious <s>Mataṅga</s> [Āgama]: Those purified by <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire oblations) and the like, and likewise by <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance) and the rest,

children.text: * lokatraye 'pi modante vimānasthā yaśasvinaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:14
children.translated_text: rejoice, abiding in celestial vehicles, illustrious ones, even in the three worlds.

children.text: * athāpnuyuḥ padaṃ śākram iṣṭvā kratuśataṃ vidheḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:15
children.translated_text: And then, by performing a hundred sacrifices according to the ordinance, they may attain the station of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra).

children.text: * yā gatiḥ śivabhaktānāṃ śāṭhyenāpi mahātmanām // MrgTV_1,2.11:16
children.translated_text: But the destiny of the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, those great souls, even [if attained] through mere pretense —

children.text: * na sā yajñasahasreṇa prāpyate munipuṃgaveti // MrgTV_1,2.11:17
children.translated_text: that is not attained even by a thousand sacrifices, O best of sages.

children.text: * apavargo 'py asmin darśane sarvāṇy āgamāgocaratvāt paraḥ tattadāgamapraṇetḥṇāṃ sāñjanatvenāsarvajñatvāt tadupadiṣṭāyā mukter muktyābhāsatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.11:18
children.translated_text: Liberation too in this system surpasses all [other] scriptural traditions, because [it transcends] the domain of [those] <s>āgamas</s>; because the authors of those respective <s>āgamas</s>, being tainted [by impurity], are not omniscient; and because the liberation taught by them is merely an appearance of liberation.

children.text: * uktaṃ ca śrīmadbhārgavottare /
children.translated_text: And it has been said in the glorious <s>Bhārgavottara</s>:

children.text: * anyatantreṣu ye muktā dharmādharmakṣayān narāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.11:19
children.translated_text: Those who are liberated in other <s>tantras</s> (scriptures), men [freed] through the exhaustion of merit and demerit —

children.text: * te 'tra rudrāṇavaḥ proktā guṇatrayavivarjitāḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.11:20
children.translated_text: they are called <s>Rudrāṇavas</s> (atoms of Rudra) here, devoid of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).

children.text: * atha kiṃ tadanyadarśanānām asphuṭatvam ity āha // MrgTV_1,2.11:21
children.translated_text: Now, what exactly is the unclarity of those other systems? He says:

children.text: vedānteṣv eka evātmā cidacidvyaktilakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vedānta</s> [systems], there is only one <s>Ātman</s> (Self), characterized by the manifestation of the conscious and the unconscious.

children.text: * ātmaivedaṃ jagat sarvaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:1
children.translated_text: This entire universe is indeed the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) alone; there is no multiplicity here whatsoever.

children.text: * tathaiko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ viśvaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:2
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'He is the one controller, the inner Self of all beings; the one universe, he who makes it manifold' —

children.text: * ityādi śrutibhiḥ paramātmaiva sakalacidacidbhāvāvirbhāvatirobhāvaprakṛtisūtaḥ paripūrṇaṣāḍguṇyavaibhavasvatantraḥ eko 'pi san saṃsṛṣṭyarthaṃ tattadvividhamanolakṣaṇopādhibhedena svabhāvāntarānuvidhāyī yathāvad avagato 'bhyudayāya bhavatīti vedāntavidaḥ pratipannāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:3
children.translated_text: by such <s>śrutis</s> (scriptural passages), the <s>Vedānta</s> scholars have concluded that the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) alone — the author of the appearance and disappearance of all conscious and unconscious entities, self-dependent in the glory of his complete six-fold divine attributes — though being one, for the purpose of cosmic involvement, conforming to other natures through the various limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) characterized by different types of minds, when properly understood, leads to spiritual elevation.

children.text: * sa eva hi sattvātmani śānta upādhau śānta iva rajobahule tu bhagavān ivājñānātmake ca tamasi mugdha ivāste na tu tato 'nyat pṛthak kiṃcid avatiṣṭhate tasyaiva tathā tathā vaicitryeṇāvasthiteḥ satyatvāt dvaitapratibhāsasya dvicandrādijñānavat bhrāntatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:4
children.translated_text: For he himself — in a <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) self with a tranquil limiting adjunct, appears as if tranquil; in one predominated by <s>rajas</s> (activity), as if lordly; and in <s>tamas</s> (darkness) whose nature is ignorance, he remains as if deluded — yet nothing else exists apart from him, since he alone abides in such and such varied states; because the appearance of duality, being like the cognition of a double moon and the like, is erroneous, while [his nature] is real.

children.text: * tathā cāha tatrabhavān bhartṛhariḥ // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:5
children.translated_text: And thus the revered <s>Bhartṛhari</s> has said:

children.text: * yathā viśuddham ākāśaṃ timiropapluto janaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a person afflicted by an eye disease [sees] the pure sky

children.text: * saṃkīrṇam iva mātrābhiś citrābhir abhimanyate // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:6
children.translated_text: as if mixed with various colored spots, and imagines it so —

children.text: * tathedam amṛtaṃ brahma nirvikāram avidyayā /
children.translated_text: so too this immortal <s>Brahman</s>, unchanging, through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),

children.text: * kaluṣatvam ivāpannaṃ bhedarūpe pravartate iti // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:7
children.translated_text: as if having attained impurity, manifests in the form of difference.

children.text: * evaṃ cābhinnam evedaṃ paraṃ brahma paramātmalakṣaṇam // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:8
children.translated_text: And thus, this Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, characterized as the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), is indeed undifferentiated.

children.text: * manasāṃ hi saṃsāradharmaiḥ sukhaduḥkhādibhir yogaḥ paramātmā tu sūrya ivāmbhaḥpratibimbabhedair upādhibhir abhinno 'pi bhinna iva pratibhāti // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:9
children.translated_text: For it is the minds that have contact with the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) such as pleasure and pain; but the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), like the sun [appearing different] through the divisions of its reflection in water, though undivided by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), appears as if divided.

children.text: * tathā ca śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) says:

children.text: * yathā hy ayaṃ jyotirātmā vivasvān apo bhinnā bahudhaiko 'nugacchan /
children.translated_text: Just as this self-luminous sun, the one [light], follows the waters divided in many ways,
