children.text: * upādhinā kriyate bhedarūpo devaḥ kṣetreṣv evam ajñas tathātmeti // MrgTV_1,2.12ab:10
children.translated_text: the divine [Self], though unborn, is made to appear in the form of difference by limiting adjuncts in the various fields — so too is the Self.

children.text: pratijñāmātram evedaṃ niścayaḥ kiṃnibandhanaḥ || MrgT_1,2.12 ||
children.translated_text: This is merely an assertion; on what basis does the certainty rest?

children.text: * om ity upapattyanupapattiparyālocanaparihāreṇa yady etad aṅgīkriyate kāmam avatiṣṭhatāṃ na tu prāmāṇikarītyā // MrgTV_1,2.12cd:1
children.translated_text: Yes — if this is accepted by setting aside the examination of logical validity and invalidity, let it stand as one pleases; but it does not [stand] in the manner of authoritative validity.

children.text: * yasmāt pratijñāmātram evaitat na tv atra hetudṛṣṭāntādisaṃbhavaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.12cd:2
children.translated_text: Because this is merely an assertion, and there is no possibility of a reason, example, and so forth [to support it].

children.text: * tadabhāvān niścayaḥ kiṃnibandhanaḥ kimāśrayaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.12cd:3
children.translated_text: In the absence of those, on what basis does the certainty rest? What is its foundation?

children.text: * pramāṇanibandhano hi niścayas tattatprameyavyavasthāpanasamartho bhavati nānyathā // MrgTV_1,2.12cd:4
children.translated_text: For certainty that is founded on valid means of knowledge is capable of establishing the respective objects of knowledge, and not otherwise.

children.text: * nanv atra pramāṇam āgamas tāvac chrutirūpaḥ pradarśita evety āha // MrgTV_1,2.12cd:5
children.translated_text: But surely the <s>āgama</s> (scripture) in the form of <s>śruti</s> (revelation) has already been presented here as the valid means of knowledge — to this he replies:

children.text: atha pramāṇaṃ tatrātmā prameyatvaṃ prapadyate /
children.translated_text: If then the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is [taken as] the valid means of knowledge there, it becomes the object of knowledge;

children.text: yatraitad ubhayaṃ tatra catuṣṭayam api sthitam || MrgT_1,2.13 ||
children.translated_text: and where these two [are present], there the [entire] fourfold [epistemological] set is also established.

children.text: * yadi pramāṇam asatyarūpaṃ paramārthataḥ paramātmana eva satyatvāt tathāvidhena pramāṇenaitat pramīyamāṇaṃ manor nimitena pradīpena san tamasāvasthitapadārthapravivecanaprāyam // MrgTV_1,2.13:1
children.translated_text: If the valid means of knowledge is of an unreal nature — since only the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is ultimately real — then this, being measured by such a [unreal] valid means, is like the discrimination of objects situated in darkness by means of a lamp that is a product of the mind [i.e., illusory].

children.text: * atha satyam eva pramāṇam evaṃ tarhi sa paramātmā prameyatvena sthitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:2
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, the valid means of knowledge is indeed real, then that <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) stands as an object of knowledge.

children.text: * pramāṇaṃ hi prameyaṃ paricchindat pramāṇatām āsādayati itarathā pramāṇataivāsya na syāt // MrgTV_1,2.13:3
children.translated_text: For a valid means of knowledge achieves its status as such by delimiting an object of knowledge; otherwise, it would not have the status of a valid means at all.

children.text: * kiṃca ataḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:4
children.translated_text: Moreover, from this:

children.text: * kim anyad yatraitad dvitayaṃ pramāṇaprameyalakṣaṇaṃ tatra pramātṛpramityātmakam anyad api dvayam anyonyasattvavyapekṣatvāt sthitam eva // MrgTV_1,2.13:5
children.translated_text: What else [follows]? Where this pair — characterized as the valid means and the object of knowledge — exists, there the other pair as well, consisting of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) and the act of knowing (<s>pramiti</s>), is also established, since they mutually presuppose each other's existence.

children.text: * na hi pramātāraṃ kartāram antareṇa pramāṇaprameyayoḥ kvacit kiṃcitkaratvaṃ karaṇakarmaṇoḥ kriyāsiddhau kartrāśrayatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.13:6
children.translated_text: For without a knower as the agent, the valid means and the object of knowledge have no efficacy anywhere, since the instrument and the object [of action] depend on the agent for the accomplishment of action.

children.text: * pramitir api kriyārūpo vyāpāras tebhyaḥ pṛthag evānvayavyatirekābhyām upalabhyata iti catuṣṭayam avaśyaṃbhāvi // MrgTV_1,2.13:7
children.translated_text: The act of knowing (<s>pramiti</s>) too, being an activity in the form of a process, is apprehended as distinct from those [other three] through the methods of agreement and difference — thus the fourfold set is inevitable.

children.text: * yad āha ākṣapādaḥ /
children.translated_text: As the venerable <s>Ākṣapāda</s> (Gautama) has said:

children.text: * catasṛṣu caivaṃvidhāsu sarvo 'pi vyavahāraḥ parisamāpyata iti // MrgTV_1,2.13:8
children.translated_text: In these four of such nature, all transactions whatsoever are completed.

children.text: * kiṃ cāta ity ata āha // MrgTV_1,2.13:9
children.translated_text: What more [follows] from this? To this he says:

children.text: advaitahānir evaṃ syān niṣpramāṇakatānyathā /
children.translated_text: In this way, the abandonment of non-duality would result; otherwise, [there would be] the absence of valid means of knowledge,

children.text: bhogasāmyāvimokṣau ca yau neṣṭāv ātmavādibhiḥ || MrgT_1,2.14 ||
children.translated_text: as well as equality of experience and non-liberation — which are not accepted by the proponents of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) doctrine.

children.text: * pramāṇaprameyavyavahārāṅgīkaraṇe sati advaitahānir ataḥ svābhyupagamavirodhaḥ tadapahnave tu niṣpramāṇakatvam kiṃca bhogasāmyam avimokṣaś cātmavādibhir anabhyupagatau doṣau prasajyete // MrgTV_1,2.13:1
children.translated_text: If the transaction of valid means and objects of knowledge is accepted, then non-duality is abandoned — hence a contradiction with one's own position; if it is denied, then there is the absence of valid means. Moreover, the two defects of equality of experience and non-liberation, which are not accepted by the <s>Ātmavādins</s> (Self-theorists), would follow.

children.text: * sarvair evātmavādibhiḥ pratyakṣavirodhabhīrubhir dṛśyamānaṃ bhogavaicitryam avaśyābhyupeyam ātmanāṃ ca muktir eṣṭavyā niḥśreyasahetutayaiva śāstrāṇāṃ pravṛtteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:2
children.translated_text: By all the <s>Ātmavādins</s> who fear contradiction with direct perception, the observed variety of experiences must necessarily be accepted, and the liberation of the selves must be sought, since scriptures are undertaken precisely for the purpose of the highest good.

children.text: * tad iha /
children.translated_text: Now, in this regard:

children.text: * nādatte kasyacit pāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:3
children.translated_text: 'The all-pervading One does not take the sin of anyone, nor indeed the merit' —

children.text: * tathā na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇīty abhyupagamāt vicitraphaladāyināṃ pratiniyatajantukṛtatvena bhogapratiniyamakāriṇāṃ karmaṇām evābhāvād bhogasāmyaprasaṅgo durnivāraḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:4
children.translated_text: likewise, because of the acceptance that 'there is no agency, nor are there actions' — since actions that yield varied fruits, which are performed by specific beings and which determine the allotment of experiences, simply do not exist [in the Vedānta view], the unwelcome consequence of equality of experience is unavoidable.

children.text: * ātmanānātve hi kaścit duḥkhitaḥ kaścit sukhita iti bhogavaicitryam upapannaṃ nānyathā // MrgTV_1,2.13:5
children.translated_text: For only when selves are many — one being unhappy, another happy — is the variety of experience logically possible, and not otherwise.

children.text: * yata eva saṃsāritāyāḥ prabhavas tatraiva niraṃśe paramātmani yadi layo mokṣas tat punar api tata eva prādurbhāvaḥ punaś ca mokṣa iti seyaṃ gatānugatikā na tu mokṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:6
children.translated_text: Since the source of worldly existence is precisely that [Supreme Self], if dissolution into that partless <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is liberation, then there would be emergence again from that very [source], and then liberation again — this would be a mere going-and-coming, but not [true] liberation.

children.text: * tathāha tatrabhavān avadhūtācāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the revered <s>Avadhūtācārya</s> has said:

children.text: * tvanmateśvaravijñānaniṣpannā api muktayaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:7
children.translated_text: Even the liberations that are accomplished through the knowledge of the Lord according to your doctrine

children.text: * bhajante nāvisaṃvādam āmbhasā iva kṛṣṭayaḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.13:8
children.translated_text: meet with failure, like crops [destroyed] by floods.

children.text: * tataś ca mokṣābhāvāt tadupāyānām ātmā vā are jñātavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:9
children.translated_text: And therefore, since liberation does not [truly] exist [in their system], [the injunctions] such as 'the Self, indeed, is to be known, is to be heard about, is to be reflected upon' —

children.text: * ityādīnām ānarthakyam // MrgTV_1,2.13:10
children.translated_text: and so forth — become purposeless.

children.text: * api cāsya paramātmanaś cetanācetanaviśvotpattihetutve cetanācetanatvaṃ prāptaṃ kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇasvabhāvānvayāt // MrgTV_1,2.13:11
children.translated_text: Moreover, if this <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is the cause of the production of the universe both conscious and unconscious, it would follow that he is both conscious and unconscious, since effects partake of the nature of their cause.

children.text: * yad āhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: * tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvās tadatadrūpahetujāḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.13:12
children.translated_text: 'Entities that are of such-and-such nature arise from causes of such-and-such nature.'

children.text: * tataś ca viruddhayor anyonyābhibhavenaivātmalābhād bhāvābhāvayor ivaikasmin kāle cetanācetanasvabhāvayoḥ paramātmani avasthānaṃ nopapadyate // MrgTV_1,2.13:13
children.translated_text: And therefore, since the two [natures] — being contradictory — can only exist through the mutual sublation of one another, like existence and non-existence, the abiding of both conscious and unconscious natures simultaneously in a single <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is not logically tenable.

children.text: * yathāha tatrabhavān kheṭakanandanaḥ /
children.translated_text: As the revered <s>Kheṭakanandana</s> has said:

children.text: * viruddhāv ekakālasthau dharmāv ekāśrayaṃ gatau // MrgTV_1,2.13:14
children.translated_text: Two contradictory properties, existing simultaneously and residing in a single substratum,

children.text: * itaretaranāśāt tau kuruto lopam ātmanaḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.13:15
children.translated_text: by mutually destroying each other, bring about the annihilation of themselves.

children.text: * na cāsyānaṅgatvāt kenacid aṅgena cetanatvaṃ kenacic cācetanatvaṃ yuktaṃ sāṅgatvābhyupagame tu kusūlādivat kāryatvāt paramakāraṇatāhāniḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:16
children.translated_text: And since it (the supreme Self) is without parts, it is not possible for it to be conscious by one part and unconscious by another; and if the possession of parts is admitted, then, like a granary and such things, because of being an effect, the status of being the supreme cause is lost.

children.text: * yathā kiṃca yad yad upādānakāraṇaṃ tat tad acetanaṃ yathā mṛdādi acetanaś cāyaṃ tattad acetanaṃ paramātmopādānakāraṇatvāt cetanatve nāsyopādānakāraṇatvam // MrgTV_1,2.13:17
children.translated_text: Just as whatever is a material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>) is unconscious, like clay and the like — and this [supreme Self] is unconscious — [because it is] the material cause of all those unconscious things, that supreme Self; if it were conscious, it could not be a material cause.

children.text: * astv acetanaḥ ko doṣa iti cet cetanānāṃ kāraṇaṃ svayam acetana iti vicitreyam uktiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:18
children.translated_text: If one asks, 'Let it be unconscious — what is the fault?' — this is indeed a remarkable statement, that the cause of conscious beings is itself unconscious!

children.text: * ācaitanyābhyupagame cāsya buddhimatkartranadhiṣṭhitasya mṛtpiṇḍāder iva na svakāryajanane sāmarthyam // MrgTV_1,2.13:19
children.translated_text: And if unconsciousness is accepted for it, then, like a lump of clay and the like, which is not presided over by an intelligent agent, it would have no capacity to produce its own effects.

children.text: * ye 'pi ca grāhakatvena svasaṃvedanasiddhā ātmāno bhoktāras tata utpannā ity ucyante te 'py utpādyatvāt ghaṭādivad acetanāḥ prasajyanta ity anekadoṣāśrayasya paramātmādvaitasyānupapattiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:20
children.translated_text: And those selves (<s>ātmans</s>) who are established as perceivers through self-awareness and are enjoyers — if they are said to arise from that [supreme Self], they too, being produced, would be unconscious like a pot and so forth. Thus the non-duality of the supreme Self (<s>paramātmādvaita</s>), which is the repository of many faults, is untenable.

children.text: * athaivaṃ vedāntavādināṃ mate nirākṛte kāpiloktāt prakṛtipuruṣavivekajñānān niḥśreyasāvāptir bhaviṣyati // MrgTV_1,2.13:21
children.translated_text: Now, when the doctrine of the <s>Vedāntins</s> has thus been refuted, will the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) come about through the discriminative knowledge of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self) as taught by <s>Kapila</s>?

children.text: * yathā cāhuḥ // MrgTV_1,2.13:22
children.translated_text: And as they say:

children.text: * evaṃ tattvābhyāsān nāsmi na me nāham ity apariśeṣāt // MrgTV_1,2.13:23
children.translated_text: Thus, through the practice of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), 'I am not, not mine, not I' — through the complete absence [of identification],

children.text: * ekāntikam ātyantikam ubhayaṃ kaivalyam āpnotīti // MrgTV_1,2.13:24
children.translated_text: one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), which is both exclusive and absolute — this is said.

children.text: * śrutir apy āha ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajā janayantīṃ sarūpāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) also says: 'The unborn one (<s>ajā</s>), the single one, red, white, and black, producing many offspring of similar form;

children.text: * ajo hy eko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahāty enāṃ bhuktabhogām ajo 'nya iti // MrgTV_1,2.13:25
children.translated_text: one unborn male (<s>aja</s>) lies with her enjoying [her]; another unborn male abandons her whose pleasures have been enjoyed.'

children.text: * etad api nirākartum āha // MrgTV_1,2.13:26
children.translated_text: To refute this too, he says:

children.text: sāṃkhyajñāne 'pi mithyātvaṃ kārye kāraṇabuddhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge too, there is falsity, due to the notion of causality in the effect.

children.text: * sāṃkhyajñāne 'py etad asamyaktvaṃ yat kārye māyodbhūtakalājanite pradhāne kāraṇabuddhiḥ paramakāraṇatābhramaḥ mūlaprakṛtir avikṛtir iti hi teṣām abhyupagamaḥ kalādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ pṛthakpṛthagupalabhyamānaprayojanānāṃ kāraṇabhūtasya jagannidhibhūtasya māyātmano 'navagamāt // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:1
children.translated_text: In <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge too, this incorrectness [exists]: namely, the notion of causality regarding the effect — the error of attributing supreme causality to <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primal matter), which is produced by <s>Kalā</s> born from <s>Māyā</s>. For their doctrine is that 'the root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is unmodified.' [This error arises] from the failure to recognize the nature of <s>Māyā</s>, which is the cause of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) beginning with <s>Kalā</s>, each of which has individually perceivable purposes, and which is the storehouse of the universe.

children.text: * uktaṃ ca kvacid guṇatattvordhvabhogyasya karmaṇo 'nupalabdhitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:2
children.translated_text: And it has been said somewhere: 'Because of the non-apprehension of <s>karma</s> (action) that is to be experienced above the <s>guṇa-tattva</s> (quality-principle),

children.text: * kaivalyam api sāṃkhyānāṃ naiva yuktam asaṃkṣayād iti // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:3
children.translated_text: even the <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> is not proper, due to the non-destruction [of karma].'

children.text: * tad ayam arthaḥ yeyaṃ kāpilaiḥ paramakāraṇatayā parikalpitā sattvarajastamolakṣaṇaguṇatrayasāmyātmikā prakṛtiḥ tasyās tāvan na guṇebhyo 'nyatvam // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:4
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is as follows: this <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), conceived by the followers of <s>Kapila</s> as the supreme cause, whose essence is the equilibrium of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) characterized as <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — it is, firstly, not different from the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: * guṇā eva prakṛtir iti hi te pratijānate guṇebhyo 'nanyatve cāvaśyam anekatvam asyāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:5
children.translated_text: For they declare '<s>Prakṛti</s> is nothing but the <s>guṇas</s>'; and if it is not different from the <s>guṇas</s>, it must necessarily be manifold.

children.text: * yac cācaitanye saty anekaṃ tatkāraṇāntarapūrvakaṃ yathā tantavo mṛtpiṇḍā vā sati ca kāraṇāntarapūrvakatve na paramakāraṇatā // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:6
children.translated_text: And that which is manifold and unconscious is preceded by another cause, like threads or a lump of clay; and if it is preceded by another cause, it cannot be the supreme cause.

children.text: * idaṃ ca te praṣṭavyāḥ draṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ saṃyogaḥ saṃsārahetus tatpūrvakaś ca viyogo 'pavargakāraṇam iti yad ucyate tatra saṃyogas tāvat puṃspradhānayor draṣṭṛdṛśyalakṣaṇa eva na parasparāśleṣarūpaḥ ubhayor apy amūrtatvena tādṛśasyānupapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:7
children.translated_text: Moreover, they should be asked this: it is said that the conjunction of the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) and the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), and that separation preceded by that [conjunction] is the cause of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). In that regard, the conjunction of <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self) and <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), characterized as seer and seen, is certainly not of the nature of mutual physical contact, since both are incorporeal and such [contact] is impossible for them.

children.text: * pradhānaṃ ca na svato dṛśyam apratyakṣatvena tasyeṣṭatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:8
children.translated_text: And <s>Pradhāna</s> is not visible by itself, since it is accepted as being imperceptible.

children.text: * na ca mahadahaṃkārādirūpeṇa pariṇateḥ draṣṭā tad draṣṭuṃ śaknoti // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:9
children.translated_text: Nor can the seer see it in its transformed form as <s>Mahat</s> (the Great), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and so forth.

children.text: * tataś ca katham anayor ādyaḥ saṃyogaḥ tadabhāvāc ca kathaṃ tatpūrvako viyogaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:10
children.translated_text: And therefore, how can there be a first conjunction of these two? And since that [conjunction] does not exist, how can there be a separation preceded by it?

children.text: * evaṃ ca saṃyogaviyogānupapatter akāraṇatvam eva puruṣārthaṃ prati pradhānasya // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:11
children.translated_text: And thus, because of the impossibility of both conjunction and separation, <s>Pradhāna</s> is simply not a cause with respect to the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self).

children.text: * itaś ca mithyātvam etadīyasya jñānasya // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:12
children.translated_text: And furthermore, the knowledge of this [Sāṃkhya system] is false —

children.text: * kuta ity āha // MrgTV_1,2.15ab1:13
children.translated_text: From where? He says:

children.text: * abhoktuḥ puruṣasya bhogāyatanena dehena bhogasādhanair indriyair bhoktavyair indriyārthair bhogena ca sukhaduḥkhavedanātmanā phalena kiṃ prayojanam // MrgTV_1,2.15ab2:1
children.translated_text: For <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self), who is not an enjoyer — what purpose is served by the body, which is the seat of experience, by the sense organs which are the instruments of experience, by the sense objects which are to be experienced, and by experience itself whose nature is the feeling of pleasure and pain?

children.text: * yataś cāsya bhogas tadadhikaraṇatatsādhanasahito 'sti ato bhoktṛtvam apahnotum aśakyam // MrgTV_1,2.15ab2:2
children.translated_text: And since experience together with its substrate and its instruments belongs to him, his nature as an enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) cannot be denied.

children.text: * yaś ca bhoktā sa katham akartā akartari kāraṇādisambandhasya nirarthakatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.15ab2:3
children.translated_text: And whoever is an enjoyer, how can he be a non-agent? For if he were a non-agent, the relation of cause and the like would be purposeless.

children.text: * dṛkkriyātmakatvam eva svarūpaṃ caitanyasya tataś ca kartṛtvanirāsāt jñatvam api nirastaṃ saṃvedanasyāpi kriyātmanaḥ kartṛtvānapagamāt // MrgTV_1,2.15ab2:4
children.translated_text: The very nature of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) consists in seeing and acting; and therefore, from the denial of agency, the capacity of knowing is also negated, since awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) too, being of the nature of action, cannot be separated from agency.

children.text: * na hi akartuḥ saṃvedanaṃ cāpy upapannam // MrgTV_1,2.15ab2:5
children.translated_text: For indeed, awareness is also not possible for a non-agent.

children.text: * itaś ca sāṃkhyajñānasya mithyātvam āha // MrgTV_1,2.15ab2:6
children.translated_text: And furthermore, he states the falsity of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge:

children.text: akartṛbhāvād bhoktuś ca svātantryād apy acittvataḥ || MrgT_1,2.15 ||
children.translated_text: Because of the non-agency of the enjoyer, and because of the independence [of <s>Pradhāna</s>], and because of its unconsciousness —

children.text: * acetanam api pradhānaṃ buddhimat kartṛpreraṇaṃ vinā svātantryeṇa kathaṃ kāryakaraṇe pravartate // MrgTV_1,2.15cd:1
children.translated_text: How does <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), which is also unconscious, engage independently in the production of effects without the impulsion of an intelligent agent?

children.text: * na hy anusaṃdhānaśūnyasya buddhimato 'pi ghuṇakīṭasyevākṣaralekhane pravṛttir yuktā kiṃ punaḥ pariṇāmino jaḍasya // MrgTV_1,2.15cd:2
children.translated_text: For it is not proper that one devoid of deliberation, even if sentient like a woodworm, should engage in writing letters — how much less so for an insentient thing that undergoes transformation?

children.text: * yaś cātra cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ sa tadadhīno na karteti prakṛtisthānāṃ neyam uktir ucitā // MrgTV_1,2.15cd:3
children.translated_text: And as for the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> here, who is dependent on that [<s>Pradhāna</s>] and is not an agent — this statement is not appropriate for those who abide in <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text: * idānīm anekāntavādinirākaraṇāya saṃkhyātas tanmataṃ pūrvapakṣayitum ucyate // MrgTV_1,2.15cd:4
children.translated_text: Now, in order to refute the <s>Anekāntavādin</s> (the Jaina proponent of many-sidedness), their doctrine is presented as the opponent's position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>), stating by enumeration:

children.text: iha sapta padārthāḥ syur jīvājīvāsravās trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here there are seven categories (<s>padārthas</s>): <s>jīva</s> (soul), <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul), and <s>āsrava</s> (influx) — these three;

children.text: saṃvaro nirjaraś caiva bandhamokṣāv ubhāv api || MrgT_1,2.16 ||
children.translated_text: <s>saṃvara</s> (stoppage), <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding), and also both <s>bandha</s> (bondage) and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: syādvādalāñchitāś caite sarve 'naikāntikatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: And all these are marked by <s>syādvāda</s> (the doctrine of conditional predication), because of their non-absolute nature.

children.text: * tatra tāvat jīvapadārthas tattantrarītyā jīvāstikāyasaṃjñayā paribhāṣitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:1
children.translated_text: Among these, firstly, the category of <s>jīva</s> (soul) is designated according to the method of that system by the name <s>jīvāstikāya</s> (the substance of the soul).

children.text: * trividhaś cāsau anādisiddhamuktabaddhabhedāt // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:2
children.translated_text: And it is of three kinds, due to the distinction of eternally perfected (<s>anādisiddha</s>), liberated (<s>mukta</s>), and bound (<s>baddha</s>).

children.text: * atrānādisiddho 'rhan jīvāstikāyākhyaḥ vyapetamohādibandho muktaḥ tadāvṛtas tu baddhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:3
children.translated_text: Here, the eternally perfected one is the <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one), called <s>jīvāstikāya</s>, free from the bondage of delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the rest; the liberated one is free from that [bondage]; but the bound one is enveloped by it.

children.text: * ajīvapadārtho 'pi pudgalākāśadharmādharmāstikāyaiś caturbhedair bhinnaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:4
children.translated_text: The category of <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul) is also divided into four varieties: <s>pudgala</s> (matter), <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>dharma</s> (medium of motion), and <s>adharma</s> (medium of rest) — as substances (<s>astikāyas</s>).

children.text: * atrāpi pṛthivyādimahābhūtāni catvāri tṛṇagulmādilatādirūpaṃ sthāvaraṃ jarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjabhedabhinnaṃ jaṅgamaṃ ceti ṣaṭprakāro 'yaṃ pudgalāstikāyaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:5
children.translated_text: Here too, this <s>pudgalāstikāya</s> (substance of matter) is of six kinds: the four great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) beginning with earth and the rest; the stationary (<s>sthāvara</s>) [beings] in the form of grass, shrubs, creepers, and the like; and the mobile (<s>jaṅgama</s>) [beings] divided into the classes of womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>), egg-born (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), moisture-born (<s>svedaja</s>), and sprouting (<s>udbhijja</s>).

children.text: * ākāśāstikāyo dvirūpaḥ lokākāśāstikāyo 'lokākāśāstikāyaś ceti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:6
children.translated_text: The <s>ākāśāstikāya</s> (substance of space) is of two forms: <s>lokākāśāstikāya</s> (cosmic space) and <s>alokākāśāstikāya</s> (trans-cosmic space).

children.text: * lokānām antarākāśaṃ lokākāśam iti smṛtam // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:7
children.translated_text: The space within the worlds is known as <s>lokākāśa</s> (cosmic space).

children.text: * alokākāśāstikāyo bahis teṣāṃ sa kīrtitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:8
children.translated_text: The <s>alokākāśāstikāya</s> (trans-cosmic space) is declared to be that which is beyond them.

children.text: * dharmāstikāyaḥ pudgalāstikāyād anyo 'bhyudayahetuḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:9
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmāstikāya</s> (substance of motion) is different from the <s>pudgalāstikāya</s> (substance of matter) and is the cause of spiritual progress (<s>abhyudaya</s>).

children.text: * adharmāstikāyo 'pi tatpratibandhakṛḍ ity ayam asāv ajīvapadārthaś catuṣprakāraḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:10
children.translated_text: The <s>adharmāstikāya</s> (substance of rest) also counteracts that [motion] — thus this category of <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul) is of four kinds.

children.text: * āsravaś cakṣurādīndriyapañcakasya yathāsvaṃ pravṛttiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:11
children.translated_text: <s>Āsrava</s> (influx) is the activity of each of the five senses beginning with the eye, each functioning in its own domain.

children.text: * tathā cāhuḥ vṛttiḥ pañcavikalpā dhruvādhruvā cakṣurādivargasya // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:12
children.translated_text: And thus they say: 'Activity is of five varieties, permanent and impermanent, belonging to the group [of senses] beginning with the eye.'

children.text: * yaiṣā sravaty ajasraṃ yatas tato 'sāv ihāsravaḥ proktaḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:13
children.translated_text: 'Since through this [activity], it flows (<s>sravati</s>) ceaselessly, therefore it is called <s>āsrava</s> (influx) here.'

children.text: * indriyasaṃyamalabdhapratiṣṭhaṃ dhyānam āsravanirodhātmakatvāt saṃvṛṇoty āsravam iti saṃvaraḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:14
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃvara</s> (stoppage) is meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) established upon the restraint of the senses; because its nature is the cessation of influx (<s>āsrava</s>), it obstructs the influx — hence it is called <s>saṃvara</s>.

children.text: * taptaśilāśayanakeśolluñcanāditapaḥsaṃcayanirjīrṇavīryaṃ karma nirjaraśabdenocyate // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:15
children.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> whose potency has been worn away by the accumulation of austerities (<s>tapas</s>) such as lying on heated stones, plucking of hair, and the like, is called by the term <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding).

children.text: * nānānirayasaṃsaraṇakāraṇaṃ mohādir aṣṭavidho gaṇaḥ svātantryavighātahetutvāt bandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:16
children.translated_text: The eightfold group beginning with delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the rest, which is the cause of wandering through various hells, is <s>bandha</s> (bondage), because it causes the obstruction of independence.

children.text: * uktaṃ ca mohādiko gaṇaś caiṣa bandho jīvasya kalpitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:17
children.translated_text: And it is said: 'This group beginning with delusion and the rest is regarded as the bondage of the <s>jīva</s> (soul).'

children.text: * lohapañjarasambaddhaṃ yathā kṣiptaṃ jalāśaye // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:18
children.translated_text: 'Just as a gourd (<s>alābu</s>) enclosed in an iron cage, when thrown into a body of water,

children.text: * alābukam adho yāti tadvaj jīvaḥ sabandhana iti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:19
children.translated_text: sinks downward — so too does the <s>jīva</s> (soul) when it has bondage.'

children.text: * prakṣīṇasarvāvaraṇatvāt svātantryasamprāptau ūrdhvapadāsādanaṃ mokṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:20
children.translated_text: <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) is the attainment of the uppermost state through the attainment of independence, because all coverings (<s>āvaraṇas</s>) have been exhausted.

children.text: * yad āhuḥ lohapañjaravicchedāt plavate 'lābukaṃ yathā // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:21
children.translated_text: As they say: 'Just as a gourd floats upon the breaking of the iron cage,

children.text: * ārohati tathā mokṣaṃ jīvo mohādisaṃkṣayāt // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:22
children.translated_text: so does the <s>jīva</s> (soul) ascend to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) through the destruction of delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the rest.'

children.text: * nityabodhasukhādyaiś ca dharmair yuktaḥ sa tiṣṭhati iti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:23
children.translated_text: 'And it abides endowed with qualities such as eternal knowledge, bliss, and so forth.'

children.text: * ete ca sapta padārthāḥ syādvādānugatāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:24
children.translated_text: And these seven categories are subject to <s>syādvāda</s> (the doctrine of conditional predication).

children.text: * tathā hi dehagrahaṇāt pūrvaṃ jīvaḥ kim asti uta neti yaḥ paryanuyuṅkte taṃ pratyanekāntavādo 'bhyupagantavyam // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:25
children.translated_text: For instance, if someone asks whether the <s>jīva</s> (soul) exists or not before the assumption of a body, the <s>Anekāntavāda</s> (doctrine of many-sidedness) must be accepted in response:

children.text: * syād asti syān nāsti syād asti ca nāsti ca syād avaktavyaṃ syād asti cāvaktavyaṃ syān nāsti cāvaktavyaṃ ca syād asti ca nāsti cāvaktavyaṃ ceti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:26
children.translated_text: 'Perhaps it exists; perhaps it does not exist; perhaps it both exists and does not exist; perhaps it is inexpressible; perhaps it exists and is inexpressible; perhaps it does not exist and is inexpressible; and perhaps it exists and does not exist and is inexpressible.'

children.text: * atra hi yadyat paryanuyojyaṃ tattat sadasat tathā samādheyam // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:27
children.translated_text: For here, whatever is questioned must be resolved as both existent and non-existent in that manner.

children.text: * tatra vācyatayāvācyatayāpi ca virodhahānis tu ghaṭanīyeti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:28
children.translated_text: And the contradiction [between] expressibility and inexpressibility must be reconciled therein.

children.text: * saptabhaṅgyamoghabrahmāstravatām ajeyam iha kiṃ tat // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:29
children.translated_text: 'For those who possess the unfailing <s>brahmāstra</s> (supreme weapon) of the sevenfold predication (<s>saptabhaṅgī</s>), what here is unconquerable?'

children.text: * yat syād asti syān nāsti syād iti pudgalibhir bhrāmyate jagat sarvam iti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:30
children.translated_text: 'By saying "perhaps it exists, perhaps it does not exist, perhaps..." the <s>Pudgalins</s> (Jainas) confuse the entire world.'

children.text: * nanu cānekāntavādinā tāvad ekāntānabhyupagamān niyamenānekāntavādo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ tathā ca svasiddhānta evaikānta iti kutaḥ sarvatra saptabhaṅgī naiṣa doṣaḥ anekāntavāde 'py ekāntānabhyupagamāt yataḥ syād anekāntaḥ syād ekāntaḥ syād anekāntaś caikāntaś ca syād avaktavyaḥ syād anekāntaś cāvaktavyaś ca syād ekāntaś cāvaktavyaś ca syād ekāntaś cānekāntaś cāvaktavyaś ceti // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:31
children.translated_text: Now, should not the <s>Anekāntavādin</s> (proponent of many-sidedness), since he does not accept any absolute position (<s>ekānta</s>), necessarily accept the <s>Anekāntavāda</s> (doctrine of many-sidedness)? And thus his own doctrine itself becomes an absolute position. So why should the sevenfold predication apply everywhere? This is no fault, because in the <s>Anekāntavāda</s> too, the absolute is not accepted. For: 'Perhaps [it is] many-sided; perhaps [it is] one-sided; perhaps it is both many-sided and one-sided; perhaps it is inexpressible; perhaps it is many-sided and inexpressible; perhaps it is one-sided and inexpressible; perhaps it is one-sided, many-sided, and inexpressible.'

children.text: * tad etal leśato dūṣayitum āha // MrgTV_1,2.17ab:32
children.translated_text: To refute this briefly, he says:

children.text: tad eva sat tadevāsad iti kena pramīyate || MrgT_1,2.17 ||
children.translated_text: That very thing is existent, that very thing is non-existent — by what means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is this ascertained?

children.text: * syād asti syān nāsti ceti yad uktaṃ tad asaṃgatam // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:1
children.translated_text: 'Perhaps it exists, perhaps it does not exist' — what has been said is incoherent.

children.text: * na hi yadyad eva vastu arthakriyākāritayā sattvenāvagamyate tat tadānīm evāsattvenaikāntataḥ kaścid apy avaiti // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:2
children.translated_text: For whatever entity is apprehended as existent through its capacity for producing an effect (<s>arthakriyākāritā</s>), no one at all apprehends that same thing at that very time as absolutely non-existent.

children.text: * kaḥ kilānudbhrāntamatiḥ puraḥprasphuradrūpe sad iti pratyayakāriṇi ghaṭādau nāyam astīti buddhiṃ kuryād asati ca tasmin prakhyopākhyāvirahiṇi sattāṃ niścinuyāt vidhiniṣedharūpayor bhāvābhāvayoḥ parasparaparihāreṇaivātmalābhāt // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:3
children.translated_text: What person of unconfused mind would, regarding a pot and the like that is manifest before the eyes and produces the cognition 'this exists,' form the notion 'this does not exist'? And regarding that which is non-existent, devoid of both appearance and description, who would ascertain existence? For existence and non-existence, having the nature of affirmation and negation, are mutually exclusive in their very nature.

children.text: * abhāvo hi tadasaṃbhavalabdhajanmāpi yadi tenaiva bhāvena sahitaḥ syāt tadānīm abhāva eva na syāt tadupamardanenaiva tasya svarūpasiddheḥ // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:4
children.translated_text: For even non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), though born from the impossibility of that [thing], if it were to be united with that very existence, then non-existence itself would not exist, since its own nature is established only through the destruction of that [existence].

children.text: * evaṃ bhāvo 'pi yadi svapratipakṣeṇābhāvenāvyatirikto bhavet tarhi bhāva eva na bhavet // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:5
children.translated_text: Likewise, if existence (<s>bhāva</s>) were to be non-different from its own opposite, non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), then existence itself would not exist.

children.text: * nanu ghaṭarūpeṇa svātmanāsti ghaṭaḥ parātmanā paṭarūpeṇa nāstīti sadasattvam uktam // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:6
children.translated_text: Now, it might be said: the pot exists by its own nature in the form of a pot, and does not exist by another's nature in the form of cloth — thus existence and non-existence have been stated.

children.text: * na tu tad yuktam // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:7
children.translated_text: But that is not correct.

children.text: * kiṃ kilaitāvatā pratipāditaṃ syāt ghaṭaḥ paṭātmanā na bhavati ghaṭe vā paṭo nāsti // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:8
children.translated_text: What indeed would be demonstrated by this much? That the pot does not exist in the nature of cloth, or that cloth does not exist in the pot?

children.text: * tad etad abhimatam evātadātmakatvena tatrāvidyamānatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:9
children.translated_text: That is precisely what is intended — because of its non-existence therein by virtue of not being of that nature.

children.text: * paṭād bhidyamāno 'yaṃ ghaṭo 'nya eveti siddhaṃ sādhyate // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:10
children.translated_text: This pot, being different from cloth, is indeed something other — thus what is already established is being proved [again].

children.text: * tad āha // MrgTV_1,2.17cd:11
children.translated_text: Therefore he says:

children.text: sad anyad asad anyac ca tad evaṃ siddhasādhyatā /
children.translated_text: 'Existence is one thing, non-existence another' — thus there is the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>).

children.text: * nanu svātmanā yathā ghaṭaḥ svasāmarthyakriyāṃ karoti evaṃ paṭātmanāpi tatkāryaṃ kuryāt na ca karoty ataḥ paṭātmanā nāsti yadi svātmanāpi parātmavan na syāt tadā svakāryam api na kuryāt tasmād asti ca nāsti cety uktam // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:1
children.translated_text: Now, just as the pot, by its own nature, performs an action through its own capacity, so too it should perform that effect by the nature of cloth — but it does not; therefore it does not exist by the nature of cloth. If it did not exist by its own nature as well, like [it does not exist] by another's nature, then it would not produce its own effect either. Therefore it has been said that it both exists and does not exist.

children.text: * tathaitad ghaṭatvam aghaṭatvaṃ ca parasparam abhinnam // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:2
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this pot-ness and non-pot-ness are non-different from each other.

children.text: * bhede hi tadbuddhyabhidhānānuvṛttir na syāt ghaṭaś cāghaṭaś ceti sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca na bhavet // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:3
children.translated_text: For if there were difference, there would be no continuity of cognition and designation 'it is a pot and a non-pot,' and co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) would not obtain.

children.text: * asti caitat tasmād ubhayātmako 'sau krameṇa tacchabdābhidheyatām udvahan syāt ghaṭaś cāghaṭaś cety avirodhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:4
children.translated_text: And this does exist; therefore it is of both natures, successively bearing denotability by those words — 'it is a pot and a non-pot' — and there is no contradiction.

children.text: * etad apy ayuktaṃ yato nāsti kaścid abhedaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:5
children.translated_text: This too is incorrect, because there is no identity whatsoever.

children.text: * tathā hi aghaṭaśabde ghaṭo na bhavatīti prasajyapratiṣedho vā syāt ghaṭād anyaḥ paṭādir iti vā paryudāsaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:6
children.translated_text: For consider: by the word 'non-pot' (<s>aghaṭa</s>), either there is a commitment-negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>) meaning 'the pot does not exist,' or an exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) meaning 'something other than a pot, such as cloth and the like.'

children.text: * ādye pakṣe ghaṭaś cāghaṭaś ca syād ity ukte ghaṭāghaṭayor avyatirekād ghaṭasyābhāva eva ghaṭa ity abhipretam // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:7
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, when it is said 'it is a pot and a non-pot,' because of the non-difference of pot and non-pot, what is intended is that the absence of the pot is itself the pot.

children.text: * evaṃ ceṣyamāṇe sarpābhāve 'pi sarpa eva syāt // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:8
children.translated_text: If this were accepted, then even in the absence of a snake, there would be a snake itself.

children.text: * tathā ca sati sarpādivat tadabhāvād api bhayaṃ syāt // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:9
children.translated_text: And that being so, from the absence of snakes and the like, there would also be fear, just as from snakes themselves.

children.text: * sasarpaniḥsarpadeśayoḥ sama evopalambho bhavet // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:10
children.translated_text: The perception in places with snakes and places without snakes would be exactly the same.

children.text: * paryudāsapakṣe 'pi ghaṭatvād anyad aghaṭatvaṃ bhinnam eva paṭatvādikaṃ kathyate // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:11
children.translated_text: In the exclusion alternative too, non-pot-ness, as something other than pot-ness, is declared to be a distinct thing such as cloth-ness and so forth.

children.text: * tac ca ghaṭatvād bhinnam // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:12
children.translated_text: And that is different from pot-ness.

children.text: * abhede hi ghaṭādiṣv api paṭabuddhyabhidhānānuvṛttir na syāt // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:13
children.translated_text: For if there were no difference, there would be no continuity of cloth-cognition and cloth-designation even in pots and the like.

children.text: * ghaṭādāv api spaṣṭe ghaṭapratyayaś ca na syāt // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:14
children.translated_text: And even when a pot and the like are clearly perceived, a pot-cognition would not arise.

children.text: * tasmān na ghaṭāghaṭayor abheda iti na sadasator ekāśrayatvam // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:15
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no identity of pot and non-pot, and hence existence and non-existence do not share a single locus.

children.text: * kiṃ ca // MrgTV_1,2.18ab:16
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: asaj jaghanyaṃ sac chreṣṭham ity api bruvate budhāḥ || MrgT_1,2.18 ||
children.translated_text: 'Non-existence is inferior, existence is superior' — thus the wise also declare.

children.text: naikatra tadapekṣātaḥ sthitam evobhayaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the two are not in one place due to mutual dependence, both therefore remain as they are.

children.text: * yad api sadasacchabdābhidheyaṃ śreṣṭhāśreṣṭharūpaṃ vastu tad api tadvido naikatrābhidadhati tasyāpi bhinnaviṣayatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:1
children.translated_text: Even that reality which is denoted by the words 'existence' and 'non-existence' and has the form of superior and inferior — those who know it do not predicate both of one and the same thing, because even that has distinct domains.

children.text: * na hi yad evāśreṣṭhaṃ tad eva śreṣṭham iti vaktuṃ śakyam // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:2
children.translated_text: For one cannot say that what is itself inferior is also itself superior.

children.text: * ayam eva hi bhāvānāṃ bhedaḥ yad viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:3
children.translated_text: This indeed is the difference among entities — namely, the superimposition of contradictory properties.

children.text: * atha mataṃ yat tac chreṣṭhāśreṣṭhatvaṃ tad ekatra sambhavaty eva apekṣāvaśāt // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:4
children.translated_text: Now if it is thought that such superiority and inferiority can indeed occur in one and the same thing by virtue of relative consideration (<s>apekṣā</s>) —

children.text: * yathāyaṃ devadatto yajñadattasakāśād abhirūpaḥ caitrāpekṣayā tu nīrūpa iti // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:5
children.translated_text: for example, this <s>Devadatta</s> is handsome in comparison with <s>Yajñadatta</s>, but ugly in comparison with <s>Caitra</s> —

children.text: * evaṃ tarhi yajñadattasyāśreṣṭhatvaṃ caitrasya ca śreṣṭhatvam ity ubhayaṃ tata ity apekṣātaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:6
children.translated_text: then the inferiority belongs to <s>Yajñadatta</s> and the superiority to <s>Caitra</s> — thus 'both therefore' means by virtue of relative consideration.

children.text: * evaṃ bhinnaṃ labdhaṃ yad api dvayaṃ tadāpekṣikatvād asatyam // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:7
children.translated_text: Even the duality thus obtained as different is unreal because it is relative.

children.text: * apekṣā hi nāma na vāstavī // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:8
children.translated_text: For relative consideration is not something real.

children.text: * tasyāḥ kila vastunaḥ sati sadbhāve kiṃ prayojanaṃ siddhasattākatvenānapekṣatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:9
children.translated_text: If the reality of a thing is already established, what purpose does relative consideration serve, since what has its existence already established needs no dependence?

children.text: * tathā cāhuḥ saṃś ca sarvo nirāśaṃso bhāvaḥ katham apekṣate // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:10
children.translated_text: And thus they say: 'Every being that is complete is free from expectation — how then can it depend on another?'

children.text: * na cālabdhasattāke vastuny apekṣāyāḥ kim api karaṇīyam asti tasyāsattvād eva tadapekṣānupapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:11
children.translated_text: Nor does relative consideration have anything to accomplish with respect to a thing that has not attained reality, since its very non-existence makes dependence on it impossible.

children.text: * tad idam uktam apekṣā na satāṃ siddher asiddher api nāsatām iti // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:12
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said: 'Relative consideration does not apply to existent things because their existence is established, nor to non-existent things because their existence is not established.'

children.text: * tad evaṃ na kathaṃcid api sadasator abhedopapattiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.19ab:13
children.translated_text: Thus, in no way whatsoever can the identity of existence and non-existence be maintained.

children.text: atha cet tadasadbhāve sadayuktataro yataḥ || MrgT_1,2.19 ||
children.translated_text: If, however, in the absence of that [soul], existence is more fitting, since —

children.text: tattkarmasaṃkarabhayād avyāpitvaṃ ca te jaguḥ /
children.translated_text: due to the fear of intermixture of <s>karmas</s>, they declared it to be non-pervasive;

children.text: sāmānyetarasaṃbandhajñānābhāvād acetasaḥ || MrgT_1,2.20 ||
children.translated_text: because of the absence of knowledge of the relation of the universal and the particular, [they are] without understanding.

children.text: * tasya dehāt pūrvaṃ sadasattvenābhimatasya vyāpakatvāt pudgalāntaraiḥ saha karmasaṃkaraḥ śaṅkyate // MrgTV_1,2.20:1
children.translated_text: Because it [the soul], regarded as both existent and non-existent prior to embodiment, would be pervasive, the intermixture of <s>karmas</s> with other individual souls (<s>pudgala</s>) is apprehended as a problem.

children.text: * vyāpakatve hi viprakīrṇānāṃ karmaṇāṃ bhoktṛn prati niyamaḥ kiṃkṛtaḥ avyāpakānāṃ tu teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ vyavasthito mohādibandhapadārtha eva tanniyāmaka iti karmasaṃkarabhayād avyāpakatvam acetasaḥ durbuddhayaḥ jagur ūcuḥ // MrgTV_1,2.20:2
children.translated_text: For if [the soul] were pervasive, what would determine the assignment of scattered <s>karmas</s> to their respective experiencers? But for the non-pervasive [soul], the very category of bondage consisting of delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the like, which is determined for each individual, is the regulator of that [assignment]. Due to the fear of intermixture of <s>karmas</s>, [they declared] non-pervasiveness — those of dull intellect (<s>acetasaḥ</s>), the foolish, declared thus.

children.text: * kuta eṣāṃ mandabuddhitvam ity āha sāmānyetarasaṃbandhajñānābhāvāt samānyenānādikālīnenātmano vyāpakatvena yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ sarvakālabhāvitvena sādhāraṇyam asya itareṇa ca muktāv eva saṃjātatvāt tathārūpeṇa tayor jñānaṃ samyagavabodhas teṣāṃ pudgalavādināṃ nāsti // MrgTV_1,2.20:3
children.translated_text: Why are they of dull intellect? He says: 'Because of the absence of knowledge of the relation of the universal and the particular' — the relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>) that obtains through the soul's pervasiveness in a universal, beginningless manner, being common to all times; and the other [relation] that arises only in liberation, having that specific form — the proper understanding of both of these does not exist among those who hold the doctrine of the individual soul (<s>pudgalavādin</s>).

children.text: * yadi hi tadavabodha eṣāṃ syāt tadā naivam ayuktam eva kalpayeyur mohādipāśāvaruddhasahajavyāpakasvabhāvasyātmanaḥ svabhāvata evāvyāpakatvābhyupagamo yas tasya viruddhatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.20:4
children.translated_text: For if they had such understanding, they would never conceive of something so unreasonable — the acceptance that the soul, whose innate nature is pervasiveness though obstructed by the bonds of delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the like, is inherently non-pervasive — because that is contradictory.

children.text: yaḥ prāg avyāpakaḥ so 'nte kathamanyādṛśo bhavet /
children.translated_text: He who was non-pervasive before — how could he become otherwise at the end?

children.text: sa vikāsādidharmā cet tato doṣaparamparā || MrgT_1,2.21 ||
children.translated_text: If he possesses the property of expansion and the like, then there follows an unending chain of defects.

children.text: * prāk pūrvaṃ saṃsārāvasthāyām avyāpako yaḥ sa kathaṃ mokṣe vyāpakaḥ vyāpakatvaṃ ca tadānīm apy abhyupagantum ayuktam // MrgTV_1,2.21:1
children.translated_text: He who was non-pervasive before, in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage) — how could he become pervasive in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)? And to accept pervasiveness even then would be incorrect.

children.text: * evaṃ hi saṃsāramuktyor aviśeṣaḥ syāt // MrgTV_1,2.21:2
children.translated_text: For in that case, there would be no distinction between <s>saṃsāra</s> (bondage) and <s>mukti</s> (liberation).

children.text: * atha tathāvidhadharmasya vikāsasaṃkocadharmitvam abhyupagamyate yad uta saṃsṛtau saṃkocam eti muktau tu vikasati iti tato vipariṇāmitvajaḍatvādyanekadoṣasantatiḥ prasajyata iti na kathaṃcid api sadasadvādimatam upasthāpayituṃ śakyam // MrgTV_1,2.21:3
children.translated_text: Now if one accepts that such a property has the nature of expansion and contraction — namely, that it contracts in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and expands in <s>mukti</s> (liberation) — then there follows an unending succession of defects such as being subject to transformation, being inert, and so on. Therefore the doctrine of those who hold existence and non-existence [of the soul] cannot be upheld in any way.

children.text: * idānīṃ pādārthikadarśanapradarśitamuktinirākaraṇāyāha // MrgTV_1,2.21:4
children.translated_text: Now, in order to refute the liberation propounded by the <s>Pādārthika</s> (Vaiśeṣika) school, he says:

children.text: ṣaṭpadārthaparijñānān mithyājñānaṃ nivartate /
children.translated_text: From the complete knowledge of the six categories (<s>padārtha</s>), false knowledge ceases;

children.text: rāgadveṣau mamatvaṃ ca tadviśeṣaguṇās tataḥ || MrgT_1,2.22 ||
children.translated_text: attachment (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and possessiveness (<s>mamatva</s>) — the qualities that are special to that [false knowledge] — thereafter

children.text: kramaśo vinivartante dehasaṃyogajā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: progressively cease, since they are born from connection with the body.

children.text: sā muktir jaḍatārūpā tato muktaḥ śavo na kim || MrgT_1,2.23 ||
children.translated_text: That liberation is of the nature of inertness — is the liberated one, then, not a corpse?

children.text: * dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ padārthānāṃ sādharmyavaidharmyatattvajñānaṃ niḥśreyasahetur ity abhyupagamāt dravyādipadārthaṣaṭkasya yathāvaj jñānād ajñānanivṛttau ragādidoṣopaśame buddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmasaṃskārāṇāṃ navānām ātmaguṇānāṃ dehasaṃyogajatvāt krameṇa nivṛttau yā muktiḥ sā buddhyādyuparame sati ātmanas tadvinākṛtasya kiṃcijjñatvoparamāj jaḍatārūpāṅgīkriyate tataḥ śavo 'pi kiṃ na muktaḥ kalpyate tasyāpi buddhyādiguṇāviraheṇecchājñānādivinākṛtatvād iti bhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.23:1
children.translated_text: Since [the Vaiśeṣikas] accept that the proper knowledge of the six categories — substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>), and inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) — in terms of their similarities and differences is the cause of the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), [they hold that] from the correct knowledge of the six categories of substance and the rest, upon the cessation of ignorance and the subsidence of defects such as attachment and the rest, the nine qualities of the self — intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), merit (<s>dharma</s>), demerit (<s>adharma</s>), and dispositions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — since they are born from connection with the body, upon their progressive cessation, that which is liberation — when intellect and the rest have subsided, since the self, deprived of these, ceases to have any cognition — is accepted as having the nature of inertness. Then why should a corpse too not be considered liberated? For a corpse too, being devoid of qualities such as intellect, is deprived of desire, knowledge, and so on. This is the purport.

children.text: * atha saugatamuktinirācikīrṣayā tanmatam anubhāṣya dūṣayati // MrgTV_1,2.23:2
children.translated_text: Now, wishing to refute the liberation of the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists), he states their doctrine and then criticizes it:

children.text: cidvyañjakasya karmādeḥ kṣaṇikatvān muhurmuhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Because <s>karma</s> (action) and the rest, which manifest consciousness (<s>cit</s>), are momentary, again and again

children.text: vyajyate jāyamānaiva kṣaṇiketi matā paraiḥ || MrgT_1,2.24 ||
children.translated_text: consciousness, being manifested even as it arises, is regarded by others as momentary.

children.text: * cijjñānaṃ grahītṛrūpaṃ saṃvedanam // MrgTV_1,2.24:1
children.translated_text: <s>Cit</s> (consciousness) is knowledge, the nature of the apprehender, direct awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>).

children.text: * sā cit vyañjakasya vyaktihetoḥ karmaṇo vyāpārasya yogasaṃgrahaṇāder yadi vā karmaṇo grāhyasya ghaṭapaṭāder ādigrahaṇāt karaṇasya cakṣurādeḥ sahakāriṇa ālokādeś cānatisthairyāt pratikṣaṇam utpadyamānaiva vyajyate prakaṭībhavati // MrgTV_1,2.24:2
children.translated_text: That <s>cit</s> (consciousness), because the <s>karma</s> (action) that manifests it — that is, the operation such as the contact of yoga and the like which is the cause of manifestation — or alternatively, because the <s>karma</s> (the apprehensible objects such as pot and cloth and the like, included by the word 'ādi'), and the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) such as the eye and the like, and the auxiliary cause (<s>sahakārin</s>) such as light and the like — because of the non-permanence of all these, consciousness, arising at every moment, is manifested, that is, becomes apparent.

children.text: * ayam arthaḥ vakṣcamāṇasatkāryavādadṛśā abhivyaktitirobhāvabhājāṃ bhāvānāṃ vyāpārabhedena avasthādeśakālādibhedena cānatisthairyāt tajjñānam api tattadupādhibhedān muhurmuhur vyajyamānaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ tad eva ca pramaṇam iti pare manyante // MrgTV_1,2.24:3
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: from the perspective of the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine of the pre-existence of the effect) to be explained hereafter, for entities that undergo manifestation and concealment, because of the non-permanence due to differences in operation, differences in condition, place, time, and so forth, knowledge too, being manifested again and again due to differences in those various limiting conditions, is momentary — and that alone is the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Thus others maintain.

children.text: * tad āhuḥ nityaṃ pramāṇaṃ naivāsti prāmāṇyād vastusaṃgateḥ // MrgTV_1,2.24:4
children.translated_text: Therefore they say: 'A permanent means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) does not exist at all, because validity requires correspondence with reality.'

children.text: * jñeyānityatayā tasyā adhrauvyāt kramajanmanaḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.24:5
children.translated_text: 'Because of the impermanence of the knowable, and because of the non-permanence of that [knowledge] due to its arising in succession.'

children.text: * cid eva hi kṣaṇikā tattadarthaprakāśarūpānubhavasiddhā na tv etātirikta ātmā vidyate saṃvedanavyatiriktasya bhedenāpratibhāsanāt // MrgTV_1,2.24:6
children.translated_text: For consciousness (<s>cit</s>) alone is momentary, established through the experience of illuminating successive objects — but there is no self (<s>ātman</s>) beyond this, since nothing distinct from awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) appears separately.

children.text: * yathāhuḥ ekam evedaṃ saṃvidrūpaṃ harṣaviṣādādyanekākāravivartaṃ paśyāmaḥ tatra yatheṣṭhaṃ saṃjñāḥ kriyantām iti // MrgTV_1,2.24:7
children.translated_text: As they say: 'We perceive this one thing alone, whose nature is consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), transforming into the many forms of joy, sorrow, and the like. Let whatever designations one wishes be applied therein.'

children.text: * saṃvedana eva kṣaṇike jaladhārāpravāhavat sadṛśaparāparotpattibhramād vikalpena sthairyam adhyāropyata ity avidyājanitā seyam ātmadṛṣṭiḥ // MrgTV_1,2.24:8
children.translated_text: In awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) alone, which is momentary, through the error of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) — due to the mistaken impression of permanence arising from the successive generation of similar [moments], like the flow of a stream of water — this notion of a self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) is born of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).

children.text: * tad uktaṃ mithyādhyāropahānārthaṃ yatno 'saty api bhoktari iti // MrgTV_1,2.24:9
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said: 'The effort to remove false superimposition (<s>mithyādhyāropa</s>) [is made] even though there is no [real] experiencer.'

children.text: * ātmagrahe hi sati tad anyatra paratvābhimānāt svaparabhedaḥ tataś ca rāgadveṣādyanarthodbhavādātmagraho bandha iti bhagavatā sugatena nairātmyabhāvanopadiṣṭā // MrgTV_1,2.24:10
children.translated_text: For when there is grasping of a self, from the attribution of otherness to what is other than oneself arises the distinction of self and other; and from that arise calamities such as attachment, aversion, and the like. Therefore the grasping of a self is bondage — and so the Blessed <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) taught the contemplation of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>).

children.text: * yad uktam ātmani sati parasaṃjñā svaparavibhāgāt parigrahadveṣau // MrgTV_1,2.24:11
children.translated_text: As it has been said: 'When there is a self, there arises the notion of another; from the distinction of self and other come possessiveness and hatred.'

children.text: * anayoḥ saṃpratibaddhāḥ sarve doṣāḥ prajāyanta iti // MrgTV_1,2.24:12
children.translated_text: 'Bound to these two, all defects arise.'

children.text: * na cābhyupagatasyāpy ātmano nityatvaṃ ghaṭate yat sat tat sarvaṃ kṣaṇikam akṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyānupapatteḥ sattāyā evāsiddhatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.24:13
children.translated_text: Moreover, even the eternality of the self, though accepted, cannot be maintained, for whatever exists is entirely momentary — since for a non-momentary thing, the impossibility of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) through either succession or simultaneity means that its very existence is unestablished.

children.text: * tad āhuḥ arthakriyāsamarthaṃ yat tad atra paramārthasat // MrgTV_1,2.24:14
children.translated_text: Therefore they say: 'That which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — that alone is ultimately real (<s>paramārthasat</s>).'

children.text: * asanto 'kṣaṇikās tasmāt kramākramavirodhataḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.24:15
children.translated_text: 'Therefore non-momentary things are non-existent, due to the contradiction of [functioning through] succession and simultaneity.'

children.text: * tathā hi nityo bhāvaḥ krameṇa vārthakriyāṃ kuryād yugapad vā // MrgTV_1,2.24:16
children.translated_text: For indeed, a permanent entity would perform causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) either successively or simultaneously.

children.text: * na tasya tāvat krameṇa karaṇam upapadyate yasmād ayam apracyuto 'nutpannasthiraikasvabhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.24:17
children.translated_text: It cannot, to begin with, perform it successively, because it, being undiminished, has an unarisen, stable, unitary nature.

children.text: * sa ca kālāntaranirvartyām arthakriyāṃ tadānīm eva kiṃ na karoti na hy asāv avasarāntarakaraṇīyaṃ svabhāvāntareṇa kuryāt svabhāvasyaikarūpatvāt svabhāvānyathābhāve hi tadvato 'pi tadavyatirekād vināśas tataś cānityatvam // MrgTV_1,2.24:18
children.translated_text: And why does it not perform at that very moment the causal efficacy that is to be accomplished at a later time? For it would not perform by a different nature what is to be done at another occasion, since its nature is of one form. And if its nature were to become otherwise, then that which possesses it would also be destroyed due to non-difference from it; and from that follows impermanence.

children.text: * athocyate sa padārtho 'rthakriyāṃ karoty eva yadi sahakāriṇo 'sya saṃnihitāḥ syuḥ tadasaṃnidhānād akurvāṇasya nāsyopālambhayogyatvam iti // MrgTV_1,2.24:19
children.translated_text: Now if it is said: that entity does indeed perform causal efficacy, provided its auxiliary causes (<s>sahakārin</s>) are present; and since they are not present, there is no ground for reproach of the entity that is not acting —

children.text: * naivaṃ sahakāriṇo 'syākiṃcitkarāś cet kim arthaṃ tān apekṣate // MrgTV_1,2.24:20
children.translated_text: This is not so. If the auxiliary causes contribute nothing to it, why does it depend on them?

children.text: * kiṃcitkaratve tu yat tat kiṃcit kurvanti tat tato 'vyatiriktaṃ vyatiriktaṃ vā vyatiriktakaraṇe kiṃ tasya tadapekṣayā tadavyatiriktakaraṇe sa eva sahakāribhiḥ kriyata ity āyātam // MrgTV_1,2.24:21
children.translated_text: And if they do contribute something, then what they contribute is either non-different from it or different from it. If they produce something different, what need has it for dependence on them? If they produce something non-different, then the result is that it itself is being produced by the auxiliary causes.

children.text: * na cāsthirasya karaṇam upapannaṃ tatsvabhāvasya sataḥ svahetubhya evotpatteḥ kṛtasya ca kartum aśakyatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.24:22
children.translated_text: And the production of what is impermanent is not tenable, since what has that nature arises from its own causes alone, and what is already produced cannot be produced again.

children.text: * atha sthirasvabhāvasyāsya sahakāriṇo 'tiśayādhānaṃ kurvanti yena kālāntare 'rthakriyāṃ karotīti // MrgTV_1,2.24:23
children.translated_text: Now if the auxiliary causes bestow an excellence (<s>atiśaya</s>) upon this entity of stable nature, by virtue of which it performs causal efficacy at a later time —

children.text: * etad apy asad yasmād anāhitātiśayāt svabhāvād āhitātiśayo 'nya eveti sthiraikasvabhāvataiva truṭyati // MrgTV_1,2.24:24
children.translated_text: This too is wrong, because a nature endowed with excellence is entirely different from a nature not endowed with excellence — and thus the very stability and unitary nature is broken.

children.text: * tathā hi sahakāribhyo 'tiśayotpattau sa pūrvotpannānāhitātiśayasva bhāvaḥ svata eva vinaṣṭo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.24:25
children.translated_text: For indeed, when an excellence arises from the auxiliary causes, the previously arisen nature devoid of excellence must be accepted as having perished of its own accord.

children.text: * tasyānaśvarasvabhāvatvena nāśahetor api tatrākiṃcitkaratvāt vinaśvarodbhavasvabhāvatve vā vaiyarthyāt tasya ca svabhāvasyāviśeṣāt pratikṣaṇam iti kṣaṇikatā // MrgTV_1,2.24:26
children.translated_text: Because its nature being imperishable, any cause of destruction would also be ineffective in its case; or if it is of a nature that arises and perishes, then [the auxiliary causes] would be superfluous. And since that nature is no different [at each moment], it follows that [destruction occurs] at every moment — hence momentariness.

children.text: * tad evaṃ na nityasya krameṇārthakriyā // MrgTV_1,2.24:27
children.translated_text: Thus, a permanent entity cannot have successive causal efficacy.

children.text: * nāpi yugapat karaṇam upapadyate yasmād yaugapadyena nirvartitārthakriyo 'pi tasmāt svabhāvān na viramet sthiraikasvabhāvatvāt svabhāvaviratau svabhāvahāniḥ kṣaṇikatvam eva // MrgTV_1,2.24:28
children.translated_text: Nor is simultaneous performance tenable, because even after having accomplished causal efficacy simultaneously, it would not cease from that nature, since it has a stable, unitary nature. And if it were to cease from its nature, that would be the loss of its nature — which is momentariness itself.

children.text: * atha nāsya svabhāvāntarayogaḥ kiṃtu na karoty evāyaṃ kāryasya tv ayaṃ vipākaḥ kṛtasya yat kartum aśakyatvam eva // MrgTV_1,2.24:29
children.translated_text: Now if it is said: there is no change of nature for it, but rather it simply does not act, and it is merely the maturation of the effect that it cannot produce what has already been produced —

children.text: * tad apy ayuktaṃ tasya tāvad arthakriyām akurvato 'syaiva sattāyā eva durlabhatvāt arthakriyāsamarthaṃ yat tad atra paramārthasat ity uktatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.24:30
children.translated_text: That too is incorrect, for when it does not perform causal efficacy, its very existence becomes untenable, since it has been said that 'whatever is capable of causal efficacy — that alone is ultimately real.'

children.text: * arthakriyākaraṇalakṣaṇāt svabhāvāt tadakaraṇātmakasvabhāvo 'nya eveti katham asya na svabhāvāntarayogaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.24:31
children.translated_text: A nature characterized by the non-performance of causal efficacy is entirely different from a nature characterized by the performance of causal efficacy — so how can there not be a change of nature for it?

children.text: * yadi ca yaugapad yenāpi kurvann anavarataṃ karoti tadā svabhāvāviśeṣāt sarvadā sarvārthakriyākaraṇaprasaṅga iti kṣaṇikam evedaṃ saṃvedanaṃ yuktaṃ na tu tadvyatiriktanityātmasiddhir iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.24:32
children.translated_text: And if, even performing simultaneously, it performs without cessation, then since there is no difference in its nature, there would follow the absurd consequence of performing all causal efficacies at all times. Therefore, only this momentary awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) is tenable, and there is no establishment of a permanent self beyond it — such is the prior position.

children.text: tadasatkarmaṇo bhogād atītānubhavasmṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the experience of <s>karma</s> (action) — that being unreal — and because of the memory of past experience,

children.text: * tad etat kṣaṇikatvaṃ saṃvedanasya nairātmyabhāvanābhyupagamanaṃ ca na yuktaṃ svasaṃvedanasiddhasya sthirarūpasyāparokṣasyātmanaḥ prakāśanāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:1
children.translated_text: This momentariness of awareness and the acceptance of the contemplation of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) are not tenable, because the self (<s>ātman</s>), which is of stable nature, directly known, and established through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), is manifest.

children.text: * nanu sadṛśaparāparakṣaṇotpattivipralabdhatvāt sthairyam asyāropitam ity uktam // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:2
children.translated_text: But it was said that stability is superimposed on it due to being deceived by the arising of similar successive moments —

children.text: * tad ayuktaṃ svātmani kriyāvirodhād adhyāropānupapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:3
children.translated_text: That is incorrect, because superimposition upon one's own self is untenable, since it contradicts the self's own activity.

children.text: * yad api kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanārtham akṣaṇikasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāvirodhāt sattāyā evāsiddhatvād yat sat tatkṣaṇikam ity anumāpanaghaṭanaṃ kṛtaṃ tatsvasaṃvedanalakṣaṇapramāṇabādhitatvād ayuktam akṣaṇikasya sataḥ sarvasya svasaṃvedanasyānubhavasiddhatvāt anaikāntikaṃ ca sarvasya sataḥ kṣaṇikatvena vyāptipradarśane sati akṣaṇikasya paramārthasato vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntasyāsaṃbhavād vipakṣavyāvṛttyadarśanena hetoḥ kevalānvayino gamakatvābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:4
children.translated_text: As for the inferential construction made to prove momentary destruction — that since a non-momentary thing cannot have existence established due to the impossibility of causal efficacy through either succession or simultaneity, whatever exists is momentary — this is incorrect because it is contradicted by the valid means of knowledge in the form of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), since the existence of everything non-momentary is established through the experience of self-awareness. And it is also inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because when the pervasion of all existing things with momentariness is asserted, a dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) of an ultimately real non-momentary thing is impossible; and since the exclusion from the counter-instance cannot be demonstrated, the reason, being purely affirmative (<s>kevalānvayin</s>), lacks probative force.

children.text: * viruddhaś cāyam asattvākhyo hetuḥ sādhyaviparyayeṇākṣaṇikatvena sarvārthakriyākāriṇi ghaṭādau siddhavyāptikatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:5
children.translated_text: And this reason called 'non-existence' is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because it has established pervasion with the opposite of what is to be proved — namely, non-momentariness — in things like pots that perform all causal efficacies.

children.text: * yad apy etad vyāptisādhanārthaṃ nityasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāvirodhād iti hetvantaraṃ tad apy āśrayāsiddhatvād ayuktam // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:6
children.translated_text: As for the other reason advanced to establish the pervasion — namely, that a permanent thing cannot have causal efficacy through either succession or simultaneity — this too is incorrect due to the unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>).

children.text: * na hi nityaḥ kaścid artho bhavadbhir abhyupagato yatrāyaṃ hetuḥ siddhaḥ syāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:7
children.translated_text: For no permanent thing is accepted by you in which this reason could be established.

children.text: * na cānityasyāpi maṇyāder arthasya krameṇānekadeśasthāṃs tāṃs tān bhāvān prakāśayato yugapac caikagṛhagatān ghaṭapaṭādīn avabhāsayataḥ kaścid virodhaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:8
children.translated_text: Nor is there any contradiction in the case of even an impermanent thing such as a jewel and the like, which illuminates various entities situated in different locations successively, and simultaneously illuminates a pot, cloth, and the like within a single room.

children.text: * api ca na tāvat kṣaṇikaṃ saṃvedanam anekakṣaṇanirvartyārthakriyānuṣṭhānasamartham utpattyanantaraṃ dhvaṃsinas tadupapattyayogāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:9
children.translated_text: Moreover, momentary awareness cannot be capable of accomplishing causal efficacy that requires many moments to complete, since for something that perishes immediately upon arising, the possibility of that [sustained activity] does not obtain.

children.text: * na cāropitaṃ sthairyaṃ tattadvyāpāranirvartanakṣamaṃ tasya ca svātmany adhyāropānupapatter ity uktatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:10
children.translated_text: And the superimposed stability is not capable of accomplishing those various functions, since, as stated, the superimposition upon one's own self is untenable.

children.text: * āropyasya cāvastutvenārthakriyānuṣṭhānam asaṃbaddham // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:11
children.translated_text: And since what is superimposed is unreal, its accomplishment of causal efficacy is incoherent.

children.text: * vastutve ca sthirasyāvabodhasyātmarūpatvenāsmābhir abhyupagamān nāsti bhedaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:12
children.translated_text: And if it is real, then since stable cognition is accepted by us as being of the nature of the self, there is no disagreement.

children.text: * kṣaṇavyatiriktaś ca sattāsantāno na kathaṃcid upalabhyate tasmāt karmānuṣṭhānadarśanānyathānupapattyā vastusiddham evāsya cidātmanaḥ sthairyam // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:13
children.translated_text: And a continuum of existence apart from [enduring] moments is not perceived in any way. Therefore, from the impossibility of explaining the observed performance of action otherwise, the stability of this conscious self (<s>cidātman</s>) is established as a reality.

children.text: * itaś caitat kṣaṇikatvam ayuktaṃ karmaṇo bhogāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:14
children.translated_text: For this further reason, momentariness is incorrect — because of the experience of <s>karma</s> (action).

children.text: * kṣaṇāntarānanvayini vijñāne karmabhogo 'nupapannaḥ yenaiva hi dṛṣṭaṃ sevākṛṣyādi karma kṛtaṃ tam eva tasya bhoktāram upalabhāmahe // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:15
children.translated_text: In a consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) that does not continue into the next moment, the experience of the fruit of <s>karma</s> is untenable. For we observe that the very one who has seen and performed actions such as service, agriculture, and so forth is the very one who experiences their fruit.

children.text: * dṛṣṭavac cādṛṣṭakalpanā yuktimatī // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:16
children.translated_text: And the inference regarding the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) is reasonable, following the analogy of the seen.

children.text: * yady ubhayajanmani śarīrādibhede 'py abhinna eka eva bhoktābhyupagamyate tadā hi karmaphalabhogo nirbādho bhavati // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:17
children.translated_text: If, even when there is difference of body and the like in both births, one single, undivided experiencer is accepted, then the experience of the fruit of <s>karma</s> is unobstructed.

children.text: * atha caityavandanākhyaṃ karmānyena kṛtam anyasyaiva tatphalena svargādinā yoga ity akṛtābhyāgamakṛtavipraṇāśaprasaṅgo durnivāraḥ // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:18
children.translated_text: But if the <s>karma</s> called worshipping a <s>caitya</s> (Buddhist shrine) is performed by one, and another altogether attains its fruit such as heaven and the like, then the unavoidable absurd consequence of the arrival of what was not done and the destruction of what was done follows.

children.text: * uktaṃ ca śrīmataṅge kṛtam ekena yat karma tadvipākaṃ paraḥ katham // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:19
children.translated_text: And it has been said in the revered <s>Mataṅga</s> [tantra]: 'How can another experience the maturation of <s>karma</s> performed by one —

children.text: * prāpnoti yuktidaurbalyād iti // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:20
children.translated_text: given the weakness of the reasoning?'

children.text: * nanu nāyaṃ doṣaḥ aihikasya karmaṇo labdhaśarīreṇa jñānasantānena paratra bhogopapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:21
children.translated_text: But [the Buddhist may object]: this is not a fault, because the fruit of action performed in this life can be experienced in the next through the stream of consciousness (<s>jñānasantāna</s>) that has obtained a body.

children.text: * tad ayuktam aśarīrasya jñānasantānasya sadbhāve pramāṇābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:22
children.translated_text: That is incorrect, because there is no valid means of knowledge for the existence of a disembodied stream of consciousness.

children.text: * karmaphalabhogānyathānupapattyā vijñānasantānasiddhis tatsiddhyā ca karmaphalabhoga ity anupapannam asthairyaṃ saṃvedanasya // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:23
children.translated_text: The establishment of the stream of consciousness through the impossibility of explaining the experience of the fruit of <s>karma</s> otherwise, and the experience of the fruit of <s>karma</s> through the establishment of that [stream] — this is circular reasoning. Therefore, the instability of awareness is untenable.

children.text: * itaś ca kṣaṇikaṃ saṃvedanam ity asat // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:24
children.translated_text: For this further reason too, the assertion that awareness is momentary is wrong.

children.text: * kuta ity āha atītānubhavasmṛteḥ atītaḥ samatikrānto yasyānubhavas tasya smaraṇāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:25
children.translated_text: From what? He says: 'Because of the memory of past experience' — because of the recollection of one whose experience has passed, that is, has elapsed.

children.text: * yadā hi sthirasva bhāva ubhayakālānusaṃdhātā ātmābhyupagamyate tanubhūtaviṣayāsaṃpramoṣarūpaṃ smaraṇam upapadyate na tu kṣaṇikatve // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:26
children.translated_text: For when a self of stable nature, who connects [experiences across] both times, is accepted, then remembrance — which has the form of non-loss of the objects that have become subtle — is tenable; but not under momentariness.

children.text: * na hi prāktanakṣaṇānubhūtasukhaduḥkhādisaṃvedanaṃ vartamānena kālāntarabhāvinā vā kṣaṇena smartuṃ śakyaṃ tasyānyatvāt yathā na devadattānubhūtaṃ tatputraḥ smarati // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:27
children.translated_text: For the awareness of pleasure, pain, and the like experienced in a prior moment cannot be remembered by the present moment or by one arising at a later time, since it is different — just as <s>Devadatta</s>'s son does not remember what was experienced by <s>Devadatta</s>.

children.text: * dṛśyate ca śaiśavādyanubhūtaṃ yauvanasthāvirādyavasthāsu smaryamāṇam // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:28
children.translated_text: And it is observed that what was experienced in childhood and the like is remembered in the states of youth, old age, and so forth.

children.text: * sāceyam atītānubhavasmṛtiḥ kṣaṇikatāṃ vijñānasya nirasyati na tu sthirasvabhāvam ātmānam anumāpayati tasya svasaṃvedanasiddhasya svānubhūtyekapramāṇatvāt // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:29
children.translated_text: And this memory of past experience refutes the momentariness of consciousness, but does not inferentially establish a self of stable nature, since that [self], being established through self-awareness, has direct experience as its sole means of valid knowledge.

children.text: * tad evaṃ karmopabhogād atītānubhavasmṛteś ca na kṣaṇikatvam upapadyate citaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:30
children.translated_text: Thus, from the experience of <s>karma</s> and from the memory of past experience, the momentariness of consciousness (<s>cit</s>) is not tenable.

children.text: * tad āha // MrgTV_1,2.25ab:31
children.translated_text: He states this:

children.text: sthitir niranvaye nāśe na smṛter nāpi karmaṇaḥ || MrgT_1,2.25 ||
children.translated_text: There is no persistence — when there is destruction without continuity — of memory, nor of <s>karma</s> (action).

children.text: * sūcyagranipatatsarṣapavadanavasthāyitvādaviśramyaiva vinaśyatsu vijñānakṣaṇeṣu proktavan na smṛter avasthiter upapattiḥ kalpyate nāpi karmaṇa ity alam alīkakalpanākulīkṛtasthitinā kṣaṇabhaṅgābhiniveśena // MrgTV_1,2.25cd:1
children.translated_text: When moments of consciousness perish without resting even for an instant, like a mustard seed falling on the tip of a needle, it is said that neither the persistence of memory nor of <s>karma</s> can be conceived. Enough with this obsession with momentary destruction that disturbs the established [truth] through false constructions.

children.text: vināśalakṣaṇo 'paiti na muktāv apy upaplavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The calamity characterized by destruction does not cease even in liberation (<s>mukti</s>);
