children.text: na cāsty anubhavaḥ kaścid bhavāvasthā varaṃ tataḥ || MrgT_1,2.26 ||
children.translated_text: and there is no experience whatsoever — the state of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>) is therefore preferable.

children.text: * śuddhacitsaṃtatisamutpādo bhavatāṃ mokṣaḥ syāt yadi vā pradīpanirvāṇarūpaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.26:1
children.translated_text: Your liberation would consist either in the arising of a pure stream of consciousness, or else it has the form of the extinction of a lamp.

children.text: * ādye pakṣe svaparikalpitasya pratikṣaṇavināśitvalakṣaṇasyopaplavasya muktāv apy anupaśamaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.26:2
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, the calamity of momentary destruction, which you yourselves have posited, does not subside even in liberation.

children.text: * dvitīye tu pradīpanirvāṇarūpatvāt saṃvedanāsaṃbhavataḥ kaścid apy anubhavo nāstīti tathāvidhāt saṃvedanavināśātmakāt kāṣṭhakuḍyādīnām api sulabhān mokṣāt saṃsārāvasthā varaṃ saugatānām iti kṛtam evaṃvidhamokṣalipsayā // MrgTV_1,2.26:3
children.translated_text: In the second alternative, since awareness is impossible due to [liberation] having the form of the extinction of a lamp, there is no experience of any kind. Therefore, since liberation of such a form — which consists in the destruction of awareness — is easily attainable even by logs, walls, and the like, the state of worldly existence is preferable for the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists). Enough with the desire for such liberation.

children.text: * tadiyatā vedāntasāṃkhyasadasatpādārthikādimateṣu asarvadarśipraṇetṛtvād vastusaṃgrahasyāsphuṭatvam asaṃbaddhatāṃ codbhāvya darśanāntarāṇām apy eṣaiva vārteti tattadabhiniveśināṃ na niratiśayaniḥśreyasayoga iti vaktum āha // MrgTV_1,2.26:4
children.translated_text: Having thus highlighted the lack of clarity and the incoherence in the apprehension of reality in the doctrines of <s>Vedānta</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the proponents of the real and unreal categories, and others — since their founders were not omniscient — in order to say that the same is the case with other doctrines too, and that those who are attached to each of them do not attain the unsurpassed supreme good, he says:

children.text: ityādy ajñānamūḍhānāṃ matam āśritya durdhiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of corrupt intellect, relying upon doctrines such as these and others, of those deluded by ignorance,

children.text: apavargam abhīpsanti khadyotāt pāvakārthinaḥ || MrgT_1,2.27 ||
children.translated_text: seek liberation — [like those] desiring fire from a firefly.

children.text: * śivaśaktividyeśvarādāv upādeyasatattve malakarmamāyādau ca heyaparamārthe yeṣāṃ nāsty avabodhaḥ teṣām ajñānamūḍhānāṃ darśanāntarapraṇetḥṇāṃ saṃbandhi mataṃ śāstram āśrityākuśalamatayo ye muktim icchanti te khadyotād agnyabhyarthinaḥ kīṭamaṇer vahniṃ lipsavaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.27:1
children.translated_text: Those who have no understanding of the reality to be accepted — <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s> (Power), <s>Vidyeśvara</s> (Lord of Knowledge), and the rest — and of the ultimate truth to be rejected — <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and the rest — of those deluded by ignorance, the founders of other doctrines, relying on their doctrines, those of unsound intellect who seek liberation are like those desiring fire from a firefly — those who wish to obtain fire from a glowworm.

children.text: * te yathā vyarthaśramās tathā te viphalakleśā bhavantīty arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.27:2
children.translated_text: Just as those [who seek fire from a firefly] labor in vain, so too these [seekers] undergo fruitless hardship — that is the meaning.

children.text: * tathā hi // MrgTV_1,2.27:3
children.translated_text: For instance:

children.text: yat kaivalyaṃ puṃsprakṛtyor vivekād yo vā sarvaṃ brahma matvā virāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) arises from the discrimination of <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) and <s>prakṛti</s> (matter), or whatever cessation comes from realizing all as <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yā vā kāścin muktayaḥ pāśajanyās tās tāḥ sarvā bhedam āyānti sṛṣṭau || MrgT_1,2.28 ||
children.translated_text: or whatever liberations are produced from the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) — all of these undergo differentiation at the time of creation.

children.text: * yad etat kapilakalpitaṃ puṃsprakṛtyor vivekāt kaivalyaṃ yā ca sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahmeti matvā dvaitavikalpaprahāṇe sati brahmaprāptiḥ yāś ca pāśajanyāḥ kāścit pāñcarātrādibhir muktayo 'bhyupagatāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.28:1
children.translated_text: Whatever isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) is conceived by <s>Kapila</s> through the discrimination of <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>prakṛti</s>, and whatever attainment of <s>Brahman</s> [is achieved] upon the abandonment of the conceptual construction of duality, having realized 'all this indeed is <s>Brahman</s>,' and whatever liberations produced from bonds are accepted by the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> and others —

children.text: * yathāhuḥ īśās tu te samabhavan prakṛteḥ parasyāḥ kṛṣṇāniruddhamakaradhvajarauhiṇeyāḥ iti // MrgTV_1,2.28:2
children.translated_text: as they say: 'They became the lords of the supreme <s>Prakṛti</s> — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Makaradhvaja</s>, and <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>.'

children.text: * yathā vā kālaikavādināṃ kālaḥ sṛjati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharati prajāḥ // MrgTV_1,2.28:3
children.translated_text: Or as those who hold time (<s>kāla</s>) as the sole [cause] say: 'Time creates beings, time withdraws creatures;

children.text: * kālaḥ supteṣu jagarti kālo hi duratikrama iti // MrgTV_1,2.28:4
children.translated_text: time is awake when [all] are asleep — time indeed is difficult to overcome.'

children.text: * yathā vā keṣāṃcit cittam eva hi saṃsāro rāgādikleśadūṣitam // MrgTV_1,2.28:5
children.translated_text: Or as some hold: 'The mind (<s>citta</s>) alone is <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), polluted by the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest;

children.text: * tad eva tadvinirmuktaṃ mokṣa ity abhidhīyata iti // MrgTV_1,2.28:6
children.translated_text: that very [mind], freed from those [afflictions], is called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).'

children.text: * etāḥ kila prakṛtikālabuddhyādīnāṃ bandhakatvena pāśarūpatvāt pāśajanyā muktayaḥ sargārambhe bhedam āyānti vinaśyantīty arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.28:7
children.translated_text: These are indeed liberations produced from bonds (<s>pāśa</s>), since <s>prakṛti</s>, time, intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and the like have the nature of bonds by being agents of bondage — they undergo differentiation, that is, they perish at the commencement of creation. This is the meaning.

children.text: * yad uktaṃ śrīmanmataṅge tasmāt pradhānaśabdena tattvam uktam acetanam // MrgTV_1,2.28:8
children.translated_text: As has been stated in the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s> [tantra]: 'Therefore by the word <s>pradhāna</s> (primary matter) is denoted a non-conscious principle (<s>tattva</s>);

children.text: * tasmāt paraṃ nāsty aparaṃ yeṣāṃ bhāvaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.28:9
children.translated_text: therefore those whose existence is founded upon nothing beyond that —

children.text: * na te muktā munivyāghra punar āyānty adhogatim iti // MrgTV_1,2.28:10
children.translated_text: they are not liberated, O tiger among sages; they return again to the lower course.'

children.text: * tathā upādāneṣu līnānāṃ punar āvartanaṃ dhruvam iti // MrgTV_1,2.28:11
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'For those who are absorbed in their material causes, return is certain.'

children.text: * teṣāṃ tu tathāvidhamithyādhyāsabhājāṃ na nirantaram ajñānadhvāntasantatir antaḥkaraṇam āvṛṇoti api tu te krameṇa vivekaprathanāt parameśvarānugrahāspadatāṃ kasmiṃścid api kāle yāsyanti // MrgTV_1,2.28:12
children.translated_text: But for those who partake of such erroneous superimposition, the continuous stream of the darkness of ignorance does not envelop their inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) without interruption; rather, they will, in the course of time, through the gradual expansion of discrimination, become recipients of the grace of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord).

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkarapārameśvare na mokṣaṃ yāti puruṣaḥ svasāmarthyāt kadācana // MrgTV_1,2.28:13
children.translated_text: And thus it has been stated in the venerable <s>Pauṣkarapārameśvara</s>: 'A soul (<s>puruṣa</s>) never attains liberation by his own power alone,

children.text: * muktvā prasādaṃ devasya śivasyāśivahāriṇa iti // MrgTV_1,2.28:14
children.translated_text: except through the grace (<s>prasāda</s>) of the Lord <s>Śiva</s>, who removes what is inauspicious.'

children.text: * athaivaṃ matāntaroktāyā mukteḥ prāguktavad asatyatve tataḥ kiṃ tadvailakṣaṇyamihatyayoḥ siddhimuktyor ity āha // MrgTV_1,2.28:15
children.translated_text: Now, if the liberation taught in other doctrines is unreal as stated above, then what is the distinction between the attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) and liberation (<s>mukti</s>) of this [system] and those? He says:

children.text: śaive siddho bhāti mūrdhnītareṣāṃ muktaḥ sṛṣṭau punar abhyeti nādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śaiva</s> [system], the perfected one shines at the summit of others; the liberated one does not again descend at the time of creation;

children.text: viśvān arthān svena viṣṭabhya dhāmnā sarveśānānīśitaḥ sarvadāste || MrgT_1,2.29 ||
children.translated_text: pervading all objects by his own radiance, ungoverned by the Lord of all, he abides forever.

children.text: * iha śāstre yaḥ siddhaḥ sa vividhabhuvanopapannavicitraiśvaryasaṃpāditatattadbhogabhāk sarvottkarṣaśālī bhavati // MrgTV_1,2.29:1
children.translated_text: In this scripture, one who is perfected (<s>siddha</s>), possessing the varied lordship obtained through diverse realms and enjoying the respective pleasures, becomes endowed with supreme eminence.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ bṛhaspatipādaiḥ yan māhātmyaṃ bhagavati paramaśive 'nupamam avyayam acintyam // MrgTV_1,2.29:2
children.translated_text: And thus it has been stated by the venerable <s>Bṛhaspati</s>: 'Whatever incomparable, imperishable, inconceivable greatness belongs to the Blessed Supreme <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: * tan māhātmyaṃ siddhe hatabandhanamaṇḍale bhavatīti // MrgTV_1,2.29:3
children.translated_text: that very greatness belongs to the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>) whose circle of bonds has been destroyed.'

children.text: * na ca darśanāntarapratipannabrahmalayasaṃvidvināśaprakṛtipuruṣavivekādyātmano mokṣasyaivaṃguṇatvam ity uktam // MrgTV_1,2.29:4
children.translated_text: And it has been stated that the liberation of the nature of absorption in <s>Brahman</s>, destruction of consciousness, discrimination of <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, and the like, as accepted by other philosophical systems, does not possess such qualities.

children.text: * yas tv asmin darśane muktaḥ sa bandhakāraṇānāṃ malakarmamāyāparameśvaranirodhaśaktīnām uparatādhikāratvāt punaḥ sargaprārambhe nādho 'bhyeti na saṃsārī bhavatīty arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.29:5
children.translated_text: But one who is liberated (<s>mukta</s>) in this system — because the causes of bondage, namely <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and the obstructing power of <s>Parameśvara</s> (<s>nirodhaśakti</s>), have their commission terminated — does not again descend at the commencement of creation, that is, does not become a <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being). This is the meaning.

children.text: * kiṃ tarhi sa karotīty āha viśvān arthān iti āvirbhūtaniratiśayasarvārthajñatvakartṛtvataḥ śivasamānamahimatvāt svatejasā samadhiṣṭhitasarvārtho 'pi san muktātmā na kiṃcit karoti karaṇīyābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,2.29:6
children.translated_text: Then what does he do? He says 'pervading all objects' — because of the manifestation of unsurpassed omniscience and universal agency, and because of having greatness equal to <s>Śiva</s>, though the liberated soul pervades all objects by his own radiance, he does not do anything, because there is nothing remaining to be done.

children.text: * evaṃ cen mukteḥ pūrvam akiṃcitkaro 'bhūt muktaś ca tadrūpa eveti ko 'sya muktau viśeṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.29:7
children.translated_text: If so, then before liberation he did nothing, and after liberation he is of the same nature — so what is the distinction in liberation?

children.text: * ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ yat sarveśānena parameśvareṇānīśitaḥ apreritas tadānīm asau bhavati // MrgTV_1,2.29:8
children.translated_text: This is the distinction: that at that time, he is ungoverned, that is, not impelled, by the Lord of all, <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: * kiṃ kiṃcid eva kālam apreryaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.29:9
children.translated_text: Is he free from being impelled only for some limited time?

children.text: * nety āha sarvadeti sarvakālaṃ taṃ pratyaprerakaḥ śivabhaṭṭārako bhavatīty arthaḥ // MrgTV_1,2.29:10
children.translated_text: No, he says 'forever' — at all times, the Blessed <s>Śiva</s> is non-impelling with respect to him. This is the meaning.

children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 3
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> (Knowledge Section), Chapter 3

children.text: athopalabhya dehādi vastu kāryatvadharmakam /
children.translated_text: Now, perceiving the body and other entities as possessing the property of being effects,

children.text: kartāram asya jānīmo viśiṣṭam anumānataḥ || MrgT_1,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: we know their maker to be a distinguished [being], through inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text: * athaśabdo'dhikārārthaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:1
children.translated_text: The word 'atha' (now) has the sense of commencement of a topic.

children.text: * atra hi patipadārthaparīkṣādhikriyata ityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:2
children.translated_text: The meaning is: here, the examination of the category of <s>pati</s> (the Lord) is commenced.

children.text: * atra ca tanukaraṇabhuvanādīnāṃ bhāvānāṃ saṃniveśaviśiṣṭatvena kāryatvaṃ buddhvā anumānenaiṣāṃ buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvaṃ pratīyata iti tātparyam // MrgTV_1,3.1:3
children.translated_text: And here, the purport is that, having understood the body, organs, worlds, and other entities to be effects by virtue of possessing a specific arrangement, it is inferred that they are preceded by an intelligent maker.

children.text: * nanu dehasyaiva tāvatkāryatvam asiddhaṃ nahi kvacit kadācid dehaḥ kenacit kriyamāṇo dṛṣṭaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:4
children.translated_text: But first, the very fact that the body is an effect is unestablished — for nowhere at any time has the body been seen being made by anyone.

children.text: * satyaṃ kenacit kriyamāṇatvaṃ dehasya na dṛṣṭam iti kartṛdarśanāpahnavo na yuktaḥ tasyānumeyatvena darśanāviṣayatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:5
children.translated_text: True, the body has not been seen being made by anyone — but this denial of seeing a maker is not valid, because the maker, being something to be inferred, is by nature beyond the domain of perception.

children.text: * dehasya tu kriyamāṇatvaṃ kathaṃ na dṛṣṭam abhūtvā bhāvitvam eva hi kāryatvaṃ tac ca dehasyopalabhyata eva // MrgTV_1,3.1:6
children.translated_text: But how has the body not been seen to be something being made? For being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) means precisely coming into being after not having existed — and that is indeed observed in the case of the body.

children.text: * tathā hi śukraśoṇitakalalādyupādānāt diha upacaye iti dhātvarthagatyā pratimāsopacīyamāno garbhastho dehaḥ pratīyate iti katham eṣa kāryatvam atikrāmet // MrgTV_1,3.1:7
children.translated_text: For thus: from the material causes of semen, blood, the embryonic mass (<s>kalala</s>), and the rest — 'diha' meaning growth or increase — the body in the womb is observed to grow month by month, according to the meaning of the verbal root. How then could it transcend the status of being an effect?

children.text: * kiṃ ca saṃniveśaviśeṣavattvād vinaśvaratvāc ca dehādeḥ kāryatvam apahnotum aśakyam // MrgTV_1,3.1:8
children.translated_text: Moreover, the status of being an effect of the body and the like cannot be denied because of their possessing specific arrangement and being perishable.

children.text: * yad yat saṃniveśaviśeṣavad vinaśvaraṃ tat tat kāryaṃ yathā ghaṭādi // MrgTV_1,3.1:9
children.translated_text: Whatever possesses specific arrangement and is perishable — that is an effect, just like a pot and the like.

children.text: * tathā caite dehādayaḥ padārthāḥ tasmād ete'pi kāryāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:10
children.translated_text: And so are these entities such as the body and the rest; therefore these too are effects.

children.text: * evaṃ ca sati dehādi vastujātaṃ dharmi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam iti sādhyo dharmaḥ kāryatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:11
children.translated_text: This being the case, the body and other existent things constitute the subject (<s>dharmin</s>); that they are preceded by an intelligent maker is the property to be proved (<s>sādhya dharma</s>); [the reason is] because of being effects.

children.text: * yad yat kāryaṃ tat tad buddhimatkartṛpūrvakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā rathādi // MrgTV_1,3.1:12
children.translated_text: Whatever is an effect is seen to be preceded by an intelligent maker, just like a chariot and the like.

children.text: * yat tu naivaṃvidhaṃ na tat kāryaṃ yathātmādi // MrgTV_1,3.1:13
children.translated_text: And whatever is not of such a kind — that is not an effect, just like the <s>ātman</s> (self) and the like.

children.text: * nanu ghuṇākṣare kārye 'pi na buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvam astīty anaikāntikaḥ kāryatvahetuḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:14
children.translated_text: But in the case of letters [formed by] wood-worms, even though they are effects, there is no precedence by an intelligent maker — therefore the reason of 'being an effect' is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

children.text: * naivaṃ tatra kāryatāyā evānanvayāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:15
children.translated_text: Not so, because in that case, the status of being an effect itself does not obtain.

children.text: * yatheṣṭasaṃcāramātra eva kila ghuṇasya kartṛtā nanu viśiṣṭasaṃniveśākṣaranirmitau // MrgTV_1,3.1:16
children.translated_text: The agency of the wood-worm consists merely in moving about as it pleases — not in the production of letters with specific arrangement.

children.text: * sa tu saṃniveśas tathā anyathāsya parisarpataḥ svabhāvata evopapadyate // MrgTV_1,3.1:17
children.translated_text: But that arrangement [of wood-worm markings], whether in this form or otherwise, is naturally produced as it crawls about of its own accord.

children.text: * nanu tadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāt ghuṇakartṛkam evākṣaram // MrgTV_1,3.1:18
children.translated_text: But since [the letter-form] exists when [the worm] is present and does not exist when [the worm] is absent, the letter is indeed made by the wood-worm.

children.text: * yadyevaṃ tat tathācāritve bhāvāt atathācāritve cākṣarasyānabhivyakter avyavadhānena ghuṇākṣarasya buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvam astīti kutaḥ kāryatvahetoranaikāntikatvam // MrgTV_1,3.1:19
children.translated_text: If so, then because [the letter] exists when it [the worm] behaves in a certain way and does not manifest when it does not behave thus — since the wood-worm letter is indeed preceded by an intelligent maker without interruption, how then is there inconclusiveness of the reason of being an effect?

children.text: * na cāyam akṛṣṭajātaiḥ śālyādibhir vanadrumādibhir vānaikāntikaḥ teṣu kartrabhāvasyāniścayāt teṣāṃ ca pakṣībhūtatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:20
children.translated_text: Nor is this [reason] rendered inconclusive by self-grown rice and the like, or by forest trees and the like, since in their case the absence of a maker is not certain, and they themselves are instances belonging to the subject class (<s>pakṣa</s>).

children.text: * nanvasiddhavyāptikasya pakṣīkaraṇamātreṇa yadi hetvābhāsānāṃ nirāsastarhi na kecana hetavo hetvābhāsāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:21
children.translated_text: But if the mere inclusion within the subject class could dispel logical fallacies of a reason whose pervasion is unestablished, then no reasons would ever be fallacious.

children.text: * bhaved etad yadyayaṃ kāryatvahetur asiddhavyāptikaḥ syāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:22
children.translated_text: This would be so if this reason of 'being an effect' had an unestablished pervasion.

children.text: * yāvatā dṛṣṭāntīkṛtadṛṣṭakartṛkaghaṭādivyatiriktās trailokyodaravartinas tanukaraṇabhuvanādayo bhāvā dharmiṇaḥ kartṛpūrvakāḥ kāryatvād upalabhyamānakartṛkaghaṭādivad ityanumāne kriyamāṇe kim anyad avaśiṣyate yatra kāryatvasya vyāptirna siddhā syāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:23
children.translated_text: Since, however, when the inference is formulated — 'The entities within the three worlds, namely bodies, organs, worlds, and the rest, which are the subjects, distinct from pots and the like whose makers are observed in the example, are preceded by a maker, because of being effects, like pots and the like whose makers are observed' — what else remains where the pervasion of being an effect would not be established?

children.text: * nanu cātrānumāne ya eva ghaṭādir dṛṣṭānte dharmī sa dṛṣṭakartṛkatvān na tāvat siṣādhīyaṣiteśvaranirvartyaḥ tasya tu kumbhakārakāryatveneśasyāsarvakartṛtvam atheśvarakartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇo ghaṭāderiṣṭaṃ tatsādhyabhraṣṭo dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratītibādhaśca // MrgTV_1,3.1:24
children.translated_text: But in this inference, the very pot and the like that constitute the subject of the example, since their maker is observed, are not sought to be proved as made by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord); and since [the pot] is an effect of the potter, [this would prove] that <s>Īśvara</s> is not the maker of all. Alternatively, if the pot and the like in the example are accepted as made by <s>Īśvara</s>, the example fails its intended proof, and there is a contradiction of cognition.

children.text: * na hi ghaṭādikam arthaṃ kulālādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyinam īśvarakartṛkatvena kaścid apyavaiti // MrgTV_1,3.1:25
children.translated_text: For no one at all cognizes pots and the like, which conform to the positive and negative concomitance of potters and the like, as being made by <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: * viruddhaścāyaṃ hetuḥ yādṛśo hi ghaṭādeḥ kartā kulālādiḥ kleśādibhāg anīśo vinaśvaraśca tādṛk jagato'pi kartā prāpnoti // MrgTV_1,3.1:26
children.translated_text: And this reason is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), for whatever kind of maker the potter and the like is for pots — subject to afflictions, non-lordly, and perishable — such a maker would follow for the world as well.

children.text: * tad uktaṃ jaiminīyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the followers of <s>Jaimini</s> have said:

children.text: * kumbhakārādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ ghaṭādau yadi ceṣyate /
children.translated_text: 'If the superintendence of a potter and the like is accepted for pots and the like,

children.text: * neśvarādhiṣṭhitatvaṃ syād asti cet sādhyahīnatā // MrgTV_1,3.1:27
children.translated_text: then the superintendence of <s>Īśvara</s> would not follow; and if it is [accepted], the intended proof is lost.'

children.text: * tathā siddhe ca dṛṣṭānte bhaveddhetor viruddhatā /
children.translated_text: 'And if [<s>Īśvara</s>'s superintendence] is established in the example, the reason becomes contradictory;

children.text: * anīśvaravināśyādikartṛkatvaṃ prasajyate // MrgTV_1,3.1:28
children.translated_text: the consequence would be that the maker is non-lordly, perishable, and the like.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.1:29
children.translated_text: Thus [say the <s>Jaiminīyas</s>].

children.text: * syād eṣa sarvadoṣāvakāśo yady asmābhir asarvaviṣayam īśvarādhiṣṭhānam upagamyate yāvatā ye 'pi tu kumbhādīnāṃ kartāraḥ kulālādayas te 'pi tatpratyavekṣaṇānugṛhītaśaktayas tattatkāryanirvartanasamarthā bhavantīti brūmaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:30
children.translated_text: There would be scope for all these defects if we accepted that <s>Īśvara</s>'s superintendence does not extend to all domains. But in fact, we maintain that even the makers of pots and the like — the potters and the rest — become capable of producing their respective effects only because their powers have been graced by his supervision.

children.text: * nanu kutraitat dṛṣṭaṃ yat kulālatantuvāyādisadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvād api ghaṭādi kāryajātam īśvarādhiṣṭhitamiti // MrgTV_1,3.1:31
children.translated_text: But where has this been seen — that even pots and other produced things are superintended by <s>Īśvara</s>, just because they exist when potters and weavers are present and do not exist when they are absent?

children.text: * kutra vā na dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ na śrutaṃ bhagavatā svayam ādiṣṭaṃ sarvajanaprasiddheṣvapi śāstreṣūddhuṣyamāṇaṃ bhavadbhiḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:32
children.translated_text: Where indeed has it not been seen? Have you not heard what the Blessed Lord himself has declared, what is proclaimed even in the scriptures well-known to all people?

children.text: * gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā /
children.translated_text: 'Having entered the earth, I sustain all beings by my power,

children.text: * puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:33
children.translated_text: and I nourish all plants, having become <s>Soma</s> (the moon), whose essence is sap.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.1:34
children.translated_text: Thus [says the Blessed Lord].

children.text: * na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram // MrgTV_1,3.1:35
children.translated_text: 'There is no moving or non-moving being that could exist without me.'

children.text: * iti śrutāv api // MrgTV_1,3.1:36
children.translated_text: And in <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) also:

children.text: * yo rudro 'gnau yo 'psu ya oṣadhīṣu yo rudro viśvā bhuvanāviveśa /
children.translated_text: '<s>Rudra</s>, who is in fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants — <s>Rudra</s>, who has entered all the worlds.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.1:37
children.translated_text: Thus [says the <s>Śruti</s>].

children.text: * ata eva bhavadudbhāvitaḥ pratītivirodho'pi nirastaḥ ajño janturanīśo'yamātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:38
children.translated_text: Therefore the contradiction of cognition raised by you is also refuted: 'The ignorant creature, powerless over its own pleasure and pain,

children.text: * īśvaraprerito gacchetsvargaṃ vā śvabhrameva vā // MrgTV_1,3.1:39
children.translated_text: impelled by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), goes to heaven or to a dog's den' —

children.text: * ityevaṃvidhāyāḥ pratyuta pratīteḥ siddhatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:40
children.translated_text: because such a cognition is in fact well established.

children.text: * na cāyaṃ viruddho hetur viparyayavyāptyabhāvāt dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi ghaṭādau svasādhyena buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvena vyāpteḥ siddhatvāt buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvavirahiṇo vipakṣād ātmāder vyāvṛttatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:41
children.translated_text: Nor is this a contradictory reason (<s>viruddha hetu</s>), because there is no reverse pervasion — since in the example-subject, pots and the like, the pervasion with its own intended proof, namely being preceded by an intelligent maker, is established; and because it is excluded from the counter-instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>), namely the <s>ātman</s> and the like, which are devoid of being preceded by an intelligent maker.

children.text: * sa viruddha ucyate yaḥ sapakṣanivṛtto'pi vipakṣameva vyāpnoti yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāditi // MrgTV_1,3.1:42
children.translated_text: That is called 'contradictory' (<s>viruddha</s>) which, even though excluded from the positive instances (<s>sapakṣa</s>), pervades only the negative instances (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — as in [the fallacious argument] 'sound is eternal, because it is produced.'

children.text: * buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvaṃ ca ghaṭasya kumbhakārakāryatvāt siddhamiti kā sādhyabhraṣṭatā // MrgTV_1,3.1:43
children.translated_text: And that a pot is preceded by an intelligent maker is established because it is an effect of the potter — so what deviation from the proposition is there?

children.text: * na ca sarva eva dṛṣṭāntadharmāḥ sādhyadharmiṇi kvāpyanumāne bhavanti yenānīśvaravināśyādikartṛkatvaprasaṅgaḥ syāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:44
children.translated_text: Nor do all properties of the example necessarily apply to the subject of the inference, so that there should be the undesirable consequence of the maker being non-divine, perishable, and so forth.

children.text: * tathā hi nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvāt ghaṭādivad ityatrāpi śabdasya kumbhakārakāryatvarauhityapārivartulyādayo ghaṭadharmāḥ kimiti na bhavantīti bhavadbhirvaktavyamiti na kiṃcidetat // MrgTV_1,3.1:45
children.translated_text: For instance, in the inference 'Sound is eternal because it is produced, like a pot' — why do not the properties of the pot such as being the effect of a potter, being red, being round, and so forth, also apply to sound? You must answer this. Therefore this [objection] amounts to nothing.

children.text: * nanvete kāryatvasaṃniveśādimattvādayo hetavaḥ kāryasyānekakartṛtāmapi sādhayantīti dharmisvarūpaviparītasādhanatvād viruddhāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:46
children.translated_text: Now, [if it is argued that] these reasons — being an effect, possessing arrangement, and the like — also establish the multiplicity of makers for the effect, and hence are contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) because they prove what is contrary to the nature of the subject —

children.text: * tathā ca maṇḍanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Maṇḍana</s> [says]:

children.text: * saṃniveśādimat sarvaṃ buddhimaddhetumadyadi /
children.translated_text: 'If everything possessing arrangement and the like has an intelligent cause,

children.text: * prasiddhasaṃniveśāder ekakāraṇatā kutaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:47
children.translated_text: how can there be a single cause for well-known arrangements?'

children.text: * rathādyavayavā nānātakṣanirmāpitā api /
children.translated_text: 'The parts of a chariot and the like, though fashioned by various carpenters,

children.text: * dṛśyante jagati prāya upakāryopakārakāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:48
children.translated_text: are seen in the world to be generally mutually supportive and supported.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.1:49
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * tad apyayuktaṃ rathādīnāṃ kāryāṇām anekatakṣaviracitānāmapi ekasthapatīcchānuvartanaṃ vinā niṣpattyadarśanāt // MrgTV_1,3.1:50
children.translated_text: That too is improper, because even effects like chariots and the like, though constructed by many carpenters, are not seen to be completed without following the will of a single master architect.

children.text: * tadevaṃ kāryatvahetunā jagato buddhimatkartṛpūrvakatvasiddhau yo 'sau tattadvaicitryasaṃpādikecchājñānakriyāśaktiyuktaḥ kartā sa ity asmadādikāryavilakṣaṇakṣityādikāryaviśeṣajanakakāraṇaviśeṣāvagamo yuktaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.1:51
children.translated_text: Thus, when it is established through the reason of being an effect that the world is preceded by an intelligent maker, that maker who possesses the powers of will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>) that accomplish the respective variety — the understanding of a special cause that produces the special effects of earth and the like, which are distinct from effects like ours, is proper.

children.text: * na caitad aprasiddhaṃ yasmādvaiśiṣṭyaṃ kāryavaiśiṣṭyād dṛṣṭaṃ lokasthitāv api lokavyavahāre'pi viśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśiṣṭameva kāraṇam anumīyate yayā vicitrabhāvanādivastucitralepādikalākalāpasyāmukhyatāṃ madhyatvam anupamasaundaryasampadaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tattatkarturapi tadgatavailakṣaṇyād vaiśiṣṭyamavasīyate // MrgTV_1,3.1:52
children.translated_text: And this is not unknown, because the distinctness [of the cause] is observed from the distinctness of the effect, even in ordinary experience. In worldly practice too, upon seeing a distinguished effect, one infers a distinguished cause indeed — for when one sees that a variegated mural painting or the like, a manifold collection of arts, possesses non-ordinariness, mediocrity, or incomparable beauty and richness, one determines the distinctness of the respective maker too, from the distinctness inherent in his work.

children.text: * ataśca // MrgTV_1,3.1:53
children.translated_text: And therefore:

children.text: yadyathā yādṛśaṃ yāvatkāryaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Whatever effect, in whatever manner, of whatever kind, and of whatever extent — its cause is likewise.

children.text: * yat kāryaṃ dhūmādi yatheti yena prakāreṇa giriguhāgatatvena tadutsaṅgavartitayā tadaparapārśvavartitvena copalabdhaṃ yādṛśaṃ ca tārṇapārṇādinā svarūpeṇa viśiṣṭaṃ yāvatparimāṇaṃ tanutararekhākāram ambudanivahabahalaṃ vā tatkāraṇaṃ vahnilakṣaṇaṃ tatheti parvatotsaṅgasthaṃ vā tacchikharaniviṣṭaṃ vā tatpaścādbhāgagataṃ vā tādṛśaṃ ca tāvat pramāṇakaṃ vālpatvabahutvena yathānumīyate // MrgTV_1,3.2ab:1
children.translated_text: Whatever effect, such as smoke and the like — in whatever manner it is observed, such as being within a mountain cave, on its lap, or on its other side — and of whatever kind, that is, distinguished by its own form as being of grass, leaves, and the like — and of whatever extent, in the shape of a thin streak or dense like a mass of rain clouds — its cause, characterized as fire, is inferred likewise: as being situated on the mountain's lap, or on its peak, or behind it; and of such a kind; and of such measure, inferred according to its smallness or abundance.

children.text: * evaṃ jagallakṣaṇakāryasya tattatprakārākāravaicitryam upalabhya tattadviśeṣaviṣayaniratiśayajñānakriyāśaktiyuktaṃ kāraṇamanumīyate // MrgTV_1,3.2ab:2
children.translated_text: Similarly, by observing the variety of manner, form, and appearance of the effect characterized as the world, a cause endowed with unsurpassed powers of knowledge and action pertaining to each respective particular is inferred.

children.text: * tac ca // MrgTV_1,3.2ab:3
children.translated_text: And that [cause]:

children.text: nityaṃ kālānavacchedād vaitatyān na pradeśagam || MrgT_1,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: is eternal, because it is not delimited by time; because of its vastness, it does not occupy a [single] location.

children.text: kramākramasamutpatteḥ kramādyutpattiśaktimat /
children.translated_text: Because of the production of [things] both in sequence and simultaneously, it possesses the power to produce [things] sequentially and so forth.

children.text: * yasyābhūtvā bhavanaṃ bhūtvā cābhavanaṃ tasya kālenāvacchedād anityatvam // MrgTV_1,3.3ab:1
children.translated_text: That whose coming-into-being after non-existence and ceasing-to-be after existence [is observed] — its non-eternality is due to delimitation by time.

children.text: * yattu pūrvāparakoṭidvayavirahāt kālānavacchinnaṃ tan nityam // MrgTV_1,3.3ab:2
children.translated_text: But that which is not delimited by time, being devoid of both prior and posterior limits, is eternal.

children.text: * kiṃ ca na tat kvacid avasthitam api tu vaitatyān mahattvād digdeśānavacchinnatvāt sarvagaṃ sarvatra tatkāryopalabdheśca vibhu tathā kramayaugapadyābhyāṃ tanukaraṇādikāryasyotpādanāt krameṇa yugapac cotpādikayā śaktyā yuktam // MrgTV_1,3.3ab:3
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is not situated in any particular place, but rather, because of its vastness (<s>vaitatya</s>), because it is not delimited by direction or location, it is all-pervading (<s>sarvagam</s>); and because its effects are perceived everywhere, it is omnipresent (<s>vibhu</s>). Likewise, because it produces effects such as making things subtle through both sequential and simultaneous [means], it is endowed with the power to produce [things] both sequentially and all at once.

children.text: * nanu jagatsṛṣṭisthityādikā tatkriyā nākaraṇikā kriyātvāt chidikriyāvat atastasyāpi karaṇena bhavitavyamityāha // MrgTV_1,3.3ab:4
children.translated_text: Now, if [it is objected that] his activity of creation, maintenance, and so forth of the world is not without an instrument, because it is an activity, like the activity of cutting — therefore he too must have an instrument — to this he says:

children.text: tasyāsti karaṇaṃ yena dṛṣṭā nākaraṇā kṛtiḥ || MrgT_1,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: He has an instrument, for no action is seen to be without an instrument.

children.text: anāgāmi ca taj jñeyaṃ kāryasyānādisaṃsthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [instrument] should be known as not having come into being [separately], because the effect [of creation] has been established from beginningless time.

children.text: * yasmādakaraṇikā kriyā na sambhavati atastasya bhagavataḥ kimapyavaśyaṃ karaṇamasti // MrgTV_1,3.4ab:1
children.translated_text: Since action without an instrument is not possible, that Blessed One necessarily has some instrument.

children.text: * tac ca kṛtyasya sargāder anāditvenāvasthānād anāgāmi anāgantukam // MrgTV_1,3.4ab:2
children.translated_text: And that [instrument], because the activity of creation and the like has existed from beginningless time, is <s>anāgāmi</s> (not newly arrived), that is, it has not come from outside.

children.text: * atha kiṃ tatkaraṇamityucyate // MrgTV_1,3.4ab:3
children.translated_text: Now, what is that instrument? It is said:

children.text: karaṇaṃ ca na śaktyanyac chaktirnācetanā citaḥ || MrgT_1,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: And the instrument is nothing other than <s>Śakti</s> (power); and the <s>Śakti</s> of the conscious one is not unconscious.

children.text: * śaktirevāsya viśveśituḥ karaṇaṃ tayaitatkriyāniṣpādanāt sā cec chādirūpeti vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.4cd:1
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s> (power) alone is the instrument of this Lord of the universe, because this activity is accomplished by her. And she has the form of will (<s>icchā</s>) and the like — this we shall explain.

children.text: * uktaṃ ca śrīmatkiraṇe // MrgTV_1,3.4cd:2
children.translated_text: And it has been said in the glorious <s>Kiraṇāgama</s>:

children.text: * icchaiva karaṇaṃ tasya yathā sadyogino matā /
children.translated_text: 'Will (<s>icchā</s>) alone is regarded as his instrument, just as for the accomplished <s>yogin</s> (<s>sadyogin</s>).'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.4cd:3
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * śaktiśca cetanarūpā nahi citsvabhāvasyācidrūpā śaktirbhavati // MrgTV_1,3.4cd:4
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śakti</s> (power) has the nature of consciousness; for one whose nature is consciousness (<s>cit</s>) cannot have a power that is devoid of consciousness.

children.text: * yac caitac chaktyātmakaṃ karaṇam // MrgTV_1,3.4cd:5
children.translated_text: And this instrument, whose nature is <s>Śakti</s> (power) —

children.text: viṣayāniyamādekaṃ bodhe kṛtye ca tattathā /
children.translated_text: is one, because of the unlimitedness of its objects, in both knowledge and action, and likewise [in other respects].

children.text: * yasya jñeyānāṃ karaṇīyānāṃ cānantyaṃ tasya karaṇair apyanantair bhavitavyam // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:1
children.translated_text: For one whose objects of knowledge and objects of action are infinite, the instruments too must be infinite.

children.text: * aparimitaviṣayaṃ ca parameśvarasya jñānaṃ kṛtyaṃ ca // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:2
children.translated_text: And the knowledge and action of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) are of unlimited scope.

children.text: * yad vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: As he will state:

children.text: * śāṃkaram jñānam // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:3
children.translated_text: 'The knowledge of <s>Śaṅkara</s>' —

children.text: * iti prakramya /
children.translated_text: beginning thus, [and then]:

children.text: * tad ekaṃ viṣayānantyād bhedānantyaṃ prapadyate /
children.translated_text: 'That one [knowledge], because of the infinity of objects, attains infinite divisions;

children.text: * kartṛtvaṃ tadabhinnatvāt tadvad evopacārataḥ // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:4
children.translated_text: agency, because of its non-difference from that [knowledge], is likewise figuratively [spoken of in the same way].'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:5
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * tasmādviṣayasya jñeyasya karaṇīyasya cāniyatatvād anavacchinnatvād ekamapi tacchaktirūpaṃ karaṇaṃ bodhaviṣaye kṛtyaviṣaye ca tathetyanavacchinnam anantam evetyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:6
children.translated_text: Therefore, because the object — what is to be known and what is to be done — is unlimited and unbounded, even the single instrument in the form of <s>Śakti</s> is likewise unlimited and infinite in the domain of knowledge and in the domain of action — this is the meaning.

children.text: * atha matāntaraniranubhāṣaṇeneśvarāstitvam eva draḍhayati // MrgTV_1,3.5ab:7
children.translated_text: Now, by not engaging with alternative doctrines, he firmly establishes the very existence of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord):

children.text: kāryaṃ na sthitijanmādi bījasya prakṛteraṇoḥ || MrgT_1,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: The effect — maintenance, creation, and so forth — is not [the work] of a seed, of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), or of the soul (<s>aṇu</s>).

children.text: pāriśeṣyān maheśasya muktasya śiva eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: By the method of elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), it belongs to <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord); for the liberated one, he is <s>Śiva</s> himself.

children.text: * nanu kimatra karaṇāpekṣeṇeśvareṇa kalpitena tasmin karmanairapekṣyeṇa kartṛtvānabhyupagamāt taccaritāni karmāṇyeva sṛṣṭisthityādikāraṇatayā bhavantviti jaiminīyāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:1
children.translated_text: Now, [the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> (Mīmāṃsakas) say:] what need is there for an imagined Lord who requires an instrument? Since we do not accept agency for him and he is independent of <s>karma</s> (action), let <s>karmas</s> (ritual actions) themselves, following their own course, be the cause of creation, maintenance, and so forth of all beings.

children.text: * yadāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: * kasyaciddhetumātrasya yadyadhiṣṭhātṛteṣyate /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever presiding agency is desired for any mere cause,

children.text: * karmabhiḥ sarvajīvānāṃ tatsiddheḥ siddhasādhanam // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:2
children.translated_text: that is already accomplished by the <s>karmas</s> of all beings — hence it is proving what is already proven.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:3
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * yadvā bījam ivāṅkurādīnāṃ kalādikāryāṇām upādānaṃ māyaivānyānapekṣiṇī sṛṣṭyādikṛd bhavatu prakṛtireva vāvyaktā etatkartṛtve nāstu yāṃ vinā tasyeśvarasyāpi tatkāryāniṣpattir upalabhyate kṣityādyātmanā pārārthyapravṛttā anyānapekṣiṇī prakṛtireva ataḥ kim īśvareṇeti kāpilāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:4
children.translated_text: Or else, just as a seed is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of sprouts and the like, let <s>Māyā</s> alone, requiring nothing else, be the agent of creation and so forth for the effects beginning with <s>Kalā</s>; or let the unmanifest <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) itself [be the cause] — for its agency there is nothing without which the Lord too could not accomplish those effects; <s>Prakṛti</s>, operating for the sake of others, requiring nothing else, in the form of earth and the like — therefore what need is there for a Lord? — thus say the followers of <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: * tathā hi /
children.translated_text: For instance:

children.text: * yad yathā pariṇāmaikasvabhāvaṃ tatra tat tataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever has transformation as its sole nature — with respect to that, from that,

children.text: * anyānapekṣi bījādisāmagrī yadvad aṅkure // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:5
children.translated_text: independently of anything else, like the aggregate of seed and the like in [producing] a sprout.'

children.text: * mahadādivikāraughapariṇāmasvabhāvakam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), whose nature is the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), has the nature of transformation into the host of modifications beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) and <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego);

children.text: * triguṇātma pradhānaṃ ca tena sāṃkhyam anīśvaram // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:6
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [is] without a Lord (<s>anīśvara</s>).'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:7
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * yadi vā puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yadbhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyam // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:8
children.translated_text: Or else, '<s>Puruṣa</s> (the cosmic person) alone is all this — whatever has been and whatever will be' —

children.text: * iti aṇoḥ puruṣād eva vivartatayā cidacillakṣaṇaviśvaprādurbhāvādi bhaviṣyati kimīśvareṇeti // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:9
children.translated_text: thus, from the soul (<s>aṇu</s>), from <s>Puruṣa</s> alone, through transformation (<s>vivarta</s>), the manifestation and so forth of the universe characterized as conscious and unconscious will come about — so what need is there for a Lord?

children.text: * tadasad bahirbījabhūtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ māyādīnāṃ cācetanānāṃ buddhimadadhiṣṭhitānāṃ sṛṣṭyādi kṛtyam upapannam ityuktatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:10
children.translated_text: That is wrong, because it has already been stated that the activity of creation and so forth is proper for <s>karmas</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, and the like — which are external seeds, unconscious, and presided over by an intelligent being.

children.text: * prakṛterapyautsukyanivṛttyarthaṃ kāryeṣu pravṛttir nitarāmayuktā tasyā ācaitanyād autsukyasya ca cetanadharmatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:11
children.translated_text: And even for <s>Prakṛti</s>, engagement in effects for the purpose of removing restlessness is entirely improper, because she is unconscious and because restlessness is a property of conscious beings.

children.text: * puruṣasyāpi pariṇāmitvādyanekadoṣopanipātāt svatantrasya cābhirucitahāner aniṣṭopanipātasya cānupapatter asvavaśatvāt sthitijanmapralayakartṛtvanirāse sati pāriśeṣyān maheśvarasyaivaitat sthitijanmādi kāryamiti pāriśeṣyānumānam anavadyamiti gamakametat // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:12
children.translated_text: And for <s>Puruṣa</s> too, because of the occurrence of many defects such as being subject to transformation, and because for an independent being the loss of what is desired and the occurrence of what is undesired are impossible, and because [the soul in bondage is] not under its own control — when the agency of maintenance, creation, and dissolution has been negated [for all these], by the method of elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), this activity of maintenance, creation, and so forth belongs to <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) alone — thus the inference by elimination is flawless. This is the demonstration.

children.text: * idamidānīṃ vivicyate yadi tāvat parameśvaraḥ kāruṇyāt saṃsārijanojjihīrṣayā jagatāṃ sthitijanmādau pravartate tatkimarthaṃ pratyuta sāṃsārikeṣu duḥkheṣu varākānimān prāṇino niyojayati atha tasyaivaṃvidha eva svabhāvaḥ tanmuktamapi jantuṃ kiṃ na saṃsārayatītyāha muktasya śiva eva saḥ satyaṃ kāruṇyādeva bhagavān prāṇino'nugrahītuṃ pravartate // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:13
children.translated_text: Now this is examined: if <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), out of compassion, with the desire to rescue those in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), engages in the maintenance, creation, and so forth of the worlds, then why does he rather subject these wretched beings to the sufferings of worldly existence? And if such is indeed his nature, then would he not subject even a liberated being to <s>saṃsāra</s> again? To this he says: 'For the liberated one, he is <s>Śiva</s> himself.' Truly, it is out of compassion alone that the Blessed One engages in bestowing grace upon beings.

children.text: * yattu duḥkhamohādinā nirayādyupabhogena vā tān saṃyojayati tannijakarmānurūpyavaśāt // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:14
children.translated_text: But the fact that he connects them with suffering, delusion, and the like, or with experiences in hells and such — that is due to the force of their own respective <s>karmas</s>.

children.text: * na ca karmāpekṣitayeśvarasya svātantryahānir ityāśaṅkanīyaṃ karaṇāpekṣayā kartuḥ svātantryavyāghātādarśanāt bhāṇḍāgārikāpekṣasya rājñaḥ prasādādidānavat // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:15
children.translated_text: Nor should it be suspected that the Lord's independence is diminished by his dependence on <s>karma</s>, since we do not see that the independence of an agent is contradicted by his dependence on an instrument — just as a king's bestowal of rewards and the like is not contradicted by his dependence on a treasurer.

children.text: * yaduktaṃ siddhagurubhiḥ // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:16
children.translated_text: As the accomplished masters (<s>siddhagurus</s>) have said:

children.text: * svatantrānyāprayojyatvaṃ karaṇādiprayoktṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'Not being directed by others who are independent, and being the director of instruments and the like —

children.text: * kartuḥ svātantryametaddhi na karmādyanapekṣitā // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:17
children.translated_text: this is the independence of the agent; it is not the non-dependence on <s>karma</s> and the like.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:18
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * na cābhuktasya karmaṇaḥ kṣayo bhavati // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:19
children.translated_text: And there is no destruction of <s>karma</s> that has not been experienced.

children.text: * tattadyoniśarīropabhogabhuktavicitrakarmakṣayatas tatsāmyād vā atyutkaṭamalaparipākavaśapravṛttaśaktipātāpasāritamalasyāvāptānugrahasya jantor nirastasamastapāśatvādāvirbhūtasarvārthatattvakartṛkasya muktātmanaḥ saṃsāryatāhetoḥ paśutvasyābhāvāc chivasvarūpa eva bhagavān bhavati na tu paśorivāsya kutsitabhavabhogopabhogahetur bhavatīti bhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:20
children.translated_text: When, through the exhaustion of varied <s>karmas</s> experienced through bodily enjoyment in various wombs, or through the equilibrium of those [karmas], or through the removal of impurity (<s>mala</s>) by the descent of <s>Śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>) occurring due to the extreme ripening of impurity — the being that has attained grace, whose entirety of bonds has been removed, and whose capacity for seeing and acting upon all things has become manifest — for such a liberated soul (<s>muktātman</s>), since the animality (<s>paśutva</s>) that is the cause of worldly existence is absent, the Blessed One becomes of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> himself; he does not become the cause of vile worldly enjoyment as for a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) — this is the purport.

children.text: * punar apīśvarakartṛkatvam eva jagato ghaṭayitum anumānaṃ pratisamādhātum ākṣipati // MrgTV_1,3.6ab:21
children.translated_text: Again, in order to establish that the world is indeed made by the Lord, he raises [an objection] to resolve it through inference:

children.text: sambandhāgrahaṇe bādhā mānasyābhyeti kasyacit || MrgT_1,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: If the relation [between the world and its maker] is not apprehended, the invalidation of some [person's] means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>) results.

children.text: * nanv asya sthitijanmādeḥ kāryasyāvinābhāvalakṣaṇasambandho yadi kadācij jagatkartrā saha kenacidapi gṛhītaḥ syāt tadaitad anumānaṃ sidhyet sambandhasyaiva tu agrahaṇāt kathaṃ nāsya bādheti yadi kasyacin mataṃ syāt tadidam apyasau pratyanuyojya ityāha // MrgTV_1,3.6cd:1
children.translated_text: Now, if the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) — the relation of this effect of maintenance, creation, and so forth — with some maker of the world had ever been apprehended by anyone, then this inference would succeed. But since the relation itself has not been apprehended, how is there no invalidation [of the inference]? If this should be someone's view, then he too should be questioned thus — so he says:

children.text: sā parasyāpi dhūmo'nyo girau māhānasādyataḥ /
children.translated_text: That [invalidation] applies to the opponent as well; smoke [seen] on a mountain is different from that [smoke] from a kitchen and the like.

children.text: * saiṣā bādhā sarvasyāpy anumānavādinaḥ prasaktā // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:1
children.translated_text: This very invalidation applies to every proponent of inference as well.

children.text: * tathā hi mahānasādigatānāṃ viśiṣṭadeśakālākārāṇām eva dhūmāgnivyaktīnāṃ sambandhagrahaṇe dhūmamātrāc ca parvatādau vahnimātrānumānam ityagṛhītasambandhaiva dhūmavyaktiḥ kathaṃ tathāvidhavahnivyaktiṃ gamayediti sambandhagrahaparyanuyogaḥ samānaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:2
children.translated_text: For consider: when the relation between specific instances of smoke and fire — possessing particular place, time, and form — located in kitchens and the like has been apprehended, and yet from mere smoke on a mountain and the like, mere fire is inferred — then a particular instance of smoke whose relation [with that particular fire] has not been apprehended, how could it lead to the knowledge of such a particular instance of fire? Thus the challenge regarding the apprehension of the relation is equally [applicable to the opponent].

children.text: * tataśca /
children.translated_text: And therefore:

children.text: * yatra syād ubhayordoṣaḥ parihāraśca vā samaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the defect or its resolution would be the same for both parties,

children.text: * naikaḥ paryanuyoktavyas tādṛgarthaviniścaye // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:3
children.translated_text: one should not challenge only one side in determining such a matter.

children.text: * iti naitad asmākameva codyam // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:4
children.translated_text: Thus this objection is not directed against us alone.

children.text: * atha dhūmamātrasyaiva vahnimātrāvinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ sambandho gṛhītaḥ tad ihāpi kāryamātrāt kartṛmātrānumānamaduṣṭam // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:5
children.translated_text: Now, if the relation characterized by the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) of mere smoke with mere fire has been apprehended, then here too the inference of a mere agent from a mere effect is not faulty.

children.text: * anyathā sarvānumānoccheda eva syāt // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:6
children.translated_text: Otherwise, there would be the annulment of all inference whatsoever.

children.text: * taduktam /
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said:

children.text: * sādhyasādhanasāmānyenāvinābhāvaniścayāt /
children.translated_text: From the ascertainment of the invariable concomitance through the universals of what is to be proved and the means of proof,

children.text: * pravṛttiranumānasya tadabhāvas tadanyathā // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:7
children.translated_text: inference operates; in the absence of that [invariable concomitance], it is otherwise [i.e., it does not operate].

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:8
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * itthaṃ ca vicitratattatkarmāśayādhivāsitabhoktṛbhogatatsādhanatadupādānādiviśeṣajñaḥ kartā anumānāntareṇānumīyata iti na kaściddoṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:9
children.translated_text: And in this way, a maker who knows the specific details of the varied <s>karmas</s> accumulated by each experiencer, their enjoyments, the means thereof, the material causes, and so forth, is inferred through another inference — and so there is no defect.

children.text: * tadidam uktaṃ tatrabhavadbṛhaspatipādaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This has been stated by the revered <s>Bṛhaspati</s>:

children.text: * bhavabhoktṛbhogasādhanatadupādānādi yo vijānāti /
children.translated_text: He who knows the experiencers of worldly existence, their enjoyments, the means thereof, and the material causes and the like —

children.text: * tamṛte bhaven nahīdaṃ puṃskarmāśayavipākajñam // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:10
children.translated_text: without him, this [world] would not exist, [for it requires] one who knows the ripening of the <s>karma</s>-dispositions of individual souls.

children.text: * iti astu tarhi īśvaraḥ kartā sa tu na tāvadaśarīraḥ pratyetavyaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:11
children.translated_text: Let it be granted then that the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is the maker; but he should not be conceived of as bodiless.

children.text: * kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptaṃ sadaiva yat // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:12
children.translated_text: For an effect is always pervaded by an agent who possesses a body —

children.text: * ityādinā dehavirahiṇaḥ kartṛtvāyogasyoktatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:13
children.translated_text: thus, because the impossibility of agency for one devoid of a body has been stated by such [reasoning].

children.text: * tathāhi // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:14
children.translated_text: For consider:

children.text: * ghaṭapaṭādi kāryaṃ śarīravataiva kriyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nāśarīreṇeti // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:1
children.translated_text: An effect such as a pot or cloth is seen to be produced only by one possessing a body, and not by one who is bodiless.

children.text: * kiṃcātaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.7ab:2
children.translated_text: What follows from this?

children.text: loke vapuṣmato dṛṣṭaṃ kṛtyaṃ so 'py asmadādivat || MrgT_1,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: In the world, activity is seen [to be performed] by one who has a body; therefore he (<s>Īśvara</s>) too [must be] like us.

children.text: * evaṃ ca sati asmadādivatkleśādiyukto'sarvajñaḥ parimitaśaktir deśādyavacchinnaḥ so 'pīśvaraḥ śarīritvāt prāpnotīti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.7cd:1
children.translated_text: And this being so, the prior position [of the opponent] is: like us, the Lord too, being embodied, would be endowed with afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and the like, non-omniscient, of limited power, and delimited by place and the like.

children.text: * siddhāntastu // MrgTV_1,3.7cd:2
children.translated_text: But the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>) is:

children.text: mūlādyasaṃbhavāc chāktaṃ vapur nas tādṛśaṃ prabhoḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of a root [impurity] and the rest, the body of the Lord is of the nature of <s>śakti</s> (power) — not like ours.

children.text: * aśarīrasyāpi tāvat svadehaspandādau kartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭamiti // MrgTV_1,3.8ab:1
children.translated_text: For even one who is bodiless is seen to have agency in the movement and the like of one's own body.

children.text: * kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptam ity uktam abhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ śarīravattve'pi bhagavato na prāguktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.8ab:2
children.translated_text: Even accepting what was said — 'an effect is pervaded by an agent who possesses a body' — we say: even if the Blessed One possesses a body, the previously stated defects do not follow.

children.text: * kuta ityāha mūlādyasaṃbhavād iti mūlaṃ malaḥ sarvānarthamūlatvāt avidyāvṛtirugglānipāpamūlakṣayādibhiḥ paryāyair vakṣyamāṇatvāc ca ādigrahaṇāt karmāṇi rodhaśaktiśca tadasaṃbhavāt // MrgTV_1,3.8ab:3
children.translated_text: Why? He says: 'Because of the impossibility of a root [impurity] and the rest' — the root is <s>mala</s> (impurity), because it is the root of all calamity, and because it will be described through synonyms such as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), disposition (<s>vṛti</s>), affliction (<s>ruk</s>), weakness (<s>glāni</s>), sin (<s>pāpa</s>), the root, decay (<s>kṣaya</s>), and so forth. By the word 'ādi' (and the rest), <s>karmas</s> and the obstructing power (<s>rodhaśakti</s>) [are included]. Because of the impossibility of these [for the Lord].

children.text: * na hi parameśvarasya malakarmādi pāśajālaṃ sambhavati yannimittaṃ prākṛtaṃ vapuḥ kalpyate api tu śāktamiti śaktisvarūpaiḥ sadyojātādibhiḥ pañcabhirmantraiḥ svecchāvinirmitamaparimitasāmarthyam adigdeśakālākāravyavacchinnam anupamamahima taccharīraṃ na tv asmadādiśarīrasadṛśam // MrgTV_1,3.8ab:4
children.translated_text: For <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) does not have the web of bonds consisting of <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s>, and so forth, on account of which a material body would be conceived. Rather, [his body] is of the nature of <s>śakti</s> (power) — fashioned by his own will through the five <s>mantras</s> whose essence is power, beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>, of unlimited capability, not delimited by place, time, or form, of incomparable majesty — that is his body, and not one resembling the bodies of beings like us.

children.text: * ata eva hi // MrgTV_1,3.8ab:5
children.translated_text: And for this very reason:

children.text: tadvapuḥ pañcabhirmantraiḥ pañcakṛtyopayogibhiḥ || MrgT_1,3.8 ||
children.translated_text: That body [of the Lord is constituted] by five <s>mantras</s> that serve the fivefold activity (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) —

children.text: īśatatpuruṣāghoravāmājair mastakādikam /
children.translated_text: from <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Sadyojāta</s> arise the head and the rest.

children.text: * yathākramam anugrahatirobhāvādānarakṣaṇotpattilakṣaṇakṛtyapañcake 'vaśyam upayogo yeṣāṃ tair īśānādibhiḥ pañcabhir mantraistat mūrdhādi vapuḥ devasyocyate ityadhyāhāraḥ // MrgTV_1,3.9ab:1
children.translated_text: The five <s>mantras</s> beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>, whose use is indispensable in the fivefold activity characterized respectively by grace (<s>anugraha</s>), concealment (<s>tirobhāva</s>), absorption (<s>ādāna</s>), preservation (<s>rakṣaṇa</s>), and creation (<s>utpatti</s>) — by these, the body of the Lord, beginning with the head, is spoken of. This is to be supplied.

children.text: * varaiḥpuṣṇāti dhyāyinaḥ iti vapuḥśabdasyānvarthatā bhaktānugrahaṇāya tattadākāragrahaṇasyāgameṣūpadiṣṭatvāt // MrgTV_1,3.9ab:2
children.translated_text: The etymological aptness of the word <s>vapus</s> (body) is: 'he nourishes (<s>puṣṇāti</s>) the meditators with boons' — because the assumption of various forms for the grace of devotees is taught in the <s>āgamas</s>.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s>:

children.text: * sādhakasya tu lakṣyārthaṃ tasya rūpamidaṃ smṛtam iti // MrgTV_1,3.9ab:3
children.translated_text: 'This form of his is taught for the purpose of being the object of meditation for the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>).'

children.text: * atha kathaṃ bhagavata īśānamūrdhatvam ityāha // MrgTV_1,3.9ab:4
children.translated_text: Now, how is <s>Īśāna</s> the head of the Blessed One? He says:

children.text: īṣṭe yena jagatsarvaṃ guṇenoparivartinā || MrgT_1,3.9 ||
children.translated_text: By which quality, which is supreme, the entire universe is ruled (<s>īṣṭe</s>) —

children.text: sa mūrdhasamadeśatvānmūrdhā nāvayavastanoḥ /
children.translated_text: that, being in a position analogous to the head, is the head — not a bodily limb.

children.text: * yena guṇena mantreṇa sarvasroto'nusrotasā mūrdhvasthitatvāt sarvānugrahahetutvādvā uparivartinā jagaccidacidātmakaṃ viśvamīṣṭe sa uttamāṅgavat sarvordhvasthitatvān mūrdheva mūrdhā na paramārthato dehāvayavaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.10ab:1
children.translated_text: By which quality — that is, by which <s>mantra</s> — which, being situated above all channels flowing downward, or because it is the cause of grace for all, is supreme — by that, the entire universe consisting of the sentient and the insentient is ruled. That, being situated above everything like the head, is the head as it were — not in ultimate reality a limb of [a physical] body.

children.text: * tatpuruṣavaktraṃ vyācaṣṭe // MrgTV_1,3.10ab:2
children.translated_text: He explains the face of <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>:

children.text: tasya tasya tanuryā pūs tasyām uṣati yena saḥ || MrgT_1,3.10 ||
children.translated_text: Of each and every being, that which is the city (<s>pūḥ</s>), the body — in which he dwells — he is

children.text: tattrāṇād vyañjanāc cāpi sa tatpuruṣavaktrakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> (that Person); because he protects that and because he manifests, he is [called] the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>-face.

children.text: * tasya tasya amaranarāderyā pūḥ purī tanustasyāṃ puri yajamānasvarūpeṇādhiṣṭhānabhāvenoṣitas tatpuruṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:1
children.translated_text: Of each and every being, god, human, and the like — that which is the city (<s>pūḥ</s>), the body — in that city, he has dwelt (<s>uṣitaḥ</s>) in the form of the indwelling self (<s>yajamāna</s>) as the presiding principle — [therefore he is] <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> (that Person).

children.text: * taduktam // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:2
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said:

children.text: * svātmaivāyaṃ vasati sakalaprāṇinām īśvaro'ntaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:3
children.translated_text: 'This Lord himself, the self, dwells within all living beings.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:4
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tatpuruṣa iti yasmād vyanakti jñānakriye trāyate janmādibhayāt tatastatpuruṣavaktraḥ vyañjanatrāṇarūpatvād vaktram ityabhidhīyate // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:5
children.translated_text: <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> — because he manifests (<s>vyanakti</s>) knowledge and action, and protects (<s>trāyate</s>) from the fear of birth and the like, therefore he is the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>-face; because it has the nature of manifesting and protecting, it is called 'face' (<s>vaktra</s>).

children.text: * iti śruteḥ // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:6
children.translated_text: Thus says scripture.

children.text: * aghorahṛdayatvaṃ vaktum āha // MrgTV_1,3.11ab:7
children.translated_text: In order to state the <s>Aghora</s>-heart, he says:

children.text: hṛdayaṃ bodhaparyāyaḥ so 'sya ghoraḥ śivo yataḥ || MrgT_1,3.11 ||
children.translated_text: The heart is a synonym for understanding (<s>bodha</s>); since he is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), he is <s>Aghora</s> (non-terrible).

children.text: parigrahasya ghoratvādghoroktir upacārataḥ /
children.translated_text: The designation 'terrible' (<s>ghora</s>) is figurative, because of the terribleness of his retinue.

children.text: * hṛdayamāśayo bodha iti paryāyaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.12ab:1
children.translated_text: The heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) is the inner disposition — 'understanding' (<s>bodha</s>) is its synonym.

children.text: * śivo bodho yasmād bhagavatas tasmādaghorahṛdayaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.12ab:2
children.translated_text: Since the understanding of the Blessed One is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), therefore he is the <s>Aghora</s>-heart.

children.text: * nanu ghoram aśreyorūpaṃ yaducyate tadghorarūpatā kathaṃ devasyetyāha parigrahasya ghoratvāditi // MrgTV_1,3.12ab:3
children.translated_text: Now, that which is called terrible (<s>ghora</s>), having the form of what is inauspicious — how can such a terrible form belong to the Lord? He says: 'Because of the terribleness of his retinue.'

children.text: * yeyaṃ parameśvarasya ghorarūpoktiḥ sā na vāstavī kiṃtu parigrahasya svaśaktyuttejitasāmarthyasyāśuddhādhvādhikārinikurambasya ghoratvād ghoraśaktirdeva upacārāducyate // MrgTV_1,3.12ab:4
children.translated_text: This designation of <s>Parameśvara</s> as having a terrible (<s>ghora</s>) form is not literal, but rather, because of the terribleness of his retinue — the host of beings presiding over the impure course (<s>aśuddhādhvan</s>), whose power has been energized by his own <s>śakti</s> — the terrible power (<s>ghoraśakti</s>) is attributed to the Lord figuratively.

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said:

children.text: * viṣayeṣveva saṃlīnān adho'dhaḥ pātayanty aṇūn /
children.translated_text: 'Those [powers] which, embracing the <s>Rudra</s>-souls that are immersed in sense objects, cast them further and further down —

children.text: * rudrāṇūn yāḥ samāliṅgya ghorataryo 'parāstu tāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.12ab:5
children.translated_text: those other, most terrible ones [are his retinue].'

children.text: * vāmadevaguhyatvam abhidhatte // MrgTV_1,3.12ab:6
children.translated_text: He states the secret (<s>guhya</s>) nature of <s>Vāmadeva</s>:

children.text: vāmas trivargavāmatvād rahasyaśca svabhāvataḥ || MrgT_1,3.12 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāma</s> — because of causing the threefold aim of life (<s>trivarga</s>) to go leftward (downward); and he is secret (<s>rahasya</s>) by nature.

children.text: vāmaṃ dhāma paraṃ guhyaṃ yasyāsau vāmaguhyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose supreme abode is <s>vāma</s> (emitting downward) and secret (<s>guhya</s>) — he is <s>Vāmaguhya</s> (the Vāma-secret one).

children.text: * dharmārthakāmalakṣaṇena trivargeṇa pralobhya vamati adho nikṣipatīti vāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.13ab:1
children.translated_text: <s>Vāma</s> — because, having enticed through the threefold aim of life (<s>trivarga</s>) characterized by <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire), he emits (<s>vamati</s>), that is, casts downward.

children.text: * svabhāvena rahasyo guhyo bhāvaḥ kathyate // MrgTV_1,3.13ab:2
children.translated_text: By nature, the secret (<s>rahasya</s>), hidden (<s>guhya</s>) state is spoken of.

children.text: * itthaṃ pṛthag anayoḥ padayorarthaṃ pradarśya vigrahaṃ karoti vāmaṃ dhāmeti // MrgTV_1,3.13ab:3
children.translated_text: Having thus shown the meaning of these two words separately, he forms the compound: '<s>vāma</s> abode' —

children.text: * diverdhātor dyutyarthatvād devaśabdena tejo'bhimatam // MrgTV_1,3.13ab:4
children.translated_text: Because the verbal root <s>div</s> has the meaning of 'shining,' the word <s>deva</s> denotes splendor (<s>tejas</s>).

children.text: * tena vāmam adhastane'dhvani vamanaśīlaṃ yattejas tadguhyam aprakaṭamasyeti vāmadevaguhyaḥ parameśvaraḥ // MrgTV_1,3.13ab:5
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Parameśvara</s> is <s>Vāmaguhya</s> (the Vāma-secret one), because that splendor (<s>tejas</s>) which is <s>vāma</s>, disposed to emitting [souls] downward into the lower course, is <s>guhya</s> (hidden, not manifest) in him.

children.text: sadyo'ṇūnāṃ mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yasyecchātas tena sadyo'bhidhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: He by whose will the embodiments of souls come into being immediately — he is called <s>Sadyojāta</s> (immediately born);

children.text: sadyo mūrtīryogināṃ vā vidhatte sadyomūrtiḥ kṛtyaśaighryān na mūrteḥ || MrgT_1,3.13 ||
children.translated_text: or, he immediately produces bodies for yogins — [he is called] <s>Sadyomūrti</s> (of immediate form) because of the swiftness of action, not because of [his own] body.

children.text: * patyuricchayā hi karmaprakṣayāya kṣipramevātmanāṃ tāstā mūrtayo jātā iti sadyojātamūrtir devaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.13ef:1
children.translated_text: For by the will of the Lord, for the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, the various embodiments of souls arise swiftly — therefore the Lord is of <s>Sadyojāta</s>-form.

children.text: * yadvakṣyati dīkṣāprakaraṇe /
children.translated_text: As will be stated in the section on <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation):

children.text: * sadyena janayetsadyo nānāniṣpannavigraham /
children.translated_text: 'By <s>Sadya</s> [the mantra], he immediately generates one of manifold accomplished form.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,3.13ef:2
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * yadvā yogināṃ tattatsamādhibhājāṃ sadyastatkṣaṇaṃ mūrtīrvidhatte proktavanmantramayasvamūrtisadṛśīṃ tanuṃ sampādayatīti acirāt svaramatābhivyañjakatvāt sadyomūrtitvaṃ na tu śīghrasaṃjātasvadehatvād ityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,3.13ef:3
children.translated_text: Alternatively, for yogins who partake of various <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions), he immediately — at that very moment — produces bodies, that is, brings about a form resembling his own <s>mantra</s>-constituted body as described. The <s>Sadyomūrti</s> designation is because of the swift manifestation of his own desired [form], not because of the quick generation of his own body — this is the meaning.

children.text: * etadeva draḍhayati // MrgTV_1,3.13ef:4
children.translated_text: He reinforces this very point:

children.text: itthaṃ śaktiḥ kurvatī dehakṛtyaṃ dehābhāvāducyate dehaśabdaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>śakti</s> (power), performing the function of a body, is called by the word 'body' due to the absence of [an actual] body.

children.text: tasyā bhedā ye 'pi vāmādayaḥ syuste 'pi proktāḥ kṛtyabhedena sadbhiḥ || MrgT_1,3.14 ||
children.translated_text: And those divisions of it such as <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest — they too have been described by the wise according to the divisions of activity.

children.text: * paramārthataḥ parameśvarasyāśarīratvāc chaktireva dehakāryaṃ kurvatī dehākhyayoktā // MrgTV_1,3.14:1
children.translated_text: In ultimate reality, since <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) is bodiless, it is <s>śakti</s> (power) alone that, performing the function of a body, is designated by the name 'body.'

children.text: * tasyāścaikasyā api kṛtyabhedād vāmādibhedabhinnatvam // MrgTV_1,3.14:2
children.translated_text: And even though that [śakti] is one, it has the division into <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest due to the differences in activity.

children.text: * yathā vahniśakter dāhyaprakāśyārthaviṣaye dāhaprakāśaprakaraṇād gauṇam anekatvaṃ vastuta ekatvāt tasyāḥ // MrgTV_1,3.14:3
children.translated_text: Just as the power of fire, though in reality one, has a figurative multiplicity due to its functions of burning and illuminating with respect to combustible and illuminable objects — because it is in reality one.

children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 4
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> (Knowledge Section), Chapter 4

children.text: sa itthaṃ vigraho'nena karaṇenāhataujasā /
children.translated_text: He, having such a body, with this instrument of unimpeded power,

children.text: karoti sarvadā kṛtyaṃ yadā yadupapadyate || MrgT_1,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: performs the [appropriate] activity always, whenever whatever is fitting.

children.text: * ittham ityanenoktaprakāreṇa mantrātmako vigraho yasya sa bhagavān itthaṃvigrahaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.1:1
children.translated_text: 'Having such a body' (<s>itthaṃvigrahaḥ</s>) — the Blessed One whose body is of the mantra-nature described above.

children.text: * aneneti /
children.translated_text: 'With this' —

children.text: * karaṇaṃ ca na śaktyanyat // MrgTV_1,4.1:2
children.translated_text: And the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is none other than <s>śakti</s> (power).

children.text: * iti prāguktenātmanā apratihatasāmarthyena karaṇena sthityādikāryajātaṃ sarvakālaṃ sarvaṃ nirvartayati // MrgTV_1,4.1:3
children.translated_text: By this, the previously described instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of unobstructed capacity — he accomplishes the entire range of effects such as maintenance and the like, at all times.

children.text: * na paraṃ yugapatkaroti yāvadyadā yadupapadyate tattadā karoti krameṇāpi sarvaṃ kāryaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.1:4
children.translated_text: He does not do everything simultaneously, but rather — whenever whatever is fitting, that he does at that time; he performs all activity even in sequence — this is the meaning.

children.text: * taduktaṃ prāk /
children.translated_text: Thus it was stated earlier:

children.text: * kramākramasamutpatteḥ kramādyutpattiśaktimat // MrgTV_1,4.1:5
children.translated_text: 'Because of the arising of things both successively and simultaneously, [the Lord] possesses the power of producing things in succession and otherwise.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,4.1:6
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * atha prathamataḥ parameśvaraḥ kiṃ karotītyāha // MrgTV_1,4.1:7
children.translated_text: Now, what does <s>Parameśvara</s> do first? He says:

children.text: tatrādau kevalāṇūnāṃ yogyānāṃ kurute'ṣṭakam /
children.translated_text: Therein, at the beginning, for the souls that are pure (<s>kevala</s>) and fit, he makes the group of eight [<s>Vidyeśvaras</s>],

children.text: vāmādiśaktibhir yuktaṃ saptakoṭiparicchadam || MrgT_1,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: endowed with the powers of <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest, attended by seventy million [<s>mantras</s>].

children.text: * tatrety evaṃ sthite sati ityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.2:1
children.translated_text: 'Therein' (<s>tatra</s>) means: this being the case.

children.text: * ekasyā eva śakter vāmādikṛtyavaśād vāmādibhedabhinnatvam ityuktam // MrgTV_1,4.2:2
children.translated_text: It has been stated that even though the power is one, it has the division into <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest due to differences in activity.

children.text: * sā ca śaktiḥ sarvajñānakriyārūpā śivavat sarvāṇūnāṃ vidyata eva teṣāṃ cānādyavidyāruddhatvāc chivānugrahaṃ vinā na tatsamānā bhavatīti prakṣīṇakārmamāyīyabandhānāṃ vijñānakevalānām añjanaparipākādyanusāreṇa tatpadayogyānām aṣṭakaṃ mantrakoṭisaptakaparivāraṃ vāmādiśaktinavakayuktaṃ ca karoti // MrgTV_1,4.2:3
children.translated_text: And that <s>śakti</s> (power), having the form of all knowledge and action, exists in all souls just as in <s>Śiva</s>; but because theirs has been obstructed by beginningless ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), without <s>Śiva's</s> grace it does not become equal to his. Therefore, for those <s>vijñānakevalas</s> (pure conscious souls) whose bonds of <s>karma</s> and <s>māyā</s> have been exhausted, who are fit for that status in accordance with the ripening of their impurity (<s>añjana</s>) and the like — he makes the group of eight [<s>Vidyeśvaras</s>], accompanied by a retinue of seven <s>koṭis</s> (seventy million) of <s>mantras</s>, and endowed with the nine powers of <s>Vāmā</s> and the rest.

children.text: * anyeṣāmapi saptakoṭisaṃkhyātānāṃ mantrāṇām ananteśādaya evāṣṭāv īśitāra iti vaktumārabhate // MrgTV_1,4.2:4
children.translated_text: To state that even for the other seventy million <s>mantras</s>, the eight beginning with <s>Ananteśa</s> are the rulers, he begins:

children.text: teṣāmanantaḥ sūkṣmaśca tathā caiva śivottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among them are <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, and likewise <s>Śivottama</s>,

children.text: ekanetraikarudrau ca trimūrtiścāmitadyutiḥ || MrgT_1,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ekanetra</s>, <s>Ekarudra</s>, <s>Trimūrti</s>, and <s>Amitadyuti</s>,

children.text: śrīkaṇṭhaśca śikhaṇḍī ca rājarājeśvareśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> — lords of kings of kings.

children.text: * rājāno lokeśā indrādayaḥ teṣāṃ rājānaḥ śatarudrāḥ tadīśvarāṇāṃ maṇḍaliprabhṛtīnāmapyeta īśvarāḥ prabhavaḥ vidyāmaheśvarā iti yāvat // MrgTV_1,4.4ab:1
children.translated_text: The kings are the world-lords (<s>Lokeśas</s>), <s>Indra</s> and the rest; the kings of those are the <s>Śatarudras</s> (Hundred Rudras); and the lords, the sources of power, of their rulers such as the <s>Maṇḍalins</s> and the rest — these are the <s>Vidyāmaheśvaras</s> (Great Lords of Knowledge).

children.text: * ete ca // MrgTV_1,4.4ab:2
children.translated_text: And these —

children.text: īṣad aprāptayogatvānniyojyāḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ || MrgT_1,4.4 ||
children.translated_text: because they have slightly fallen short of [complete] union [with <s>Śiva</s>], they are to be directed by the Supreme One.

children.text: * adhikāramalāṃśāvaśeṣāt kiṃcidanavāptaparameśvarasāmyā ityasyaite preryāḥ // MrgTV_1,4.4cd:1
children.translated_text: Because of the residual portion of the impurity of their commission (<s>adhikāramala</s>), they have not quite attained equality with <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) — hence these are to be impelled [by him].

children.text: * athaiṣāmaṣṭānāmapi sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvasambhavāt kiṃsvid abhinnarūpatvamuta kaścidviśeṣa ityāha // MrgTV_1,4.4cd:2
children.translated_text: Now, since omniscience and omnipotence are possible for all eight of these as well, is their nature undifferentiated, or is there some distinction? He says:

children.text: sarvajñatvādiyoge'pi niyojyatvaṃ malāṃśataḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though endowed with omniscience and the rest, they are to be directed due to the residual portion of impurity;

children.text: parasparaṃ viśiṣyante mantrāś caivam adhaḥ sthitāḥ || MrgT_1,4.5 ||
