children.translated_text: they are distinguished from one another, and the <s>mantras</s> stationed below [are distinguished] likewise.

children.text: * yadyapi sarve sarvārthadṛkkriyāḥ tathāpyekaikasya svasvādhovartino niyojyā iti preryatālakṣaṇamalāṃśāvaśeṣād adho'vasthitānām eṣām ūrdhvasthamavekṣya kalayā kartṛtvasya nyūnatvamiti parasparaviśeṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.5:1
children.translated_text: Even though all [of them] possess the vision and action pertaining to all objects, nevertheless each one's subordinates stationed below him are to be directed — and due to the residual portion [of impurity] characterized as directability, in comparison with those stationed above, the agency of those stationed below is diminished by a degree — thus there is mutual distinction.

children.text: * taduktam /
children.translated_text: As it has been said:

children.text: * yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmād ūrdhvamiṣyate /
children.translated_text: 'He who is superior in qualities to another is regarded as being above him' —

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,4.5:2
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: * na kevalameta eva viśiṣyante yāvat tadadhovartino mantrā apyevameva parasparaviśeṣabhājaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.5:3
children.translated_text: Not only are these [<s>Vidyeśvaras</s>] distinguished from one another, but even the <s>mantras</s> stationed below them are likewise possessed of mutual distinction.

children.text: * tāneva mantrān viśinaṣṭi // MrgTV_1,4.5:4
children.translated_text: He now differentiates those very <s>mantras</s>:

children.text: te ca mantreśvaravyaktaśivaśaktipracoditāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those [<s>mantras</s>], impelled by <s>Śiva's</s> power manifested through the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (Lords of Mantras),

children.text: kurvantyanugrahaṃ puṃsāṃ yadā yeṣāṃ sa yujyate || MrgT_1,4.6 ||
children.translated_text: bestow grace upon souls whenever and upon whomever it is fitting.

children.text: * te ca mantrāḥ parāparamantreśvaravyaktayā śivaśaktyā vyāpāritā yogyatānurūpyeṇa kadācitkeṣāṃcidanugrahaṃ kurvanti na tu yogyatānapekṣam atiprasaṅgāt // MrgTV_1,4.6:1
children.translated_text: And those <s>mantras</s>, set into operation by the power of <s>Śiva</s> manifested through the higher and lower <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, sometimes bestow grace upon certain [souls] in accordance with their fitness — but not without regard to fitness, as that would lead to over-extension.

children.text: prayoktṛdehasāpekṣaṃ tadardhamakhile'dhvani /
children.translated_text: Half of them, requiring the body of an officiant, having performed their commission in the entire course (<s>adhvan</s>),

children.text: kṛtvādhikāraṃ sthityante śivaṃ viśati seśvaram || MrgT_1,4.7 ||
children.translated_text: at the end of [the cosmic] maintenance, enter the state of <s>Śiva</s> together with the Lords.

children.text: * teṣāṃ saptakoṭisaṃkhyātānāṃ mantrāṇāmardhaṃ prayoktḥṇām anugrahītḥṇāṃ dehaṃ śarīram āśrayatvenāpekṣamāṇam īśvaramapekṣata iti tatsāpekṣam ācāryādhikaraṇeśvarāpekṣam akhile māyīye'dhvani svamadhikāram anugrāhyānugrahalakṣaṇaṃ nirvartya sthitikālasyānte māyīyasyādhvano'pyuparamasamaye seśvaramiti mantreśvaraiḥ sahitaṃ śivasāyujyaṃ gacchati // MrgTV_1,4.7:1
children.translated_text: Of those <s>mantras</s> numbering seventy million, half — requiring, that is, depending upon the body of the officiants, the ones to be graced, and also depending on the Lord, that is, dependent on the preceptor and the presiding lord — having completed their commission in the entire <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) course, their commission characterized as the gracing of those to be graced, at the end of the period of maintenance, at the time of cessation of the <s>māyīya</s> course — 'together with the Lords' means together with the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> — they attain union with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: * aparasyārdhasya kā vārttetyāha // MrgTV_1,4.7:2
children.translated_text: What then of the other half? He says:

children.text: vinādhikaraṇenānyatpradhānavikṛter adhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The other [half], without [requiring] an officiant, below <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primordial Matter) and its modifications,

children.text: kṛtvādhikāramīśeṣṭam apaiti svādhvasaṃhṛtau || MrgT_1,4.8 ||
children.translated_text: having performed the commission desired by the Lord, departs at the dissolution of its own course.

children.text: * anyad aparam ardhamīśeṣṭamiti yatra yatra parameśvarasyānugrahecchā tatra tatra tadicchayaiva vinādhikaraṇenety ācāryalakṣaṇam adhikaraṇam anapekṣyaiva pradhānā cāsau vikṛtiśceti pradhānavikṛtiḥ śuddhavidyā asyā adhaḥ sarvatra māyīye cādhvani svamadhikāraṃ kṛtvā svasyādhvano'nugrahamārgasya saṃhṛtau samāptau apaiti apavṛjyate // MrgTV_1,4.8:1
children.translated_text: The other, the remaining half — 'desired by the Lord' means wherever <s>Parameśvara</s>'s (the Supreme Lord's) will to grace exists, there, by his will alone — 'without an officiant' means without depending on the officiant characterized as a preceptor; <s>Pradhānavikṛti</s> is <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), which is both primary substance and modification; below this, everywhere in the <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) course, having performed its commission, at the completion of the dissolution of its own course, that is, the path of grace — it departs, it is liberated.

children.text: * taduktaṃ tatrabhavadbhiḥ sadyojyotiḥpādaiḥ /
children.translated_text: As has been said by the revered <s>Sadyojyotiḥ</s>:

children.text: * jagati kṛte tatrārdhaṃ mantrāṇāṃ śivasamāhṛtān puṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When the world has been created, therein half of the <s>mantras</s>, having graced the souls gathered by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: * anugṛhya yāti hi vinā daiśikamūrtiṃ prayuktamīśena // MrgTV_1,4.8:2
children.translated_text: depart without the form of a preceptor, being employed by the Lord' —

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,4.8:3
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: * itthaṃ mantrānuktvā mantreśvarānvaktum āha // MrgTV_1,4.8:4
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken of the <s>mantras</s>, in order to speak of the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (Lords of Mantras), he says:

children.text: tato'nantādyabhivyaktaḥ patīnāṃ granthitattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, manifested by <s>Ananta</s> and the rest, from the knot-principle (<s>granthitattva</s>), of the lords

children.text: kalādyārabdhadehānāṃ karotyaṣṭādaśaṃ śatam || MrgT_1,4.9 ||
children.translated_text: whose bodies commence with <s>kalā</s> (the principle of limited agency), he creates one hundred and eighteen.

children.text: * tac ca sātmakamākramya viśramāyāvatiṣṭhate // MrgTV_1,4.9:1
children.translated_text: 'And entering that which contains the selves within it, he remains for rest' —

children.text: * iti antarviśrāntāṇusaṃghātaṃ māyātattvaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ tasmād granthitattvatas tadgarbhādhikāriṇāṃ kalādyārabdhaśarīrāṇāṃ maṇḍalyādīnāṃ patīnāmaṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śatam ananteśādyabhivyaktaḥ parameśvaraḥ karoti kalādyārabdhadehatvam eṣāṃ karotītyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.9:2
children.translated_text: thus, from the <s>Māyā</s> principle, to be described [later], which contains within it the aggregate of resting souls — from the knot-principle, that is, from within that [<s>Māyā</s>], <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), manifested through <s>Ananteśa</s> and the other [<s>Vidyeśvaras</s>], creates one hundred and eighteen lords such as the <s>Maṇḍalins</s> and the rest, who hold commissions within that [<s>Māyā</s>] and whose bodies commence with <s>kalā</s> and the other [principles]. The meaning is: he creates their embodiment commencing with <s>kalā</s>.

children.text: * nanu ca /
children.translated_text: But surely —

children.text: * aṣṭādaśādhikaṃ cānyacchataṃ māyādhikāriṇām /
children.translated_text: 'And another one hundred and eighteen, of those who preside over <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: * vidyeśvarāṇām // MrgTV_1,4.9:3
children.translated_text: of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (Lords of Knowledge)' —

children.text: * ityādinā sākṣāt parameśvarānugṛhītatvam eṣāmuktam iha tv anantādyabhivyaktasya bhagavatas tatkaraṇamucyata iti virodhaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.9:4
children.translated_text: by such [earlier statements], it was stated that these were directly graced by <s>Parameśvara</s> himself, but here it is said that the Blessed One manifested through <s>Ananta</s> and the rest creates them — this is a contradiction.

children.text: * naivaṃ yato'nantādīnāmeva kalādiyogakaraṇe kartṛtvaṃ natu parameśvarasya /
children.translated_text: Not so, because it is <s>Ananta</s> and the others alone who have the agency in effecting the conjunction with <s>kalā</s> and the rest, not <s>Parameśvara</s> [directly] —

children.text: * śuddhe'dhvani śivaḥ kartā prokto'nanto'site prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the pure course, <s>Śiva</s> is declared to be the creator; <s>Ananta</s> is the lord in the impure [course]' —

children.text: * iti śruteḥ // MrgTV_1,4.9:5
children.translated_text: thus says the scripture.

children.text: * sa tu kalādiyogino bhogabhujastān sākṣādanugṛhṇātīti na kaściddoṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.9:6
children.translated_text: But he directly graces those who are conjoined with <s>kalā</s> and the rest and who experience enjoyments — therefore there is no defect.

children.text: * te 'pyanyeṣāṃ viniyoktāra ityāha // MrgTV_1,4.9:7
children.translated_text: They too are directors of others — he says:

children.text: tān apyāviśya bhagavān sāñjanān bhuvanādhipān /
children.translated_text: Entering those [<s>Mantreśvaras</s>] as well, the Blessed One [creates] the rulers of the worlds, who are tainted [by impurity],

children.text: yebhyaḥ sarvamidaṃ yeṣāṃ śaktiḥ karmanibandhanā || MrgT_1,4.10 ||
children.translated_text: from whom all this [emerges], and whose power is bound by <s>karma</s> (action).

children.text: * tānapi maṇḍaliprabhṛtīn aṣṭāv adhiṣṭhāya sa parameśvaro'nyānapi brahmaprabhṛtīn samalān bhuvaneśān uttejitadṛkkriyāśaktīn karotīti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.10:1
children.translated_text: Presiding over those eight as well, beginning with the <s>Maṇḍalins</s>, that <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) also creates others — the lords of the worlds beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, who are tainted [by impurity], by enlivening their powers of vision and action — the connection is with the previous [verse] itself.

children.text: * kiṃvidhān ityāha yebhyaḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamalakṣaṇam āvirbhavatīti śeṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.10:2
children.translated_text: Of what kind? He says: 'From whom all this' — the universe characterized as the movable and immovable emerges — this is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: * yeṣāṃ śaktiḥ karmanibandhanā karmapāśo yeṣām uparodhakatvān na nivṛttaḥ sakalānāmevaiṣāṃ parameśvarād anugraho yataḥ // MrgTV_1,4.10:3
children.translated_text: 'Whose power is bound by <s>karma</s>' — those whose bond of <s>karma</s> has not ceased due to its obstructive nature — since the grace of <s>Parameśvara</s> comes to these <s>sakalas</s> (embodied souls) alone.

children.text: * na parametāneva karoti yāvat // MrgTV_1,4.10:4
children.translated_text: And not only these does he create, but also —

children.text: praṇetḥn paśuśāstrāṇāṃ paśūṃs tadanuvartakān /
children.translated_text: the authors of the <s>paśuśāstras</s> (scriptures of the bound), and the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) who follow those [scriptures],

children.text: svasādhyakārakopetān kāladhāmāvadhisthitān || MrgT_1,4.11 ||
children.translated_text: endowed with their own ends and means, stationed [in realms] extending up to [the world of] <s>Kāla</s> (Time).

children.text: * paśuśāstrāṇām ārhatasāṃkhyapāñcarātrādīnāṃ praṇetḥn arhatkapilaprabhṛtīṃs tadanuṣṭhātḥṃśca paśūn svasādhyena tattacchāstropadiṣṭena phalena tatsādhanahetubhiḥ kārakaiśca yuktān kālāgnibhuvanāntaṃ yāvatkarotīti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.11:1
children.translated_text: The authors of the <s>paśuśāstras</s> — the scriptures of the <s>Ārhatas</s> (Jains), <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, and the like — namely <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and the rest; and the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) who practice those [scriptures]; endowed with the fruits taught in their respective scriptures and with the means that are the causes of those [fruits] — he creates them extending up to the world of <s>Kālāgni</s> (the Fire of Time). The connection is with the previous [verse] itself.

children.text: * athaitānsṛṣṭvā devaḥ kiṃ karotītyāha // MrgTV_1,4.11:2
children.translated_text: Now, having created these, what does the Lord do? He says:

children.text: sthitau sakārakānetān samākramya svatejasā /
children.translated_text: During the period of maintenance, having pervaded these [beings] together with their instruments by his own splendor,

children.text: yunakti svārthasiddhyarthaṃ bhūtair anabhilakṣitaḥ || MrgT_1,4.12 ||
children.translated_text: he yokes [them] for the accomplishment of their own purposes, unperceived by [other] beings.

children.text: * etān kārakair bhogasādhanais tattvabhāvabhuvanādibhir yuktān svatejasā nijecchāśaktyā samyagadhiṣṭhāya svārthasiddhyartham ityātmīyasya vyāpārasya sampattaye yadvā svairātmabhir arthyata ityartho bhogāpavargalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārthaḥ tasya niṣpattyarthaṃ niyojayati na tūnmattavat nāpy aprayojanaṃ prayojanānuddeśena mandasyāpyapravṛtteḥ naca krīḍārthaṃ rāgādivirahiṇas tadasaṃbhavāt nāpyātmanimittaṃ paripūrṇatvāt // MrgTV_1,4.12:1
children.translated_text: These [beings], endowed with instruments — the means of experience such as principles (<s>tattvas</s>), existences (<s>bhāvas</s>), worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>), and the rest — having properly presided over them by his own splendor, that is, by his own power of will, he yokes them 'for the accomplishment of their own purposes' — meaning for the completion of his own activity, or alternatively, the purpose sought by the selves, namely the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (aim of man) characterized as enjoyment and liberation — for its accomplishment he directs them; not like a madman, nor without purpose, since even a fool does not act without some objective in view; nor for the sake of play, since for one devoid of attachment and the like, that is impossible; nor for his own sake, since he is already complete.

children.text: * bhūtaiḥ prāṇibhiravidyāvaśādaviditataddṛkkriyaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.12:2
children.translated_text: 'Unperceived by beings' — living beings, due to the power of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), do not perceive his vision and action.

children.text: * tadiyatā sṛṣṭisthitī uktvā saṃhāraṃ vaktum āha // MrgTV_1,4.12:3
children.translated_text: Having thus described creation and maintenance insofar as they pertain to him, in order to describe dissolution, he says:

children.text: bhogasādhanamākṣipya kṛtvā kāraṇasaṃśrayam /
children.translated_text: Having withdrawn the means of experience and having made [all] rest in the cause,

children.text: tac ca sātmakamākramya viśramāyāvatiṣṭhate || MrgT_1,4.13 ||
children.translated_text: and having entered that [cause] which contains the selves within it, he remains for rest,

children.text: bhavināṃ bhavakhinnānāṃ sarvabhūtahito yataḥ /
children.translated_text: since he is the benefactor of all beings who are wearied by existence.

children.text: * ityante bhogasādhanaṃ tanukaraṇabhuvanādi upasaṃhṛtya kāraṇe māyākhye līnaṃ kṛtvā tac ca māyākhyaṃ kāraṇam antarnihitātmavrātamadhiṣṭhāya saṃsāriṇāṃ bhavādhvabhramaṇaśrāntānāṃ viśramārtham avatiṣṭhate niruddhavyāpārāṃs tāṃs tān karotītyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.14ab:1
children.translated_text: At the end [of the cosmic cycle], having withdrawn the means of experience — bodies, instruments, worlds, and the rest — having dissolved them into the cause called <s>Māyā</s>, and having presided over that cause called <s>Māyā</s> which contains the multitude of selves deposited within it, he remains for the rest of the transmigrating souls wearied by wandering in the path of existence — the meaning is: he causes those various [souls] to have their activity suspended.

children.text: * kuta ityāha sarvabhūtahito yataḥ yasmāt sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ hitāya pravṛttaḥ parameśvaraḥ khedāpanodāya viśrāntiṃ svāpalakṣaṇāmeṣāṃ karoti // MrgTV_1,4.14ab:2
children.translated_text: Why? He says: 'Since he is the benefactor of all beings' — because <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) is engaged in the welfare of all beings, he creates rest for them in the form of cosmic sleep for the removal of their fatigue.

children.text: * tatastu // MrgTV_1,4.14ab:3
children.translated_text: And then —

children.text: svāpāvasānam āsādya punaḥ prāgvatpravartate || MrgT_1,4.14 ||
children.translated_text: having reached the end of the cosmic sleep, he commences activity again as before.

children.text: * vakṣyamāṇakālaparimāṇasya svāpasyānte bhūyaḥ pūrvavad aharmukhe parameśvaraśceṣṭate // MrgTV_1,4.14cd:1
children.translated_text: At the end of the cosmic sleep of the time-duration to be described, again, as before, at the dawn [of a new cycle], <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) engages in activity.

children.text: * tatsvāpe'pi kriyādiśaktayas tattatkāryaniṣpādanodyuktā bhavantītyāha // MrgTV_1,4.14cd:2
children.translated_text: Even during that cosmic sleep, the powers of action and the rest are eager to accomplish their respective functions — he says:

children.text: svāpe'pyāste bodhayan bodhayogyān rodhyān rundhan pācayankarmikarma /
children.translated_text: Even during the cosmic sleep he abides — awakening those fit to be awakened, obstructing those fit to be obstructed, ripening the <s>karma</s> (actions) of those with <s>karma</s>,

children.text: māyāśaktīr vyaktiyogyāḥ prakurvan paśyansarvaṃ yadyathā vastujātam || MrgT_1,4.15 ||
children.translated_text: making manifest the powers of <s>Māyā</s> that are ready for manifestation, seeing all things — whatever and however the totality of entities may be.

children.text: * jāgradavasthāyāmiva svāpāvasthāyāmapi malaparipākatāratamyāpekṣayā bodhanārhān bodhayan rodhanārhān rodhanaśaktyārundhan karmiṇāṃ karmāṇi pariṇāmayan māyāśaktīśca prasavābhimukhīḥ kurvan sarvaṃ cidacittattvabhāvabhūtabhuvanātmakaṃ yathāvadavalokayannāste // MrgTV_1,4.15:1
children.translated_text: Just as in the waking state, so too in the state of cosmic sleep — with regard to the gradations of ripeness of impurity (<s>mala</s>), awakening those worthy of awakening, obstructing those worthy of obstruction through the power of obstruction, ripening the <s>karmas</s> (actions) of those who have <s>karma</s>, making the powers of <s>Māyā</s> ready for emanation, and surveying everything consisting of conscious and unconscious principles, existences, beings, worlds, and the like — he abides as it truly is.

children.text: * yadyatheti na tv asmadādivat ayathāvastvavabhāso 'pyasya bhavatīti vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,4.15:2
children.translated_text: 'Whatever and however' — but unlike us and others, even an appearance of things as they are not does not occur for him — this we shall explain.

children.text: * tadiyatā jagatsṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsalakṣaṇaṃ kṛtyatrayamihoktamiti prakaraṇopasaṃhāraḥ // MrgTV_1,4.15:3
children.translated_text: Thus, insofar as it pertains to him, the triad of cosmic functions — creation, maintenance, and destruction of the world — has been stated here; this is the conclusion of the section.

children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 5
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> (Knowledge Section), Chapter 5

children.text: tamaḥśaktyadhikārasya nivṛttes tatparicyutau /
children.translated_text: Upon the cessation of the commission of the power of darkness (<s>tamas</s>), at the falling away from that [bondage],

children.text: vyanakti dṛkkriyānantyaṃ jagadbandhuraṇoḥ śivaḥ || MrgT_1,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> manifests the infinity of vision and action of the soul (<s>aṇu</s>), the creator of the world.

children.text: * tamaso malasya śakteśca bhagavatsambandhinyā vāmākhyāyā yo 'sāv adhikāro nyagbhāvanavyāpṛtatvaṃ tasya nivṛttervirāmāt yāsau paricyutiḥ kaivalyābhimukhībhāvaḥ tathā coktaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve /
children.translated_text: Of darkness, that is, of <s>mala</s> (impurity), and of the power — the one called <s>Vāmā</s>, belonging to the Blessed One — the commission (<s>adhikāra</s>), which is the activity of subjugating [the soul], upon its cessation, its termination — the falling away from that, which is the turning towards <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation). And thus it has been said in the glorious <s>Svāyambhuva</s>:

children.text: * kṣīṇe tasminyathā sā syātparaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ prati // MrgTV_1,5.1:1
children.translated_text: 'When that is exhausted, then that [soul] would [proceed] towards the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>)' —

children.text: * iti tasyāṃ tatparicyutau satyāṃ jagaduddharaṇapravaṇaḥ parameśvaro dṛkkriyānantyamaṇorātmanaḥ prakaṭīkaroti // MrgTV_1,5.1:2
children.translated_text: thus, when that falling away has occurred, <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), intent on the deliverance of the world, makes manifest the infinity of vision and action of the soul (<s>aṇu</s>).

children.text: * satyorevānantayor dṛkkriyayor malāvacchannatvād āvṛtānantyayos tatpariṇaterāvaraṇāpagamādabhivyaktiḥ kriyate na tv apūrvotpāda ityuktaṃ vakṣyāmaśca satkāryavāde // MrgTV_1,5.1:3
children.translated_text: Since the two — vision and action — though truly infinite, have their infinity veiled and covered by <s>mala</s> (impurity), through the ripening of that [impurity] the covering is removed and manifestation is effected — but there is no origination of something previously non-existent. This has been stated, and we shall explain it further in the discussion of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine of the pre-existence of effects).

children.text: yānvimocayati svāpe śivāḥ sadyo bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: Those whom he liberates during the cosmic sleep become <s>Śivas</s> immediately;

children.text: saṃhṛtau vā samudbhūtāv aṇavaḥ patayo'thavā || MrgT_1,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: whether during dissolution or during creation, they become souls (<s>aṇus</s>) or lords (<s>patis</s>).

children.text: * svāpāvasthitān yānparameśvaro'nugṛhṇāti te tu tatkāla eva śivāḥ sampadyante na tv adhikāriṇo bhavanti teṣāṃ malāṃśān avaśeṣato'preryatvena śivatvayogāt tadānīṃ cādhikāriṇāmanupayogāt // MrgTV_1,5.2:1
children.translated_text: Those who are situated in the state of cosmic sleep and whom <s>Parameśvara</s> graces — they attain the state of <s>Śiva</s> at that very moment and do not become holders of commissions, because the absence of any residual portion of their impurity makes them fit for <s>Śivahood</s> rather than being directed, and because at that time there is no use for commissioned [agents].

children.text: * kiṃca saṃhāre sṛṣṭau vā yānvimocayati te 'pi sadya eva śivāḥ sampadyante na vyatirekeṇa // MrgTV_1,5.2:2
children.translated_text: Moreover, those whom he liberates during dissolution or during creation — they too become <s>Śivas</s> immediately, without exception.

children.text: * athaveti anayoḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakālayor añjanaparipākavailakṣaṇyatas tatkṣaṇaṃ śivatvavyaktyā niradhikāramūrtibhājaḥ sādhikārāḥ patitvayogino vā ātmāno bhavantītyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.2:3
children.translated_text: Or — with the word 'or' (<s>athavā</s>) — at these two times of creation and dissolution, due to the difference in the maturity of their impurity (<s>añjana</s>), at that very moment, through the manifestation of <s>Śivahood</s>, they become either those who partake of the status of a form without commission, or those who partake of lordship with commission — this is the meaning.

children.text: * tatra saṃhāre yeṣām adhikāravān anugrahaste tadānīṃ rudrāṇavaḥ sṛṣṭau tv adhikāriṇo bhavitāraḥ sargārambhe tu sādhikārānugrahānugṛhītāḥ pataya iti parāparavidyeśvarādyadhikārabhājo bhavantīti // MrgTV_1,5.2:4
children.translated_text: In that regard, at the time of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), those for whom grace accompanies a commission — they are then <s>Rudrāṇavas</s> (Rudra-souls); in creation, they will become those bearing a commission. But at the commencement of creation, those who are graced with a commission — the Lords (<s>pati</s>) — they become recipients of the offices of higher and lower <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and the like.

children.text: * atha sṛṣṭisaṃhārakālayor aśrutamapi kathamanugrāhyāṇāṃ śivatvaṃ labhyata iti cet labhyata eva malaparipākasya parameśvarānugrahasya cāniyatakālatvāt // MrgTV_1,5.2:5
children.translated_text: Now, if it is asked: how do the souls to be graced attain <s>Śivahood</s> at the times of creation and dissolution, which are not mentioned [in the text]? — they do indeed attain it, because the ripening of impurity (<s>mala</s>) and the grace of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) are not restricted to any particular time.

children.text: * athaivaṃ sargasaṃhārasvāpakāleṣu anugṛhītānāṃ muktiviśeṣamuktvā sthitikālānugṛhītānāṃ tadviśeṣamāha // MrgTV_1,5.2:6
children.translated_text: Now, having stated the particular type of liberation for those who are graced during creation, dissolution, and the state of cosmic sleep (<s>svāpa</s>), he describes the particular type for those graced during the period of maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>):

children.text: rudramantrapatīśānapadabhājo bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: They attain the stations of <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Mantra</s>-lords, lords of the <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s> —

children.text: sthitau yānanugṛhṇāti gurumāsthāya cidvataḥ || MrgT_1,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: those whom he graces during the period of maintenance, through a <s>guru</s> (spiritual teacher), the conscious ones.

children.text: * gurvadhikaraṇaḥ parameśvaraḥ sthitikāle cidvata iti tadanudhyānavaśāt parāparaniḥśreyasaviṣayayā praśasyayā citā yuktānyānaṇūnanugṛhṇāti te mandatīvrādiśaktisampātavailakṣaṇyāt pañcāṣṭakādirudrāṇāṃ saptakoṭisaṃkhyātānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ tatpatīnāṃ ca vidyeśvarāṇām īśānasya ceśvarasadāśivāntalakṣaṇasya sambandhi padaṃ bhajanta iti tatpadabhājas tatsālokyādipadayogino bhavatītyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.3:1
children.translated_text: <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), acting through the medium of a <s>guru</s>, during the period of maintenance, graces certain souls — 'the conscious ones' meaning those endowed with praiseworthy consciousness directed toward the higher and lower supreme good through meditation upon him. They, due to the distinction in the descent of <s>Śakti</s> (power) — mild, intense, and so forth — attain the stations associated with the <s>Rudras</s> of the groups of five, eight, and the like, with the seventy million <s>mantras</s>, with their lords the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, and with <s>Īśāna</s> characterized as extending up to <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>. 'Attaining those stations' means they become recipients of <s>sālokya</s> (co-residence) and other forms of union with those stations — this is the meaning.

children.text: * nanu śaktipātaviśeṣāt tattatpadabhāktvaṃ cet tarhi tadviśeṣaḥ kathaṃ jñeyaḥ ityāha // MrgTV_1,5.3:2
children.translated_text: But if the particular station is determined by the particular descent of <s>Śakti</s>, then how is that distinction to be recognized? He says:

children.text: yeṣāṃ śarīriṇāṃ śaktiḥ patatyapi nivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: For those embodied beings upon whom <s>Śakti</s> (power) descends, even for the sake of cessation [of worldly existence],

children.text: teṣāṃ talliṅgam autsukyaṃ muktau dveṣo bhavasthitau || MrgT_1,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: the sign of that [descent] is: eagerness for liberation, aversion to continued worldly existence,

children.text: bhaktiśca śivabhakteṣu śraddhā tacchāsake vidhau /
children.translated_text: devotion to the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, and faith in the scriptural injunctions that teach that [path].

children.text: anenānumitiḥ śiṣṭahetoḥ sthūladhiyāmapi || MrgT_1,5.5 ||
children.translated_text: Through this, inference is possible even for those of gross intellect, regarding the remaining cause [of bondage].

children.text: * aśarīriṇāṃ tāvadgurubhiḥ śaktipātasya durlakṣatvāc charīravatāṃ yeṣāṃ pārameśvarī śaktirapunarāvirbhāvāya patati teṣāṃ tatpāte muktyutkaṇṭhā saṃsāradveṣaḥ parameśvarabhaktipareṣu bhaktiḥ tacchāsake śāstre śraddhā ceti liṅgaṃ cihnam // MrgTV_1,5.5:1
children.translated_text: For bodiless beings, the descent of <s>Śakti</s> is difficult for <s>gurus</s> to discern. But for those who are embodied, upon whom the power of <s>Parameśvara</s> descends for the sake of non-return [to worldly existence], the signs of that descent are: yearning for liberation (<s>mukti</s>), aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), devotion to those devoted to <s>Parameśvara</s>, and faith in the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) that teaches that [path].

children.text: * anenaiva cihnenāprakarṣavatā avaśiṣṭasya saṃsārasthitihetoḥ pāśajālasyāsūkṣmabuddhīnām apyanumānam /
children.translated_text: And through this very sign, even those who are not of subtle intellect can infer the remaining cause of continued worldly existence — the web of bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) — even in its non-fully-manifest form.

children.text: * pūrvoktānāṃ cihnānāmeva mandatve sati paśoḥ pāśaśaithilyamāndyaṃ mandamatayo 'pyanuminvanti iti bhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.5:2
children.translated_text: The purport is: when the aforementioned signs are mild, even those of dull intellect infer the slackness and mildness of the bonds of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).

children.text: * nanu kimanenātyantāpūrveṇa śaktipātaniścayena sakaladarśanaprasiddhaṃ tāvadidaṃ kaivalyaprāptikāraṇaṃ liṅgatvena kiṃ na niścīyate // MrgTV_1,5.5:3
children.translated_text: But why this determination of the descent of <s>Śakti</s>, which is entirely unprecedented? Why not ascertain as a sign the cause of attaining <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) that is well known in all doctrines?

children.text: * yaduktam /
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: * na hṛṣyatyupakāreṇa nāpakāreṇa kupyati /
children.translated_text: 'He who does not rejoice at benefit, nor is angered by harm,

children.text: * yaḥ samaḥ sarvabhūteṣu jīvanmuktaḥ sa iṣyate // MrgTV_1,5.5:4
children.translated_text: who is equal toward all beings — he is regarded as liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>).'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,5.5:5
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tatrāha // MrgTV_1,5.5:6
children.translated_text: To that, he replies:

children.text: paśudṛgyogasiddhānāṃ karmavyaktidvayaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: For those who have attained accomplishment through the doctrines and <s>yoga</s> of the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>), the pair of manifestations of action is equal,

children.text: jyeṣṭhādiphalayogyānāṃ sādhikārāsu muktiṣu || MrgT_1,5.6 ||
children.translated_text: for those eligible for the fruit of the highest [station] and the like, in liberations that bear a commission;

children.text: upāyādaravaiśiṣṭyān mṛgyate tattrayaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: but through the distinction in care for the means, a triad of those [manifestations] is sought.

children.text: * paśudṛgbhiḥ pāśavair jñānaistaduktena ca patañjaliprabhṛtipraṇītena yogena ye siddhāḥ sattvaguṇaprasādān mādhyasthyaṃ prāptāsteṣāṃ yatkarmabhyām upakārāpakārarūpābhyāṃ ceṣṭābhyāṃ prasādakrodhalakṣaṇaṃ vyaktidvayaṃ samamiti nāpakāriṇi krodhavyaktir nāpyupakāriṇi prītivyaktir mādhyasthyād evaitadbhavatu nāsmābhir niṣidhyate // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:1
children.translated_text: For those who have attained accomplishment through the doctrines of the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) and through the <s>yoga</s> taught by them, as prescribed by <s>Patañjali</s> and others — who have attained equanimity through the clarity of the <s>sattva</s> quality (<s>guṇa</s>) — in their case, the pair of manifestations through the two actions of benefit and harm, namely the manifestation of satisfaction and anger, is equal. That is, there is no manifestation of anger toward one who harms, nor manifestation of joy toward one who benefits, due to equanimity alone. Let this be so — we do not prohibit it.

children.text: * iha punarayaṃ viśeṣaḥ yadadhikāravatīṣu muktiṣu viṣayeṣūpāyasya dīkṣādeḥ // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:2
children.translated_text: But here there is this distinction: with regard to liberations that bear a commission, which are the domains of the means such as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the like —

children.text: * lokadharmamayī dīkṣā śivadharmamayī tathā // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:3
children.translated_text: '<s>Dīkṣā</s> (initiation) that consists of worldly <s>dharma</s>, and likewise that which consists of <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>dharma</s>' —

children.text: * ityādinā vakṣyamāṇād vaiśiṣṭyād ādarasya ca tattatpadaprāptiprītiśraddhātmanovailakṣaṇyāt yathoktaṃ śrīmatsūkṣmasvāyambhuve /
children.translated_text: because of the distinction to be described beginning thus, and because of the distinction in care — namely, the distinctive quality of joy, faith, and devotion toward attaining the respective station — as stated in the revered <s>Sūkṣma</s> and <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [āgamas]:

children.text: * yo yatrābhilaṣed bhogānsa tatraiva niyojitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever desires enjoyments in whatever [realm], he is appointed to that very [station],

children.text: * siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyāt // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:4
children.translated_text: through the power of <s>mantras</s> in the division of accomplishments.'

children.text: * iti tasmād upāyādaravailakṣaṇyān mantramaheśvarādipadaprāptilakṣaṇajyeṣṭhaphalayogyatāṃ mantreśvarapadaśaktyātmakaphalārhatvaṃ pañcāṣṭakādyaparādhikāri padayojanāyogyatāṃ ca niścetuṃ karmavyaktitrayaṃ mṛgyate anviṣyate // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:5
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the distinction in care for the means, the triad of manifestations of action is sought — that is, investigated — in order to ascertain eligibility for the highest fruit characterized by the attainment of the station of <s>Mantramaheśvara</s> and the like, worthiness for the fruit consisting of the power of the station of <s>Mantreśvara</s>, and eligibility for the station of the subordinate offices of the groups of five, eight, and the like.

children.text: * bhaktiśraddhābhivyaktitāratamyād utkṛṣṭamadhyamāpakṛṣṭarūpasādhikārāpavargapadabhāja ityanugrāhyā bhavantītyāśayaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:6
children.translated_text: The purport is: through the gradation in the manifestation of devotion and faith, souls become recipients of the superior, middling, and inferior stations of liberation that bear a commission.

children.text: * yac caitat sādhikāramuktitrayaṃ darśitam tataḥ // MrgTV_1,5.7ab:7
children.translated_text: And this triad of liberation with commission that has been shown — from that:

children.text: dvayorvyaktikaraḥ kaścic cyutisiddhivilakṣitaḥ || MrgT_1,5.7 ||
children.translated_text: For two [of them], there is an impediment that causes manifestation [of karma], characterized by fall and attainment.

children.text: * madhyamāpakṛṣṭayor muktyor uparyadhovartinaḥ padasya prāpyatayā svasmāt padāt cyutisambhavena ca kaścidvyaktikaro'ntarāyaḥ natv anantaram evāpavargasya prāptiḥ // MrgTV_1,5.7cd:1
children.translated_text: For the middling and inferior liberations, since the station above and below is to be attained and since fall from one's own station is possible, there is an impediment that causes the manifestation [of residual karma]; liberation is not attained immediately.

children.text: * tṛtīyasyāṃ tu tatpadādhikārasamāptisamanantareṇaiva tallābhaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.7cd:2
children.translated_text: But for the third [highest liberation], the attainment of that station occurs immediately upon the completion of the commission for that station.

children.text: * atha kiṃnimittam etac cihnavaicitryaṃ yadvaśāttritvaṃ sādhikārāyā mukterityāha // MrgTV_1,5.7cd:3
children.translated_text: Now, what is the cause of this variety of signs, by virtue of which liberation with commission becomes threefold? He says:

children.text: īṣadarthanivṛtte tu rodhakatve tamaḥpateḥ /
children.translated_text: When the obstructing power of the lord of darkness (<s>tamaḥpati</s>) has slightly ceased,

children.text: bhavantyetāni liṅgāni kiṃcicchiṣṭe ca dehinām || MrgT_1,5.8 ||
children.translated_text: and when a little [of it] remains, these signs arise for embodied beings.

children.text: * tamaḥpateḥ kriyādṛṅniroddhur vāmadevanāthasya yadrodhakatvaṃ tasmin kiṃcin nivṛtte manāg avaśiṣṭe ca sati etac cihnatāratamyaṃ śarīriṇāṃ bhavati // MrgTV_1,5.8:1
children.translated_text: The lord of darkness (<s>tamaḥpati</s>), <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the lord who obstructs vision and action — when his obstructing power has slightly ceased and a little remains, this gradation of signs arises for embodied beings.

children.text: * ata eva // MrgTV_1,5.8:2
children.translated_text: For this very reason:

children.text: yogyatātrayam apyetat samatītya maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Transcending even this triad of eligibility, <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord)

children.text: svāpe'ṇumanugṛhṇāti sādhikāramidaṃ yataḥ || MrgT_1,5.9 ||
children.translated_text: graces the soul during cosmic sleep (<s>svāpa</s>), because this [eligibility] pertains to [liberation] with commission.

children.text: * etadyogyatātrayam anapekṣyaiva svāpe'ṇumanugṛhṇāti aṇumiti jātāvekavacanam yogyatāvaicitryeṇānugrahavaicitryamaṇūnāṃ tadānīṃ na karotīti bhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.9:1
children.translated_text: Without regard to this triad of eligibility, he graces the soul during cosmic sleep. 'Soul' (<s>aṇu</s>) is used in the singular to denote the class. The purport is: he does not at that time differentiate the grace of the souls according to the variety of eligibility.

children.text: * atraiva hetumāha sādhikāramidaṃ yataḥ yasmādyogyatātrayamadhikārāpekṣam // MrgTV_1,5.9:2
children.translated_text: He states the reason for this: 'Because this pertains to [liberation] with commission' — because the triad of eligibility depends on commission.

children.text: * na ca tadānīmadhikāropayogaḥ tasmān nāpekṣate // MrgTV_1,5.9:3
children.translated_text: And at that time, commission has no applicability; therefore he does not take it into account.

children.text: sargamūle tṛtīyāyāṃ svāpavadbhūtasaṃhṛtau /
children.translated_text: At the root of creation, in the third [type of dissolution], the dissolution of beings, which is like cosmic sleep —

children.text: * bhaviṣyati sargārambhe saṃhāropānte vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ ca bhūtasaṃhṛtau yānanugṛhṇāti te śivāḥ sampadyante svāpāvasthānugṛhītāṇuvat // MrgTV_1,5.10ab:1
children.translated_text: At the commencement of creation, at the end of dissolution, in the third dissolution of beings of the type to be described — those whom he graces attain <s>Śivahood</s>, just like the souls graced during cosmic sleep.

children.text: * svāpe'ṇumanugṛhṇātīti yatprāguktaṃ tato'ṇuśabdaṃ lakṣayitum āha // MrgTV_1,5.10ab:2
children.translated_text: In order to indicate the referent of the word 'soul' (<s>aṇu</s>) in the earlier statement 'he graces the soul during cosmic sleep,' he says:

children.text: sa yad vyapāsya kriyate tadvidho yo 'ṇur ucyate || MrgT_1,5.10 ||
children.translated_text: That soul is called one who, when that [bondage] is removed, is made [into Śiva].

children.text: * sa ityanantaroktaḥ sargādau tṛtīye ca bhūtasaṃhāre svāpe ca yo 'nugrāhyaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.10cd:1
children.translated_text: 'That' refers to what was just mentioned — the soul to be graced at the beginning of creation, at the third dissolution of beings, and during cosmic sleep.

children.text: * yo yad vyapāsyāpanīya tādṛgvidhaḥ kriyate abhivyaktaśivabhāvaḥ sampadyate so 'ṇuśabdavācyo jñeyaḥ aṇuḥ sann apavṛjyata iti yāvat // MrgTV_1,5.10cd:2
children.translated_text: The one who, when that [bondage] is removed — that is, taken away — is made into such a form, that is, whose <s>Śiva</s>-nature becomes manifest, is to be known as denoted by the word 'soul' (<s>aṇu</s>). The meaning is: being a soul, he is liberated.

children.text: * tadevaṃ bodhayanbodhayogyān iti yatprāguktaṃ taddṛkkriyānantyavyaktyā pradarśitam // MrgTV_1,5.10cd:3
children.translated_text: Thus, what was stated earlier as 'awakening those who are fit to be awakened' has been demonstrated through the manifestation of infinite vision and action.

children.text: * yadapi rodhyānrundhan ityādi sūcitaṃ tat yānvimocayati svāpe ityanena keṣāṃcideva tathāvidhānugrahabhāktve sati anyeṣām arthākṣipto rodha itikṛtvā na vipañcitam // MrgTV_1,5.10cd:4
children.translated_text: And as for what was indicated by 'obstructing the obstructable' and so forth — that, since only certain souls are recipients of such grace through 'those whom he liberates during cosmic sleep,' the obstruction of others is implied; hence it was not elaborated.

children.text: * idānīṃ tu pācayankarmikarma ityuktaṃ nirvarṇayitum āha // MrgTV_1,5.10cd:5
children.translated_text: Now, in order to explain what was said as 'ripening the <s>karma</s> of the <s>karmic</s> beings,' he says:

children.text: tathā bījaṃ śarīrādeḥ pācayaty āniveśanāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, he ripens the seed of the body and the like, up to the point of cessation [of the body].

children.text: * bhagavataḥ śaktayaḥ sarvakāryeṣu prasṛtāḥ // MrgTV_1,5.11ab:1
children.translated_text: The powers of the Blessed One are extended into all effects.

children.text: * tābhiḥ śarīrendriyajātyāyurbhogakāraṇaṃ karma dehabhājāṃ tatsvāpe pācayati phaladānonmukhamāpādayati // MrgTV_1,5.11ab:2
children.translated_text: Through them, he ripens the <s>karma</s> that is the cause of the body, senses, birth-class, lifespan, and experience of the embodied beings during their cosmic sleep — that is, he brings it to the point of being ready to yield its fruit.

children.text: * yasmāt // MrgTV_1,5.11ab:3
children.translated_text: Because:

children.text: na yogyatāṅgamabhajat sadyaḥ syādauṣadhādivat || MrgT_1,5.11 ||
children.translated_text: Were it not to undergo the auxiliary process of maturation (<s>yogyatāṅga</s>), it would [need to] yield fruit immediately, like a medicinal herb and the like.

children.text: * yogyatāyā arhatvasyāṅgaṃ sampādakaṃ pākākhyaṃ saṃskāram abhajad anāsevyamānaṃ tat karma sadyastatkṣaṇaṃ harītakyādyauṣadhamiva na syān na bhavetphaladamiti śeṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.11cd:1
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s>, not undergoing the process called ripening (<s>pāka</s>) that is the auxiliary of eligibility — that is, not being subjected to [maturation] — would, like the medicinal herb <s>harītakī</s> and the like, yield its fruit immediately at that very instant. The remainder is: it would not yield fruit [properly].

children.text: * yadāhuḥ aprāptapākaṃ harītakyādidravyaṃ sadapi svakāryasampādanāśaktaṃ yogyatāṅgasya pākasyānāsādanāditi // MrgTV_1,5.11cd:2
children.translated_text: As they say: 'A substance such as <s>harītakī</s> and the like, even though existing, is incapable of producing its proper effect when it has not attained ripening, because it has not undergone the process that is the auxiliary of eligibility.'

children.text: * evaṃ sadapi karmāpakvaṃ tatphaladānāśaktam ataḥ pākāpekṣaṃ pākaścāsya na svataḥ sambhavatītyāha // MrgTV_1,5.11cd:3
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>karma</s>, even though existing, when unripened is incapable of yielding its fruit. Therefore it depends on ripening. And that ripening does not come about of its own accord — he says:

children.text: pākārhamapi tat paktuṃ neśātmānamātmanā /
children.translated_text: Even though fit for ripening, that [karma] is not capable of ripening itself by itself.

children.text: dharmasāmānya evāyaṃ sarvasya pariṇāminaḥ || MrgT_1,5.12 ||
children.translated_text: This is a universal property of everything that undergoes transformation.

children.text: * pākayogyamapi tat svayamātmānamātmanā na pācayitum īśam // MrgTV_1,5.12:1
children.translated_text: Even though fit for ripening, that [karma] is not capable of ripening itself by itself.

children.text: * sarvasyaiva hi pariṇāmino vastunaḥ kṣīrāderivāyaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ yatkimapyapekṣya pariṇāmitvaṃ nānyathā pariṇāmitvāc ca karmaṇo'pyanyāpekṣo vipākaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.12:2
children.translated_text: For indeed, of everything that undergoes transformation — like milk and the like — this is the common property: that transformation occurs only in dependence on something, not otherwise. And since <s>karma</s> too undergoes transformation, its maturation depends on something else.

children.text: * anena māyāśaktīrvyaktiyogyāḥ prakurvan ityetadapi prakāśitaṃ tasyāpi pariṇāmitvāt // MrgTV_1,5.12:3
children.translated_text: By this, what was stated as 'making the powers of <s>Māyā</s> fit for manifestation' is also elucidated, since that [<s>Māyā</s>] too undergoes transformation.

children.text: * na caiṣāṃ malamāyākarmaṇāṃ pariṇāmakatvamanīśena suśakamityuktam // MrgTV_1,5.12:4
children.translated_text: And it has been said that the transformation of these — <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and <s>karma</s> (action) — is not easily accomplished without a Lord (<s>īśa</s>).

children.text: * īśatīty aduṣṭam īśa ivācarati iti sarvaprātipadikebhya ityeke iti kvipaḥ smaraṇāt // MrgTV_1,5.12:5
children.translated_text: '<s>Īśa</s>' — [the word] is formed from the root '<s>īś</s>' meaning 'to be capable' [with the <s>kvip</s> suffix]; or it means 'one who behaves like a lord,' by [the rule that suffixes are applicable] to all nominal stems — so say some — since the <s>kvip</s> suffix is remembered [in grammar].

children.text: * tadiyatā tāvatsarvakartṛtvaṃ parameśvarasya pratipāditam // MrgTV_1,5.12:6
children.translated_text: Thus far, the omnipotent agency (<s>sarvakartṛtva</s>) of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) has been demonstrated.

children.text: * ata eva cāsya sarvajñatvaṃ sidhyatītyāha // MrgTV_1,5.12:7
children.translated_text: And from this very fact, his omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) is also established — he says:

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvakartṛtvāt sādhanāṅgaphalaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: He is omniscient because of his omnipotent agency, together with the means, auxiliaries, and fruits.

children.text: yo yaj jānāti kurute sa tadeveti susthitam || MrgT_1,5.13 ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows whatever he does — that is well established.

children.text: * sarvakartṛtvād eveśvarasya sarvajñatvaṃ sarvaviṣayajñānaṃ vinā sarvakartṛtānupapatteḥ // MrgTV_1,5.13:1
children.translated_text: From the omnipotent agency of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) alone follows his omniscience — knowledge of all objects — because omnipotent agency is untenable without it.

children.text: * yo hi yadyatkriyāsiddhiṃ tadaṅgāni tatphalāni ca jānāti tasyaiva vicitratattatkārakopayogābhisaṃdhānavatas tattatkartṛtvaṃ ghaṭate kuvindāderiva paṭādikṛtau // MrgTV_1,5.13:2
children.translated_text: For indeed, whoever knows the accomplishment of each and every action, its auxiliaries, and its fruits — for him alone, who has the intention of employing the various appropriate instruments for each respective action, is the agency for each respective action tenable — just as for a weaver and the like in producing cloth and so forth.

children.text: * ato yastu tatrājñaḥ sa tatkāryakaraṇāya nālaṃ bāliśa iva nyāyavidyādyupanyāsa ityetatsusthitamityavyabhicārīti // MrgTV_1,5.13:3
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who is ignorant of a thing is not capable of producing that effect — like an ignorant person in the exposition of logic and the like. This is 'well established' — meaning invariable.

children.text: tac cāsyāvṛtiśūnyatvān na vyañjakamapekṣate /
children.translated_text: And his [omniscience], because of the absence of obstruction, does not depend on a revealer.

children.text: tan na sāṃśayikaṃ tasmādviparītaṃ na jātucit || MrgT_1,5.14 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is never doubtful, nor ever erroneous.

children.text: * śivasya tat sarvajñatvam anādyāvaraṇaśūnyatvān na vyañjakāpekṣam nāpi saṃsāriṇa iva saṃśayaviparyayānadhyavasāyayuktam ata eva hetoḥ // MrgTV_1,5.14:1
children.translated_text: The omniscience of <s>Śiva</s>, because of the absence of beginningless obstruction, does not depend on a revealer; nor is it, like that of a worldly being (<s>saṃsārin</s>), accompanied by doubt, error, or non-determination — for this very reason.

children.text: * tathāhi // MrgTV_1,5.14:2
children.translated_text: For indeed:

children.text: yāni vyañjakamīkṣante vṛtatvān malaśaktibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those [cognitions] that look for a revealer, because they are veiled by the powers of impurity (<s>mala</s>) —

children.text: vyañjakasyānurodhena tāni syur vyāhatānyapi || MrgT_1,5.15 ||
children.translated_text: depending on the revealer, they may even be contradicted.

children.text: * yāni kila jñānāni malaśaktyāvṛtatvādbhoganiṣpādanāya vyañjakaṃ kalādyapekṣante tāni vyañjakasya kalādeḥ svalpaprakāśakaraṇāt tathāvidhavyañjanabhāji jñeyaviṣaye vyāghātavantyapi bhavanti // MrgTV_1,5.15:1
children.translated_text: Those cognitions which, because they are veiled by the power of impurity (<s>mala</s>), require a manifesting agent such as <s>kalā</s> and the rest for the accomplishment of experience — since the manifesting agent <s>kalā</s> and the rest produce only a small degree of illumination, those cognitions, though participating in such manifestation, may also be obstructed with respect to their knowable objects.

children.text: * na caiśvaraṃ jñānamevaṃvidhaṃ pūrvoktādevāvṛtiśūnyatvāt kāraṇāt // MrgTV_1,5.15:2
children.translated_text: But the knowledge of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is not of this kind, for the previously stated reason of being devoid of such veiling.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ śrīkiraṇe /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said in the glorious <s>Kiraṇāgama</s>:

children.text: * anādimalamuktatvātsarvajño'sau tataḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Because of being free from beginningless impurity (<s>mala</s>), he is omniscient; therefore he is <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,5.15:3
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * yataścaivamataḥ // MrgTV_1,5.15:4
children.translated_text: And since this is so, therefore:

children.text: nādhyakṣaṃ nāpi tallaiṅgaṃ na śābdamapi śāṃkaram /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (the Auspicious One) shines forth — neither perceptual, nor inferential based on that,

children.text: jñānamābhāti vimalaṃ sarvadā sarvavastuṣu || MrgT_1,5.16 ||
children.translated_text: nor verbal — immaculate, always, with respect to all objects.

children.text: * akṣasavyapekṣaṃ hi jñānaṃ pratyakṣamakṣavyāpāraṇāt tadabhāve'bhāvāt tadbhāve bhāvānuvidhāyitvāc ca vyāhatamapi syāt // MrgTV_1,5.16:1
children.translated_text: For knowledge that depends on the senses is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>); since it operates through the functioning of the senses, it would be absent in their absence, and would conform to their presence — hence it may also be obstructed.

children.text: * na caivaṃ śāmbhavaṃ jñānamato na pratyakṣam nāpyānumānikaṃ tasya pratyakṣādhīnavṛttitvāt śābdatvaṃ tu dūrāpāstam atyantaparokṣārthaviṣayatvāt tasya // MrgTV_1,5.16:2
children.translated_text: But the knowledge of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) is not like this, therefore it is not perceptual; nor is it inferential, since inference depends on perception for its functioning; and verbal knowledge (<s>śābda</s>) is far removed, because the Lord's knowledge pertains to objects that are supremely beyond [sense perception].

children.text: * na ca kiṃcidbhagavataḥ parokṣamataḥ sarvaviṣayaṃ tasya jñānaṃ prakāśate // MrgTV_1,5.16:3
children.translated_text: And nothing is beyond the cognition of the Blessed One; therefore his knowledge illuminates all objects.

children.text: * nanu /
children.translated_text: But [one may object]:

children.text: * pañcavaktrastripañcadṛk /
children.translated_text: 'Five-faced, having fifteen eyes' —

children.text: * ityādinā śrūyata evāgameṣvīśvarasya śarīrendriyayogaḥ tatsadbhāve'pi kasmān na tatsavyapekṣe īśvarasya jñānakriye // MrgTV_1,5.16:4
children.translated_text: thus in the <s>āgamas</s> the Lord's connection with body and sense organs is indeed heard; when these exist, why should <s>Īśvara</s>'s knowledge and action not depend on them?

children.text: * nāsya jñānakriyopayogī śarīrendriyayogaḥ svabhāvata eva sarvārthakriyā śaktimattvādicchāmātreṇaiva sargasthityādikaraṇakṣamatvāt // MrgTV_1,5.16:5
children.translated_text: His connection with body and sense organs is not serviceable for his knowledge and action, because by his very nature he possesses the power to accomplish all purposes, and because he is capable of performing creation, maintenance, and the rest by mere will (<s>icchā</s>) alone.

children.text: * bhaktānugrahaṇārthaṃ cākāragrahaṇamanyathā nirākāre dhyānapūjādyayogāt // MrgTV_1,5.16:6
children.translated_text: The assumption of form is for the sake of granting grace to devotees; otherwise, for one who is formless, meditation, worship, and the like would be impossible.

children.text: * yaduktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare /
children.translated_text: As has been stated in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s> [āgama]:

children.text: * sādhakasya tu lakṣyārthaṃ tasya rūpamidaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of the practitioner's (<s>sādhaka</s>'s) contemplation, this form of his has been declared —

children.text: * sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato 'kṣiśiromukham // MrgTV_1,5.16:7
children.translated_text: with hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,5.16:8
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: tadekaṃ viṣayānantyādbhedānantyaṃ prapadyate /
children.translated_text: That one [knowledge], because of the infinity of objects, attains infinite divisions;

children.text: kartṛtvaṃ tadabhinnatvāttadvadevopacārataḥ || MrgT_1,5.17 ||
children.translated_text: agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>), because of its non-difference from that [knowledge], is likewise [infinite] figuratively.

children.text: * yathāvasthitavastvavabhāsātmanas tāvattadīyasyaikasya jñānasya jñeyānantyād upādhibhedāt kṛtamaupacārikamānantyam śāstrātmano'pi srotobhedādadhyetṛbhedāt pravartayitṛbhedāt // MrgTV_1,5.17:1
children.translated_text: As for the one knowledge belonging to him, which has the nature of illuminating objects as they are — its figurative infinity is produced by the infinity of knowable objects and by the differences of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>); and even for [knowledge] in the form of scripture, [there is figurative infinity] due to differences of streams [of transmission], differences of students, and differences of promulgators.

children.text: * teṣāṃ ca parāparatvād gauṇamevānantyam // MrgTV_1,5.17:2
children.translated_text: And because of the relative superiority and inferiority among these, the infinity is only figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>).

children.text: * sarvajñānakriyārūpā śaktirekaivaśūlinaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.17:3
children.translated_text: 'The single power of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śūlin</s>), whose form is all knowledge and action' —

children.text: * ityanayā dṛśā tasmāj jñānādabhinnatvātkartṛtvamapi tathaivopacārādānantyaṃ pratipadyate // MrgTV_1,5.17:4
children.translated_text: in accordance with this perspective, therefore, agency too, because of its non-difference from that knowledge, likewise attains figurative infinity.

children.text: * atha nirvarṇitopasaṃhārāya vyākhyeyopakṣepāya cāyaṃ ślokaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.17:5
children.translated_text: Now, this verse serves to conclude what has been described and to introduce what is to be explained:

children.text: sattāsvarūpakaraṇārthavidheyadṛgbhir leśoditābhiriti ye vidurīśatattvam /
children.translated_text: Those who know the truth of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) through [the five aspects of] existence, essential nature, instrument, purpose, activity, and knowledge, set forth in brief —

children.text: te mocayanti bhavino bhavapaṅkamagnān no vistareṇa puruṣāḥ paśupāśarūpam || MrgT_1,5.18 ||
children.translated_text: they liberate beings sunk in the mire of worldly existence; not [those who know] in detail the nature of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) or of the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>).

children.text: * athopalabhya dehādi vastu kāryatvadharmakam /
children.translated_text: 'Now, perceiving the body and other entities as possessing the property of being effects,

children.text: * kartāramasya jānīmaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.18:1
children.translated_text: we know their maker' —

children.text: * ityādinā tāvadīśvarasya sattā sādhitā // MrgTV_1,5.18:2
children.translated_text: by this [verse], first the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> was established.

children.text: * nityaṃ kālānavacchedādvaitatyān na pradeśagam /
children.translated_text: 'Eternal, because not limited by time; because of ubiquity, not confined to place;

children.text: * kramākramasamutpatteḥ kramādyutpattiśaktimat // MrgTV_1,5.18:3
children.translated_text: because of producing both successive and simultaneous [effects], possessing the power to produce successive and other [effects]' —

children.text: * iti tatsvarūpamuktam // MrgTV_1,5.18:4
children.translated_text: by this, his essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) was stated.

children.text: * karaṇaṃ ca na śaktyanyacchaktir nācetanā citaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.18:5
children.translated_text: 'And the instrument is nothing other than <s>Śakti</s> (power); and <s>Śakti</s> is not unconscious, being [a power] of consciousness (<s>cit</s>)' —

children.text: * ityanena karaṇaṃ kathitam // MrgTV_1,5.18:6
children.translated_text: by this, the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) was described.

children.text: * viniyogaphalaṃ muktirbhuktir apyanuṣaṅgataḥ // MrgTV_1,5.18:7
children.translated_text: 'The fruit of the application is liberation (<s>mukti</s>); enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) also incidentally' —

children.text: * ityamunārthaḥ prayojanamupavarṇitam // MrgTV_1,5.18:8
children.translated_text: by this, the purpose (<s>artha</s>), the goal, was described.

children.text: * jagajjanmasthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvavimuktayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Creation, maintenance, destruction, concealment, and liberation of the world —

children.text: * kṛtyam // MrgTV_1,5.18:9
children.translated_text: the activity (<s>kṛtya</s>)' —

children.text: * ityanena pañcavidhaṃ vidheyamuktam // MrgTV_1,5.18:10
children.translated_text: by this, the fivefold activity (<s>vidheya</s>) was stated.

children.text: * dṛkca asya jñānam /
children.translated_text: And his vision (<s>dṛk</s>), that is, knowledge —

children.text: * nādhyakṣaṃ nāpi tallaiṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'neither perceptual, nor inferential based on that' —

children.text: * ityādinā nirṇītamiti // MrgTV_1,5.18:11
children.translated_text: by this and what follows, it was determined.

children.text: * etābhiḥ sattāsvarūpakaraṇārthavidheyadṛgbhiḥ saṃkṣepoktābhir īśatattvaṃ ye viduḥ jānanti te puruṣāḥ saṃsārakardamanimagnān saṃsāriṇo mocayanti na tu vistareṇa paśurūpaṃ pāśarūpaṃ vā īśvaraṃ ye viduḥ yathā // MrgTV_1,5.18:12
children.translated_text: Those persons who know the truth of <s>Īśvara</s> through these [five aspects of] existence, essential nature, instrument, purpose, activity, and knowledge, set forth in brief — they liberate beings sunk in the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). But not [those who know] in detail the nature of the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) or the nature of the <s>pāśa</s> (bonds) as <s>Īśvara</s>, such as:

children.text: * ātmaivedaṃ sarvam /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>ātman</s> (self) alone is all this;'

children.text: * puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam // MrgTV_1,5.18:13
children.translated_text: '<s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit) alone is all this.'

children.text: * ityevaṃvidhapuruṣarūpeśvaravādinaḥ karmakālāvyaktādipāśarūpeśvaravādino vā paśūnāṃ svayam evānādyajñānanimagnatvenākiṃcitkaratvāt pāśānāṃ ca tatpāśana eva caritārthatvāt tattatsaṃyoge viyogādau vā nigalādivat parāpekṣatve satyanīśvaratvāt // MrgTV_1,5.18:14
children.translated_text: Thus, those who proclaim <s>Īśvara</s> in the form of <s>puruṣa</s>, or those who proclaim <s>Īśvara</s> in the form of bonds such as <s>karma</s>, time, the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), and the like — because bound souls (<s>paśu</s>), being themselves sunk in beginningless ignorance, are incapable of anything; and because the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) have fulfilled their purpose in the very binding [of souls]; and because when it comes to joining and separating [souls with bonds], like fetters, they require dependence on another and are thus not lordly —

children.text: * tathāvidheśvarāvabodhāt paramocanaṃ sakalalokopahāsāvahaṃ yataḥ // MrgTV_1,5.18:15
children.translated_text: the claim of supreme liberation through the understanding of such a [false] <s>Īśvara</s> invites the ridicule of all the worlds.

children.text: * paśuśabdaścātra samanantaraprakaraṇopakramyamāṇātmatattvopakṣepāyopahṛtaḥ // MrgTV_1,5.18:16
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>paśu</s>' (bound soul) here is introduced to anticipate the topic of the <s>ātma-tattva</s> (the principle of the self) to be commenced in the immediately following section.

children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 6
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> (Knowledge Section), Chapter 6

children.text: atha viśvanimittasya prāptaṃ lakṣaṇamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the characterization of the <s>ātman</s> (self), which is the cause of the universe, has been reached;

children.text: tadīśoktau gataprāyaṃ tathāpyuddeśa ucyate || MrgT_1,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: it was mostly covered in the discussion of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord); nevertheless, a summary is stated.

children.text: * athedānīṃ pāścātyapaṭalāntasūcitābhidhānasyātmano lakṣaṇamucyata iti pāṭalikaprākaraṇikau sambandhau jñeyau // MrgTV_1,6.1:1
children.translated_text: Now, the characterization of the <s>ātman</s>, whose description was indicated at the end of the preceding chapter, is being stated — the connections both to the chapter and to the section should be understood.

children.text: * sautrādayastu prāgvadunneyāḥ pratipaṭalamucyamānā atipaunaruktyamāvahanti // MrgTV_1,6.1:2
children.translated_text: But the connections pertaining to the <s>sūtra</s> and the rest should be inferred as before; stating them for each chapter would cause excessive repetition.

children.text: * viśvasya jagato nimittaṃ pravartanaheturātmā tadbhogasādhanāya tanukaraṇabhuvanādīnāmutpatteḥ // MrgTV_1,6.1:3
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> is the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) of the universe, the cause that sets it in motion, because for the sake of its experience, the production of bodies, organs, worlds, and the like takes place.

children.text: * tasyātmano lakṣaṇamīśvaroktyanantaram avasaraprāptaṃ kathyate // MrgTV_1,6.1:4
children.translated_text: The characterization of that <s>ātman</s>, which arises as appropriate after the discussion of <s>Īśvara</s>, is being stated.

children.text: * tac ca yadyapi /
children.translated_text: And even though —

children.text: * tena svabhāvasiddhena bhavitavyaṃ jagatkṛtā // MrgTV_1,6.1:5
children.translated_text: 'By that [Lord], who is the maker of the world, it must be that he is established by his own nature' —

children.text: * ityatra īśvarasiddhyanuṣaṅgeṇa // MrgTV_1,6.1:6
children.translated_text: in this [verse], incidentally to the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s>,

children.text: * caitanyaṃ dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tadastyātmani sarvadā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness), in the form of vision and action, always exists in the <s>ātman</s>,

children.text: * sarvataśca yato muktau śrūyate sarvatomukham // MrgTV_1,6.1:7
children.translated_text: and [it is] all-pervasive, since in liberation it is heard to be omnidirectional' —

children.text: * ityādinoktaprāyaṃ kathitakalpaṃ tathāpyuddeśaḥ sopapattikatatsvarūpasaṃkṣepa ucyate // MrgTV_1,6.1:8
children.translated_text: by this and other [verses] it was mostly stated, that is, nearly fully described — nevertheless, a summary of its essential nature together with reasoning is stated.

children.text: kāryaṃ kṣityādi karteśastatkartur nopayujyate /
children.translated_text: The earth and the like are effects; their maker is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord); [the world] is not useful to that maker,

children.text: na svārthamapyacidbhāvān nānarthyaṃ kartṛgauravāt || MrgT_1,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: nor for its own sake, because of being non-conscious; nor is it purposeless, because of the dignity of the maker.

children.text: * kāryatvaṃ tāvatkṣityādereva saṃniveśādimattvena prāk kathitam // MrgTV_1,6.2:1
children.translated_text: First, the status of the earth and the rest as effects was stated earlier by virtue of their possessing specific arrangement and the like.

children.text: * tasya ca kartā prāguktābhiryuktibhirīśaḥ siddhaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.2:2
children.translated_text: And the maker of that [world] has been established as <s>Īśvara</s> by the arguments stated previously.

children.text: * tattu kāryaṃ tadupayogi vā syāt svopayogi anupayogi anyopayogi veti catvāraḥ pakṣāḥ // MrgTV_1,6.2:3
children.translated_text: But that effect — it may be useful to him [the maker], useful to itself, useful to no one, or useful to another — these are the four alternatives.

children.text: * tatra na tāvadīśvaropayogi nahi pṛthivyādibhistasya svātmanyarthakriyā kācitkriyate nityaparipūrṇasvarūpatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.2:4
children.translated_text: Among these, first, it is not useful to <s>Īśvara</s>, for the earth and the like do not serve any purpose for him in his own self, since his essential nature is eternally complete.

children.text: * na ca tat kṣityādi kāryaṃ kṣityādyarthameva kriyate teṣāmācaitanyāt karaṇīyasyābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,6.2:5
children.translated_text: Nor is the effect of earth and the like made for the sake of the earth and the rest themselves, because they are non-conscious and have nothing to be accomplished.

children.text: * cetanasya hi dharmādicaturvargaprepsoḥ karaṇīyaṃ sambhavati na paṭādeḥ // MrgTV_1,6.2:6
children.translated_text: For it is a conscious being, desirous of the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) beginning with <s>dharma</s>, that can have something to accomplish — not a cloth and the like.

children.text: * na caitat kāryamanarthakaṃ kartṛgauravāt // MrgTV_1,6.2:7
children.translated_text: Nor is this effect purposeless, because of the dignity of the maker.

children.text: * sāmānyenāpi kartrā yatkāryaṃ kriyate tan nānarthakaṃ bhavati kiṃ punaḥ parameśvaravyāpāritair jagatkartṛbhirbrahmādibhiḥ // MrgTV_1,6.2:8
children.translated_text: Even an ordinary maker does not produce a purposeless effect — how much less so [the effects produced by] <s>Brahmā</s> and others who are the world-creators engaged by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord)?

children.text: * tatkāryakaraṇe ca na prayojanaṃ prāk pradarśitam // MrgTV_1,6.2:9
children.translated_text: And the purpose in making that effect was demonstrated earlier.

children.text: * tat kṣityādi kāryam // MrgTV_1,6.3:1
children.translated_text: That effect of earth and the like —

children.text: * kaścātra para ityāha // MrgTV_1,6.3:2
children.translated_text: who is this 'other' [for whose sake it is made]? He says:

children.text: pāriśeṣyātparārthaṃ tat kṣetrajñaḥ sa parastayoḥ /
children.translated_text: By the method of elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), it is for the sake of another; that [other] is the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field), who is distinct from both of those —

children.text: * kartṛkāryayoḥ paro'nyaḥ prastutābhidhānaḥ kṣetrajño yaś cātmetyarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.3ab:1
children.translated_text: distinct from both the maker and the effect, the 'other' who has been mentioned is the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, who is the <s>ātman</s> (self) — this is the meaning.

children.text: * atra cārvākacchāyayā ātmanirāsāyedam āśaṅkyate // MrgTV_1,6.3ab:2
children.translated_text: Here, following the shadow of <s>Cārvāka</s> [materialism], the following objection is raised for the purpose of denying the <s>ātman</s>:

children.text: paro dehastadarthatvātparārthāḥ kṣmādayo nanu || MrgT_1,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: The 'other' is the body; since the [elements] serve it, are not the earth and the like for the sake of another [i.e., the body]?

children.text: * nanūpalabhyamānaprayojanānāṃ kṣityādīnāṃ parārthatvamastu sa tv atra paraḥ kāya eva yasyārambhakāś copayoginaśca pṛthivyaptejovāyavaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.3cd:1
children.translated_text: Let the earth and the like, whose purpose is observed, be for the sake of another — but that 'other' here is the body itself, for which the elements earth, water, fire, and air are the originators and the servants.

children.text: * tasmān na kṣityādīnāṃ parārthatvenātmanāmanumānam // MrgTV_1,6.3cd:2
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no inference of the <s>ātman</s> from the fact that the earth and the like are for the sake of another.

children.text: * atrottaraṃ // MrgTV_1,6.3cd:3
children.translated_text: To this, the reply:

children.text: kāyo 'py acittvādānyārthyaṃ sutarāṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: The body too, because of being non-conscious, all the more attains the status of being for the sake of another.

children.text: * deho'pi parārtha eva ācaitanyāt pṛthivyādivaditi tasyāpy ānyārthyaṃ pārārthyaṃ sutarāmupapadyate // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:1
children.translated_text: The body too is for the sake of another, because of its non-consciousness, just like the earth and the like — hence its being for the sake of another is all the more established.

children.text: * tataśca dehasya kṣityādīnāṃ ca parārthatvātpara ātmaivātra yuktyupapannaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:2
children.translated_text: And therefore, since both the body and the earth and the like are for the sake of another, the 'other' that is the <s>ātman</s> alone is reasonable here, supported by argument.

children.text: * nanu dehādanyatra yadi caitanyaṃ syāt syādetadevam // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:3
children.translated_text: But if consciousness existed somewhere other than the body, then this would indeed be so.

children.text: * pṛthvyādicaturbhūtavikārake prāṇādikāraṇībhūte garbhādau saṃvidudbhavaḥ kiṇvādidravyavikāre bhavaśaktyutpattivat // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:4
children.translated_text: In the embryo and the like, which is a transformation of the four gross elements beginning with earth, and which becomes the cause [of consciousness] through <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, consciousness arises — just as the power of intoxication arises in the transformation of substances such as yeast and the like.

children.text: * tathāhi kṛśo'haṃ sthūlo'hamiti śarīra evāhaṃpratyayo dṛṣṭaḥ na ca tadvyatirikta ātmā upalabhyate dehe'styātmā ityasya aśve viṣāṇamityādivat pratyakṣanirākṛtatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:5
children.translated_text: For thus: 'I am thin,' 'I am fat' — the I-cognition (<s>aham-pratyaya</s>) is observed with reference to the body alone; and no <s>ātman</s> distinct from it is apprehended. The claim 'there is an <s>ātman</s> in the body' is like 'there are horns on a horse' — refuted by perception.

children.text: * atha parārthāścakṣurādayaḥ saṃghātatvāt śayanādyaṅgavadityādinā karaṇādīnāṃ kartṛprayojyatvādinā vā anumānenātmā prasādhyate na tadyuktaṃ tasyātmāpalāpinaścārvākān pratyasiddheḥ // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:6
children.translated_text: Now, if the <s>ātman</s> is to be established by the inference 'the eyes and other [organs] are for the sake of another, because they form an aggregate, like the parts of a bed' and similar [arguments], or by the inference that the organs and the like are directed by an agent — that is not valid, because for the <s>Cārvākas</s> who deny the <s>ātman</s>, [inference itself] is unestablished [as a means of knowledge].

children.text: * nahy eṣāṃ pratyakṣād anyatkiṃcit pramāṇaṃ siddhāv api vā anumīyamānasyātmano devadattādivatparatvaṃ prasajyate // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:7
children.translated_text: For these [Cārvākas] accept no means of knowledge other than perception; and even if the <s>ātman</s> were inferred, the consequence would be that it is 'other' like <s>Devadatta</s> and the rest [i.e., a separate entity].

children.text: * yatkila svayaṃ prakāśate sa evātmā tatprakāśyastu para iti viviktatayā ātmaparabhāvasya prakāśamānasyaiva saṃkaro'navasthānaṃ ca syāt // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:8
children.translated_text: For what shines by itself — that alone is the <s>ātman</s>; what is illuminated by it is the 'other.' But since the distinction of self and other manifests only as illuminated [by consciousness], there would be intermixture [of self and other] and instability.

children.text: * taduktam /
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: * ātmā yadi bhavenmeyastasya mātā bhavetparaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If the <s>ātman</s> were an object of knowledge, then its knower would be the other;

children.text: * para ātmā tadānīṃ syātsa paro yastu mīyate // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:9
children.translated_text: the <s>ātman</s> would then be the other — for 'other' is that which is measured.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:10
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: * prakāśate saṃvidekā tadanyattu prakāśyate /
children.translated_text: 'Awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) alone shines of itself; whatever is other than it is illuminated [by it];

children.text: * prakāśyaṃ ca bhavetkarma tac ca kartrā vinā katham // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:11
children.translated_text: and what is illuminated would be the object (<s>karma</s>) — and how can that exist without an agent (<s>kartṛ</s>)?'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:12
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * tasmān nānumānena dehavyatirikta ātmā upalabhyate apitu caitanyaviśiṣṭaḥ kāya eva vastusann ityāśaṅkayāha // MrgTV_1,6.4ab1:13
children.translated_text: Therefore, an <s>ātman</s> distinct from the body is not apprehended through inference; rather, the body itself, characterized by consciousness, is a real entity — to address this objection, he says:

children.text: * atha manyase kāya eva cetanātmakaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.4ab2:1
children.translated_text: Now, if you think that the body itself has the nature of consciousness —

children.text: * tathāhi yasminnupacite yasyopacayaḥ yadapacaye ca apacayaḥ tattadātmakaṃ yathā vahnyupacayāpacayayor upacayāpacayāv anugacchedauṣṇyam // MrgTV_1,6.4ab2:2
children.translated_text: for thus: that which grows when that [the body] grows, and that which diminishes when that diminishes — that has the nature of that [the body]; just as heat, which follows the increase and decrease of fire, [has the nature of fire].

children.text: * yauvanasthāvirabhojanalaṅghanādihetukau ca dehasambandhināv upacayāpacayāv anukurvadvijñānaṃ dehātmakameva ato deha eva cetana iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.4ab2:3
children.translated_text: And growth and decline, which belong to the body and are caused by youth, old age, eating, fasting, and the like — the consciousness that follows these is of the nature of the body itself. Therefore the body alone is conscious — this is the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

children.text: * athaitatpratikṣepaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.4ab2:4
children.translated_text: Now, the refutation of this:

children.text: cetanaścet na bhogyatvādvikāritvāc ca jātucit || MrgT_1,6.4 ||
children.translated_text: If [the body is said to be] conscious — no, because it is an object of enjoyment, and because it undergoes modification —

children.text: bhogyā vikāriṇo dṛṣṭāścidvihīnāḥ paṭādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: cloth and the like are seen to be objects of enjoyment and subject to modification, and they are devoid of consciousness.

children.text: * so 'pyevaṃ dehaścetanaḥ kadācin na bhavati bhogyatvādvikāritvāc ca // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:1
children.translated_text: That body too is never conscious, because it is an object of enjoyment and because it undergoes modification.

children.text: * ye ye kecana vikāriṇaḥ pariṇāmino bhogyāśca te te hy acetanā dṛṣṭāḥ yathā paṭādayaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:2
children.translated_text: Whatever things are subject to modification and transformation, and are objects of enjoyment — all those are seen to be unconscious, like cloth and the like.

children.text: * sa deho'pyevaṃvidhaḥ tasmān na cetanaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:3
children.translated_text: The body too is of this kind; therefore it is not conscious.

children.text: * nanv aṅganādibhir bhogyatvamanaikāntikaṃ bhogyatve'pi tatrācaitanyābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:4
children.translated_text: Now, [if it is objected that] the reason of being an object of enjoyment is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) because of women and the like — since even though they are objects of enjoyment, there is no absence of consciousness in them —

children.text: * nānaikāntikaṃ tadīyasya dehasyaiva bhogyatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:5
children.translated_text: It is not inconclusive, because it is only their body that is the object of enjoyment.

children.text: * yadyevaṃ nirjīvasya dehasya kathaṃ nopabhogaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:6
children.translated_text: If so, why is there no enjoyment of a lifeless body?

children.text: * bhavatyeva tadavasthocita upabhogaḥ kravyādādeḥ na punaḥ kāntādeḥ kāminyādyavasthāyā yenāvasthāntarāpatter vikāritvena bībhatsarasahetutvāt // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:7
children.translated_text: There is indeed enjoyment appropriate to that state — by flesh-eating animals and the like; but not by a lover and so forth, because it has passed into another state and, being subject to modification, causes the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) of disgust.

children.text: * taduktir atraiva /
children.translated_text: The expression of this is found here itself:

children.text: * kva tadvaktraṃ kva tadadharamadhu kvāyatākṣyāḥ kaṭākṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where is that face? Where is the nectar of those lips? Where is the sidelong glance of that long-eyed one?' —

children.text: * ityādi // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:8
children.translated_text: and so forth.

children.text: * evaṃ gajāśvādāv api jñeyam // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:9
children.translated_text: The same should be understood in the case of elephants, horses, and the like.

children.text: * tasmāt sthitametat vikāritvādbhogyatvāc ca dehasyācaitanyam ācaitanyāc ca pārārthyamiti // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:10
children.translated_text: Therefore it is established that the body is unconscious because of being subject to modification and because of being an object of enjoyment; and because of being unconscious, it exists for the sake of another.

children.text: * punarapi paramatam āśaṅkate // MrgTV_1,6.5ab1:11
children.translated_text: Again he raises the opponent's view:

children.text: * yasminsati yasya bhāvo yadabhāve cābhāvastat tatkāryaṃ śītamiva himasya // MrgTV_1,6.5ab2:1
children.translated_text: When something is present and [another] exists [because of it], and when that [first thing] is absent and [the second] is absent — that [second] is the effect of the first, like cold is of snow.

children.text: * sati ca śukraśauṇitātmakadehārambhakabhūtaviśeṣapariṇāme sattvādasati ca pradhvaste tasminnasattvāc caitanyaṃ bhūtaviśeṣapariṇāmakṛtamiti vā yady aveṣi // MrgTV_1,6.5ab2:2
children.translated_text: If you hold that when the transformation of the special elements constituting the body made of semen and blood is present, consciousness exists, and when that [body] is destroyed and [those elements are] absent, consciousness is absent — and therefore consciousness is produced by the transformation of the special elements —

children.text: * tadetadanupapannaṃ yasmāt // MrgTV_1,6.5ab2:3
children.translated_text: this too is untenable, because:
