children.text: yasminsati ca sattvādvā na satyapi śave citiḥ || MrgT_1,6.5 ||
children.translated_text: Even if [consciousness supposedly exists] because of [the body's] presence — even when a corpse is present, there is no consciousness.

children.text: * yatsadbhāva eva yasya bhāvastattasya kāryamiti niyamo'trāvaśyaṃ pratijñātavyo'nyathā tadabhāve'pi bhavatas tatkāryatvāyogāt yathāgnisadbhāva eva sambhavan dhūmo'gnikāryaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:1
children.translated_text: The rule that 'whatever exists only when something [else] is present is the effect of that' must necessarily be maintained [strictly]; otherwise, even in the absence of that [supposed cause], the status of being its effect would not hold — just as smoke, which occurs only in the presence of fire, is the effect of fire.

children.text: * evaṃ ca śarīrārambhakabhūtasadbhāva eva bhāvaḥ tadabhāve cābhāva eva caitanyasya yadi syāt taddehasambandhitayā pratīyeta // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:2
children.translated_text: And thus, if consciousness existed only in the presence of the elements constituting the body and were absent in their absence, then it would be apprehended as connected with the body.

children.text: * yāvatā śarīrasadbhāve'pi garbhādāv uttarakālaṃ ca cetanāpagamo dṛṣṭaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:3
children.translated_text: Whereas the departure of consciousness is observed even when the body is present — in the embryonic state and at later times [such as deep sleep and death].

children.text: * tan na sati sattvaṃ dehārambhakacaitanyasādhakam // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:4
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'existing when [the body] is present' does not establish that body-constituting elements produce consciousness.

children.text: * nanu mṛtaśarīre'pi prāṇādyātmakasya vāyorūṣmarūpasya ca tejaso'pagamān na jīvāvasthāyāmiva śarīrārambhakabhūtasadbhāvas tasmād atrācetanatvam yac ca tat sati sattvam anaikāntikīkartum aśaktam // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:5
children.translated_text: Now, [if it is argued that] even in a dead body, because of the departure of wind in the form of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest, and of fire in the form of heat, the body-constituting elements are not present as in the living state — therefore there is unconsciousness therein; and the [argument of] 'existing when present' cannot be rendered inconclusive —

children.text: * maivam // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:6
children.translated_text: Not so.

children.text: * gatāsavo'pi hi kecana calatsaṃdhayaḥ soṣmāṇaśca kiyantaṃ kālamupalabhyante // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:7
children.translated_text: For some who have died are observed for some time to have moving joints and warmth.

children.text: * teṣāṃ ca jīvadavasthāvad dehārambhakabhūtasadbhāve'pi na caitanyasambhavaḥ garbhāvasthāyāṃ ca sakalasāmagrīsadbhāve'pi kadācic caitanyāsaṃbhavaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:8
children.translated_text: And even though the body-constituting elements are present in them as in the living state, consciousness does not occur; and in the embryonic state too, even when all the constituents are present, consciousness sometimes does not occur.

children.text: * tasmātsati sattvamanaikāntikameva // MrgTV_1,6.5cd1:9
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'existing when present' is indeed inconclusive.

children.text: * nanu jīvadavasthāyāṃ pariṇāmavaiśiṣṭyāc caitanyasambhavas tathāvidhapariṇāmābhāvāt gatāsudehe tadabhāva iti punarapi cārvākabhūmikayaivāśaṅkyate // MrgTV_1,6.5cd:10
children.translated_text: Now, [if it is argued that] in the living state, consciousness occurs because of the distinctiveness of the transformation, and in the dead body there is absence [of consciousness] because such a transformation is absent — this is again objected from the very standpoint of the <s>Cārvāka</s> (materialist):

children.text: * kaumārayauvanādyavasthābhedād avāntaratattadavasthāviśeṣabhedena ca dehārambhakabhūtapariṇāmakṛtatattadvaiśiṣṭyāj jīvadavasthāyāṃ yac caitanyamasti tat tathāvidhabhūtapariṇāmakṛtatattadghaṭapaṭaśakaṭādyanekārthaprakāśakāni sakramāṇi hi vijñānāni pūrvapūrvanirodhe saty uttarottarāṇi pariṇāmavaiśiṣṭyādeva bhavanti nānyata iti na dehād anyac caitanyamiti codyam // MrgTV_1,6.5cd2: 1
children.translated_text: The consciousness that exists in the living state, arising from the respective distinctiveness produced by the transformation of the body-constituting elements due to differences in stages such as childhood, youth, and so forth, and due to differences in sub-states within each stage — those cognitions that illuminate various objects such as pots, cloths, carts, and so on, [arising] sequentially, each arising upon the cessation of the previous one, occur solely from the distinctiveness of the transformation and from nothing else — therefore consciousness is not different from the body. This is the objection.

children.text: * atra parihāraḥ // MrgTV_1,6.5cd2: 2
children.translated_text: Here is the refutation:

children.text: pariṇāmasya vaiśiṣṭyādasti cet na smṛtistadā /
children.translated_text: If [consciousness exists] because of the distinctiveness of transformation, then there would be no memory.

children.text: * tadeti pratyarthaṃ sakramasaṃvedanaviśeṣasya pariṇāmitvābhyupagame sati smṛtir nāvakalpate // MrgTV_1,6.6ab:1
children.translated_text: 'Then' (<s>tadā</s>) — if the acceptance of transformation is applied to the particular sequential awareness [arising] for each object, then memory cannot be accounted for,

children.text: * pariṇāmaviśeṣāṇāṃ kramabhāvināṃ bhinnatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.6ab:2
children.translated_text: because the distinctive stages of transformation, being sequential, are different [from each other],

children.text: * asaṃviditasyānyaviditasya cānyenāsmaraṇāt // MrgTV_1,6.6ab:3
children.translated_text: and because what has not been experienced [by oneself], or what has been experienced by another, cannot be remembered by yet another.

children.text: * nahy ananubhūtaṃ devadattānubhūtaṃ vā caitrādinā smartuṃ śakyam // MrgTV_1,6.6ab:4
children.translated_text: For indeed, what has not been experienced, or what has been experienced by <s>Devadatta</s>, cannot be remembered by <s>Caitra</s> and the like.

children.text: * evaṃ mā bhūt smṛtiḥ kiṃ naśchinnamiti cet tadapyayuktamityāha // MrgTV_1,6.6ab:5
children.translated_text: If [one says], 'Let there be no memory — what does it matter to us?' — even that is improper, he says:

children.text: nāpyevaṃ supratītatvāt smartā kāyetaro'styataḥ || MrgT_1,6.6 ||
children.translated_text: Nor [can it be] so, because [memory] is well-established; therefore there exists a rememberer other than the body.

children.text: * sakalalokaprasiddhasmṛtyapahnavas tāvan na śakyaḥ smṛtiś caivam upapadyate dehasyāsakṛtpariṇāmitve'pi ekasvabhāvas tadanyas tadarthasaṃnidhau tattajjñānasyānya evānubhavitā sa evānusaṃdhātā syāditi // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:1
children.translated_text: First of all, the denial of memory, which is well-known to all people, is impossible. And memory is accounted for in this way: even though the body undergoes repeated transformation, there is one entity of a single nature, other than it — when objects are presented to him, he alone, being the experiencer of each cognition, is also the one who recognizes [them later].

children.text: * ata ityasmāt smṛtyanyathānupapattilakṣaṇādapi hetordehādanyaḥ smartāstīti // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:2
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this very reason — characterized as the impossibility of memory being otherwise [explained] — there exists a rememberer other than the body.

children.text: * na ca vācyaṃ kimebhiḥ parānumānāsahiṣṇor vyarthair hetvādibhiriti yataś cārvākasyānicchorapi durgatasya daurgatyamiva balād evānumānaṃ khyātimanubadhnāti // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:3
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said, 'What use are these futile reasons and the like to one who cannot tolerate the inference of others?' — for even the <s>Cārvāka</s>, though unwilling, like poverty to the destitute, inference inevitably attaches itself to his repute.

children.text: * tathā hi tena pratyakṣaikapramāṇavādināpi caturmahābhūtavyatiriktatattvāntarānabhyupagame mṛtpāṣāṇādisthāvaralakṣaṇā pṛthivī jalādiś ca saraḥsaritsamudrādir nādṛṣṭasya guṇabhedena sarvaṃ pratyakṣeṇāvagāhituṃ śakyaṃ tasya pratiniyatavyaktihetutvenāśeṣajagadantargatapadārthaviṣayānvayagrahaṇākṣamatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:4
children.translated_text: For even he, who maintains that perception alone is the valid means of knowledge and does not accept any principle beyond the four great elements — earth in the form of stones and boulders, water in the form of lakes, rivers, and oceans — cannot apprehend everything through perception alone by differences in properties of the unseen; because [perception], having fixed individual causes, is incapable of grasping the universal connection pertaining to all objects within the entire world.

children.text: * api ca yatra kāṭhinyaṃ sā pṛthivī sthalopalaparvatādivat pṛthivītvābhāve kāṭhinyasyābhāvaś cābādāv iva yac ca dravasvarūpaṃ taj jalaṃ tailaghṛtakṣīrāder apy udakatvād ityādyanvayagrahaṇam anumānāṅgaṃ kalpanīyam // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:5
children.translated_text: Moreover, [statements like] 'wherever there is hardness, that is earth, as in solid ground, stones, and mountains; in the absence of earthness, hardness is absent, as in water and such; whatever has the nature of fluidity is water, because even oil, ghee, and milk have the nature of water' — such grasping of universal connection is an element of inference and must be constructed [through reasoning].

children.text: * dharmiṇi ca dehe pakṣīkṛte tadgatasya kāṭhinyādeḥ pṛthivyādidharmatvaniścayāt pṛthivyādibhūtacatuṣṭayārabdhatvamapi nānumānaṃ vināvagantuṃ śakyam // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:6
children.translated_text: And when the body is taken as the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), from the determination that hardness and the like belonging to it are properties of earth and so forth, even the fact that [the body] is composed of the four elements of earth and the rest cannot be known without inference.

children.text: * kiṃ ca pratyakṣameva pramāṇaṃ nānumānamiti pramāṇāpramāṇacintā nāsya pratyakṣaniśceyā // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:7
children.translated_text: Moreover, the inquiry into whether perception alone is a valid means of knowledge and inference is not — this itself cannot be determined by perception.

children.text: * yathāha dharmakīrtiḥ /
children.translated_text: As <s>Dharmakīrti</s> says:

children.text: * pramāṇetarasāmānyasthiter anyaviyogataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From the common persistence of valid means and non-valid means, and from the exclusion of others,

children.text: * pramāṇāntarasadbhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:8
children.translated_text: the existence of another means of valid knowledge [is established].'

children.text: * iti na paraṃ pratyasiddhatvam anumānasya // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:9
children.translated_text: Thus, it is not [the case] that inference is merely unestablished for the opponent.

children.text: * tatpratyāyanārthaṃ ceha pariśeṣānumānaṃ prakaraṇārambhe darśitaṃ na tu svasaṃvedanasiddhatvenāparokṣasyātmanaḥ sādhanāya tatra pramāṇāntarasyānupayogāt // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:10
children.translated_text: And the inference by elimination presented at the beginning of this section is for the purpose of demonstrating that [to others]; it is not for the purpose of proving the self, which is directly known (<s>aparokṣa</s>) as established through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), since another means of knowledge is of no use there.

children.text: * yad āhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: * anubhūtau pramāṇānāṃ pariniṣṭhā samāpyate /
children.translated_text: 'The culmination of valid means of knowledge is completed in experience (<s>anubhūti</s>);

children.text: * svatas tayaiva yā jñaptiḥ kiṃ tatrānyaiḥ pramāntaraiḥ // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:11
children.translated_text: the knowledge that arises from that by itself — what need is there for other means of knowledge?'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:12
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * gatametat // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:13
children.translated_text: This has been explained.

children.text: * yattu /
children.translated_text: Now as for [the verse]:

children.text: * pariṇāmasya vaiśiṣṭyādasti cen na smṛtistadā // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:14
children.translated_text: 'If [consciousness exists] because of the distinctiveness of transformation, then there would be no memory' —

children.text: * ity akhaṇḍanameva ślokārdhaṃ tad etac chivāvasthāyāṃ sūkṣmatarasaṃvedanasambhave'pi pariṇāmasya vaiśiṣṭyāditi smṛtyabhāvapratipādakatvena paramatāśaṅkayā vyākhyāya samādhīyate yaduta nāpyevaṃ supratītatvāt na hy evaṃ kvacitprasiddhaṃ yadgatāsoḥ sūkṣmatarasaṃvedanamasti smṛtistu nāstītyapitu supratītametat yan nirjīve vapuṣi kāṣṭhādāv iva saṃvin nāstyeveti tasmād dehād anyaḥ smartāstītyevamapi vyākhyāyamāne na kaściddoṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:15
children.translated_text: this half-verse is itself a complete refutation. It is also explainable [in another way]: even though in the state of <s>Śiva</s> a subtler awareness might exist, [the verse], having the import of establishing the absence of memory [under the materialist premise] through the objection 'if because of the distinctiveness of transformation,' is resolved by the [second] statement 'nor [can it be] so, because it is well-established.' For it is nowhere well-known that a dead [body] has subtler awareness but lacks memory; rather, what is well-established is that in a lifeless body, as in a log of wood, awareness simply does not exist. Therefore, there exists a rememberer other than the body — even when explained in this way, there is no fault.

children.text: * evaṃ paśupadārthaṃ prasādhya tadviśeṣān vaktum āha // MrgTV_1,6.6cd:16
children.translated_text: Having thus established the category of <s>paśu</s> (the bound soul), in order to state its specific characteristics, he says:

children.text: nāvyāpako na kṣaṇiko naiko nāpi jaḍātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: It [the soul] is not non-pervasive, not momentary, not single, nor of inert nature;

children.text: nākartā bhinnacidyogī pāśānte śivatāśruteḥ || MrgT_1,6.7 ||
children.translated_text: not a non-agent, and not one endowed with adventitious consciousness — because at the end of the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>), <s>Śivahood</s> is declared by scripture.

children.text: * sa cātmā nāvyāpakaḥ nāpi kṣaṇikaḥ deśakālābhyām anavacchinnatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.7:1
children.translated_text: And that self (<s>ātman</s>) is not non-pervasive, nor is it momentary, because it is not delimited by space or time.

children.text: * tadāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus they say:

children.text: * anavacchinnasadbhāvaṃ vastu yad deśakālataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That entity whose existence is not delimited by space or time —

children.text: * tan nityaṃ vibhu cecchantītyātmano vibhunityate // MrgTV_1,6.7:2
children.translated_text: that is eternal and pervasive, so they declare — hence the eternality and pervasiveness of the self.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,6.7:3
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * na cāsāv ekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is it single [in number];

children.text: * eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā /
children.translated_text: 'One Lord, the inner self of all beings' —

children.text: * iti pratipannānāṃ brahmavidāmiva janmamaraṇakaraṇādipratiniyamadarśanasya puruṣabahutvajñāpakasyāpahnotum aśakyatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.7:4
children.translated_text: even for the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> who accept [this], the observation of the fixed regulation of birth, death, organs, and the like, which indicates the plurality of selves (<s>puruṣas</s>), cannot be denied.

children.text: * na ca naiyāyikavaiśeṣikāṇāmiva jaḍaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.7:5
children.translated_text: Nor is it inert (<s>jaḍa</s>) as [held by] the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>.

children.text: * nāpi sāṃkhyānāmivākartā // MrgTV_1,6.7:6
children.translated_text: Nor is it a non-agent as [held by] the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>.

children.text: * na ca keṣāṃcidivāgantunā citā yuktaḥ // MrgTV_1,6.7:7
children.translated_text: Nor is it, as some hold, endowed with adventitious consciousness.

children.text: * kutaḥ ityāha pāśānte śivatāśruteḥ pāśānāmavidyādīnām ante tatpratibandhakatvavyapagame yato 'syātmanaḥ śivatvavyaktiḥ śrūyate // MrgTV_1,6.7:8
children.translated_text: Why? He says: 'Because at the end of the bonds, <s>Śivahood</s> is declared by scripture' — because when the bonds such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest come to an end, when their obstructive nature ceases, the manifestation of the <s>Śivahood</s> of this self is declared by scripture.

children.text: * tathā coktam /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said:

children.text: * athātmamalamāyākhyakarmabandhavimuktaye /
children.translated_text: 'Now, for the liberation from the bondage of impurity (<s>mala</s>), <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s> that [afflicts] the self,

children.text: * vyaktaye ca śivatvasya śivāj jñānaṃ pravartate // MrgTV_1,6.7:9
children.translated_text: and for the manifestation of <s>Śivahood</s>, knowledge proceeds from <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,6.7:10
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the quote].

children.text: * na ca tacchivatvam avyāpakatvādidharmayuktaṃ jñatvakartṛtvarahitaṃ vā // MrgTV_1,6.7:11
children.translated_text: And that <s>Śivahood</s> is not endowed with properties such as non-pervasiveness and the like, nor is it devoid of the capacity of knowing and acting.

children.text: * nityaṃ kālānavacchedād vaitatyān na pradeśagam // MrgTV_1,6.7:12
children.translated_text: 'Eternal, because it is not delimited by time; because of its vastness, it does not occupy a [single] location' —

children.text: * ityādinā pratyuta tadvilakṣaṇatvasyopapāditatvāt // MrgTV_1,6.7:13
children.translated_text: by such [earlier statements], the distinctness [of Śivahood from such properties] has been demonstrated.

children.text: * na ca vyāpakatvanityatvāder muktāv evodayāt saṃsāryavasthāyām abhāva iti mantavyam asadutpattyasambhavasyopapādayiṣyamāṇatvād iti // MrgTV_1,6.7:14
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought that pervasiveness, eternality, and the like, since they arise only in liberation, are absent in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage) — because the impossibility of the origination of what did not previously exist will be demonstrated.

children.text: Mṛgendratantra, Vidyāpāda, 7
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgendratantra</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> (Knowledge Section), Chapter 7

children.text: athāvidyādayaḥ pāśāḥ kathyante leśato'dhunā /
children.translated_text: Now the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are briefly described,

children.text: yeṣāmapāye patayo bhavanti jagato 'ṇavaḥ || MrgT_1,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: upon whose cessation the souls (<s>aṇus</s>) become lords (<s>patis</s>) of the world.

children.text: * atheti paśupadārthād anantaramavidyā ajñānamañjanamāṇavaḥ pāśa ādau yeṣāṃ te karmamāyārodhaśaktyākhyāḥ pāśāḥ adhunā idānīṃ leśataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ kathyante yeṣām apagame paśutvān muktvā aṇava ātmāno jagataḥ patayo bhavanti /
children.translated_text: 'Now' (<s>atha</s>) — immediately after the category of <s>paśu</s> (the bound soul): <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>ajñāna</s> (nescience), <s>añjana</s> (impurity), <s>āṇava</s> (the innate impurity) — the bond (<s>pāśa</s>) mentioned first among them; those called <s>karma</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and the obstructive power (<s>rodhaśakti</s>) — these bonds are now briefly described. Upon whose cessation — having been freed from the state of being bound souls (<s>paśutva</s>) — the souls (<s>aṇus</s>), the selves, become lords (<s>patis</s>) of the world.

children.text: * tatra śivavad anyānadhīnasvātantryābhivyaktir muktātmanāṃ patitvaṃ vidyeśvarādyadhikārabhājāṃ tu pañcavidhakṛtyakāritvam // MrgTV_1,7.1:1
children.translated_text: Therein, the lordship (<s>patitva</s>) of liberated souls consists in the manifestation of their self-dependent freedom, like <s>Śiva</s>; while for those who hold commissions such as the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and the rest, it consists in performing the fivefold activity.

children.text: * atha mukteḥ prāk kuto'vasīyate pāśitatvamaṇoriti cet jñānakriyayoḥ sarvārthatāvyāhateḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, if it is asked: how is it ascertained, prior to liberation, that the soul is bound by fetters (<s>pāśa</s>)? [The answer is:] because its powers of knowledge and action are obstructed from extending to all objects.

children.text: * anyathā hi // MrgTV_1,7.1:2
children.translated_text: For otherwise:

children.text: pāśābhāve pāratantryaṃ vaktavyaṃ kiṃnibandhanam /
children.translated_text: In the absence of bonds (<s>pāśa</s>), what is the basis for declaring the dependence [of the soul]?

children.text: svābhāvikaṃ cenmukteṣu muktaśabdo nivartate || MrgT_1,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: If it is inherent, then the word 'liberated' (<s>mukta</s>) would lose its applicability to liberated souls.

children.text: * pāśarahitasya hipuṃso na baddhatvam abaddhasya ca kiṃkṛtaṃ pāratantryaṃ yad anicchato 'py asyāniṣṭaprāptir iṣṭavyāghātaśca bhavati /
children.translated_text: For a person free from bonds is not bound; and for one who is not bound, what is the cause of that dependence — namely, that even against his will, he encounters the undesired and suffers the frustration of the desired?

children.text: * atha manyase nāsya tatpāratantryaṃ pāśakṛtam api tu svābhāvikam iti tarhi muktāṇuṣu muktaśabdasya nivṛttiḥ // MrgTV_1,7.2:1
children.translated_text: Now, if you think that this dependence is not caused by bonds but is inherent in nature, then the word 'liberated' would lose its applicability to liberated souls.

children.text: * vyapagatapāśe hi muktaśabdo loke prasiddhaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.2:2
children.translated_text: For in common usage, the word 'liberated' is well-known as applying to one whose bonds have been removed.

children.text: * etadeva ghaṭayann āha // MrgTV_1,7.2:3
children.translated_text: He elucidates this very point:

children.text: bandhaśūnyasya vaśitā dṛṣṭā baddhasya vaśyatā /
children.translated_text: One who is free from bondage is seen to have mastery; one who is bound has subjection.

children.text: etāvatī te baddhatvamuktatve baddhamuktayoḥ || MrgT_1,7.3 ||
children.translated_text: This much constitutes the bondage and liberation of the bound and the liberated.

children.text: * iyadeva tadbaddhasya baddhatvaṃ yatpāśitatve satyapāśitavaśyatā svatantraparameśvarāyattatvam ityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.3,1:1
children.translated_text: This alone is the bondage of the bound one — that in the presence of being fettered, there is subjection to the fetters, meaning dependence on the independent <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord).

children.text: * muktasya caitāvadeva tanmuktatvaṃ yad baddhatvāpagamāt tadvaśitvaṃ svātantryābhivyaktiḥ // MrgTV_1,7.3,1:2
children.translated_text: And the liberation of the liberated one is just this much — that upon the removal of bondage, there is mastery, the manifestation of independence.

children.text: * tathā hi loke'pi bandharahito vaśī baddhaśca vaśya ityucyate // MrgTV_1,7.3,1:3
children.translated_text: For in the world too, one who is free from bonds is called a master, and one who is bound is called a subject.

children.text: * kimata ityāha // MrgTV_1,7.3,1:4
children.translated_text: What follows from this? He says:

children.text: * tattasmāddhetor yad etadātmana iṣṭaprāptyādau pāratantryaṃ tadbaddhatvaṃ gamayati iti śeṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.3,2:1
children.translated_text: Therefore — from this reason — that this dependence of the soul regarding the attainment of the desired and so forth indicates its bondage. This is to be supplied.

children.text: * nahy abaddhasya svātantryavyāghāto bhavatīti // MrgTV_1,7.3,2:2
children.translated_text: For one who is not bound never has his independence thwarted.

children.text: * na ca tad ātmano 'nādikālīnatayājñānakriyāśaktivan nityam eṣṭavyam aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt // MrgTV_1,7.3,2:3
children.translated_text: Nor should that [bondage] be considered eternal for the soul, like the powers of knowledge and action that are beginningless — because that would lead to an undesirable consequence.

children.text: * tathāhi // MrgTV_1,7.3,2:4
children.translated_text: For consider:

children.text: tatpāratantryaṃ baddhatvaṃ tasminnitye cidādivat /
children.translated_text: If that dependence, which is bondage, were eternal in the soul like consciousness (<s>cit</s>) and the rest,

children.text: muktisādhanasaṃdoho vyartho'lam anayā dhiyā || MrgT_1,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: the entire collection of means to liberation would be useless — enough with this notion!

children.text: * tasminn ātmanaḥ pāratantrye nitye'bhyupagamyamāne kadācidapi tadanucchedān muktisādhanakalāpaḥ parair apīṣṭo jñānayogādir anarthakaḥ svātantryābhivyaktyabhāvāt sadaivātmano baddhatayāvasthiter ity alam anayā dhiyā nivāryatām īdṛśī saṃsārānucchittiheturmatiriti bhāvaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.4:1
children.translated_text: If this dependence of the soul were accepted as eternal, then since it could never be destroyed, the collection of means to liberation — knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), <s>yoga</s>, and the like, desired even by others — would be purposeless, because the manifestation of independence would never occur and the soul would remain forever in the state of bondage. Enough with this notion! — the import is: let such a view, which is the cause of the perpetuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>, be abandoned.

children.text: * tasmāt sthitam etatpāśakṛtaṃ pāratantryaṃ pāśāś cāñjanādayaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.4:2
children.translated_text: Therefore it is established that dependence is caused by the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>), and the bonds are <s>añjana</s> (impurity) and the rest.

children.text: * sa kilātmā // MrgTV_1,7.4:3
children.translated_text: That soul indeed —

children.text: nityavyāpakacicchaktinidhir apyarthasiddhaye /
children.translated_text: though it is a repository of eternal, all-pervading power of consciousness (<s>cit</s>), for the accomplishment of its ends

children.text: pāśavaṃ śāmbhavaṃ vāpi nānviṣyaty anyathā balam || MrgT_1,7.5 ||
children.translated_text: it does not seek any power other than that of bonds or that of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva).

children.text: * yadi hy aṇur anādyavidyoparuddhacicchaktir na bhavet tadānīṃ nityavyāpakacicchaktyāspadatve satyapi kathaṃ bhavāvasthāyāṃ bhogalakṣaṇasyārthasya niṣpattaye paśoridaṃ pāśavaṃ paśūcitaṃ kalādyuttejanaṃ svasāmarthyasyānviṣyaty apekṣate muktinimittaṃ ca kathaṃ śāmbhavaṃ balam anveṣate nānyathā balaṃ pratīkṣate pāśānabhyupagame sati svabhāvata evāmalacitsvarūpatvāt tadanveṣaṇasyānarthakyāt // MrgTV_1,7.5:1
children.translated_text: For if the soul were not one whose power of consciousness has been obstructed by beginningless ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), then, though being the abode of eternal, all-pervading power of consciousness, how in the state of worldly existence would it seek this power belonging to the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) — the befitting stimulation of <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) and the rest for the accomplishment of its ends characterized as enjoyment? And how would it seek the power of <s>Śambhu</s> as the means of liberation? It would not otherwise seek any [external] power — because if bonds were not accepted, then since its nature would inherently be pure consciousness, there would be no purpose in such seeking.

children.text: * yataś cāvasthādvaye 'pyayaṃ pāśavaṃ vā pārameśvaraṃ vā balottejanamapekṣate tasmāt kimapyasyāsti jñānakriyāsaṃnirodhakaṃ yatkṛtaḥ svātantryavyāghātaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.5:2
children.translated_text: And since in both states [of bondage and liberation] it seeks either the power of the bonds or the power of the Lord for stimulation, therefore there is something that obstructs its powers of knowledge and action, on account of which its independence is thwarted.

children.text: tadāvaraṇam asyāṇoḥ pañcasrotasi śāṃkare /
children.translated_text: That covering of this soul, in the five-streamed scripture of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva),

children.text: paryāyair bahubhirgītam adṛṣṭaṃ paśubhiḥ sadā || MrgT_1,7.6 ||
children.translated_text: has been proclaimed by many synonyms, [and it is] ever unseen by the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>).

children.text: * asyātmanas tadāvaraṇam añjanaṃ pañcasrotasi śaive śāstre vakṣyamāṇair nāmabhir abhihitam // MrgTV_1,7.6:1
children.translated_text: That covering of the soul, [called] <s>añjana</s> (impurity), has been described in the <s>Śaiva</s> scripture with the names to be stated.

children.text: * tattu paśubhiḥ paśuśāstrapraṇetṛbhiḥ kadācidapi na buddham // MrgTV_1,7.6:2
children.translated_text: But the bound souls — those who authored the scriptures of the bound (<s>paśuśāstra</s>) — never perceived it.

children.text: * atha kair nāmabhis tacchāstreṣūktam ityāha // MrgTV_1,7.6:3
children.translated_text: Now, by what names is it spoken of in those scriptures? He says:

children.text: paśutvapaśunīhāramṛtyumūrchāmalāñjanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By [the synonyms] <s>paśutva</s> (the state of being bound), <s>paśunīhāra</s> (the mist of bondage), <s>mṛtyu</s> (death), <s>mūrcchā</s> (delusion), <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>añjana</s> (collyrium/defilement),

children.text: avidyāvṛtirugglānipāpamūlakṣapādibhiḥ || MrgT_1,7.7 ||
children.translated_text: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>vṛti</s> (disposition), <s>ruk</s> (affliction), <s>glāni</s> (weakness), <s>pāpa</s> (sin), <s>mūla</s> (root), <s>kṣapa</s> (destruction), and so forth.

children.text: * na ca tadekaikasminnātmani bhinnam api tv ekam anekacidāvārakaśaktiyuktam ityāha // MrgTV_1,7.7:1
children.translated_text: And that [impurity] is not separate in each individual soul, but is one, possessing the power to veil multiple consciousnesses. He says:

children.text: tadekaṃ sarvabhūtānām anādi nibiḍaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: That is one for all beings, beginningless, dense, and vast,

children.text: pratyātmasthasvakālāntāpāyiśaktisamūhavat || MrgT_1,7.8 ||
children.translated_text: as if having a host of powers that reside in each soul and depart at their own [appointed] time.

children.text: * tadāvaraṇaṃ caturdaśavidhasyāpi bhūtasargasyaikam eva // MrgTV_1,7.8:1
children.translated_text: That covering is one for the entire creation of fourteen types of beings.

children.text: * kasmād ityatraiva viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa hetumāha anādīti yasmād vakṣyamāṇayopapattyā tat sarvabhūtānām anādi na māyīyabandhanavad āgantukam ata evaikam // MrgTV_1,7.8:2
children.translated_text: Why? Through the qualifications given here itself, he states the reason: 'beginningless' — because, as will be established through the reasoning to follow, it is beginningless for all beings, not adventitious like the bondage of <s>māyā</s>; and therefore it is one.

children.text: * anekatve hi tasyācetanatvāt kāraṇāntarapūrvakatvenānāditvānupapattiḥ // MrgTV_1,7.8:3
children.translated_text: For if it were many, since it is unconscious, its beginninglessness would be impossible because of its being preceded by another cause [i.e., it would have to have an origin].

children.text: * na ca kāraṇāntarapūrvakatve'pi kalādivat pāramparyeṇa bandhakatvādanāditvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti vācyaṃ yathoktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe /
children.translated_text: Nor can it be said that even with being preceded by another cause, it would still be beginningless by being a binder in succession, like <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) and the rest — for as stated in the glorious <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: * yathānādir malas tasya karmāpyevam anādikam /
children.translated_text: 'Just as <s>mala</s> (impurity) of the soul is beginningless, so too <s>karma</s> (action) is beginningless.'

children.text: * yadyanādi na saṃsiddhaṃ vaicitryaṃ kena hetunā // MrgTV_1,7.8:4
children.translated_text: 'If [it is] beginningless, then by what cause is the established diversity [of souls' conditions] accomplished?'

children.text: * tasmādanādikaṃ karma māyāpyevaṃ bhavettathā // MrgTV_1,7.8:5
children.translated_text: 'Therefore <s>karma</s> is beginningless, and <s>māyā</s> too would be likewise.'

children.text: * iti tadvirahiṇaḥ śivasyeva punarbandhāsaṃbhavāt // MrgTV_1,7.8:6
children.translated_text: Thus, [if mala were adventitious,] just as for <s>Śiva</s> who is free from it, re-bondage would be impossible [for liberated souls].

children.text: * tatsadbhāve vā na malarahitatvamiti vakṣyāmaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.8:7
children.translated_text: Or, if it existed [as adventitious], freedom from <s>mala</s> would not be [possible] — this we shall explain.

children.text: * nibiḍaṃ ghanamabhedyamityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.8:8
children.translated_text: 'Dense' (<s>nibiḍa</s>) means thick, impenetrable — this is the meaning.

children.text: * vyāpakānām ātmanām āvārakatvāt mahat // MrgTV_1,7.8:9
children.translated_text: 'Vast' (<s>mahat</s>) — because it covers the souls which are all-pervading.

children.text: * pratyātmasthena svasvapariṇāmakālāpasāriṇā śaktivrātena yuktam // MrgTV_1,7.8:10
children.translated_text: [It is] endowed with a host of powers that reside in each individual soul and depart at the time of each one's maturation.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ tattvatrayanirṇaye /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said in the <s>Tattvatrayanirṇaya</s>:

children.text: * malaśaktayo vibhinnāḥ pratyātmaṃ caiva tadguṇāvarikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The powers of <s>mala</s> are differentiated, residing in each soul and covering its qualities.'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,7.8:11
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tac cāñjanam // MrgTV_1,7.8:12
children.translated_text: And that <s>añjana</s> (impurity) —

children.text: tadanādistham arvāgvā taddhetus tadato'nyathā /
children.translated_text: if it has existed in [the soul] since beginningless time, or if it [has attached] later — its cause [must be stated]; otherwise,

children.text: ruṇaddhi muktānevaṃ cenmokṣe yatnastato mṛṣā || MrgT_1,7.9 ||
children.translated_text: it would obstruct even liberated souls — if so, then effort toward liberation is vain.

children.text: * tatteṣām ātmanām anādau kāle sthitamanādisthaṃ na tv ādimattvena sthitam // MrgTV_1,7.9:1
children.translated_text: That covering has stood in those souls since beginningless time — it is 'abiding since the beginningless' (<s>anādistha</s>), not as having a beginning.

children.text: * atraiva yuktimāha arvāgveti yadi hy ādimattvenātmasusthitaṃ tadabhyupagamyate tadā tadyoge hetuḥ vācyaḥ ityadhyāhāraḥ // MrgTV_1,7.9:2
children.translated_text: He states the reasoning here itself through 'or later' (<s>arvāgvā</s>) — if it is accepted that [the impurity] was established as having a beginning in the soul, then a cause for its conjunction must be stated — this is to be supplied.

children.text: * tad ato'nyatheti yadi tu tadañjanamato 'nyatheti hetum anapekṣyaivātmānam āśliṣyati tadānīṃ muktān apyātmano ruṇaddhi uparuddhadṛkkriyān karotīti prasaktam // MrgTV_1,7.9:3
children.translated_text: 'Otherwise from that' (<s>tadato'nyathā</s>) — if that <s>añjana</s> (impurity) 'otherwise,' that is, without depending on a cause, embraces the soul, then it follows that it would obstruct even liberated souls — that is, it would render their vision and action obstructed.

children.text: * ko doṣa iti cet mokṣe yatnastato mṛṣeti // MrgTV_1,7.9:4
children.translated_text: What is the defect in that, one might ask? [The answer is:] 'Then effort toward liberation is vain.'

children.text: * muktātmāno'pi yadi punaḥpunar malena yujyante tato gajasnānaprāye 'smin mokṣe mithyaiva yatnaḥ bhūyo'pi malayogataḥ saṃsāritāyāḥ sambhavāt // MrgTV_1,7.9:5
children.translated_text: If liberated souls too were to be conjoined with <s>mala</s> (impurity) again and again, then in this liberation which would be like the bathing of an elephant, effort would be truly futile, since the possibility of returning to the state of a transmigrating soul through renewed conjunction with <s>mala</s> would remain.

children.text: * tasmān nāgantukamātmanāṃ malaṃ kiṃ tarhi anādi // MrgTV_1,7.9:6
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>mala</s> of souls is not adventitious; rather, it is beginningless.

children.text: * tathā coktaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuvādau /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been said in the glorious <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and other [texts]:

children.text: * athānādir malaḥ puṃsāṃ paśutvaṃ parikīrtitam /
children.translated_text: 'Now, the beginningless <s>mala</s> (impurity) of souls is declared to be their <s>paśutva</s> (state of being bound).'

children.text: * iti // MrgTV_1,7.9:7
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * athāsyaiva yuktyantaramāha // MrgTV_1,7.9:8
children.translated_text: Now he states another reasoning for this very point:

children.text: tadekaṃ bahusaṃkhyaṃ tu tādṛg utpattimad yataḥ /
children.translated_text: That is one; but if it were many, since such a thing would be originated [i.e., have a beginning] —

children.text: * tadañjanam ekam anekatve pramāṇābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,7.10ab:1
children.translated_text: That <s>añjana</s> (impurity) is one, because there is no evidence for its being many.

children.text: * yato yasmāt tādṛgiti tathāvidham anekatvapariṇāmitvādiguṇayuktaṃ yad anekaṃ ghaṭādivad utpadyamānaṃ dṛṣṭam // MrgTV_1,7.10ab:2
children.translated_text: 'Since' (<s>yataḥ</s>) — because something of that kind, possessing qualities such as multiplicity and susceptibility to transformation, when it is many, is seen to be originated like pots and the like.

children.text: * na caitad utpattimad anādyātmāvārakatvāt ata ekam anekatve hi kāraṇapūrvakatvād asyādimattvaṃ syāt // MrgTV_1,7.10ab:3
children.translated_text: But this [mala] is not originated, because it covers the souls from beginningless time; therefore it is one — for if it were many, it would have a beginning because of being preceded by a cause.

children.text: * pratyātmasthasvakālāntāpāyiśaktisamūhavat /
children.translated_text: 'As if having a host of powers that reside in each soul and depart at their own [appointed] time' —

children.text: * iti yaduktaṃ tad upapādayitum āha // MrgTV_1,7.10ab:4
children.translated_text: in order to establish what was said [previously], he says:

children.text: kiṃtu tacchaktayo'nekā yugapanmuktyadarśanāt || MrgT_1,7.10 ||
children.translated_text: However, its powers are many, because liberation is not observed to occur simultaneously.

children.text: * ekasyāpyasyānekāḥ pratyātmasthāś citkriyāsaṃnirodhikā nityāḥ śaktaya eṣṭavyāḥ // MrgTV_1,7.10cd:1
children.translated_text: Even though this [mala] is one, its powers — which reside in each individual soul and obstruct consciousness and action, and which are eternal — must be accepted as many.

children.text: * anyathaikatve sati ekasmāt puruṣādapasṛte tasmin sarveṣāṃ tulyakālaṃ muktiḥ syāt // MrgTV_1,7.10cd:2
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if it were [entirely] one, when it departed from a single soul, liberation would occur simultaneously for all at the same time.

children.text: * yatastu na muktir yaugapadyenopalabhyate tasmāt kāraṇāt tacchaktibahutvābhyupagamo yuktaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.10cd:3
children.translated_text: Since, however, liberation is not observed to occur simultaneously, therefore the acceptance of the multiplicity of its powers is reasonable.

children.text: * na ca tās tacchaktayaḥ svātantryeṇa rundhanti apasaranti vā kiṃ tarhi // MrgTV_1,7.10cd:4
children.translated_text: And those powers of it do not obstruct or depart independently; rather —

children.text: tāsāṃ māheśvarī śaktiḥ sarvānugrāhikā śivā /
children.translated_text: The power of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), which is all-gracing and auspicious (<s>śivā</s>),

children.text: dharmānuvartanādeva pāśa ityupacaryate || MrgT_1,7.11 ||
children.translated_text: because it follows the nature of [those powers], is figuratively called a 'bond' (<s>pāśa</s>).

children.text: * prāvṛtīśabale karma // MrgTV_1,7.11:1
children.translated_text: 'The variegated power, <s>karma</s>' —

children.text: * ityādinā prāk malena nāntarīyakatayoddiṣṭāṃ parameśvararodhaśaktiṃ vyāpāreṇa lakṣayati tāsāṃ malaśaktīnāṃ citkriyāsaṃnirodhakatvalakṣaṇasya dharmasyānuvartanāddhetoḥ śaivī śaktiḥ pāśatayopacaryate // MrgTV_1,7.11:2
children.translated_text: by such [earlier statements], the obstructing power (<s>rodhaśakti</s>) of <s>Parameśvara</s>, previously indicated as inseparable from <s>mala</s>, is here characterized by its function: because it follows the nature (<s>dharma</s>) of the powers of <s>mala</s> — that is, the property of obstructing consciousness and action — for this reason the power of <s>Śiva</s> is figuratively designated as a bond (<s>pāśa</s>).

children.text: * na ca tatra mukhyaṃ pāśatvam // MrgTV_1,7.11:3
children.translated_text: But bondage is not its primary nature.

children.text: * kuta iti viśeṣaṇadvāreṇātraiva hetuḥ sarvānugrāhikā śiveti // MrgTV_1,7.11:4
children.translated_text: Why? Through the qualifications given here itself, the reason [is stated]: 'all-gracing and auspicious (<s>śivā</s>).'

children.text: * sā hi sakalajagadanugrahasvabhāvatvena tacchreyaḥprasādhikā // MrgTV_1,7.11:5
children.translated_text: For that [power], having the nature of grace toward the entire universe, is the effectuator of its welfare.

children.text: * evaṃ ca // MrgTV_1,7.11:6
children.translated_text: And thus —

children.text: pariṇāmayaty etāśca rodhāntaṃ kārkacittviṣā /
children.translated_text: It matures these [powers of mala] up to the point of obstruction, with the harshness of its radiance;

children.text: yadonmīlanamādhatte tadānugrāhikocyate || MrgT_1,7.12 ||
children.translated_text: when it effects the unfolding [of the soul], then it is called 'the grace-bestowing one.'

children.text: * pariṇāmaśabdāt prātipadikāddhātvarthe iti ṇici kṛte pariṇāmayatīti rūpam // MrgTV_1,7.12:1
children.translated_text: From the nominal stem <s>pariṇāma</s>, applying the causal suffix <s>ṇic</s> in the sense of the verbal root, the form <s>pariṇāmayati</s> (causes to mature) is derived.

children.text: * etāśca sarvabhūtagatās tasya sambandhinī śaktiḥ rodhāntaṃ tadadhikārakālaṃ yāvat pariṇāmena yojayatī patiśaktiḥ kārkacittviṣā hetubhūtayonmīlanaṃ yadā karoti tadānugrāhiketyucyate // MrgTV_1,7.12:2
children.translated_text: These [powers of mala] residing in all beings — the power belonging to the Lord matures them through transformation up to the limit of their commission-period (<s>adhikārakāla</s>). [It is] the power of the Lord (<s>patiśakti</s>); when, with its causative radiance and harshness, it effects the unfolding [of the soul], then it is called 'the grace-bestowing one.'

children.text: * kaśabdena mūrdhā sadānugrahaikavyāpāra īśānaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.12:3
children.translated_text: By the syllable 'ka' [in <s>kārkacit</s>], [is meant] the head — <s>Īśāna</s>, whose sole activity is perpetual grace.

children.text: * īśānamūrdheti mantraliṅgam // MrgTV_1,7.12:4
children.translated_text: '<s>Īśāna</s>-head' — this is a <s>mantra</s>-marker.

children.text: * sa eva sakalajagadanugrahe nityodyuktatvād arkeṇopamitaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.12:5
children.translated_text: He himself, being eternally engaged in the grace of the entire universe, is compared to the sun.

children.text: * tataḥ pravṛttayā paraśreyaḥprakāśikayā jñānabhāsā tayonmīlitasvarūpāṇām aṇuvargāṇāṃ yadonmīlanam āśayavikāsanaṃ karoti tadānugrāhikā bhaṇyate // MrgTV_1,7.12:6
children.translated_text: From the light of knowledge proceeding from that [Īśāna], which illuminates the supreme good for others, when the unfolding — the opening of the inner disposition — of the classes of souls whose nature has been made manifest by that [light] is effected, then [that power] is called 'the grace-bestowing one.'

children.text: * atra muniḥ praśnayati // MrgTV_1,7.12:7
children.translated_text: Here the sage poses a question:

children.text: śambhoś cidādyanugrāhyaṃ tadvirodhitayā mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The grace-recipients of <s>Śambhu</s> — consciousness (<s>cit</s>) and the rest — being mutually opposed,

children.text: yugapan na kṣamaṃ śaktiḥ sarvānugrāhikā katham || MrgT_1,7.13 ||
children.translated_text: [grace toward all] simultaneously is not possible; so how is the power all-gracing?

children.text: kathaṃ bhūtopakārārthaṃ pravṛttasya jagatprabhoḥ /
children.translated_text: How is it fitting that the Lord of the universe, who is engaged for the benefit of beings,

children.text: apakārakamāviśya yujyate tunnatodanam || MrgT_1,7.14 ||
children.translated_text: entering that which causes harm, engages in prodding and piercing?

children.text: * citaḥ sakalātmānaḥ ādigrahaṇād acito malakarmamāyātatkāryāṇi // MrgTV_1,7.14:1
children.translated_text: '<s>Cit</s>' refers to all the conscious souls (<s>sakalātmānaḥ</s>); by the word 'ādi' (and the rest), the unconscious [entities are meant] — <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and their effects.

children.text: * tadetatsarvaṃ sarveśitvādeva kila parameśvarasyānugrāhyam // MrgTV_1,7.14:2
children.translated_text: And all of this is indeed to be graced by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), precisely because he is the Lord of all.

children.text: * tac cānugrāhyatvam eṣāṃ cidacitāṃ pāśyapāśānāṃ tulyakālaṃ na ghaṭate // MrgTV_1,7.14:3
children.translated_text: But the gracing of these — the conscious and the unconscious, the bonds and the bound — cannot take place simultaneously.

children.text: * tathā hy acitāṃ pāśānāmanugrahe pāśyasya pratyuta tiraskāraḥ syāt nānugrahaḥ citām anugrahe ca tadbandhānāṃ nyagbhāvanamiti parasparavirodhitvād yugapad eṣām anugrahānupapattiḥ // MrgTV_1,7.14:4
children.translated_text: For if the unconscious bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) were graced, that would constitute a disregard for the bound soul (<s>pāśya</s>), not grace; and if the conscious [souls] were graced, that would entail the subjugation of their bonds — therefore, since these are mutually contradictory, the simultaneous grace of both is untenable.

children.text: * tatkathaṃ sarvānugrāhikā śaktiruktā // MrgTV_1,7.14:5
children.translated_text: Then how can the power [of <s>Śiva</s>] be said to grace all?

children.text: * kiṃ ca kṛpayā sarvabhūtānām anugrahapravṛttasya patyur upakārasyāpakārakaṃ duḥkhadam āṇavādipāśajālam anugṛhya āvṛtadṛkkriyāśaktitvād asvātantryādivyathitānāṃ paramātmanāṃ bandhakānugraheṇa vyathitavyathanaṃ na yuktamiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.14:6
children.translated_text: Moreover, for the Lord who, out of compassion, is engaged in the grace of all beings — to grace the web of bonds such as the <s>āṇava</s> (innate impurity) and the rest, which are harmful and cause suffering, and [thereby] to afflict the Supreme Selves (<s>paramātmans</s>) who are already distressed by the loss of independence due to the veiling of their powers of vision and action, through the grace of their binders — this would not be proper. Such is the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

children.text: * siddhāntastu // MrgTV_1,7.14:7
children.translated_text: But the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>) is:

children.text: na todanāya kurute malasyāṇor anugraham /
children.translated_text: He does not grace the impurity (<s>mala</s>) for the sake of tormenting the soul;

children.text: kiṃtu yatkriyate kiṃcit tadupāyena nānyathā || MrgT_1,7.15 ||
children.translated_text: rather, whatever is done, is done by means [appropriate to the end], and not otherwise.

children.text: * satyaṃ cidacitām anugrāhikā śaktiḥ // MrgTV_1,7.15:1
children.translated_text: True, the power [of <s>Śiva</s>] graces both the conscious and the unconscious.

children.text: * na cāsyās tulyakālamapi tadanugraho 'nupapannaḥ parasparavirodhābhāvāt // MrgTV_1,7.15:2
children.translated_text: And the simultaneous grace of both is not untenable, because there is no mutual contradiction.

children.text: * na tv aṇor vyathanārthaṃ malasya pariṇāmarūpamanugrahaṃ karoti api tv anugrahāyaiva // MrgTV_1,7.15:3
children.translated_text: But he does not effect the grace of <s>mala</s> (impurity) in the form of its ripening for the purpose of tormenting the soul — rather, it is precisely for the sake of grace [of the soul].

children.text: * tathā hi yat kiṃcidupāyena kartumucitaṃ tan nānupāyena // MrgTV_1,7.15:4
children.translated_text: For indeed, whatever is proper to be accomplished by means, that [cannot be accomplished] without means.

children.text: * ayaṃ ca sādhūpāyaḥ yaduta // MrgTV_1,7.15:5
children.translated_text: And this is the proper means, namely:

children.text: na sādhikāre tamasi muktirbhavati kasyacit /
children.translated_text: For no one can there be liberation while the darkness (<s>tamas</s>, i.e., <s>mala</s>) still has its commission active;

children.text: adhikāro'pi tacchakteḥ pariṇāmān nivartate || MrgT_1,7.16 ||
children.translated_text: and the commission itself ceases through the ripening of that power [of <s>mala</s>].

children.text: so 'pi na svata eva syādapi yogyasya vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [ripening] too cannot occur of itself, even for a thing that is fit for it,

children.text: sarvathā sarvadā yasmāc citprayojyamacetanam || MrgT_1,7.17 ||
children.translated_text: because in every way and at all times, the unconscious is directed by the conscious.

children.text: * yāvatkila malasyādhikāras tāvan na muktiḥ kasyacidbhavati // MrgTV_1,7.17:1
children.translated_text: As long as the commission of <s>mala</s> (impurity) persists, so long liberation does not occur for anyone.

children.text: * tannivṛttir eva muktiśabdābhidheyā // MrgTV_1,7.17:2
children.translated_text: The cessation of that [commission] alone is what is denoted by the word 'liberation' (<s>mukti</s>).

children.text: * yataḥ adhikāraśca tacchakteḥ pariṇāmāt samāpyate sa ca pariṇāmas tadarhasyāpi vastuno na svato bhavituṃ śaktaḥ sarvaprakāreṇa sarvakālaṃ cācetanasya cetanaprayuktasya tattatkāryadarśanāt // MrgTV_1,7.17:3
children.translated_text: Because the commission [of <s>mala</s>] comes to an end through the ripening of that power — and that ripening, even for an entity that is fit for it, is unable to occur by itself, since in every manner and at all times, the unconscious is seen to accomplish its respective effects only when directed by the conscious.

children.text: * tasmāc cidanugrahasya tadarthāñjanādipariṇāmasya ca parasparam avirodha iti prathamacodyanirāsaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.17:4
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no contradiction between the grace of the conscious [soul] and the ripening of <s>añjana</s> (impurity) and the rest for its sake — thus the refutation of the first objection.

children.text: * atha dvitīyasya parihāraḥ // MrgTV_1,7.17:5
children.translated_text: Now the resolution of the second [objection]:

children.text: yathā kṣārādinā vaidyastudann api na rogiṇam /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician, though causing pain to the patient with caustic substances and the like,

children.text: koṭāv iṣṭārthadāyitvād duḥkhahetuḥ pratīyate || MrgT_1,7.18 ||
children.translated_text: is not regarded as a cause of suffering, because ultimately he bestows the desired result.

children.text: * pāśāvṛtadṛkkriyāvṛttiṣv aṇuṣu tattatpāśaśaktyanuvartanadvāreṇa janmadrāvaṇādiduḥkhadāyitvād vāmo 'pi parameśvaras tadabhyudayāyaiva pravṛttatvān na duḥkhahetur avagamyate yathā vaidyaḥ kṣāraśastrādinā rogiṇaṃ vyathayann api koṭau prānte abhimatasyārogyalakṣaṇasyārthasya sādhakatvāt vyathāheturapi na duḥkhadāyitvenaiva jñāyate // MrgTV_1,7.18:1
children.translated_text: Though <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), by operating through the power of the respective bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) upon the souls whose vision and action are veiled by the bonds, causes suffering in the form of birth, decay, and the like, he appears as if adverse; yet because he is engaged solely for their spiritual elevation, he is not understood as a cause of suffering — just as a physician, though causing pain to the patient with caustic substances, surgical instruments, and the like, because ultimately he is the agent of the desired result characterized as health, though a cause of pain, is not known as one who causes suffering alone.

children.text: * nanv atyantaśuddhasvarūpasya bhagavataḥ kiṃ pāśadharmānuvartanenety āha // MrgTV_1,7.18:2
children.translated_text: But for the Blessed One whose nature is utterly pure, what is the purpose of following the properties of the bonds? He says:

children.text: sarvagatvān maheśasya nādhiṣṭhānaṃ vihanyate /
children.translated_text: Because of <s>Maheśvara's</s> (the Great Lord's) omnipresence, his presiding [over the unconscious] is not obstructed;

children.text: na ca yatrāsti kartavyaṃ tasminn audāsyam eti saḥ || MrgT_1,7.19 ||
children.translated_text: and wherever there is something to be done, he does not remain indifferent to that.

children.text: * acidadhiṣṭhānaṃ bhagavato na vihanyate sarvagatvān maheśatayā sarvakartṛtvāc ca // MrgTV_1,7.19:1
children.translated_text: The presiding of the Blessed One over the unconscious is not obstructed, because of his omnipresence and because of his universal agency as the Great Lord.

children.text: * yatra yatra kartavyaṃ kimapyasti tatra tatra ca tādarthyam etyāpi tattatkartur adhiṣṭhānena sarvadaiva sarvaṃ karotītyuktam īśvarasiddhau // MrgTV_1,7.19:2
children.translated_text: And wherever there is anything whatsoever to be done, there he engages for that purpose as well — yet he does everything at all times through the presiding [over all]. This has been stated in the <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s> (Proof of the Lord).

children.text: * udāsta ityudāsas tasya bhāva audāsyam akartṛtvam ityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.19:3
children.translated_text: '<s>Udāsta</s>' [means] he who is indifferent; <s>audāsya</s> is the state of that — meaning non-agency.

children.text: * tadevaṃ yugapat sarvānugrāhitvaṃ śakteḥ prasādhya tadeva ghaṭayann anugrahaśabdārtham āha // MrgTV_1,7.19:4
children.translated_text: Having thus established the simultaneous universal grace of the power [of <s>Śiva</s>], now harmonizing that very [conclusion], he states the meaning of the word '<s>anugraha</s>' (grace):

children.text: dharmiṇo 'nugraho nāma yattad dharmānuvartanam /
children.translated_text: The grace of a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is that which is called the following of its properties (<s>dharmas</s>);

children.text: na so 'sti kasyacij jātu yaḥ patyā nānuvartyate || MrgT_1,7.20 ||
children.translated_text: there is no property of anything whatsoever that is not followed [i.e., presided over] by the Lord.

children.text: * dharmiṇo 'nugrāhyasya dharmāṇāṃ yad anuvartanaṃ so 'nugrāhakasyānugrahaḥ kramavikasvarasvarūpāṇāṃ padmānāmiva vivasvataḥ // MrgTV_1,7.20:1
children.translated_text: The following of the properties of the one to be graced (<s>dharmin</s>) — that is the grace of the one who graces, like the sun for lotuses whose nature is to bloom progressively.

children.text: * sa iti tathāvidho dharmaḥ kasyacidapi dharmiṇo nāsti yaḥ parameśvareṇa nānuvartyate nādhiṣṭhīyate tasya sarvavyāpakatvāt // MrgTV_1,7.20:2
children.translated_text: 'That' — such a property of any property-bearer whatsoever does not exist that is not followed, that is, not presided over by <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), because of his all-pervading nature.

children.text: * evaṃ ca // MrgTV_1,7.20:3
children.translated_text: And thus —

children.text: gatādhikāranīhāravīryasya sata edhate /
children.translated_text: When the commission [of <s>mala</s>] has ended and the potency of the fog-like darkness [i.e., impurity] [has been exhausted], the grace of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) increases;

children.text: paśor anugraho 'nyasya tādarthyād asti karmaṇaḥ || MrgT_1,7.21 ||
children.translated_text: and for the other [i.e., the bonds], grace exists through the purposefulness of <s>karma</s> (action) directed toward that [end].

children.text: * gataḥ samāptaḥ kriyādṛkpratirodhakatvarūpo 'dhikāro yasya tadgatādhikāraṃ nīhārasya tamaso malasya sambandhi vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ yasya tasya tathāvidhasya sataḥ paśor baddhātmano 'nugraha edhate vardhate bahulībhavati nivṛttādhikārāyāṃ malaśaktāv iti yāvat // MrgTV_1,7.21:1
children.translated_text: 'Whose commission has ended' — the commission, whose nature is the obstruction of action and vision, has been completed; the potency, the capability, belonging to the fog-like darkness, that is, the impurity (<s>mala</s>) — of such a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), a fettered self, the grace increases, grows, becomes abundant — that is, when the power of <s>mala</s> whose commission has ceased [is exhausted].

children.text: * anyasya tu malādeḥ pāśajālasya yat karmaṇaḥ pariṇāmitādes tādarthyaṃ tatprayojakatvaṃ tasmād anugraho bhavati // MrgTV_1,7.21:2
children.translated_text: But for the other — the web of bonds such as <s>mala</s> and the rest — whatever purposefulness, that is, instrumentality toward that [end], exists in <s>karma</s> (action) through its ripening and the like — from that, grace comes about.

children.text: * baddhātmavimuktyai yat pariṇāmitāprayojakatvaṃ sa eva pāśānām anugraha ityarthaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.21:3
children.translated_text: The ripening and instrumentality [of <s>karma</s>] toward the liberation of the bound self — that itself is the grace of the bonds. This is the meaning.

children.text: * evaṃ ca prakṛte kiṃ vyavasthitam ityāha // MrgTV_1,7.21:4
children.translated_text: And what then has been established in the present context? He says:

children.text: boddhṛtvapariṇāmitvadharmayor anuvartanam /
children.translated_text: The following of the properties of being a knower and of undergoing transformation,

children.text: malasya sādhikārasya nivṛttestatparicyutau || MrgT_1,7.22 ||
children.translated_text: upon the cessation of the commission of <s>mala</s> (impurity), at the falling away from that [bondage] —

children.text: * malasya sādhikārasyety āṇavasyāñjanasyādhikāranivṛttes tadbhāvabhāvinyā anādikālīnāyāḥ parameśvararodhaśakter apagamonmukhyāḥ paricyutau kiṃcic chithilībhāve sati boddhṛtvadharmānuvartanam ātmano'nugrahaḥ pariṇāmitvadharmānuvartanaṃ pāśānāmiti // MrgTV_1,7.22:1
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>mala</s> that still has its commission' — of the innate impurity (<s>āṇava</s>, <s>añjana</s>): upon the cessation of the commission, [and] upon the loosening, the slight relaxation, of the falling away — [which involves] the withdrawal of the beginningless obstructing power of <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose existence is contingent upon the existence of that [commission] — the following of the property of being a knower is the grace of the self; the following of the property of undergoing transformation is [the grace] of the bonds.

children.text: * upasaṃharann āha // MrgTV_1,7.22:2
children.translated_text: Concluding, he says:

children.text: ityevaṃ yaugapadyena kramātsughaṭa eva hi /
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, the simultaneity [of grace to both conscious and unconscious] is well-established through [its proper] sequence;

children.text: māyāyāḥ sādhikārāyāḥ karmaṇaścokta eva te || MrgT_1,7.23 ||
children.translated_text: and the grace of <s>Māyā</s> that still has its commission, and of <s>karma</s> (action), has also been stated to you.

children.text: * ityevam uktayā yuktyā yaugapadyena cidacitor anugraho na viruddhaḥ kramāt sughaṭa eva na durupapādaḥ // MrgTV_1,7.23:1
children.translated_text: Thus, by the reasoning stated, the simultaneous grace of the conscious and the unconscious is not contradictory; through [proper] sequence it is perfectly well-established, not difficult to demonstrate.

children.text: * malavac ca māyāyāśca kalādikṣityantasvādhikārasahitāyāḥ kalādyāvirbhāvalakṣaṇas tadupasaṃhārātmakaśca karmaṇastu phaladānaunmukhyāpādanātmakaḥ so 'yamanugraho māyākarmaṇor anukto 'pyukta eva jñeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And like <s>mala</s> (impurity), the grace of <s>Māyā</s> too — together with its commission extending from <s>kalā</s> down to earth — characterized as the manifestation of <s>kalā</s> and the rest, and [the grace] that has the nature of the withdrawal of those [products]; and the grace of <s>karma</s>, characterized as bringing about the readiness for the bestowal of fruits — this grace of <s>Māyā</s> and <s>karma</s>, though not explicitly stated, should be understood as having been stated,

children.text: * sarvathā sarvadā yasmāc citprayojyam acetanam /
children.translated_text: since 'in every way and at all times, the unconscious is directed by the conscious' —

children.text: * iti sāmānyena sarvasyaivoktatvād iti // MrgTV_1,7.23:2
children.translated_text: because everything has been stated in general terms by this [principle].

children.text:
...
(to be continued)
